actual-bonus-frame-energy.relation_to_goal:
This is a coupled replacement for every false independent-bonus inequality.
It uses the same common directions, positive weights, endpoint widths, and
support deficits.  Applied to the three-cap certificate, actual endpoint
contributions dominate the \(E_i\), so the result gives a frame-sensitive
total payment that cannot be prescribed independently of the middle cover.
actual-bonus-frame-energy.statement:
In the notation of accepted fact `508b5d8f1a3d6fca`, let
\(u_1,u_2,u_3\) be nonparallel positively spanning unit directions with
weights \(\alpha_i>0\) satisfying
\(\sum_i\alpha_i u_i=0\).  Put
\[
v_i=\alpha_i u_i,\quad K=-(A_0+A_2),\quad
m=\min\{a_0,a_2\},
\]
\[
D_i=\frac{w_0(u_i)^2}{a_0}+\frac{w_2(u_i)^2}{a_2},
\qquad
E_i=(\gamma_0^{u_i}\square\gamma_2^{u_i})(d_{u_i}(z)).
\]
Prove the dichotomy: either some \(E_i\ge m\), or
\[
\sum_{i=1}^3\alpha_i\sqrt{D_iE_i}
\ge
\sqrt{2|\det(v_1,v_2)|\,|K|}.
\]
In the second case, deduce
\[
\sum_{i=1}^3E_i
\ge
\frac{2|\det(v_1,v_2)|\,|K|}
{\sum_{i=1}^3\alpha_i^2D_i}.
\]
actual-bonus-frame-energy.status_reason: Accepted fact `de3c80720a026e04` proves the registered actual-bonus dichotomy and the weighted common-frame energy lower bound.
actual-bonus-frame-energy.success_criterion:
A proof must derive the quantitative support-area lower bound or cite it only
after acceptance, handle negative deficits via positive parts, justify the
case split \(E_i<m\), apply the width-sensitive cap estimate with the correct
inequality direction, and verify the final Cauchy--Schwarz denominator.

adaptive-centroid-segment.statement:
In the balanced compatible regime, analyze the one-parameter family
\[
z_t=(1-t)\frac{c_0+c_2}{2}+t c_1,\qquad 0\le t\le1.
\]
Derive an exact halfspace-depth lower bound for at least one explicitly chosen
\(t\), or give an exact compatible triple proving that every point in this
segment can have depth below \(2T/9\).
adaptive-centroid-segment.status_reason:
Accepted lemma `009a0ffca7cbccd8` proves an exact lower bound for every point

adaptive-centroid-segment.success_criterion:

affine-slack-concavity.relation_to_goal: Accepted fact `a5309a9087686166` identifies the exact statistic missing from the three-cover proof. Any bound contradicting its necessary inequality rules out a low-mass cover and proves a middle-slice witness. This route attacks the cover globally rather than choosing a point first.
affine-slack-concavity.statement:
In the minimal family \(A_1=(A_0+A_2)/2\), suppose at most three strict low-mass halfspaces cover the middle slice as in accepted fact `a5309a9087686166`. Use the concavity of the one-dimensional projection densities of \(A_0,A_2\), together with the joint cover, to derive a quantitative lower bound on
\[
\sum_r E_r
\]
or an equivalent upper bound on \(\sum_r d_r\) that is stronger than the cap-area relaxation.
affine-slack-concavity.status_reason: Accepted lemma `541afa94853c6bab` gives the exact full-distribution affine-slack defect formula and reduces its sharp cap-conditioned extremum to at most three tent components per outer projection density. It also inserts those sharp one-halfspace defects into the accepted three-cover inequality.
affine-slack-concavity.success_criterion: Produce a proved bound that rules out covers on a nonempty portion of the strict residual area strip not already certified by accepted area-only facts, or an exact sharp extremal formula for one halfspace in terms of normalized concave projection densities and signed support clearances. A formula using only zero-threshold cap areas does not meet the criterion.

affine-slack-moment-brunn-minkowski.relation_to_goal:
This is a distance-weighted strengthening of the same-direction cap
containment used throughout the proof graph.  Unlike exact-cell areas, it
retains how far points lie from the cutting line and is a possible input to
the common-frame bridge and deformation-growth subgoals.
affine-slack-moment-brunn-minkowski.statement:
Let \(A_0,A_1,A_2\subset\mathbb R^2\) be compact two-dimensional
convex bodies satisfying \((A_0+A_2)/2\subseteq A_1\).  Let \(f\) be
affine and \(L\in\mathbb R\).  Define
\[
I_0=\int_{A_0}(L-f(x))_+\,dx,\qquad
I_1=\int_{A_1}(-f(z))_+\,dz,\qquad
I_2=\int_{A_2}(-L-f(y))_+\,dy.
\]
Prove
\[
I_1^{1/3}\ge\frac{I_0^{1/3}+I_2^{1/3}}2.
\]
Cover zero moments, affine-constant cases, measurability, and all boundary
conventions.
affine-slack-moment-brunn-minkowski.status_reason:
The exact obstacle packet
`.math-prover/handoffs/870906085a8d4b14.md` gives compatible square
counterexamples with \(I_0>0\) and \(I_1=I_2=0\), including a nonconstant
affine function.  It also identifies the valid conditional statement when
both closed endpoint slack caps are nonempty.  Thus the registered
unconditional subgoal is false and is closed negatively.
affine-slack-moment-brunn-minkowski.success_criterion:
Construct the three lifted subgraph bodies in \(\mathbb R^3\), prove their
midpoint containment exactly from compatibility and affinity, identify their
volumes with the three slack moments, and apply three-dimensional
Brunn–Minkowski with every degenerate case justified.

affine-slack-moment-nonempty-endpoints.relation_to_goal:
This is the valid finite-interior form of the false unconditional
slack-moment claim recorded under
`affine-slack-moment-brunn-minkowski`. It retains transverse distance
from the cutting line and can be applied only in canonical rows whose
accepted incidence hypotheses force both endpoint caps to be nonempty.
It does not by itself prove a common-level charge or the locked target.
affine-slack-moment-nonempty-endpoints.statement:
Let \(A_0,A_1,A_2\subset\mathbb R^2\) be compact two-dimensional
convex bodies satisfying \((A_0+A_2)/2\subseteq A_1\). Let \(f\) be
affine and \(L\in\mathbb R\). Define
\[
I_0=\int_{A_0}(L-f(x))_+\,dx,\qquad
I_1=\int_{A_1}(-f(z))_+\,dz,\qquad
I_2=\int_{A_2}(-L-f(y))_+\,dy.
\]
Assume both closed endpoint slack caps
\[
A_0\cap\{f\le L\},\qquad A_2\cap\{f\le-L\}
\]
are nonempty. Prove
\[
I_1^{1/3}\ge\frac{I_0^{1/3}+I_2^{1/3}}2,
\]
including touching zero-moment cases, constant affine functions, and
all boundary conventions.
affine-slack-moment-nonempty-endpoints.status_reason:
Accepted fact `c33057d413e5306c` proves the registered conditional
slack-moment inequality with compact convex lifted sets. It covers

affine-slack-moment-nonempty-endpoints.success_criterion:
Give a complete lifted-body proof. Prove compactness, convexity,
midpoint containment, and the exact volume identities, and justify the
three-dimensional Brunn–Minkowski step when either nonempty lift has

all-triangle-full-profile-theorem.statement: Assume \(A_0,A_1,A_2\) are nondegenerate triangles satisfying \((A_0+A_2)/2\subseteq A_1\). Prove the locked \(2T/9\) centerpoint conclusion for this entire finite-dimensional class, including the strict residual area strip, using the exact full middle profile and allowing the endpoint allocation to depend on direction. Do not replace the endpoint infimal convolution by a common allocation, a fixed endpoint depth, or the maximum of two support-extreme routings.
all-triangle-full-profile-theorem.success_criterion: A complete proof for all relative positions and area regimes with exact cap formulas, or a fully exact compatible triangular counterexample to the locked target. Partial homothetic, aligned-edge, or open-subfamily results do not close this subgoal but may be submitted only if they remove a sharply defined remaining branch.

anchored-weighted-tail-dual.relation_to_goal: This is the exact analytic hypothesis produced by the homothetic geometric reduction. anchored-weighted-tail-dual.statement:
Let \(h\) be a nonnegative concave probability density on an anchored support interval \([0,L]\), extended by zero only for defining tails, and suppose \(\int_0^L yh(y)\,dy=1\). Prove
\[
G(1)+a^2G(w_0)+c^2G(w_2)\ge \frac{2(1+a^2+c^2)}9
\]
for every \(a\ge c>0\) satisfying \(1<a^2+c^2\), \(a+c<2\), and \(a^2<1+c^2\), and every real \(w_0,w_2\) satisfying \(aw_0+cw_2=2\). Seek a direct dual or lower-convex-envelope certificate valid for one-kink extremizers.
anchored-weighted-tail-dual.status_reason: Accepted fact `52e60b02804280c7` proves the full anchored weighted-tail inequality by a uniform affine tent-kernel minorant.
anchored-weighted-tail-dual.success_criterion: A complete proof for every anchored support length and threshold ordering, preferably as an affine minorant of the tent kernel at peak barycenter \(3-L\), or one exact remaining chamber with all other chambers discharged.

asymmetric-triangle-mixture.statement:
Let \(\Delta\) be any rational nondegenerate triangle and set
\[
A_1=\Delta,\qquad A_0=\frac9{10}\Delta,\qquad

balanced-middle-trace-safety.relation_to_goal:
At an equal-six-sector point, each of the three concurrent fan lines bisects

that at least two selected rows exceed the target.  Accepted fact

balanced-middle-trace-safety.statement:
Let \(A_0,A_1,A_2\subset\mathbb R^2\) be compatible compact
two-dimensional convex bodies.  Write
\[
M=\max\{|A_0|,|A_2|\},\qquad m=\min\{|A_0|,|A_2|\},\qquad
a=|A_1|,\qquad T=M+m+a,
\]
and assume \(M-m<a<M+m\).  Prove that every nonhorizontal closed
halfspace whose height-one trace bisects \(A_1\) has mixed mass at least
\[
\frac{2T}{9}.
\]
The endpoint allocation is arbitrary and must not be fixed independently in
the two endpoint slices.
balanced-middle-trace-safety.status_reason: Accepted fact `de475287446868b2` proves the registered balanced-trace safety statement with joint endpoint optimization and all limiting cases.
balanced-middle-trace-safety.success_criterion:
Derive the sharp endpoint infimal-convolution lower envelope from the

\[
\eta(E)=|A_1\cap E|+m\nu(E),
\]

\(2T/9\) with respect to \(\eta\).

balanced-profile-threshold-inequality.relation_to_goal:
By the exact Helly alternative in accepted fact `d2d117bcc58a1ba0`, an empty
middle depth region in the residual regime produces three profile halfplanes
with empty intersection and positive balancing weights, which is equivalent
to the strict reverse of the displayed inequality after normalization.
Therefore the inequality rules out every counterexample without choosing
slopes or sign cells.
balanced-profile-threshold-inequality.statement:
Assume the locked problem and the strict area-triangle region. Put
\(t=2T/9\), and let \(\rho_q(t)\) be the exact directional threshold from
accepted fact `d2d117bcc58a1ba0`, so that the middle depth region is
\[
A_1\cap\bigcap_{q\in\mathbb S^1}\{z:q\cdot z\ge\rho_q(t)\}.
\]
Prove that for every three directions \(q_1,q_2,q_3\) and positive weights
\(\alpha_1,\alpha_2,\alpha_3\) satisfying
\[
\sum_{i=1}^3\alpha_iq_i=0,
\]
one has the translation-invariant balanced threshold inequality
\[
\sum_{i=1}^3\alpha_i\rho_{q_i}(t)\le0.
\]
balanced-profile-threshold-inequality.success_criterion:
Success is a proof from the cap profiles, compatibility, and convexity,
including repeated or limiting directions and all threshold-attainment
issues. If the statement is false, give an exact compatible polygonal triple
and exact directions for which the strict reverse holds, and determine
whether that example merely refutes this stronger middle-witness statement
or is a counterexample to the locked theorem.

balanced-triple-covering-inequality.relation_to_goal: Accepted fact `d2d117bcc58a1ba0` reduces emptiness of the middle \(t\)-depth region to at most three positively balanced directions. The displayed same-index inequality would contradict three row masses below \(t\) and hence prove nonemptiness of the middle depth region in every residual case not already closed by an outer-slice witness.
balanced-triple-covering-inequality.statement: At \(t=2T/9\), prove the finite balanced-triple covering inequality needed by the exact Helly-Farkas reduction: whenever three middle-plane lower caps with positively balanced normals cover \(A_1\), and the corresponding two outer thresholds are paired as \(r_i+\lambda_i\) and \(r_i-\lambda_i\), compatibility forces at least one same-index three-slice cap sum to be at least \(t\). If this statement is too strong, identify the weakest extra hypothesis supplied by a genuine empty depth-region certificate, or construct an exact compatible counterexample to the proposed inequality.
balanced-triple-covering-inequality.status_reason: Accepted fact `2fdbcddaa185b50e` gives an exact compatible rational-triangle counterexample to the unconditional same-index covering and weighted profile-threshold inequalities. The example has a large outer slice and therefore does not refute the locked target; any valid replacement must include the strict residual hypotheses excluding direct slice witnesses.
balanced-triple-covering-inequality.success_criterion: A complete geometric proof retaining the same row index throughout, or an exact compatible rational-polygon counterexample with all cap areas and the balanced cover checked exactly. Aggregate-first estimates already known to fail do not count.

\[
D_i=u_i+v_i+c_i,
\]
and let \(W\) be the weighted exact-cell functional of accepted fact `91cb5bfc71da49ac`. Prove the crossing-asymmetry implication
\[
W=0
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
(D_1-D_2)^2+(D_2-D_3)^2+(D_3-D_1)^2>0.
\]

\]

\]

\[
r_i=|R_{\{i\}}|,\qquad t=r_N,\qquad k=|K|,
\]
and impose accepted fact `e1361027c1dda6fa`: if \(r_1r_2r_3>0\), then
\[
\left(\sum_{i=1}^3\sqrt{r_i+\frac{2t}{9}}\right)^2\le2k,
\]
while in every support pattern
\[
\left(\sum_{i=1}^3\sqrt{r_i}\right)^2<2k.
\]

Decide whether these conditions are jointly feasible with equality in the all-double excess
\[
\sum_i u_i+m+q_N+\sum_{|G|=2}r_G+2r_N
=\frac{2M-m-k}{3}.
\]

canonical-alternating-cone-hull.relation_to_goal:
The two independent round-039 investigations reduce the cyclic singleton
inequality to this homogeneous collective hull inequality. A proof gives the
sharp cyclic singleton bound, strictly in the displaced three-slice

canonical-alternating-cone-hull.statement:
Let three distinct lines through the origin divide \(\mathbb R^2\) into six
open sectors, and let \(Q_1,Q_2,Q_3\) be three alternate sectors. Let
\(K_i\subseteq\overline{Q_i}\) be compact convex sets containing the origin,
with areas \(a_i=|K_i|\), and put
\[
H=\operatorname{conv}(K_1\cup K_2\cup K_3).
\]
Decide the sharp inequality
\[
|H|\ge
\frac12\left(\sqrt{a_1}+\sqrt{a_2}+\sqrt{a_3}\right)^2
\]
for arbitrary sector angles, including all zero-area and equality cases.
Equivalently, for \(H_{ij}=\operatorname{conv}(K_i\cup K_j)\), decide
\[
\sum_{i<j}|H_{ij}|
\ge
\frac32\sum_i a_i+\sum_{i<j}\sqrt{a_i a_j}.
\]
canonical-alternating-cone-hull.status_reason: Accepted theorem fact `22d750674c663f88` proves the sharp alternating-cone hull inequality, the exact pair-hull identity, all zero-area cases, sharpness for every fan, and the full equality classification.

canonical-alternating-cone-reduction.relation_to_goal:

canonical-alternating-cone-reduction.statement:
Let three distinct lines through \(0\) divide the plane into six sectors, and
let \(Q_1,Q_2,Q_3\) be alternate sectors. Assume the following terminal
triangle statement: whenever a triangle \(T\) containing \(0\) is cut by the
three lines, with
\[
A_i=|T\cap Q_i|,
\qquad
b=|T|-\sum_i A_i,
\]
then for every \(0\le d_i\le A_i\),
\[
b\ge
\sum_{i<j}\sqrt{d_i d_j}-\frac12\sum_i d_i.
\]

Prove that this statement implies, for all compact convex
\(K_i\subseteq\overline{Q_i}\) containing \(0\),
\[
\left|\operatorname{conv}(K_1\cup K_2\cup K_3)\right|
\ge
\frac12\left(\sqrt{|K_1|}+\sqrt{|K_2|}+\sqrt{|K_3|}\right)^2.
\]
Handle zero areas, fan-ray contacts, parallel adjacent bridge supports, and
all limiting cases explicitly.

canonical-concurrent-triangle-fan.relation_to_goal:
The exact round-041 determinant reduction shows that this is the only

canonical-concurrent-triangle-fan.statement:
Let
\[
\alpha,\beta,\gamma,\rho,\sigma,\tau>0,\qquad
\alpha+\beta+\gamma=1,
\]
and assume
\[
\frac{\alpha}{\alpha+\gamma}\le \rho\le1+\frac{\gamma}{\beta},
\qquad
\frac{\alpha}{\alpha+\beta}\le \sigma\le1+\frac{\beta}{\gamma},
\qquad
\frac{\beta}{\alpha+\beta}\le \tau\le1+\frac{\alpha}{\gamma},
\]
\[
\sigma+\tau\ge1,\qquad
\frac1\sigma+\frac1\rho\ge1,\qquad
\rho+\frac1\tau\ge1.
\]
Define
\[
A_1=2\beta\gamma+\beta^2(1-\rho)+\gamma^2(1-\sigma),
\]
\[
A_2=2\gamma\alpha+\gamma^2(1-\tau)
     +\alpha^2\left(1-\frac1\rho\right),
\]
\[
A_3=2\alpha\beta+\alpha^2\left(1-\frac1\sigma\right)
     +\beta^2\left(1-\frac1\tau\right),
\]
\[
b=\gamma^2(\sigma+\tau-1)
  +\alpha^2\left(\frac1\sigma+\frac1\rho-1\right)
  +\beta^2\left(\rho+\frac1\tau-1\right).
\]
Prove or refute that, for every \(0\le d_i\le A_i\),
\[
b\ge
\sqrt{d_1d_2}+\sqrt{d_2d_3}+\sqrt{d_3d_1}
-\frac12(d_1+d_2+d_3).
\]
Determine all equality cases.

canonical-crossing-regularity.statement:

I=\{a\in\mathbb R:\mu(a)<t\}.
\]
Prove that \(\mu\) is continuous and piecewise quadratic with finitely many pieces and has tails \(c+m\) and \(c+M\). If \(c+m\ge t\) and \(I\ne\varnothing\), prove that \(I\) is bounded, \(L:=\inf I\in\mathbb R\), and \(\mu(L)=t\). \]

\[
0<|A_0\cap\{f_j\le L_j\}|<M,\qquad
0<|A_2\cap\{f_j\le-L_j\}|<m
\quad(j=1,2,3).
\]
Prove
\[
L_1+L_2+L_3\ge-1.
\]
canonical-finite-interior.success_criterion: Derive the sum bound from the shared planar realization, compatibility, and the three crossing equalities. Independent scalar optimization of the three directions is not sufficient and does not count. All inequalities and equality cases must be explicit.

canonical-hull-sign-saturation.relation_to_goal: The round-029 generic rectangle example shows that plain convexity permits zero new area. If the same saturation is realizable with true canonical sign cells, the hull-charge route has no positive coefficient and should be abandoned. If sign geometry forbids it, the proof must state the surviving positive-area or multiplicity conclusion that can replace the false whole-source charge.
canonical-hull-sign-saturation.statement:
Use the canonical exact sign-cell geometry of accepted facts `0e51a47a9add571f` and `78d1d57e3961c4e4`. Fix an opposite small-outer pair
\[
E=\overline{Q_{\{j\}}},\qquad
F=\overline{Q_{N\setminus\{j\}}},\qquad
H=\operatorname{conv}(E\cup F),
\]
and a positive-area large-outer cell \(P_0\) with all three shifted affine coordinates positive.

Decide whether the zero-new-area saturation
\[
\frac{P_0+H}{2}
=
\frac{P_0+E}{2}\cup\frac{P_0+F}{2}
\quad\text{up to a null set}
\]
can occur when the two triples of affine coordinates have the common canonical linear parts and their required constant sums.
canonical-hull-sign-saturation.status_reason: Accepted fact `c472ceb412ca0594` proves that true canonical sign geometry forbids zero-new-area saturation: the opposite-cell hull image contains a positive-area slab subset \(-1<f_j<0\), disjoint from both endpoint images and lying in the stated double/triple middle cells.
canonical-hull-sign-saturation.success_criterion: Give explicit affine functions and rational convex polygons realizing saturation, with every sign cell and constant-sum condition checked, or prove it impossible by an exact sign-specific representation argument. A generic convex-set example or qualitative bridge filling alone does not count.

canonical-interior-all-cell-sum.relation_to_goal: This is the exact missing step recorded for `canonical-finite-interior`. It retains the shared planar sign-cell realization discarded by cap-area, cover-excess, and core-versus-exact-one relaxations.
canonical-interior-all-cell-sum.statement:
Assume the complete hypotheses of `canonical-finite-interior`, and use accepted fact `624b129b68e0fdee` to obtain the three crossing equalities. Suppose for contradiction that \(L_1+L_2+L_3<-1\). Partition \(A_0,A_2,K\) into all exact sign cells defined in `canonical-sign-cell-incidence`.

Prove the strict resource inequality
\[
\sum_{j=1}^3u_j+
\left(\sum_{j=1}^3v_j-m\right)+
\left(\sum_{j=1}^3c_j-k\right)
>
\frac{2M-m-k}{3}
\]
by summing the valid Minkowski inclusions over all exact sign-pattern pairs and accounting for every overlap. This contradicts the crossing identity and proves the finite all-interior branch.
canonical-interior-all-cell-sum.success_criterion: Give an explicit finite summation argument with justified multiplicities. Each use of Brunn–Minkowski must have a convex source and target, and overlaps in \(K\) must be counted exactly or with a proved bound. Reusing only one-direction inequalities or the core-versus-exact-one inclusions does not meet the criterion.

canonical-lifting-allocation.relation_to_goal: All noncanonical three-cover arrangements have been eliminated in exact working-memory reductions, and accepted fact `8f5f00ddd4f22d2f` converts failure of the locked target to a strict low-mass cover. The displayed theorem contradicts strict mass below \(2T/9\) for the sole canonical arrangement, thereby closing the arbitrary-enlargement bridge and the locked target.
canonical-lifting-allocation.statement:
Let \(A_0,A_2,K\subset\mathbb R^2\) be nonempty two-dimensional convex polytopes with \(B=(A_0+A_2)/2\subseteq K\), let \(M=\max\{|A_0|,|A_2|\}\), \(m=\min\{|A_0|,|A_2|\}\), \(k=|K|\), \(T=M+m+k\), and assume the exact residual area regime. Suppose three proper closed halfspaces \(H_j=\{\ell_j\le0\}\) have interiors covering \(\{1\}\times K\). In the sole surviving canonical normalization, write
\[
\ell_j(h,w)=f_j(w)+a_j(h-1),\qquad
\sum_{j=1}^3f_j(w)=-1,\qquad
\sum_{j=1}^3a_j<-1,
\]
with nonzero pairwise nonparallel planar normals.

Put
\[
c_j=|K\cap\{f_j\le0\}|,\quad
u_j=|A_0\cap\{f_j-a_j\le0\}|,\quad
v_j=|A_2\cap\{f_j+a_j\le0\}|,
\]
\[
d_j=\int_{A_0\times A_2}
\mathbf1_{\{f_j\le0\}}\!\left(\frac{z_0+z_2}{2}\right)
\,dz_0\,dz_2,
\quad
\eta_j=c_j+\frac{d_j}{M},
\quad
e_j=u_j+v_j-\frac{d_j}{M}.
\]
Prove the lifting-aware allocation
\[
\max_{1\le j\le3}\{\eta_j+e_j\}
=
\max_{1\le j\le3}\{c_j+u_j+v_j\}
\ge\frac{2T}{9}.
\]
Equivalently, if every \(\eta_j<2T/9\), prove that some \(j\) satisfies \(e_j\ge2T/9-\eta_j\).
canonical-lifting-allocation.success_criterion: Prove the allocation using the shared height shifts, the bounded triangular nonnegative cell at height zero, the full negative cover at height two, compatibility, and the true midpoint law. All residual endpoints, null boundaries, and cap-empty or cap-full cases must be included. If false, give an exact full-dimensional convex-polytopal counterexample with all three lifted halfspaces individually below \(2T/9\); such an object would be a candidate counterexample to the locked theorem and must verify every slice and cover condition exactly.

canonical-localized-slab-charge.relation_to_goal: Accepted facts `c472ceb412ca0594` and `9922bcace1cdc113` give \(s_j>0\) and locate it inside positive-coefficient middle cells, while accepted fact `b530304a83fe1e51` supplies the valid convex partial-sign-union inclusions. Therefore the displayed charge implies \(W>0\), contradicts the crossing equalities, and closes the opposite-pair branch whenever \(P_0\) has positive area.
canonical-localized-slab-charge.statement:
Assume the complete canonical finite-interior hypotheses and crossing equalities. Fix \(j\in N=\{1,2,3\}\), write \(N\setminus\{j\}=\{k,\ell\}\), and suppose
\[
p_0>0,\qquad q_{\{j\}}>0,\qquad q_{\{k,\ell\}}>0.
\]
Use the exact cells and weighted functional
\[
W=
\sum_J(3|J|-2)p_J+
\sum_H(3|H|-2)q_H+
\sum_G(3|G|-2)r_G
\]
from the accepted canonical facts. Let
\[
H=\operatorname{conv}\!\left(
\overline{Q_{\{j\}}}\cup\overline{Q_{\{k,\ell\}}}
\right),
\qquad
s_j=
\left|
\frac{P_0+H}{2}\cap\{-1<f_j<0\}
\right|
\]
as in accepted fact `9922bcace1cdc113`. Prove the localized joint charge
\[
W\ge s_j.
\]
canonical-localized-slab-charge.success_criterion: Prove the displayed inequality by charging the actual measurable slab subset through explicit midpoint images or convex partial unions, with every source and target multiplicity justified. Merely adding the strict Brunn--Minkowski inequality to the previously recorded scalar system does not meet the criterion. If \(W\ge s_j\) is too strong, a complete candidate proving \(W\ge\lambda s_j\) for an explicit universal \(\lambda>0\) also meets the strategic criterion; an obstacle must give the first false localized charge and an exact convex realization.

canonical-no-opposite-all-double-excess.relation_to_goal: Accepted fact `91cb5bfc71da49ac` proves that this is the only non-single-double support in the no-opposite-pair finite-interior branch, and that the displayed inequality is exactly \(W>0\) for this support. Since the crossing equalities force \(W=0\), the inequality eliminates the entire all-double branch.
canonical-no-opposite-all-double-excess.statement:
Assume the complete canonical finite-interior hypotheses, the exact sign-cell convention, and the three crossing equalities used in accepted fact `91cb5bfc71da49ac`. Suppose
\[
\mathcal S_Q=\{N,\{1,2\},\{1,3\},\{2,3\}\}.
\]
With the notation of `91cb5bfc71da49ac`, prove the strict geometric inequality
\[
\sum_{i=1}^3u_i+m+q_N
+\sum_{|G|=2}r_G+2r_N
>
\frac{2M-m-k}{3}.
\]
The proof must use the common affine-plane realization and the midpoint inclusion \((A_0+A_2)/2\subseteq K\), not merely the scalar crossing identities.
canonical-no-opposite-all-double-excess.status_reason: Accepted fact `d4c563e79383e2f7` already excludes every actual-counterexample realization in the canonical finite-interior all-double support. The stronger standalone strict-excess statement registered here, without all hypotheses used by that fact, is not proved and is no longer needed for the locked theorem.
canonical-no-opposite-all-double-excess.success_criterion: Give an explicit convex-union, section, or transport argument with exact cell multiplicities proving the displayed strict inequality, including every proper-cell boundary case. Exploit the absence of all singleton \(Q\)-cells and the positive area of all three doubletons. A scalar area calibration or a restatement of the crossing equalities does not meet the criterion. If the proposed route fails, isolate the first false joint geometric inequality and give an exact convex realization of that failure without searching for a counterexample to the locked theorem.

canonical-no-opposite-pair.relation_to_goal: Together with the opposite-pair slab branch, this covers all possible small-outer sign supports in the finite-interior case. The task is combinatorial-geometric, not an area-only linear relaxation: every surviving support must be compatible with convexity and the common affine plane.
canonical-no-opposite-pair.statement:
Assume the complete canonical finite-interior hypotheses, exact sign-cell incidence, and crossing equalities. Suppose the small-outer sign cells contain no positive-area opposite singleton/complement pair:
\[
q_{\{j\}}q_{N\setminus\{j\}}=0
\qquad(j=1,2,3).
\]
Classify all realizable positive-area sign supports and prove
\[
W>0,
\]
or reduce the branch to a strictly smaller explicit family of supports with a stated remaining geometric inequality.
canonical-no-opposite-pair.status_reason: Accepted fact `91cb5bfc71da49ac` exhaustively classifies the realizable no-opposite-pair supports as the three single-double families and the all-double family, supplies exact rational triangle realizations, and reduces the branch to the two explicit strict cover-excess inequalities (6) and (7). This meets the registered success criterion without claiming the remaining strict inequalities.
canonical-no-opposite-pair.success_criterion: Give an exhaustive support classification with exact convexity exclusions, followed by a proved weighted inequality for each surviving support. If a family remains, state its exact positive cells and the one missing inequality. Listing Boolean supports without realizability checks does not count.

canonical-no-opposite-single-double-exce.relation_to_goal: Accepted fact `91cb5bfc71da49ac` proves that this is one of only two realizable support families in the no-opposite-pair finite-interior branch, and that the displayed inequality is exactly \(W>0\) for this family. Since the crossing equalities force \(W=0\), the inequality rules out all three permuted single-double supports.
canonical-no-opposite-single-double-exce.statement:
Assume the complete canonical finite-interior hypotheses, the exact sign-cell convention, and the three crossing equalities used in accepted fact `91cb5bfc71da49ac`. Let \(N=\{1,2,3\}\), let \(\{j,k,\ell\}=N\), and suppose
\[
\mathcal S_Q=\{N,\{j\},\{k\},\{j,k\}\}.
\]
With the notation of `91cb5bfc71da49ac`, prove the strict geometric inequality
\[
\sum_{i=1}^3u_i+q_{\{j,k\}}+2q_N
+\sum_{|G|=2}r_G+2r_N
>
\frac{2M-m-k}{3}.
\]
The proof must use the common affine-plane realization and the midpoint inclusion \((A_0+A_2)/2\subseteq K\), not merely the scalar crossing identities.
canonical-no-opposite-single-double-exce.success_criterion: Give an explicit convex-union, section, or transport argument with exact cell multiplicities that proves the displayed strict inequality for every permutation and all proper-cell boundary cases. A scalar linear combination of already known one-direction or partial-union area inequalities does not meet the criterion. If the proposed route fails, isolate the first false joint geometric inequality and give an exact convex realization of that failure without searching for a counterexample to the locked theorem.

canonical-opposite-band-section.relation_to_goal: Accepted facts `c472ceb412ca0594` and `9922bcace1cdc113` place positive endpoint images in the disjoint bands \(f_j<-1\) and \(f_j>0\), and a positive slab inside \(-1<f_j<0\). Round-032 and round-033 obstacles show that neither source projection nor available-weight bookkeeping can charge the slab. A contradiction from concavity of the actual section-length function of \(Z\), coupled to the crossing level, closes the positive-\(P_\varnothing\) opposite-pair branch.
canonical-opposite-band-section.statement:
Assume the complete canonical finite-interior hypotheses and crossing equalities. Fix \(j\in N\), write \(N\setminus\{j\}=\{k,\ell\}\), and assume
\[
p_\varnothing q_{\{j\}}q_{\{k,\ell\}}>0.
\]
Put
\[
H=\operatorname{conv}\!\left(
\overline{Q_{\{j\}}}\cup\overline{Q_{\{k,\ell\}}}
\right),
\qquad
Z=\frac{P_\varnothing+H}{2}\subseteq K.
\]
Use sections of the convex set \(Z\) parallel to the level lines of \(f_j\), together with the common crossing value, to prove that no such configuration exists.
canonical-opposite-band-section.success_criterion: Give the exact affine normalization, define the section-length function and its Jacobian, derive the needed concavity or mixed-area inequality, and show algebraically how all three crossing equalities make it impossible. Endpoint and slab positivity alone does not meet the criterion. An obstacle must retain the crossing equalities or isolate one sharply stated missing section inequality.

canonical-opposite-chamber-filling.relation_to_goal: The zero-weight calibration places all small-outer mass in an opposite singleton/complement chamber pair and assigns zero bridge mass. This lemma rules out that equality pattern for an actual two-dimensional convex outer body.
canonical-opposite-chamber-filling.statement:
Let \(q_1,q_2,q_3\) be nonconstant affine coordinates on \(\mathbb R^2\) with pairwise nonparallel zero lines and
\[
q_1+q_2+q_3=-\sigma<0.
\]
Let \(Q\subset\mathbb R^2\) be a nonempty two-dimensional convex polytope, and let
\[
Q_J=Q\cap\{q_j\le0\ (j\in J),\ q_j>0\ (j\notin J)\}.
\]
Prove, for every \(j\), that
\[
|Q_{\{j\}}|>0,\quad |Q_{\{1,2,3\}\setminus\{j\}}|>0
\]
forces positive total area in the five remaining nonempty sign cells. Give the exact chamber-path or bridge cells that must have positive area and treat boundary contacts.
canonical-opposite-chamber-filling.status_reason: Accepted fact `78d1d57e3961c4e4` proves that positive area in an opposite singleton/complement chamber pair forces positive area in a bridge chamber, with an exhaustive crossing-order and boundary analysis.
canonical-opposite-chamber-filling.success_criterion: Give a self-contained convexity proof showing that positive-area subsets in the two opposite chambers force a positive-area bridge, not merely a line segment. State the relabeled conclusion and all null-boundary cases.

canonical-opposite-hull-charge.relation_to_goal: Accepted fact `78d1d57e3961c4e4` implies \(\Delta_j>0\). Hence the displayed inequality forces \(W>0\) and closes every finite-interior branch containing an opposite singleton/complement pair. The round-028 obstacle shows that the strict hull inequality alone, without this joint charge, is insufficient.
canonical-opposite-hull-charge.statement:
Assume the complete canonical finite-interior hypotheses, the exact sign-cell notation of accepted fact `0e51a47a9add571f`, and the crossing equalities. Fix \(j\in\{1,2,3\}\) such that
\[
q_jq_{\{1,2,3\}\setminus\{j\}}>0.
\]
Define
\[
\Delta_j=
\left|
\operatorname{conv}\!\left(
\overline{Q_{\{j\}}}\cup
\overline{Q_{\{1,2,3\}\setminus\{j\}}}
\right)\right|
-q_j-q_{\{1,2,3\}\setminus\{j\}},
\]
and
\[
W=
\sum_J(3|J|-2)p_J+
\sum_H(3|H|-2)q_H+
\sum_G(3|G|-2)r_G.
\]
Prove the joint hull-charge inequality
\[
W\ge\Delta_j.
\]
canonical-opposite-hull-charge.success_criterion: Derive the inequality from explicit convex-hull or Minkowski inclusions across \(A_0,A_2,K\), with all cell multiplicities justified. The proof must charge the actual hull excess \(\Delta_j\), not merely show it is positive. A scalar combination of prior partial-union inequalities does not count.

canonical-opposite-slab-bm.relation_to_goal: This is the quantitative inequality directly supplied by the accepted sign slab. Unlike the failed whole-source hull charge, the two endpoint images and the slab are pairwise disjoint for canonical reasons. The inequality can be combined with crossing equalities in the opposite-pair branch.
canonical-opposite-slab-bm.statement:
Under the hypotheses and notation of accepted fact `c472ceb412ca0594`, put
\[
p_0=|P_0|,\qquad q_j=|Q_{\{j\}}|,\qquad
q_{k\ell}=|Q_{\{k,\ell\}}|,
\]
and
\[
s_j=
\left|
\frac{P_0+H}{2}\cap\{-1<f_j<0\}
\right|.
\]
Prove
\[
\left|\frac{P_0+H}{2}\right|
\ge
\frac14(\sqrt{p_0}+\sqrt{q_j})^2
+
\frac14(\sqrt{p_0}+\sqrt{q_{k\ell}})^2
+s_j,
\]
and hence
\[
|K|>
\frac14(\sqrt{p_0}+\sqrt{q_j})^2
+
\frac14(\sqrt{p_0}+\sqrt{q_{k\ell}})^2.
\]
canonical-opposite-slab-bm.status_reason: Accepted fact `9922bcace1cdc113` proves the pairwise-disjoint endpoint-and-slab Brunn--Minkowski charge and the resulting strict lower bound for \(|K|\), without making any claim about the rest of the hull difference.
canonical-opposite-slab-bm.success_criterion: Give the exact set disjointness and two planar Brunn--Minkowski applications, including null boundaries and closure areas. No additional unproved localization of the rest of the hull difference is allowed.

canonical-opposite-slab-certificate.relation_to_goal: The crossing equalities give \(W=0\), so the displayed strict inequality closes every finite-interior branch with a positive large-outer zero cell and an opposite small-outer pair. The round-029 obstacle shows that the slab must be retained explicitly rather than replaced by a generic hull excess.
canonical-opposite-slab-certificate.statement:
Assume the complete canonical finite-interior hypotheses and crossing equalities. Suppose that, for some \(j\), the cells
\[
P_0,\qquad Q_{\{j\}},\qquad Q_{N\setminus\{j\}}
\]
all have positive area. Use accepted fact `c472ceb412ca0594`, the strict slab inequality in `canonical-opposite-slab-bm`, accepted fact `b530304a83fe1e51`, and the exact crossing identities to prove
\[
W=
\sum_J(3|J|-2)p_J+
\sum_H(3|H|-2)q_H+
\sum_G(3|G|-2)r_G>0.
\]
canonical-opposite-slab-certificate.success_criterion: Exhibit an explicit algebraic combination of valid convex-source inequalities yielding the strict weighted sum. Account for the slab exactly in the relevant middle cells and justify every multiplicity. Merely appending the strict slab BM inequality to a scalar system with slack does not count; an obstacle must give the exact surviving scalar calibration.

canonical-opposite-target-side-charge.relation_to_goal: The endpoint images \(U,V\) and the slab lie in disjoint \(f_j\)-bands and occupy only the displayed target cells. Their coefficients use available Q- and R-cell weights while reserving one unit of slab area. Therefore the displayed inequality yields \(W\ge s_j>0\), closing the positive-\(P_\varnothing\) opposite-pair branch. The round-032 obstacle shows why the slab cannot instead be projected back to bridge Q-cells with bounded multiplicity.
canonical-opposite-target-side-charge.statement:
Assume the hypotheses and notation of `canonical-localized-slab-charge`. Fix \(j\in N\), write \(N\setminus\{j\}=\{k,\ell\}\), and define
\[
U=\frac{P_\varnothing+\overline{Q_{\{j\}}}}2,
\qquad
V=\frac{P_\varnothing+\overline{Q_{\{k,\ell\}}}}2.
\]
Let \(s_j\) be the positive slab area of accepted fact `9922bcace1cdc113`. Prove the target-side inequality
\[
2p_\varnothing\le
q_{\{j\}}+4q_{\{k,\ell\}}+|U|
+\left|V\cap\left(R_{\{k\}}\cup R_{\{\ell\}}\right)\right|
+4|V\cap R_{\{k,\ell\}}|
+3s_j.
\]
canonical-opposite-target-side-charge.status_reason: Accepted counterexample fact 4b7d14106fb321c7 gives an exact rational admissible realization satisfying all three genuine lower crossings, strict canonical tails, positive opposite cells, and the positive slab, while strictly reversing the registered target-side inequality. The subgoal is false and this route is abandoned.
canonical-opposite-target-side-charge.success_criterion: Give a complete proof from the actual target subsets \(U,V\), the slab, the three crossing equalities, and exact convex incidence. Justify disjointness, boundary-null conventions, and every coefficient. A scalar calibration or source-side bounded-multiplicity charge does not meet the criterion. If false, give the first exact target-side failure while retaining all crossing equalities.

canonical-opposite-weighted-section.relation_to_goal: The crossing equalities and \(Z\subseteq K\) force the reverse non-strict inequality. Therefore the displayed strict estimate is exactly the missing contradiction in the positive-\(P_\varnothing\) opposite-pair branch. Round-034 proves that section concavity and three-band positivity alone are insufficient; the proof must use the Minkowski source representation and the canonical tail constraints.
canonical-opposite-weighted-section.statement:
Assume the complete canonical finite-interior hypotheses and crossing equalities. Fix \(j\in N\), write \(N\setminus\{j\}=\{k,\ell\}\), and assume
\[
p_\varnothing q_{\{j\}}q_{\{k,\ell\}}>0.
\]
Put
\[
H=\operatorname{conv}\!\left(
\overline{Q_{\{j\}}}\cup\overline{Q_{\{k,\ell\}}}
\right),
\qquad
Z=\frac{P_\varnothing+H}{2}.
\]
Let
\[
\Phi(x)=(f_j(x),f_k(x)),\qquad
\mathcal J=\left|\det D\Phi^{-1}\right|,
\]
and let \(\ell_Z(s)\) be the length of the \(f_k\)-section of \(\Phi(Z)\) at \(f_j=s\). Prove
\[
\sum_{i\in N}(u_i+v_i)
+
\mathcal J\left(
\int_{-\infty}^{-1}\ell_Z(s)\,ds
+2\int_{-1}^{0}\ell_Z(s)\,ds
+\int_{0}^{\infty}\ell_Z(s)\,ds
\right)
>3t.
\]
canonical-opposite-weighted-section.success_criterion: Derive the strict inequality from endpoint sections or mixed areas of \(P_\varnothing\) and \(H\), with the exact affine Jacobian and every cap contribution stated. Use the tail constraints quantitatively. Qualitative positivity or the previously recorded Brunn--Minkowski endpoint bound does not meet the criterion. A failure must isolate the first false source-section inequality while retaining the full canonical hypotheses.

canonical-partial-sign-unions.relation_to_goal: The exact-pair Brunn–Minkowski inequalities are insufficient because their target unions overlap. Partial sign unions keep adjacent exact cells together as one convex source and one convex target, allowing stronger nonlinear area inequalities that may control those overlaps.
canonical-partial-sign-unions.statement:
Under the hypotheses and notation of accepted fact `0e51a47a9add571f`, put
\[
p_i=f_i-L_i,\qquad q_i=f_i+L_i,\qquad r_i=f_i.
\]
For disjoint \(A,B\subseteq\{1,2,3\}\), define the partial sign sets
\[
P[A;B]=A_0\cap\{p_i\le0\ (i\in A),\ p_i>0\ (i\in B)\},
\]
and define \(Q[C;D]\) and \(R[E;F]\) analogously.

Prove the complete partial-sign convex-union calculus: express every partial set as a disjoint union of exact cells from `0e51a47a9add571f`, classify the forced-empty cases from the three plane sums, and prove every midpoint inclusion
\[
\frac{P[A;B]+Q[C;D]}2
\subseteq R[A\cap C\,;\,B\cap D].
\]
Determine exactly when the inclusion can be strengthened by the plane-sum offsets, and state all boundary-null conventions.
canonical-partial-sign-unions.status_reason: Accepted fact `b530304a83fe1e51` proves the complete partial-sign Boolean calculus, forced emptiness, exact target refinements, strongest convex coordinate envelopes, sharpness, and null-boundary conventions.
canonical-partial-sign-unions.success_criterion: Give a self-contained Boolean-lattice formula for source and target unions, prove convexity, all forced-empty cases, every midpoint inclusion, and sharpness of any claimed strengthening. This is an auxiliary incidence lemma, not the final resource inequality.

canonical-partial-union-bm-certificate.relation_to_goal: The round-025 calibration satisfies every exact-pair Brunn–Minkowski inequality but need not satisfy nonlinear inequalities for convex unions of adjacent cells. A valid weighted certificate from those union inequalities closes the finite all-interior branch.
canonical-partial-union-bm-certificate.statement:
Assume the complete hypotheses of `canonical-finite-interior`, \(L_1+L_2+L_3<-1\), and the crossing equalities from accepted fact `624b129b68e0fdee`. Use accepted fact `0e51a47a9add571f` and all valid convex partial-sign-union inclusions to prove
\[
\sum_J(3|J|-2)p_J+
\sum_H(3|H|-2)q_H+
\sum_G(3|G|-2)r_G>0.
\]
Equivalently, prove the strict resource inequality required by `canonical-interior-all-cell-sum`.
canonical-partial-union-bm-certificate.success_criterion: Exhibit an explicit finite family of convex-union inclusions and a rigorous algebraic combination of their area inequalities yielding the displayed strict bound. Every overlap and every use of strictness must be justified. A scalar calibration or an assertion that a suitable weighting exists does not count.

canonical-partial-union-nonstrict.relation_to_goal: The strict certificate failed because the scalar equality calibration satisfies every individual partial-union inequality. A nonstrict certificate plus an equality characterization can still prove the desired strict bound once actual convex filling excludes the equality pattern.
canonical-partial-union-nonstrict.statement:
Under the complete hypotheses of `canonical-finite-interior` and \(L_1+L_2+L_3<-1\), let \(p_J,q_H,r_G\) be the exact sign-cell areas. Using accepted facts `0e51a47a9add571f` and `b530304a83fe1e51`, prove the nonstrict weighted inequality
\[
\sum_J(3|J|-2)p_J+
\sum_H(3|H|-2)q_H+
\sum_G(3|G|-2)r_G\ge0.
\]
Characterize every equality pattern allowed by the full system of convex partial-sign-union Brunn–Minkowski inequalities.
canonical-partial-union-nonstrict.status_reason: The exact recorded obstacle shows that \(W=0\) is an algebraic identity under the three crossing equalities, so the registered nonstrict inequality has no geometric content and cannot furnish an equality class. The replacement target is a direct strict bridge-filling inequality.
canonical-partial-union-nonstrict.success_criterion: Exhibit an explicit finite algebraic combination of valid convex-union area inequalities proving nonnegativity, and derive equality conditions. An unchecked numerical optimization or a claim that suitable weights exist does not count.

canonical-quantitative-common-frame-brid.relation_to_goal:
Accepted fact `d3afd91c459bcce8` proves only that this bridge has positive
area.  The quantitative inequality records the missing transverse common-
frame scale and shows that bridge collapse requires the offset gap

canonical-quantitative-common-frame-brid.statement:
Under the common affine-plane and exact-cell hypotheses of accepted fact
`0e51a47a9add571f`, relabel so that
\[
f_1+f_2+f_3=-1,\qquad L_1+L_2+L_3<-1,
\]
and assume \(p=|P_\varnothing|>0\), \(|Q_1|>0\), and \(|Q_2|>0\).
Set
\[
\Delta=-1-(L_1+L_2+L_3),\qquad
\mathcal T_P=\{f_i>L_i:\ i=1,2,3\},\qquad
\Theta=|\mathcal T_P|,\qquad \alpha=p/\Theta.
\]
Let \(y_1,y_2\) be the area centroids of \(Q_1,Q_2\), put
\(q_i(y)=f_i(y)+L_i\), and define
\[
A=\frac{q_1(y_2)-q_1(y_1)}{\Delta},\qquad
B=\frac{q_2(y_1)-q_2(y_2)}{\Delta},\qquad
L=\max\{A,B\},\qquad l=\min\{A,B\}.
\]
Prove \(A,B>1\) and
\[
\left|
\operatorname{conv}\left(
\frac{P_\varnothing+\overline{Q_1}}2
\cup
\frac{P_\varnothing+\overline{Q_2}}2
\right)\cap R_{12}
\right|
>
\frac{pL}{\Delta l\left(1+\sqrt{1-\alpha}\right)}.
\]
Treat \(\alpha=1\), closures, null cutting lines, and every affine
normalization exactly.

\[

\]
Assume
\[
|C_0|=|C_1|=|C_2|=|C_3|=\frac{|Q|}{4}.
\]
Prove that \(Q\) is a triangle and the three cutting lines are its medial lines.
canonical-quarter-cap-rigidity.status_reason: Accepted fact `8234d1112ec2f031` is stronger than this subgoal and directly implies that three disjoint quarter-area caps with a quarter-area central remainder force a triangle cut by its medial lines.

canonical-root-tail-concurrent-fan-cross.statement:

\[

\]
and put
\[
c_i=\left|K\cap\{\ell_i\le0\}\right|.
\]
Assume
\[
c_1\le\frac{|K|}{2},
\qquad
c_2\le\frac{|K|}{2}.
\]
Prove
\[
c_3|K|\ge (|K|-c_1)(|K|-c_2).
\]
canonical-root-tail-concurrent-fan-cross.status_reason: Accepted fact `5384a5033810a417` proves the registered concurrent-fan inequality for every compact two-dimensional convex body, with all equality and boundary cases covered through accepted predecessors. and put

\[

\]
\[
Q_J=A_2\cap\{f_j\le-L_j\ (j\in J),\ f_j>-L_j\ (j\notin J)\},

\[

\]
Give the complete realizable sign-type table and prove every midpoint incidence forced by affinity. In particular, prove the exact rule relating a pair \((P_J,Q_H)\) to the possible middle cells \(R_G\), identify all impossible cells, and enumerate every pair for which the midpoint image lies in a single convex middle cell rather than a nonconvex union.
