Alternatively, give exact rational polygons satisfying every displayed hypothesis and violating the conclusion; such a packet refutes this analytic bridge, not by itself the locked theorem.

canonical-support-one-sided-convex.relation_to_goal: Accepted fact `b0a6a33598b0969e` proves the result for affine height functions. In the \(\Gamma>0\) branch, concavity should replace the affine monotonicity split: two midpoint-forced values of \(a_R\) bound its integral on the interval between them. The \(\Gamma=0\) algebra is unchanged. This would close the complete one-sided convex-body support branch.
canonical-support-one-sided-convex.statement:
Assume `canonical-support-interval-tail-full` and restrict to
\[
P=\{(x,y):-\delta\le x\le0,\ 0\le y\le h_P(x)\},
\]
\[
Q=\{(x,y):\delta+2\le x\le\delta+2+w,\ -h_Q(x)\le y\le0\},
\]
\[
R=\{(x,y):0\le x\le r,\ -a_R(x)\le y\le c_R(x)\},
\]
where \(w,r>0\), the four height functions are nonnegative concave functions on their respective compact intervals, each body has positive area, and
\[
\frac{P+Q}{2}\subseteq R.
\]
Prove
\[
b+d\le m+k-t.
\]
canonical-support-one-sided-convex.status_reason: Accepted fact `25960e1c7ab04d71` proves that the complete normalized one-sided convex-body branch with arbitrary finite nonnegative concave section heights is inconsistent. It handles nonsmooth functions, endpoint discontinuities, and both \(\Gamma>0\) and \(\Gamma=0\) cases.
canonical-support-one-sided-convex.success_criterion: Give a complete proof for arbitrary concave heights, including nonsmooth functions, zero endpoint heights, and null threshold fibers. Justify every Cavalieri identity and the concavity integral bound. Reproving only the affine case does not count.

canonical-support-one-sided-rectangles.relation_to_goal: This exact rectangle chamber contains the round-028 calibration that satisfies either crossing equality separately but not both. Deciding the joint system is the smallest algebraic test of whether the two crossings together repair the support-tail bound. A counterexample refutes the normalized bridge; a proof isolates the first genuinely joint algebraic mechanism.
canonical-support-one-sided-rectangles.statement:
Assume `canonical-support-interval-tail-full` and restrict to
\[
P=[-\delta,0]\times[0,h],\qquad
Q=[\delta+2,\delta+2+w]\times[-q,0],
\]
\[
R=[0,r]\times[-a,c],
\]
where all six parameters are positive and the full midpoint inclusion \((P+Q)/2\subseteq R\) holds. Areas, \(t\), and all cap and tail quantities are defined as in the normalized subgoal.

Decide whether the two crossing equalities, both crossing-direction tail conditions, the contact-direction tail condition, and the residual area domain force
\[
b+d\le m+k-t.
\]
canonical-support-one-sided-rectangles.status_reason: Accepted fact `7c6fea74731dcb53` proves that the complete one-sided rectangle chamber is empty: midpoint inclusion, both crossing equalities, and \(\beta_R+m\ge t\) already contradict the exact rectangle cap formulas. Hence the registered tail inequality holds throughout this chamber.
canonical-support-one-sided-rectangles.success_criterion: Compute every cap area exactly and eliminate the six positive parameters. Give either a complete inequality proof for the full displayed chamber, including all threshold orderings for \(r\) relative to \(1\), or explicit rational parameters verifying every hypothesis and violating the conclusion. Numerical feasibility alone does not count.

canonical-support-one-sided-trapezoids.relation_to_goal: Accepted fact `7c6fea74731dcb53` proves this when all four section-height functions are constant. This subgoal is the next polygonal class: it preserves the decisive one-sided sign arrangement while allowing every section length to vary affinely. A proof identifies which part of the rectangle contradiction survives concavity.
canonical-support-one-sided-trapezoids.statement:
Assume `canonical-support-interval-tail-full` and restrict to
\[
P=\{(x,y):-\delta\le x\le0,\ 0\le y\le h_P(x)\},
\]
\[
Q=\{(x,y):\delta+2\le x\le\delta+2+w,\ -h_Q(x)\le y\le0\},
\]
\[
R=\{(x,y):0\le x\le r,\ -a_R(x)\le y\le c_R(x)\},
\]
where \(w,r>0\), and \(h_P,h_Q,a_R,c_R\) are nonnegative affine functions, each body has positive area, and
\[
\frac{P+Q}{2}\subseteq R.
\]
Areas, crossing caps, positive tails, \(t\), and the residual area conditions are those of the normalized support subgoal.

Prove
\[
b+d\le m+k-t.
\]
canonical-support-one-sided-trapezoids.status_reason: Accepted fact `b0a6a33598b0969e` proves that no one-sided affine section-height trapezoid configuration satisfies the full normalized support hypotheses. It handles all affine slopes, zero endpoint heights, and both \(\Gamma>0\) and \(\Gamma=0\) cases, so the registered tail inequality holds throughout this class.
canonical-support-one-sided-trapezoids.success_criterion: Compute the two crossing caps exactly from affine endpoint values and use both crossing equalities jointly. Give a complete proof for all zero endpoint heights and all threshold orderings, or explicit rational affine functions satisfying every normalized hypothesis and violating the conclusion. A proof for constant heights or a numerical search does not count.

canonical-support-overlap-subtracted.relation_to_goal: The round-029 calibration shows that raw spill pieces can lie inside the exclusive images \(X_-,X_+\), so subtracting those images is necessary. This is the precise nonlocal transport still capable of closing `canonical-support-endpoint-spill`.
canonical-support-overlap-subtracted.statement:
Assume every hypothesis and notation of `canonical-support-endpoint-spill`. Construct a measurable monotone horizontal area-quantile pairing between the relevant submasses of \(N\) and \(B_0\), and let \(\mathcal S_0\) be its multiplicity-one midpoint image. Put
\[
X_-=\frac{N+B_-}{2}\subseteq D_-,
\qquad
X_+=\frac{N+B_+}{2}\subseteq D_+.
\]
Prove the overlap-subtracted transport bounds
\[
\left|(\mathcal S_0\cap D_-)\setminus X_-\right|\le e_\alpha,
\qquad
\left|(\mathcal S_0\cap D_+)\setminus X_+\right|\le e_\beta,
\]
together with the quantitative lower bound on the remaining middle image needed to derive
\[
e_\alpha+e_\beta+q_0+r_0
\ge\frac{2M-m-k}{3}.
\]
canonical-support-overlap-subtracted.status_reason: The registered subgoal does not specify the paired submasses when \(|N|\ne|B_0|\), so \(\mathcal S_0\) and its requested areas are not well-defined. The exact round-030 obstacle gives distinct admissible monotone multiplicity-one constructions. No mathematical claim can be verified until a unique pairing rule and quantitative lower bound are registered.
canonical-support-overlap-subtracted.success_criterion: Define the paired submasses, quantile map, midpoint image, and its multiplicity rigorously. Prove every set inclusion and area comparison, including unequal source masses and null fibers. The result must supply the exact final coefficient. If either displayed bound is false, give exact convex-polytopal endpoint data and identify the corrected target.

canonical-tail-centroid-clearance.relation_to_goal: The displayed inequality implies \(I_i=\varnothing\) for some \(i\ne q\) and therefore closes the infinite-left-tail branch. The previous proof attempt already establishes \(c_i\ge4k/9\) and the sharp necessary complementary-cap inequality; the new step must couple the nonparallel \(q\)- and \(i\)-cap positions.
canonical-tail-centroid-clearance.statement:
Under the hypotheses of `canonical-tail-exclusion`, suppose \(c_q+m<t\), and let \(g\) be the centroid of \(K\). Prove
\[
\max_{\substack{i\ne q\\ f_i(g)<0}}
\left[
c_i+\inf_{a\in\mathbb R}
\left(
|A_0\cap\{f_i\le a\}|+
|A_2\cap\{f_i\le-a\}|
\right)
\right]\ge t.
\]
The maximum is over a nonempty set because \(f_q(g)>0\) and \(f_1(g)+f_2(g)+f_3(g)=-1\).
canonical-tail-centroid-clearance.status_reason: Accepted counterexample fact `fccb04e93a38cb32` disproves the registered centroid-negative-direction maximum under every stated hypothesis. Any tail-exclusion proof must use both indices different from the tail direction, including a centroid-excluding index.
canonical-tail-centroid-clearance.success_criterion: Give a complete joint two-direction proof using compatibility, the centroid positions, and the common affine plane. Treat all cap-empty, cap-full, and equality cases. Do not search for a counterexample to the locked theorem.

canonical-tail-common-fiber.relation_to_goal: The round-029 scalar calibration satisfies every separately bounded density inequality. The displayed pointwise identity retains the coupling discarded by those bounds. A sufficient common-fiber inequality closes the \(q\)-sensitive transport and the tail empty-wedge branch.
canonical-tail-common-fiber.statement:
Assume the complete hypotheses and notation of `canonical-tail-q-transport`. Put
\[
P=A_0\cap\{f_i>a,\ f_\ell>b\},\qquad
V_i=A_2\cap\{f_i\le-a\},\qquad
V_\ell=A_2\cap\{f_\ell\le-b\},
\]
and \(W=V_i\cap V_\ell\). For measurable \(B\subseteq A_2\), let
\[
g_B(z)=4\,|P\cap(2z-B)|
\]
be the midpoint density of \(P\times B\). Use the pointwise identity
\[
g_{V_i}+g_{V_\ell}=g_{A_2}+g_W,
\]
which follows from \(V_i\cup V_\ell=A_2\), before applying any density bound.

Prove a common-fiber convex-union inequality strong enough to imply
\[
9c_q+3(u_i+u_\ell+w+E_K)+11m\ge4M+k.
\]
canonical-tail-common-fiber.success_criterion: Give an explicit pointwise or integrated inequality using the four densities \(g_{V_i},g_{V_\ell},g_{A_2},g_W\), the three middle sign chambers, and exact multiplicities. Derive the coefficient \(9\) algebraically. Reverting to separate bounds \(g_B\le4\min\{|P|,|B|\}\) does not count. An obstacle must show the first false common-fiber inequality or an exact convex realization of the round-029 calibration.

canonical-tail-empty-wedge.relation_to_goal: The two-direction tail proof reduces to an ordinary Brunn–Minkowski estimate when both upper endpoint wedges have positive area. The displayed empty small-outer wedge is the precise case where that estimate becomes void and where the lift defect, rather than midpoint convolution alone, must be used.
canonical-tail-empty-wedge.statement:
Under the hypotheses of `canonical-tail-unrestricted-pair`, let \(\{i,\ell,q\}=\{1,2,3\}\) and suppose, toward contradiction, that there are shifts \(a,b\) with
\[
c_i+|A_0\cap\{f_i\le a\}|+|A_2\cap\{f_i\le-a\}|<t,
\]
\[
c_\ell+|A_0\cap\{f_\ell\le b\}|+|A_2\cap\{f_\ell\le-b\}|<t.
\]
Handle the exact missing subcase
\[
A_2\cap\{f_i>-a,\ f_\ell>-b\}=\varnothing
\]
and derive a contradiction from \(c_q+m<t\), compatibility, and the common affine plane.
canonical-tail-empty-wedge.success_criterion: Use the fact that the two lower caps cover \(A_2\), retain their overlap and the corresponding geometry on \(A_0\) and \(K\), and prove one lifted mass reaches \(t\). Include all strict/equality and empty/full cap cases. Do not replace the task by the known-false midpoint-only inequality.

canonical-tail-exclusion.relation_to_goal: When \(c_q+m<t\), the feasible set \(I_q\) contains a left ray. The displayed implication is exactly what prevents choosing three shifts in \(I_1\times I_2\times I_3\) with sum below \(-1\). It closes the infinite-lower-crossing branch of the canonical lifting allocation.
canonical-tail-exclusion.statement:
Let \(A_0,A_2,K\subset\mathbb R^2\) be nonempty two-dimensional convex polytopes with \((A_0+A_2)/2\subseteq K\). Relabel so that \(|A_0|=M\ge m=|A_2|\), put \(k=|K|\) and \(t=2(M+m+k)/9\), and assume the exact residual area domain of accepted fact `15bb2c1680a0254e`.

Let \(f_1,f_2,f_3\) be nonconstant affine functions with pairwise nonparallel linear parts and
\[
f_1+f_2+f_3=-1.
\]
Define
\[
c_j=|K\cap\{f_j\le0\}|,\qquad
\mu_j(a)=c_j+|A_0\cap\{f_j\le a\}|+|A_2\cap\{f_j\le-a\}|,
\]
and \(I_j=\{a:\mu_j(a)<t\}\).

Prove the tail-exclusion implication
\[
c_q+m<t\ \text{for some }q
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
I_i=\varnothing\ \text{for some }i\ne q.
\]
canonical-tail-exclusion.success_criterion: Give a complete proof using compatibility and the shared identity \(f_1+f_2+f_3=-1\), including strict equality endpoints and cap-empty or cap-full cases. A failure packet must identify the first missing joint inequality; searching for a counterexample is secondary.

canonical-tail-q-transport.relation_to_goal: The round-028 Cavalieri identity shows that multiplicity-only midpoint transport loses exactly the hypothesis \(c_q+m<t\). The displayed bound restores that quantity. Since \(c_q+m<t\), it implies \(D>0\), hence the required tail empty-wedge inequality and the remaining tail-exclusion subcase.
canonical-tail-q-transport.statement:
Assume the complete hypotheses and notation of `canonical-tail-section-charge`. Put
\[
A=u_i+u_\ell+w+E_K,\qquad
D=3A+k+4m-2M.
\]
Retain the two strict \(i\)- and \(\ell\)-direction low-mass inequalities and the individual third-direction quantity \(c_q\). Prove the \(q\)-sensitive transport inequality
\[
D\ge9(t-c_q-m),
\]
equivalently
\[
9c_q+3(u_i+u_\ell+w+E_K)+11m\ge4M+k.
\]
canonical-tail-q-transport.success_criterion: Give a chamber-sensitive fiber transport or exact convex-union argument proving the displayed coefficient \(9\). The proof must show where the individual \(q\)-cap area enters and must control midpoint-source multiplicity. Reusing only total middle overlap \(E_K\), the empty-wedge cover, or marginal cap inequalities does not count. An exact auxiliary counterexample must satisfy both strict low-mass inequalities and every hypothesis other than the final conclusion.

canonical-tail-section-charge.relation_to_goal: The displayed inequality is exactly the only positive-constant gap in the empty-small-outer-wedge branch of `canonical-tail-exclusion`. It is parallel to, but not logically dependent on, the support-contact interval lemma. Proving it closes the remaining tail subcase.
canonical-tail-section-charge.statement:
Assume the complete hypotheses of `canonical-tail-empty-wedge` and the exact reduction recorded in `.math-prover/round-027/tail-empty-wedge-obstacle.md`. Thus the two lower small-outer caps cover \(A_2\), and the desired contradiction reduces to
\[
u_i+u_\ell+w+E_K\ge\frac{2M-k-4m}{3}.
\]
Choose a common affine coordinate system adapted to a separating support line of the empty upper wedge. Express \(u_i+u_\ell+w+E_K\) exactly as integrals of vertical interval lengths and overlap lengths for \(A_0,A_2,K\). Prove the displayed inequality by a layer-by-layer charge that uses the full midpoint inclusion
\[
\frac{A_0+A_2}{2}\subseteq K.
\]
canonical-tail-section-charge.success_criterion: Give the affine normalization, exact Cavalieri identities, and a proved pointwise or integrated charge with the coefficient \((2M-k-4m)/3\). Every source interval used in a midpoint inclusion must be specified, and overlap multiplicities must be exact. Qualitative positivity, marginal cap inequalities, and the known-false midpoint-only proxy do not count. If the proposed charge is false, give an exact auxiliary convex-polytopal counterexample and state which original hypothesis is still unused.

canonical-tail-unrestricted-pair.relation_to_goal: The displayed maximum is exactly the tail-exclusion conclusion \(I_j=\varnothing\) for some \(j\ne q\). Accepted fact `fccb04e93a38cb32` shows that restricting the maximum to centroid-negative directions is false, so the proof must use both remaining nonparallel directions jointly.
canonical-tail-unrestricted-pair.statement:
Under the hypotheses of `canonical-tail-exclusion`, suppose \(c_q+m<t\). Prove
\[
\max_{j\ne q}
\left[
c_j+\inf_{a\in\mathbb R}
\left(
|A_0\cap\{f_j\le a\}|+
|A_2\cap\{f_j\le-a\}|
\right)
\right]\ge t.
\]
canonical-tail-unrestricted-pair.success_criterion: Give a complete proof using both directions different from \(q\), compatibility, and the common affine plane. Include all empty/full/equality cases. Do not search for a counterexample to the locked theorem; a failure packet must isolate the first missing two-direction inequality.

canonical-three-cap-square-root.relation_to_goal: The symmetric all-double calibration has \(|C_i|=|Q|/4\), so it attains the proposed bound. If equality forces \(Q\) to be a triangle and the cuts to be its medial lines, the calibration is not common-plane realizable because the middle central cell violates the resulting homothetic area bound. The unequal form may also supply a joint inequality for the full all-double branch.
canonical-three-cap-square-root.statement:
Let \(Q\subset\mathbb R^2\) be a nonempty two-dimensional convex polygon. Let three lines cut from \(Q\) halfplane caps \(C_1,C_2,C_3\) whose interiors are pairwise disjoint, and assume the remaining set
\[
C_0=\overline{Q\setminus(C_1\cup C_2\cup C_3)}
\]
is convex. Cutting-line boundaries have zero area. Prove the sharp inequality
\[
\sqrt{\frac{|C_1|}{|Q|}}+
\sqrt{\frac{|C_2|}{|Q|}}+
\sqrt{\frac{|C_3|}{|Q|}}
\le\frac32,
\]
and classify every equality case.
canonical-three-cap-square-root.status_reason: Accepted fact `8234d1112ec2f031` proves the registered product inequality, the square-root inequality, and the complete equality characterization.
canonical-three-cap-square-root.success_criterion: Give a proof for arbitrary convex polygons, not only triangles. Derive the constant \(3/2\) and a complete equality classification, including degenerate cap boundaries. An external theorem may be used only with its exact statement, primary source, and applicability check. If false, give an exact rational convex polygon and cutting lines.

canonical-triangle-fan-parameterization.relation_to_goal:
This is the geometric-to-algebraic bridge between accepted minimizer fact
`e16916ffe774b4a9` and the registered balanced and unbalanced
concurrent-triangle subgoals. Without it, the algebraic inequalities do not yet
apply to every minimizing triangle.
canonical-triangle-fan-parameterization.statement:
Let three distinct lines through \(0\) divide the plane into six sectors, and
let \(Q_1,Q_2,Q_3\) be alternate sectors. Let \(T\) be a nondegenerate
triangle with \(0\in\operatorname{int}T\) and with one vertex assigned to each
\(\overline{Q_i}\). Normalize \(|T|=1\), put
\[
A_i=|T\cap Q_i|,
\qquad
b=|T|-\sum_iA_i.
\]

Prove that, after cyclic relabeling, there exist
\[
\alpha,\beta,\gamma,\rho,\sigma,\tau>0,\qquad
\alpha+\beta+\gamma=1,
\]
satisfying every endpoint and side-order constraint in
`.math-prover/round-043/concurrent-triangle-fan-statement.md`, and that the
four displayed formulas there give exactly these \(A_1,A_2,A_3,b\).
Handle vertices and side intersections on fan rays by an exact argument or a
justified limit.
canonical-triangle-fan-parameterization.status_reason: Accepted fact `55870afe6d5fc27f` proves the registered parameterization, including all endpoint, side-order, area, and fan-ray boundary cases.
canonical-triangle-fan-parameterization.success_criterion:
Give a self-contained barycentric or determinant derivation of every parameter,
bound, side-order inequality, and area formula. A diagram-based assertion or
an appeal to the unverified round-041 obstacle is insufficient.

cap-vector-bm.relation_to_goal:
This gives direction-free necessary conditions on every possible low-mass
halfspace. It is the exact scalar input for both finite-cover arguments and
the Minkowski-equality residual family, rather than another special-case
point calculation.
cap-vector-bm.statement:
Let a compatible triple \(A_0,A_1,A_2\) be given, and let \(H\) be a
proper non-slice-parallel closed halfspace. Put
\[
b_i=\left|\{w\in A_i:(i,w)\in H\}\right|.
\]
Prove the two exact cap-vector inequalities
\[
\sqrt{b_0}+\sqrt{b_2}\le 2\sqrt{b_1},
\qquad
\sqrt{a_0-b_0}+\sqrt{a_2-b_2}
\le 2\sqrt{a_1-b_1},
\]
including all zero-area and boundary cases.
cap-vector-bm.status_reason:
The exact square-prism halfspace in the recorded obstacle has cap vector
\((0,0,1/4)\), contradicting the first proposed inequality; the opposite
halfspace contradicts the complementary inequality. Therefore the registered
unconditional lemma is false. Conditional nonempty-cap inequalities may still
be used, but they do not close this subgoal.
cap-vector-bm.success_criterion:
Return a self-contained proof from compatibility and planar
Brunn--Minkowski. Treat the complementary caps without assuming their
boundary has zero mass unless that fact is explicitly justified from the
non-slice-parallel hypothesis.

capacity-one-phase-deficit-transfer.relation_to_goal: This is the minimal reusable mathematical content common to the three attachments. It retains positive arithmetic deficit and may supply joint cross-height payments in the remaining canonical boundary, tail, and finite-interior branches without requiring impossible global phase core.
capacity-one-phase-deficit-transfer.statement:
Let \(C\subset\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d\) be compact and convex, \(q_0=(b,v_0)\in C\), \(0<\alpha<1\), and \(D=(1-\alpha)C+\alpha q_0\). Suppose Borel maps \(\rho:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb Z^n\) and \(a:\mathbb R^n\to C\) satisfy
\[
\pi_{\mathbb R^n}a(q)=b+\frac{\rho(q)-q}{\alpha},
\qquad
|\rho^{-1}(z)|\le1\quad(z\in\mathbb Z^n).
\]
For every affine \(L\), prove the exact phase-deficit transfer
\[
\mu(C\cap\{L\ge0\})
\ge
\operatorname{vol}_{n+d}
\left\{(q,r)\in D:
L(q,r)\ge\alpha\bigl(L(q_0)-L(a(q))\bigr)
\right\}.
\]
Derive the \(n=1,d=2,\alpha=1/2\) reflected paired-support corollary for a compatible three-slice triple.
capacity-one-phase-deficit-transfer.status_reason: Accepted fact `d1c7a9b4c142230a` proves the complete capacity-one phase-deficit transfer and the exact reflected three-slice paired-support corollary, meeting every registered success criterion.
capacity-one-phase-deficit-transfer.success_criterion: Give a self-contained measure-theoretic proof with Borel source sections, Fubini/Tonelli, target-fiber capacity, closed-halfspace boundaries, empty fibers, and finite mixed measure. For the three-slice corollary, define the interpolated sections and support maxima exactly and derive the factor \(1/8\). Do not include novelty or large-box claims.

centrally-symmetric-outers.relation_to_goal: This is the first broad nonhomothetic subclass suggested by the accepted two-density shear example. It tests whether exact midpoint symmetry can replace the common-density hypothesis and supplies a reusable base case for later middle-enlargement transfer.
centrally-symmetric-outers.statement: Assume the minimal family \(B=(A_0+A_2)/2\), and assume \(A_0,A_2\) are centrally symmetric about their respective centroids, without assuming that they are homothetic or affinely equivalent. Prove the locked \(2T/9\) conclusion for this entire shape class, if true, at an explicit point.
centrally-symmetric-outers.status_reason: Accepted theorem `3ae05f8a66594860` proves the complete minimal Minkowski-sum family whenever both outer bodies are centrally symmetric about their centroids, without any equality or homothety assumption, using an explicit witness in both the large-slice and balanced regimes.
centrally-symmetric-outers.success_criterion: Give a self-contained proof for all centrally symmetric outer polytopes, treating both the balanced and large-slice regimes, with the exact chosen point and every tilted and slice-parallel halfspace checked. Do not restrict to rectangles or equal outer bodies.

centroid-general-envelope.relation_to_goal:
The accepted small-\(c\) theorem used a uniform coarse estimate. A sharper
closed envelope can certify larger portions of the exact residual domain and
identify the first genuine parameter obstruction without another continuum
search.
centroid-general-envelope.statement:
For a common-vertex homothetic triangle triple
\[
(A_0,A_1,A_2)=(a\Delta,\Delta,c\Delta),\qquad a\ge c>0,
\]
derive an explicit lower envelope \(L(a,c)\) for the actual three-slice depth
at the middle centroid. The envelope must optimize the common-slope outer-cap
sum over all six projected-vertex chambers and combine it with the exact
middle cap fraction.
centroid-general-envelope.status_reason: The explicit finite envelope is no longer strategically needed because accepted theorem `aef70a60593c53a2` proves the target directly over the full residual triangle domain.
centroid-general-envelope.success_criterion:
Give a finite explicit formula or the minimum of finitely many algebraic
expressions, with proof that every direction, slope, tied case, and horizontal
halfspace is included. A restatement of the polynomial-system normal form is
not sufficient.

centroid-middle-bm-shortcut-audit.relation_to_goal: Taking the centroid of the middle slice gives \(r\ge4K/9\) by the planar Grünbaum inequality. Midpoint inclusion applied to the chosen and complementary endpoint caps suggests the other two displayed Brunn–Minkowski constraints. If the scalar implication were true, it would give a short direct proof of the locked target. An exact counterexample proves that these marginal area constraints discard essential common-plane geometry and closes this shortcut before further proof work is spent on it.
centroid-middle-bm-shortcut-audit.statement:
Let \(A,B,K>0\), \(0<p<A\), \(0<q<B\), and \(0<r<K\). Assume
\[
K\ge \frac{(\sqrt A+\sqrt B)^2}{4},\qquad
r\ge\frac{4K}{9},
\]
\[
(\sqrt p+\sqrt q)^2\le4r,\qquad
(\sqrt{A-p}+\sqrt{B-q})^2\le4(K-r).
\]
Decide whether these scalar inequalities imply
\[
p+q+r\ge\frac{2(A+B+K)}9.
\]
centroid-middle-bm-shortcut-audit.status_reason: Accepted fact `a7902cdbe6483b59` gives an exact strictly positive rational counterexample to the proposed scalar implication. It satisfies every nonempty, non-full hypothesis and therefore closes the audit by disproving the shortcut, without making any claim against the locked geometric theorem.
centroid-middle-bm-shortcut-audit.success_criterion: Success is either a complete exact proof of the scalar implication or a strictly positive rational sextuple \((A,B,K,p,q,r)\) satisfying every displayed hypothesis and violating the conclusion. Every square-root comparison and the final strict inequality must be certified exactly. A floating-point search or a construction with an empty or full endpoint cap does not count.

centroid-misalignment.relation_to_goal:
Accepted fact `4dfa9b673b27fea1` settles \(\delta=0\), while the exact obstacle
to using \(c_1\) shows that arbitrary displacement cannot be ignored. A stable
extension would reduce the genuine geometric residual class.
centroid-misalignment.statement:
Quantify how the centroid displacement
\(\delta=c_1-(c_0+c_2)/2\) affects the middle-slice depth argument, and prove the
\(2T/9\) target under an explicit nonzero tolerance or with an alternative
point depending on \(\delta\).
centroid-misalignment.status_reason:
Accepted lemma `e480e624b1618fae` proves the target throughout an explicit
positive neighborhood of affine centroid alignment. The sufficient condition
compares \(\|c_1-(c_0+c_2)/2\|\) with the centroidal inradius of \(A_1\) and
the slice areas. This closes the stated tolerance subgoal, not the full
misaligned regime.
centroid-misalignment.success_criterion:
Produce a self-contained inequality with a geometrically defined displacement
or slack parameter and an explicit hypothesis implying depth \(2T/9\).
Alternatively give an exact family showing that no bound depending only on the
centroid displacement magnitude and slice areas can work.

closed-homothetic-boundary.relation_to_goal: The strict residual theorem leaves out the natural boundary \(a+c=2\). Its algebra appears non-singular there, and that endpoint is exactly the canonical family supplied by Brunn-Minkowski equality normalization.
closed-homothetic-boundary.statement:
Extend the accepted anchored-tail and geometric reduction mechanism from \(a+c<2\) to the closed range \(a+c\le2\), under
\[
a\ge c>0,\qquad 1<a^2+c^2,\qquad a^2<1+c^2.
\]
Prove the resulting middle-centroid theorem for common-center homothetic convex bodies. In particular, combine the \(a+c=2\) case with accepted normalization `eee2bdfe64ccf5b1` and shear invariance `ecee03aff61db31e` to settle the Brunn-Minkowski area-equality family.
closed-homothetic-boundary.status_reason: Accepted theorem `ea0056993c3a877d` extends the anchored-tail argument to the closed parameter range \(a+c\le 2\), proves the common-center homothetic convex-body conclusion on the boundary, and settles the full Brunn-Minkowski area-equality family after the accepted normalization and invariances.
closed-homothetic-boundary.success_criterion: A self-contained candidate theorem checking every place strictness was used, proving the endpoint reduction and tail inequality, and applying the accepted shear normalization with matching parameter hypotheses.

concave-density-tent-decomposition.relation_to_goal: The failed affine-density extremality route shows that a single tent is insufficient. A correct common-support tent mixture would identify the true finite-dimensional extremal problem and prevent another invalid localization.
concave-density-tent-decomposition.statement: Prove an exact representation theorem for a compactly supported nonnegative concave probability density \(h\) on \([0,L]\) with mean \(1\): after harmless endpoint normalization, represent \(h\) as a probability mixture of normalized triangular tents \(h_{L,\tau}\), \(0\le\tau\le L\); prove \(3/2\le L\le3\), the barycenter constraint \(\mathbb E[\tau]=3-L\), and the corresponding convex-envelope formula for every finite linear combination of tail values \(G(t)\).
concave-density-tent-decomposition.status_reason: Accepted fact `c415ce7703455561` gives the exact canonical tent-mixture representation, support-length range, peak barycenter, lower-convex-envelope formula, and at-most-two-tent attainment.
concave-density-tent-decomposition.success_criterion: A complete measure-theoretic or elementary proof, including endpoint-face cases, normalization constants, moment identities, and an exact lower-convex-envelope statement.

concurrent-triangle-fan-balanced.relation_to_goal:
Because \(A_1+A_2+A_3+b=1\), the displayed inequality is equivalent to
the required three-cap inequality in the balanced-root branch. Together with
`concurrent-triangle-fan-unbalanced`, it closes
`canonical-concurrent-triangle-fan`.
concurrent-triangle-fan-balanced.statement:
Under all hypotheses and definitions in
`.math-prover/round-043/concurrent-triangle-fan-statement.md`, assume that
\[
\sqrt{A_i}\le \sqrt{A_j}+\sqrt{A_k}
\]
for every permutation \((i,j,k)\) of \((1,2,3)\). Prove
\[
\sqrt{A_1}+\sqrt{A_2}+\sqrt{A_3}\le\sqrt2.
\]
Determine all equality cases.
concurrent-triangle-fan-balanced.status_reason:
Accepted fact `b798e4964b158052` proves every balanced-root branch and shows
that equality occurs exactly at
\(\alpha=\beta=\gamma=1/3\), \(\rho=\sigma=\tau=1\), and
\(d_1=d_2=d_3=2/9\).
concurrent-triangle-fan-balanced.success_criterion:
Give a self-contained exact proof under every endpoint and side-order
constraint. An admissible proof may use an explicit Gram-matrix or generalized
eigenvalue certificate, but every auxiliary matrix inequality and equality
condition must be proved.

concurrent-triangle-fan-unbalanced.relation_to_goal:
The box maximum in the dominant-root branch is
\(2\sqrt{A_jA_k}\). This subgoal is exactly the unbalanced half of
`canonical-concurrent-triangle-fan`.
concurrent-triangle-fan-unbalanced.statement:
Under all hypotheses and definitions in
`.math-prover/round-043/concurrent-triangle-fan-statement.md`, prove that if
\[
\sqrt{A_i}\ge \sqrt{A_j}+\sqrt{A_k}
\]
for some permutation \((i,j,k)\) of \((1,2,3)\), then
\[
b\ge 2\sqrt{A_jA_k}.
\]
Determine all equality cases, including cases with a zero \(A_\ell\).
concurrent-triangle-fan-unbalanced.status_reason:
Accepted fact `e3e665e2576b37cc` proves every dominant-root branch, including
zero-cap cases, and shows the required inequality is strict there.
concurrent-triangle-fan-unbalanced.success_criterion:
Give a self-contained exact proof under every endpoint and side-order
constraint. Numerical evidence or an unexpanded computer-algebra assertion is
insufficient. State whether equality is attained or only approached at
excluded boundary limits.

convex-extension-support-clearance.relation_to_goal:
Applied rowwise to crossing-completion data, this is a necessary convexity
filter strictly stronger than the accepted scalar interval
`6f6869df3d151764`.  It rejects interval survivors before attempting to
construct a compatible middle polygon or a finite low-mass cover.
convex-extension-support-clearance.statement:
Let \(B\subset\mathbb R^2\) be a compact two-dimensional convex body
contained in a closed halfplane \(H\), and let \(K\supseteq B\) be a compact
convex body.  Put
\[
A=|K\setminus B|,
\qquad
e=|(K\setminus B)\cap H|.
\]
Prove that \(e<A\) implies
\[
e\ge
\inf_{z\in\partial H}
\left(|\operatorname{conv}(B\cup\{z\})|-|B|\right).
\]
For a rational convex polygon \(B\), derive the visible-edge formula showing
that the infimum is the exact minimum of a finite convex piecewise-linear
rational function along \(\partial H\).
convex-extension-support-clearance.status_reason:
Accepted fact `cf1a8ff16a0da82a` proves the registered convex
support-clearance inequality, its attainment and zero cases, and the exact
rational visible-edge minimization formula.
convex-extension-support-clearance.success_criterion:
A complete convexity proof, including support contact and boundary cases,
plus an exact visible-edge formula and rational finite minimization for
polygonal \(B\).

counterexample-boundary-low-r-asymmetric.relation_to_goal: The symmetric two-empty-full template is excluded by the residual chamber, while accepted fact `8d5e52a54e5db729` leaves only \(m/M<1/3\) for failure in the doubly empty-full pattern. An exact finite cover in this asymmetric residual family is a full disproof of the locked target; an exact realization of the canonical boundary data without a cover still isolates the next missing constraint.
counterexample-boundary-low-r-asymmetric.statement:
Search for a rational compatible finite-boundary configuration in the remaining range
\[
0<\frac{m}{M}<\frac13,\qquad M<m+k,
\]
with one strict-empty or support-contact lower-crossing row, at least one of the other two rows proper-proper or nonbisecting on the middle slice, all canonical tails, three genuine lower crossings, and \(L_1+L_2+L_3<-1\). Test whether the associated strict-low halfspaces can be completed to a finite cover of all three slices.
counterexample-boundary-low-r-asymmetric.success_criterion: Success is a `final` rational counterexample with exact one-sided lower-crossing verification and exact cover. A useful obstacle must identify and exhaust a precise rational polygonal ansatz while retaining \(M<m+k\); scalar cell tables or symmetric empty-full bisections do not meet the criterion.

counterexample-crossing-completable-tran.relation_to_goal: Accepted fact `6f6869df3d151764` is a cheap necessary filter for completing an endpoint pair to the three crossing equalities. Accepted fact `8f5f00ddd4f22d2f` turns any exact compatible rational strict-low cover into a full counterexample to the locked target. This subgoal therefore searches only cores that survive the newest exact crossing obstruction before solving the expensive convex-extension and cover problems.
counterexample-crossing-completable-tran.statement:
Search for rational compact convex polygons \(A_0,A_2\), pairwise nonparallel rational affine functions \(f_1,f_2,f_3\) with \(f_1+f_2+f_3=-1\), and rational levels \(L_1,L_2,L_3\), in the accepted residual range
\[
0<\frac{m}{M}<\frac38,\qquad M=\lvert A_0\rvert\ge m=\lvert A_2\rvert,
\]
such that the mandatory midpoint core \(B=(A_0+A_2)/2\) passes the crossing-completion interval in accepted fact `6f6869df3d151764`. Construct a rational convex polygon \(K\supseteq B\) realizing all three prescribed extension cap areas and all three genuine lower crossings. Then search for a finite rational family of halfspaces of mass strictly below \(2(M+m+\lvert K\rvert)/9\) whose interiors cover all three slices. The endpoint and middle normal fans must be genuinely transverse; exclude common-normal triangles and candidates protected by an aligned symmetric core.
counterexample-crossing-completable-tran.success_criterion: Success is a `final` rational counterexample with exact polygon vertices, exact midpoint containment, three exact genuine lower-crossing audits, exact strict halfspace masses, and exact slice-cover certificates. A useful negative result must exhaust a sharply declared transverse polygonal family after imposing the crossing-completion interval. A scalar allocation, floating-point no-hit, or candidate failing the interval does not meet the criterion.

counterexample-displaced-homothetic-tria.relation_to_goal: This family contains the near-miss configuration of accepted fact `82c768ad30501452` but allows the midpoint triangle to move inside \(A_1\) and the three cover thresholds to vary independently. Since both endpoint slices are triangles, any strict three-row solution is a full locked counterexample by accepted fact `64760c76cadff481`.
counterexample-displaced-homothetic-tria.statement:
Let \(A_1=\Delta\) and \(g\) be its centroid. Search rational parameters \(u,v>0\), \(p\in\mathbb Q^2\), and three rational barycentric thresholds \(s_1,s_2,s_3\) for
\[
A_0=p+u(\Delta-g),\qquad
A_2=p+v(\Delta-g).
\]
Require
\[
\frac{A_0+A_2}{2}\subseteq\Delta,
\]
the exact strict residual area strip, and
\[
s_1+s_2+s_3<1,
\]
so that the three middle corner-cap interiors cover the plane. For each row optimize the endpoint slope exactly. Find parameters for which all three actual row masses are strictly below \(2T/9\).
counterexample-displaced-homothetic-tria.status_reason:
Accepted fact `d5966531454de35f` proves that every displaced-homothetic
triangle triple in the registered family has at least one barycentric
corner row whose fully optimized mass is strictly greater than
\(2T/9\). It covers all translations, independent thresholds with sum
below one, positive homothety scales in the residual strip, and every
endpoint allocation breakpoint. Thus the registered corner-row search
family contains no counterexample.
counterexample-displaced-homothetic-tria.success_criterion: Success is an exact rational strict full counterexample, with each one-dimensional endpoint allocation minimized over every breakpoint and stationary point. A numerical candidate must be rationalized and rechecked exactly. If the whole declared family is proved safe, an exact elimination is also useful.

counterexample-low-m-five-cap-realizatio.relation_to_goal: The converse in `a6fbd3f54d7ec4c7` states that any actual rational realization reconstructs five strict-low halfspaces covering the three-slice set. It is therefore a finite exact disproof of the locked theorem. The last two caps create no additional existence obstruction in this low-\(M\) range.
counterexample-low-m-five-cap-realizatio.statement:
Use the converse direction of accepted fact `a6fbd3f54d7ec4c7` in the range
\[
\frac{T}{3}<M<\frac{4T}{9}.
\]
Find rational compatible convex polygons and rational affine halfspaces realizing its low-\(M\) five-cap normal form, with every one of the five exact slice-mass sums strictly below \(2T/9\). Retain the four-defect identity and necessary inequality of accepted fact `3081dc9f6b1f023f`; do not search only scalar Venn tables.
counterexample-low-m-five-cap-realizatio.success_criterion: Success is a complete rational polygonal realization submitted as a `final` counterexample packet. A scalar allocation, nonconvex cell table, or floating-point feasibility result is insufficient. A rigorous proof that a sharply declared polygon family cannot realize the normal form is an acceptable obstacle.

counterexample-nine-halfspace-slicewise-.relation_to_goal: Accepted fact `8f5f00ddd4f22d2f` proves that these three slicewise covers are exactly a finite counterexample certificate. Previous bounded searches using a single global family of at most five halfspaces do not exhaust this nine-halfspace certificate space. Any exact rational realization therefore disproves the locked target directly.
counterexample-nine-halfspace-slicewise-.statement: Find rational compatible compact two-dimensional convex polygons \(A_0,A_1,A_2\) and, for each \(j\in\{0,1,2\}\), at most three rational closed halfspaces \(H_{j1},H_{j2},H_{j3}\) such that every \(H_{jr}\) has total three-slice mass strictly below \(2T/9\), while the interiors of \(H_{j1},H_{j2},H_{j3}\) cover \(\{j\}\times A_j\). Allow the nine halfspaces to be completely different across the three target slices. Search the accepted residual range, prioritizing \(m/M<3/8\), genuinely transverse nonhomothetic polygons, and candidates without a large aligned symmetric core.
counterexample-nine-halfspace-slicewise-.success_criterion: Success is a `final` packet with rational polygon vertices, exact midpoint containment, exact strict masses for every used halfspace, and exact infeasibility of the closed complements on each target slice. A useful negative result must exhaust a sharply declared polygonal family with all three independent slicewise cover optimizations; a directional grid or floating-point no-hit is insufficient.

counterexample-opposite-asymmetric-low-r.relation_to_goal: Any exact finite strict-low-mass cover is a full counterexample to the locked target. Accepted facts `4b7d14106fb321c7` and `76d3bb559c4ad4be` show that the old target-side charge is false but its rational seed remains safe solely because the center of its large symmetric endpoint has depth \(M/2\). This subgoal removes that identified protection rather than retuning the already failed charge.
counterexample-opposite-asymmetric-low-r.statement:
Starting from the exact opposite-pair lower-crossing realization of accepted fact `4b7d14106fb321c7`, search for a rational compatible three-slice configuration with
\[
\frac{m}{M}<\frac38
\]
that preserves a positive opposite pair and genuine lower-crossing orientation but is not protected by a centrally symmetric large endpoint with \(M/2\ge2T/9\). The search may perturb all polygon vertices and affine rows. A successful configuration must supply a finite rational family of strict-low-mass halfspaces whose interiors cover all three slices.
counterexample-opposite-asymmetric-low-r.success_criterion: Success is a `final` packet with rational vertices and halfspace coefficients, exact compatibility, exact strict slice-mass margins, and an exact cover proof. A negative result must exhaust a sharply declared asymmetric polygon family. Numerical improvement without rationalization is working memory only.

counterexample-quantile-clearance-surviv.relation_to_goal:
Any exact survivor would be the first generic transverse core to pass all
three accepted prefilters and would provide a focused route to a rational
counterexample.  A complete exact directional-family obstruction would
show that moving the zero lines or affine constants is insufficient.
counterexample-quantile-clearance-surviv.statement:
For the exact generic transverse endpoint triangles and nonsymmetric
six-vertex midpoint core in accepted fact `19703e1e768865b1`, find rational
pairwise nonparallel linear forms
\[
\lambda_1+\lambda_2+\lambda_3=0
\]
that pass the accepted projection-quantile budget strictly.  Then search
over affine constants and crossing levels, applying in order the scalar
completion interval `6f6869df3d151764` and the convex support-clearance
fact `cf1a8ff16a0da82a`.  Construct a compatible rational middle polygon
and strict-low cover only after all filters pass.
counterexample-quantile-clearance-surviv.status_reason: Accepted fact `eeb8a6b3b5e04d6c` proves that every triple of nonzero real linear forms summing to zero fails the accepted projection-quantile budget for the registered fixed endpoint pair. This is stronger than exhausting a sharply declared rational direction family, so no scalar-completion or support-clearance stage can be reached.
counterexample-quantile-clearance-surviv.success_criterion:
An exact rational strict counterexample certificate, or an exact
exhaustion of a sharply declared rational direction family against the
quantile, scalar-completion, and support-clearance filters.

counterexample-regime-a-trapezoid.relation_to_goal: The parent Regime-A normal form already supplies the required finite halfspace certificate. An exact rational nonconstant-width trapezoid satisfying every strict condition gives a full locked counterexample; the known constant-width exclusion does not cover this family.
counterexample-regime-a-trapezoid.statement: Search the still-open nonconstant-width trapezoid family in the Regime-A normal form of accepted fact `f37aced9de558c8d`. Require rational \(h\) in its small residual interval, rational homothetic outer bodies \(A_2=hA_0\), and a rational middle trapezoid \(K\supseteq(1+h)A_0/2\) with nonzero width slope. Find an actual strict realization of all three low row masses that lies outside the constant-width/sheared-parallelogram families already excluded by accepted fact `f99c8b38fb488605`.
counterexample-regime-a-trapezoid.status_reason: Accepted fact `2b34891225e24670` eliminates every member of the declared rational nonconstant-width trapezoid search: it allows arbitrary real width slope and shear, both endpoint widths strictly positive, and an arbitrary compact two-dimensional convex middle body containing the required homothetic midpoint body. The broader triangular-limit subgoal remains open separately.
counterexample-regime-a-trapezoid.success_criterion: Success is an exact rational strict full counterexample, or a rigorous elimination of the entire declared trapezoid family. Numerical solver output must be converted to exact polygon vertices and all cap areas checked from the original halfspaces.

counterexample-rotated-survivor-variable.relation_to_goal: This fixed compatible family has empty closed depth erosion by accepted fact `9aa8eaca3b60ecf3`, admits a pairwise nonparallel projection-budget survivor, and satisfies every slice-area balance inequality. The previously tested fan fails by only a small exact positive margin. A strict three-row realization would be the first candidate to reach scalar completion in this genuinely transverse family and could be completed to a locked counterexample.
counterexample-rotated-survivor-variable.statement:
Fix
\[
A_0=\operatorname{conv}\{(0,0),(2,0),(0,1)\},
\]
the rotated area-\(1/16\) parallelogram
\[
A_2=\operatorname{conv}\{\epsilon(3/4,1/4)+\delta(-1/160,3/160):
\epsilon,\delta\in\{-1,1\}\},
\]
its midpoint core \(B=(A_0+A_2)/2\), and
\[
K_s=\operatorname{conv}(B\cup\{(0,s)\}),
\qquad
\frac{361}{480}\le s\le\frac{241}{320}.
\]
Find pairwise nonparallel rational directions \(n_1+n_2+n_3=0\), affine constants \(u_1+u_2+u_3=1\), and height levels \(L_i\) such that all three exact row masses are strictly below
\[
\frac{2(|A_0|+|K_s|+|A_2|)}9.
\]
If such rows exist, complete an exact rational \(N=4\) or \(N=5\) cover. Otherwise exhaust a sharply declared nontrivial direction chamber containing or adjacent to the width-separation direction \((3,1)\).
counterexample-rotated-survivor-variable.status_reason: Accepted fact `264a2405f063bba5` gives a uniform explicit depth point for every member of the registered rotated endpoint and middle family, covering all tilted and horizontal halfspaces. Hence no change of fan directions, weights, constants, or height levels can yield a counterexample in this family.
counterexample-rotated-survivor-variable.success_criterion: Success is an exact rational strict three-row realization followed by an exact finite cover, submitted as a final counterexample packet. A negative result must exhaust a precisely declared continuous or algebraic fan chamber with exact endpoint infimal-convolution and middle-cap inequalities; a directional grid or floating no-hit is only working memory.

counterexample-sage-exact-cover-search.relation_to_goal:
Any strict rational realization is a full counterexample: the finite
low-mass cover implies that no point of \(S\) has depth \(2T/9\). This search
does not rely on an incomplete directional sampling of the depth function.
Exact slice clipping is the right primitive because the measure is the sum of
three planar areas; a three-dimensional intersection volume is irrelevant.
counterexample-sage-exact-cover-search.statement:
Construct and use an exact-rational Sage search for a counterexample to the
locked three-slice problem. The search variables are rational compact
two-dimensional convex polygons \(A_0,A_1,A_2\) and a finite rational
halfspace cover \(H_1,\ldots,H_N\), with \(N\in\{3,4,5\}\). Require
\[
\frac{A_0+A_2}{2}\subseteq A_1
\]
and, writing \(T=|A_0|+|A_1|+|A_2|\),
\[
\mathcal H_2(S\cap H_j)<\frac{2T}{9}\qquad(j=1,\ldots,N),
\]
while the interiors of the \(H_j\) cover all three slice polygons.

Search the current accepted residual domain, with special priority on
\(m/M<50/(93+12\sqrt{21})\), but do not impose canonical finite-interior
or no-opposite assumptions unless they follow from the chosen certificate.
counterexample-sage-exact-cover-search.success_criterion:
Success is a `final` counterexample packet giving rational polygon vertices,
rational halfspace coefficients, an exact compatibility certificate, exact
cover verification, and exact strict mass margins against \(2T/9\).

A useful negative result must precisely declare and exhaust a finite search
domain, record the Sage version and deterministic seed, and verify every
pruning rule. A floating-point no-hit, directional grid, or unverified
rational rounding is only working memory.

counterexample-specific-asymmetric-trian.relation_to_goal: An exact finite cover is a `final` counterexample to the locked problem. This triple lies in the accepted \(m/M<3/8\) chamber, breaks the large-endpoint central symmetry that protected the previous opposite-pair seed, and is not a shear-equivalent common-homothety family because the middle triangle is not the required homothetic midpoint slice.
counterexample-specific-asymmetric-trian.statement:
Let
\[
A_0=\operatorname{conv}\{(0,0),(0,20/11),(11/10,0)\},
\]
\[
A_2=\operatorname{conv}\{(0,0),(0,2/11),(11/100,0)\},
\qquad
A_1=\operatorname{conv}\{(0,0),(2,0),(0,1)\}.
\]
Then \((A_0+A_2)/2\subseteq A_1\), the areas are \(1,1,1/100\), and the locked threshold is \(67/150\). Find a finite family of rational closed halfspaces, each of total three-slice mass strictly below \(67/150\), whose interiors cover all three slices; or prove that this exact triple has a point of depth at least \(67/150\).
counterexample-specific-asymmetric-trian.status_reason: Accepted fact `5df6b20873701985` proves that the fixed asymmetric rational triangle triple is safe: an explicit rational point in the middle slice has exact three-slice depth strictly above \(67/150\). The proof exhausts all halfspace directions and height slopes through 57 exact chambers and separate multi-vertex and horizontal cases. Therefore no strict-low halfspace cover exists for this triple.
counterexample-specific-asymmetric-trian.success_criterion: Success requires rational halfspace coefficients, exact Sage \(\mathbb Q^2\) clipping of all three masses, exact strict margins, and an exact empty-complement proof for every slice. A numerical depth grid is only a locator. A negative result must certify a concrete point against every halfspace direction, not merely exhaust bounded integer normals.

counterexample-triangle-n3-matrix-search.relation_to_goal: Accepted fact `64760c76cadff481` is an if-and-only-if reconstruction theorem. Any strict rational feasible point of this system gives a compact rational polytope with three triangular integer slices and no point of depth \(2T/9\). It is therefore a full disproof of the locked target, not an auxiliary counterexample.
counterexample-triangle-n3-matrix-search.statement:
Find exact rational matrices \(U,V,L\in\mathbb Q^{3\times3}\) and \(\sigma\in\mathbb Q^3\) satisfying the \(N=3\) counterexample system of accepted fact `64760c76cadff481`. In addition, use the surviving normal form of accepted fact `09393c6edf1fc4e2`:
\[
\det L\ne0,\qquad
q:=\sigma_1+\sigma_2+\sigma_3>1,
\]
\[
B=|\det V|=\max\{|\det U|,|\det V|\},
\qquad
1+|\det U|<2B.
\]
All compatibility, strict residual-strip, column-sum, and three exact cap inequalities from `64760c76cadff481` must hold literally.
counterexample-triangle-n3-matrix-search.success_criterion: Success is an exact rational strict feasible point, with every cap branch and inequality checked directly, submitted as a `final` counterexample packet. A no-hit search is only useful working memory unless it exhausts a precisely declared finite or algebraic domain.

coupling-domination.relation_to_goal:
Accepted fact `1790a353b242874b` proves this only for the independent
coupling because its counterexample computation needed independence. The
domination argument itself appears coupling-free. Certifying that
generalization would allow the main strategy to choose a coupling adapted to
the geometry rather than being locked to convolution.
coupling-domination.statement:
Let \(\pi\) be any probability coupling of the uniform probability measures
on \(A_0\) and \(A_2\), let \(\nu_\pi\) be the midpoint pushforward, and put
\[
\eta_\pi(E)=|A_1\cap E|+\min\{a_0,a_2\}\nu_\pi(E).
\]
Prove that the normal-form three-slice mass through \((1,c)\) dominates
\(\eta_\pi\) on the corresponding middle halfplane for every such coupling,
including slice-parallel halfspaces.
coupling-domination.status_reason:
Accepted lemma `1e5a9785593e5f6a` proves the registered domination for
every probability coupling with uniform outer marginals. Independence is not
needed for the event inclusion or marginal charging. This closes the
domination subgoal but leaves open how to select a coupling whose midpoint
mixture has sufficient planar depth.
coupling-domination.success_criterion:
Return a self-contained proof with exact marginal and event-inclusion
arguments, or an explicit coupling showing failure. State clearly that the
lemma alone does not select an advantageous coupling or prove the locked
target.

deep-midpoint-brunn-minkowski-transfer.relation_to_goal:
This is the positive global mechanism surviving the Fable consultation.
It couples endpoint and middle payments in the same direction through
compatibility and planar Brunn--Minkowski, rather than summing unrelated
indices. The centroid specialization should close a new unconditional
area region and supply the basic transfer inequality for the remaining
fixed-allocation intersection problem.
deep-midpoint-brunn-minkowski-transfer.statement:
Let \(A_0,A_1,A_2\subset\mathbb R^2\) be the slices of the locked
problem, so \((A_0+A_2)/2\subseteq A_1\). For \(i\in\{0,2\}\), let
\(x_i\in A_i\) have planar halfspace depth at least \(\beta_i\) in
\(A_i\), and put \(z=(x_0+x_2)/2\).

Prove
\[
 d_{A_1}(z)\ge
 \frac{(\sqrt{\beta_0}+\sqrt{\beta_2})^2}{4},
\]
and prove that \(z\) belongs to the exact endpoint fixed-allocation
region \(\mathcal E(b)\) of accepted fact `66f17f4981c30108` for every
\(0\le b\le\min(\beta_0,\beta_2)\).

Then take \(x_i=g_i\), put
\[
 M=\max(a_0,a_2),\qquad m=\min(a_0,a_2),\qquad
 z_0=\frac{g_0+g_2}{2},
\]
and prove the exact mixed-depth bound
\[
 h_S((1,z_0))
 \ge
 \min\left\{
 a_0+a_1,\ a_1+a_2,\
 \frac{(\sqrt M+\sqrt m)^2+4m}{9}
 \right\}.
\]
Conclude that the locked target holds whenever
\[
 2a_1\le2\sqrt{Mm}+3m-M.
\]

equivalent by compactness and planar Helly to \(M(1)<D=q(1)=4/9\), and would
refute the registered outer-middle activation lemma. Exact infeasibility would
close the first concrete calibration exposed by that obstacle and identify
which joint endpoint payment prevents an outer-only zero.
deformation-triangle-equality-cover-test.statement:
Let
\[
A_0=\operatorname{conv}\{(0,0),(2,0),(0,1)\},
\quad
A_2=\operatorname{conv}\{(0,0),(1/2,0),(1/2,1/4)\},
\]
\[
A_1=\operatorname{conv}\{(0,0),(3/2,0),(0,5/4)\}.
\]
These compatible rational triangles have areas \(1,1/16,15/16\), so
\[
t=\frac{2(|A_0|+|A_1|+|A_2|)}9=\frac49.
\]
Decide exactly whether there exist at most three proper closed halfspaces in
\(\mathbb R^3\), each having total three-slice mass strictly below \(4/9\),
whose height-one trace interiors cover \(\{1\}\times A_1\).
deformation-triangle-equality-cover-test.status_reason:
Accepted fact `97757545b16e824d` proves that the displayed middle centroid has
depth at least \(4/9\), so no family of strict-low-mass height-one trace
interiors covers the middle triangle. This exactly resolves the registered
fixed-instance test in the negative. The parent
`deformation-outer-middle-activation` subgoal remains open for arbitrary
compatible triples.
deformation-triangle-equality-cover-test.success_criterion:
Success is either exact rational halfspaces with verified strict clipping
masses and exact infeasibility of their closed height-one complements on
\(A_1\), or a complete exact semialgebraic or geometric certificate excluding
all triples of trace directions and height slopes. Sampling directions,
testing selected middle points, or floating-point infeasibility is not enough.

deformation-triangle-three-row.relation_to_goal: Accepted facts `a49f2b26cc468e4c` and `fa47d2b2236c29fd` identify this conclusion as the triangular-endpoint outer-middle activation gate at (D=q). Accepted fact `50cb740c6bf85957` proves it for (mu/A\ge9/25). The prior round reduced the complementary range to a genuinely three-row coupling problem; this subgoal requires the new common-vertex-matrix mechanism instead of independent scalar or rowwise Brunn-Minkowski bounds.
deformation-triangle-three-row.statement:
Let (A_0,A_2\subset\mathbb R^2) be nondegenerate triangles of areas (A\ge\mu>0), and let (L\subset\mathbb R^2) be a compact two-dimensional convex polygon satisfying
\[
\frac{A_0+A_2}{2}\subseteq L,
\qquad |L|=A-\mu,
\qquad \frac\mu A<\frac9{25}.
\]
Put
\[
S=(\{0\}\times A_0)\cup(\{1\}\times L)\cup(\{2\}\times A_2),
\qquad D=\frac{4A}{9}.
\]
Prove
\[
\max_{z\in L}h_S((1,z))\ge D
\]
by excluding every exact Helly certificate of at most three strict-low profile halfplanes. The proof must retain the common projected vertex matrices of both endpoint triangles across all rows. Alternatively, give exact rational triangles and a rational polygon (L) for which the full global middle optimum is strictly below (D).
deformation-triangle-three-row.success_criterion: Success is a complete proof for arbitrary endpoint triangles and arbitrary compatible polygonal (L) in the displayed small-ratio range, with the Helly reduction and every two- or three-row case certified, or an exact rational global counterexample. A scalar relaxation, one projected order, fixed centroid, or finite directional sample is insufficient.

deformation-triangular-outer-activation.relation_to_goal: For a triangle, the maximum planar halfspace depth equals (4/9) of its area by accepted fact `fa47d2b2236c29fd`. Hence (D=4M/9) in the notation of accepted fact `a49f2b26cc468e4c`, while the equality (D=q) is exactly (|L|=M-m). The statement is therefore the full triangular-endpoint case of the open outer-middle activation gate. Accepted fact `50cb740c6bf85957` proves it when the smaller-to-larger outer depth ratio is at least (9/25), leaving precisely the small-ratio regime stated here.
deformation-triangular-outer-activation.statement:
Let (A_0,A_2\subset\mathbb R^2) be nondegenerate triangles of areas (M\ge m>0), and let (L\subset\mathbb R^2) be a compact two-dimensional convex polygon satisfying
\[
\frac{A_0+A_2}{2}\subseteq L,
\qquad |L|=M-m.
\]
For
\[
S=(\{0\}\times A_0)\cup(\{1\}\times L)\cup(\{2\}\times A_2),
\]
prove
\[
\max_{z\in L}h_S((1,z))\ge\frac{4M}{9},
\]
or give exact rational (A_0,A_2,L) for which the full global middle optimum is strictly below (4M/9). The proof or disproof must cover the only unresolved ratio range (m/M<9/25); accepted fact `50cb740c6bf85957` already covers (m/M\ge9/25).
deformation-triangular-outer-activation.success_criterion: Success is a uniform proof for arbitrary compatible triangular endpoints and arbitrary polygonal (L) in the stated small-ratio regime, including equality cases, or an exact rational counterexample that certifies the full global middle maximum rather than testing selected points or directions. A fixed-centroid bound or a finite directional sample is insufficient.

deformation-two-coordinate-intersection.relation_to_goal: The round-126 same-index selector is false because identical endpoint data on two negative rows need not identify the paying middle row. The simultaneous intersections \(P^-\) and \(K^-\) couple both negative coordinates, and their midpoint sum lies inside the positive contact cap of \(L\). The displayed lower bound therefore closes the surviving contact cell; a rational all-three-strict example refutes the paired-cap route.
deformation-two-coordinate-intersection.statement:
Assume the two-negative support-contact chamber of `deformation-contained-coordinate-pairing`:
\[
z_1,z_2<0<z_3,
\qquad
-\sigma_3=\max_{x\in P}x_3,
\qquad
\sigma_3<\min_{x\in K}x_3.
\]
Suppose all three paired-cap row totals are strictly below \(4A/9\). Put \(\tau_j=-\sigma_j\) and
\[
P^-=P\cap\{s_1\le\tau_1,\ s_2\le\tau_2\},
\qquad
K^-=K\cap\{s_1\le-\tau_1,\ s_2\le-\tau_2\}.
\]
Prove
\[
\frac{(\sqrt{|P^-|}+\sqrt{|K^-|})^2}{4}
\ge\frac{4A}{9}-\mu
\]
from the exact two triangle-cap profiles, \(\tau_1+\tau_2+\tau_3\ge1\), and the contact conditions. Conclude from midpoint containment that the contact row cannot be strict. Alternatively, give exact rational \(P,K,L,\sigma\) satisfying every hypothesis and all three strict rows.
deformation-two-coordinate-intersection.status_reason: The exact obstacle in handoff `52e263eb5af74c82.md` proves that the registered lower bound is numerically impossible when `sqrt(mu/A) < (-3+2 sqrt(11))/15`, even for the whole endpoint triangles. An integral calibration satisfies containment, contact, the shift sum, and two strict rows while violating the bound. The next route must split at this threshold and use strictness of the final negative row directly.
deformation-two-coordinate-intersection.success_criterion: The proof must calculate or bound the intersection areas jointly, not multiply independent marginal bounds, must use the common shifts and exact contact equalities, and must justify every containment and strict boundary. A refutation must give rational vertices and shifts, exact areas, midpoint containment, and all three strict totals.

directional-allocation-topological-selec.relation_to_goal: The fixed-allocation architecture is refuted by accepted fact `23dcab2387927bc4`, while accepted fact `65512ded3a06d971` leaves a continuous direction-dependent allocation. A topological argument is the natural global alternative because it may coordinate those directionwise choices without forcing them to be constant.
directional-allocation-topological-selec.statement: Using the exact continuous threshold \(q\mapsto\rho_q(2T/9)\) and the unique continuous directionwise outer allocation, determine whether a genuinely topological selection principle on \(\mathbb S^1\) forces the Wulff intersection \(A_1\cap\bigcap_q\{z:q\cdot z\ge\rho_q(2T/9)\}\) to be nonempty. Prove a precise KKM, degree, antipodal, or interval-selection lemma from the accepted structural properties, or give an exact abstract or compatible geometric obstruction showing that those properties are insufficient.
directional-allocation-topological-selec.status_reason: Accepted fact `9328166a552ec875` supplies the exact Wulff-Helly-Farkas nonemptiness criterion and an abstract antipodally equivariant counterexample showing that continuity and unique continuous directionwise allocation are insufficient. The unresolved input is exactly the balanced-threshold inequality for every positive-spanning triple.
directional-allocation-topological-selec.success_criterion: A fully stated and proved topological lemma whose hypotheses are verified from accepted facts and whose conclusion yields the required nonempty Wulff intersection, or a rigorous obstruction demonstrating exactly which additional cross-direction property is missing.

directional-outer-allocation-continuity.relation_to_goal:
Accepted fact `17ca54faa05ad878` gives the exact directionwise outer
minimization but no cross-direction selection theorem. Continuity and
uniqueness of its outer mass allocation would remove one genuine obstacle
to a KKM or Borsuk--Ulam treatment of the balanced-threshold inequality. It
does not exchange the remaining endpoint maximization with the direction
variable and does not itself prove that inequality.
directional-outer-allocation-continuity.statement:
Assume the setting and notation of accepted fact `17ca54faa05ad878`,
but retain the direction variable \(q\in\mathbb S^1\). Fix
\[
  0<t<a_1+\min(a_0,a_2).
\]
For each \(q\), let \(Q_{i,q}\), \(E_q\), and the zero-demand conventions
\(D_{1,q}(0)=E_q(0)=-\infty\) be exactly those of that fact. Prove that the
minimum
\[
 \rho_q(t)=\min_{0\le a\le t}
 \max\left\{D_{1,q}(a),\frac12E_q(t-a)\right\}
\]
has a unique optimizer \(a_*(q)\), after demands exceeding \(a_1\) or
\(\min(a_0,a_2)\) are excluded by the \(+\infty\) conventions, and that
\[
 q\longmapsto a_*(q),\qquad q\longmapsto\rho_q(t)
\]
are continuous on \(\mathbb S^1\).
directional-outer-allocation-continuity.status_reason:
Accepted fact `65512ded3a06d971` proves the registered statement in full:
joint continuity of directional cap quantiles, strict positive-demand
monotonicity of the endpoint threshold, uniqueness of the outer optimizer,
continuity of both the optimizer and \(\rho_q(t)\), and all zero-demand and
capacity-active endpoint cases.
directional-outer-allocation-continuity.success_criterion:
Success requires a complete proof of joint directional continuity of the
cap quantiles and endpoint threshold, strict monotonicity sufficient for
optimizer uniqueness, and all cases where one demand is zero or a feasible
interval endpoint is active. If uniqueness or continuity is false, give an
exact compatible polygonal counterexample and identify the weakest valid
upper-hemicontinuity or connected-valued replacement. A pointwise argument
that ignores the zero-demand discontinuities does not meet the criterion.

duality-reduction.relation_to_goal:
This is an independent route intended to produce a reusable bridge rather than
another special case. It may support either a universal proof or a certified

duality-reduction.statement:
Find a rigorous minimax, separation, or extremal reduction for the balanced
three-slice problem that converts the continuum of candidate points and
halfspaces into a finite or otherwise tractable certificate while preserving
the exact \(2/9\) target.
duality-reduction.status_reason:
The accepted lemma `8f5f00ddd4f22d2f` gives an exact finite counterexample
certificate: at most three low-mass halfspaces per slice, hence at most nine in
total, with exact polygon-clipping and linear-infeasibility checks.
duality-reduction.success_criterion:
Produce a self-contained equivalence or one-way reduction with exact
quantifiers and no unproved compactness or minimax interchange. State precisely
how a resulting finite certificate would imply or disprove the locked target.

edge-frame-global-budget-regime.statement:

\[
m=\min\{a_0,a_2\},\qquad M=\max\{a_0,a_2\}.
\]
Prove that one certificate halfspace has mass at least
\[
\frac{4a_1}{9}+\frac{m}{3}.
\]
Consequently, if \(M-a_1\le m/2\), prove that one has mass at least
\(2T/9\), so no global counterexample can have such a certificate.
edge-frame-global-budget-regime.status_reason:

empty-full-arbitrary-curvature-dual.relation_to_goal: This is the dimension-free form of the accepted straddling two-kink certificate. It excludes every finite three-kink localization, and indeed every finite curvature measure, in the full-right interior-left chamber without enumerating atom orders.
empty-full-arbitrary-curvature-dual.statement:
Fix \(x,\ell,b>0\) with \(x+\ell+b=1\), put
\(\lambda=x+\ell\), and define
\[
D=\frac{16\ell-9(b+\ell)^2}{2},\qquad
K_0=\frac{5b^2-6b\ell+5\ell^2}{2},
\]
\[
a_*(t)=\frac{-t^2+2t+9x^2-2x}{2},
\]
\[
k_*(t)=
\begin{cases}
\dfrac{(t-x)(16\ell-5t+11x-6)}2,&x\leq t\leq\lambda,\\
\dfrac{8\ell^2+3t^2-6t-3x^2+6x}2,&\lambda\leq t\leq1.
\end{cases}
\]
For every \(h\geq0\) and every finite nonnegative Borel measure
\(\mu\) on \([x,1]\), prove
\[
a_*(1)h+\int_x^1a_*(t)\,d\mu(t)<D
\]
implies
\[
K_0+k_*(1)h+\int_x^1k_*(t)\,d\mu(t)>0.
\]

empty-full-arbitrary-curvature-dual.success_criterion: Produce one explicit nonnegative \(A\)-budget multiplier whose ray slack is nonnegative for every \(t\in[x,1]\), prove the constant slack is nonnegative on the whole parameter domain, and integrate the pointwise inequality. All equalities at \(t=\lambda\) and \(t=1\) must be included.

empty-full-general-width-theorem.relation_to_goal: This is the unrestricted concave-width version of the accepted one-kink theorem. It closes the remaining one-dimensional empty-full/support-contact model after the finite-curvature localization, including interior-left and endpoint-left clipping and both right clipping alternatives.
empty-full-general-width-theorem.statement:
Let \(v:[0,1]\to(0,\infty)\) be nondecreasing and concave, with
canonical endpoint values. Fix \(0<\lambda<r<1\), define
\[
\psi_\lambda(u)=\max\{-v(u),\min\{u-\lambda,v(u)\}\},
\]
\[
I=\int_0^1v(u)\,du,\qquad
p=\frac12+\frac1{2I}\int_0^1\psi_\lambda(u)\,du,\qquad
q(r)=\frac{\int_0^rv(u)\,du}{I}.
\]
Prove
\[
p<\frac49
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
q(r)>p
\quad\text{and}\quad
4p+5q(r)>4.
\]
empty-full-general-width-theorem.status_reason:
Accepted fact `52cbc42a8e62feb7` proves the unrestricted theorem for

empty-full-general-width-theorem.success_criterion: Give one complete proof covering the four clipping endpoint alternatives and every weak boundary.
