endpoint-contribution.relation_to_goal:
This subgoal tries to turn convex compatibility into quantitative mass on a
second slice, reducing the unresolved parameter region without assuming
homothetic or identical slices.
endpoint-contribution.statement:
Derive an exact cross-slice contribution inequality at a slice centroid that
strictly improves the bound \(h_S((k,g_k))\ge4a_k/9\), and use it to settle a
nonempty part of the balanced area regime not covered by \(a_k\ge T/2\).
endpoint-contribution.status_reason:
The accepted counterexample `4092c268dbe610f6` shows that no universal
positive additive \(c\,a_1\) contribution can improve the endpoint-centroid
bound, even for equal balanced slices. This closes the proposed endpoint route,
not the universal theorem.
endpoint-contribution.success_criterion:
Produce a proved inequality with all constants and hypotheses explicit, plus a
derived area region in which the \(2T/9\) target follows. If no such inequality
can hold, give an exact compatible convex-polytopal counterexample to the
specific proposed inequality.

endpoint-product-cover-payment.relation_to_goal:
For the strict three-halfspace certificate in accepted fact
`d2d117bcc58a1ba0`, \(x_i+y_i\) is exactly the endpoint contribution of
the \(i\)-th halfspace.  This product-space covering inequality would provide
the missing quantitative payment without any Brunn--Minkowski cap transfer.
Combined with a valid bonus covering inequality it closes at least the area
regime \(\max(a_0,a_2)-a_1\le\min(a_0,a_2)/2\).
endpoint-product-cover-payment.statement:
Let \(A_0,A_2\subset\mathbb R^2\) be planar convex bodies of positive
areas \(a_0,a_2\).  Let \(f_i:\mathbb R^2\to\mathbb R\) be affine and
\(s_i\in\mathbb R\) for \(i=1,2,3\).  Assume the open halfplanes
\(\{f_i<0\}\) cover \(\mathbb R^2\).  Define
\[
C_{0i}=\{x\in A_0:f_i(x)-s_i\le0\},\qquad
C_{2i}=\{x\in A_2:f_i(x)+s_i\le0\},
\]
and \(x_i=|C_{0i}|\), \(y_i=|C_{2i}|\).  Prove
\[
A_0\times A_2\subseteq
\bigcup_{i=1}^3\bigl((C_{0i}\times A_2)\cup(A_0\times C_{2i})\bigr),
\]
and consequently
\[
\sum_{i=1}^3\left(\frac{x_i}{a_0}+\frac{y_i}{a_2}\right)\ge1,
\qquad
\sum_{i=1}^3(x_i+y_i)\ge\min\{a_0,a_2\}.
\]
endpoint-product-cover-payment.status_reason:
Accepted fact `0b5d84877f51b7c3` proves the endpoint product-space
cylinder cover and the normalized and unweighted payment inequalities,
including all strict/closed boundary conventions.
endpoint-product-cover-payment.success_criterion:
A complete proof must check the affine midpoint identity, strict versus closed
boundary conventions, the product-set cover for every endpoint pair, the
product-measure union bound, and the final unweighted inequality for both
orders of \(a_0,a_2\).

equality-cap-vector-obstruction.relation_to_goal:
Inconsistency would rule out a middle-slice low-mass cover for this residual
area pattern using only accepted finite-cover and cap-vector information.
An exact feasible vector system would prove that this scalar relaxation
cannot settle the full Minkowski-equality family and prevent repeated work.
equality-cap-vector-obstruction.statement:
For the accepted rational Minkowski-equality area triple
\[
(a_0,a_1,a_2)=\left(\frac{77}{2},\frac{307}{8},5\right),
\]
decide whether the following scalar relaxation is already inconsistent.
There are at most three cap vectors
\((b_{0r},b_{1r},b_{2r})\) with total mass below \(2T/9\), each satisfying
both cap-vector Brunn--Minkowski inequalities, while
\[
\sum_r b_{1r}\ge a_1,\qquad
\sum_r\left(\frac{b_{0r}}{a_0}+\frac{b_{2r}}{a_2}\right)\ge1.
\]
equality-cap-vector-obstruction.status_reason:
The exact feasible vectors in the recorded packet meet the registered
success criterion by proving feasibility of the scalar system. They are not
geometric halfspaces. Moreover, the separate cap-vector obstacle shows that
the proposed square-root inequalities are not unconditional necessary
conditions, so this scalar route cannot decide the equality family.
equality-cap-vector-obstruction.success_criterion:
Give either an exact inequality proof of infeasibility or explicit rational
cap vectors satisfying every displayed weak inequality and strict mass
bound. A feasible scalar system is only an obstacle to this relaxation, not
a geometric counterexample.

extreme-diagonal-coupling.relation_to_goal:
Accepted fact `1e5a9785593e5f6a` converts a positive answer directly into a
three-slice depth certificate. A negative answer shows that replacing the
independent product by the simplest geometry-aligned coupling still does not
settle this near-extremal instance.
extreme-diagonal-coupling.statement:
For the fixed triple in `extreme-nested-triangle-depth`, couple the uniform
outer probabilities by a common uniform \(U\in\Delta\):
\[
X_0=\frac{201}{200}U,\qquad
X_2=\frac{101}{1000}U.
\]
Then the midpoint is uniform on \((553/1000)\Delta\). Decide exactly whether
the coupled mixture
\[
\eta_\pi=|\Delta\cap\cdot|
+\left(\frac{101}{1000}\right)^2D\,
  \operatorname{Unif}\!\left(\frac{553}{1000}\Delta\right)
\]
has a point of halfplane depth at least
\(1010113D/2250000\).
extreme-diagonal-coupling.status_reason: The fixed geometric triple is already certified positive by accepted facts `c0a4f6ae5d1dab55` and `ecee03aff61db31e`. Verifying one particular coupling would no longer change the proof state, so this route-specific subgoal is abandoned as redundant.
extreme-diagonal-coupling.success_criterion:
Compute the exact maximum or give an explicit point with a complete
all-halfplane lower bound. For a negative answer, give at most three rational
halfplanes whose interiors cover \(\Delta\), with each coupled-mixture mass
strictly below the exact threshold. Symmetry guesses or numerical
optimization alone do not count.

extreme-middle-cover.relation_to_goal:
Nonexistence proves that some middle-slice point reaches the locked target.
Existence supplies the exact middle-slice component of a possible finite
counterexample certificate but does not decide the two outer slices.
extreme-middle-cover.statement:
For the fixed extreme nested-triangle triple, decide whether the middle slice
\(\{1\}\times\Delta\) can be covered in its interior by at most three actual
three-dimensional halfspaces, each of total three-slice mass strictly below
\(1010113D/2250000\).
extreme-middle-cover.status_reason: Accepted fact `c0a4f6ae5d1dab55` supplies a point contained in no halfspace of mass below \(2T/9\), so the middle slice cannot have the proposed strict-low-mass interior cover.
extreme-middle-cover.success_criterion:
Give either explicit rational halfspaces with exact triangle-cap areas and an
exact linear interior-cover certificate, or a self-contained inequality
proving that no such at-most-three cover can exist. Sampled directions or an
\(\eta\)-cover are insufficient.

extreme-nested-triangle-depth.relation_to_goal:
This triple is obtained from the accepted strict balanced mixture
counterexample `82c768ad30501452` by an area-preserving affine shear on each
slice. Its largest outer slice and middle slice are both just below \(T/2\);
the outer-centroid \(4/9\) bound misses the target by only
\[
\frac{2(1+(101/1000)^2-(201/200)^2)}9D.
\]
Deciding the actual three-slice depth tests the locked theorem at the first
exact instance where the independent-mixture bridge fails.
extreme-nested-triangle-depth.statement:
Let \(\Delta\) be a rational nondegenerate triangle of area \(D\), with
homotheties centered at one vertex, and set
\[
A_0=\frac{201}{200}\Delta,\qquad
A_1=\Delta,\qquad
A_2=\frac{101}{1000}\Delta.
\]
Decide the exact locked depth conclusion for this fixed compatible balanced
triple, whose threshold is
\[
\frac{2T}{9}=\frac{1010113}{2250000}D.
\]
extreme-nested-triangle-depth.status_reason: Accepted fact `c0a4f6ae5d1dab55` gives an explicit middle-slice point with depth at least \(2T/9\) for the fixed vertex-centered triple.
extreme-nested-triangle-depth.success_criterion:
Return either an explicit point in one of the three slices with a complete
all-halfspace proof at the exact threshold, or the full at-most-three
strict-low-mass halfspace covers for all three slices required by accepted
fact `8f5f00ddd4f22d2f`. A low-mass cover of only one slice or failure of one
point is an obstacle, not a decision.

finite-certificate-search.relation_to_goal:
Accepted fact `8f5f00ddd4f22d2f` reduces a genuine disproof to at most nine
strict low-mass halfspaces. This subgoal turns counterexample search into an
exact finite target rather than relying on sampled depths.
finite-certificate-search.statement:
Use the accepted finite-cover equivalence to construct a complete exact
counterexample certificate for rational polygonal slices, or prove that such a
certificate cannot exist in a sharply delimited minimal polygon family.
finite-certificate-search.status_reason:
Accepted theorem `bdcb254b7e7c3718` computes exact depth \(1/2\) at a point of
the fixed rational pentagon family proposed in round 3. Hence no strict
low-mass finite-cover certificate exists for that precisely stated family,
meeting the alternative success criterion. This closes that test family, not
the search for counterexamples in other families.
finite-certificate-search.success_criterion:
Supply rational or real-algebraic polygon vertices, at most three halfspaces per
slice, exact clipped-area calculations showing mass \(<2T/9\), and exact linear
infeasibility certificates for the three slice covers. Alternatively prove
nonexistence for a precisely stated family using exact inequalities.

finite-slope-localization.relation_to_goal: The coefficient \(2/9\) is asymptotically sharp, so a proof cannot come from a stronger scalar constant. A valid localization would reduce the exact mixed-area and Minkowski-centroid coupling to the extremal profile exhibited by the rectangle-triangle family.
finite-slope-localization.statement: Prove or refute the finite-slope localization proposed in the accepted round-18 obstacle: for the sharp outer-deficit functional in the small-\(r\) residual strip, reduce arbitrary polygonal hypograph profiles and fiber placements to an edge-order transition with one constant projection density and one affine increasing projection density.
finite-slope-localization.status_reason: Accepted fact `18fa46bbd1c0c9d4` closes the full residual minimal-family gap without the proposed localization. The returned localization counterexample remains unverified and is not needed on the critical path.
finite-slope-localization.success_criterion: Provide a complete variation, mass-transport, or polygonal edge-exchange argument preserving every constrained quantity, followed by the finite extremal calculation; or give an exact counterexample to the localization statement and identify the next extremal class.

five-cap-affine-normal-form.relation_to_goal: This removes every combinatorial incidence pattern from the five-cap case and leaves two actual-body branches split at \(|A_2|=4T/9\). Closing both branches, together with accepted six-cap reduction, proves the locked theorem.
five-cap-affine-normal-form.statement:
Assume a strict five-halfspace cover of the locked set. Prove, after arbitrarily small outward perturbation, relabeling, and possibly reflecting height, the following exhaustive normal form:

1. Three proper nonparallel halfspaces have equations
\[
f_j(z)+(h-1)s_j\le0,\qquad
f_1+f_2+f_3=-1,\qquad \sum_js_j>1,
\]
and cover the full planes at heights \(0\) and \(1\).
2. At height \(2\), their common complementary region \(Q\) is a bounded nondegenerate triangle. With \(R=A_2\cap Q\), the other two actual halfspaces cover \(R\), have private points there, and
\[
\frac T3<|R|<\frac{4T}{9},\qquad
\frac T3<|A_2|<\frac T2.
\]
3. Either the last two sections cover all of \(A_2\), forcing \(|A_2|<4T/9\), or one of the first rows together with the last two forms a second positive Farkas plane cover.
4. Retain the exact five mass inequalities, global surplus \(<T/9\), midpoint-graph identity, and nonnegative height-shift defects stated in the packet proof.
five-cap-affine-normal-form.status_reason: Accepted fact `a6fbd3f54d7ec4c7` proves every registered five-cap normal-form clause, including the actual-cover converse, branch split, and midpoint/surplus identities.
five-cap-affine-normal-form.success_criterion: Success requires the interior-minimal and planar-Helly reductions, all Farkas normalizations and horizontal/parallel cases, private witnesses, exact area interval for \(R\), the branch dichotomy, and the midpoint/surplus identities with actual affine height coupling. A free incidence or scalar table is insufficient.

five-cap-cover-exclusion.relation_to_goal: Together with the six-cap case and accepted fact `9b0c3eb7dcfba2c2`, this proves the locked theorem. The five-cap case has only \(T/9\) total multiplicity surplus and should be the sharper global cover branch.
five-cap-cover-exclusion.statement:
Assume the locked problem. Prove that five closed halfspaces \(H_1,\ldots,H_5\) covering \(S\) cannot all satisfy
\[
\mathcal H_2(S\cap H_j)<\frac{2T}{9}.
\]
Use the actual planar sections on all three convex slices and midpoint compatibility. A useful first reduction is to take a minimal cover, apply planar Helly to the induced cover of each \(A_i\), and retain the exact total overlap budget
\[
\sum_{j=1}^5\mathcal H_2(S\cap H_j)-T<\frac{T}{9}.
\]
five-cap-cover-exclusion.success_criterion: Success is a complete cover contradiction with all empty/full/horizontal section cases, or an exact compatible rational polygonal triple and five explicit three-dimensional halfspaces forming a strict low-mass cover, which would disprove the locked theorem. An abstract incidence table without realizable halfspaces does not count.

five-cap-high-m-branch.relation_to_goal: This closes the only high-\(M\) five-cap incidence type. Together with the low-\(M\) branch, the accepted six-cap shifted reversal, and `9b0c3eb7dcfba2c2`, it proves the locked theorem.
five-cap-high-m-branch.statement:
In the five-cap normal form of accepted fact `a6fbd3f54d7ec4c7`, assume
\[
\frac{4T}{9}\le M:=|A_2|<\frac T2.
\]
Retain the first positive Farkas plane-cover identity for rows \(1,2,3\) and the second identity formed by one shared row \(r\in\{1,2,3\}\) with rows \(4,5\). Prove that the exact global cover multiplicity surplus is at least \(T/9\), contradicting the strict five-cap budget.
five-cap-high-m-branch.success_criterion: Success requires a complete surplus allocation using both actual affine plane-cover identities, the shared row, all five height slopes, midpoint compatibility, and private witnesses, including equality at \(M=4T/9\); or an exact rational realization of the full normal form violating the bound. A free two-hypergraph or scalar mass table is insufficient.

five-cap-low-m-branch.relation_to_goal: Accepted fact `a6fbd3f54d7ec4c7` proves that any realization in this range automatically extends to a strict five-halfspace cover by two lifted bisecting caps of \(A_2\). Hence exclusion closes the low-\(M\) five-cap branch, while an exact realization disproves the locked theorem.
five-cap-low-m-branch.statement:
In the five-cap normal form of accepted fact `a6fbd3f54d7ec4c7`, assume
\[
\frac T3<M:=|A_2|<\frac{4T}{9}.
\]
Prove that no compatible convex bodies, nonparallel affine functions \(f_1+f_2+f_3=-1\), and height slopes with \(\sum_js_j>1\) can make all three actual row masses
\[
|A_0\cap\{f_j-s_j\le0\}|
+|A_1\cap\{f_j\le0\}|
+|A_2\cap\{f_j+s_j\le0\}|
\]
strictly smaller than \(2T/9\).
five-cap-low-m-branch.success_criterion: Success is a complete actual-body contradiction retaining the same-index midpoint graphs and height-shift defects, or exact rational polygons, rows, and slopes satisfying every strict inequality and compatibility, followed by the explicit two-cap lift from the accepted normal form. Scalar cap tables do not count.

five-cap-low-m-chain-rigidity.relation_to_goal: The accepted low-\(M\) defect ledger gives the strict reverse inequality for every five-cap realization. Therefore this simultaneous-chain rigidity closes the entire low-\(M\) five-cap branch; a rational violation extends to a literal five-halfspace disproof by `a6fbd3f54d7ec4c7`.
five-cap-low-m-chain-rigidity.statement:
Under the complete low-\(M\) normal form and notation of accepted facts `a6fbd3f54d7ec4c7` and `3081dc9f6b1f023f`, prove
\[
\left(\sum_jb_j-k\right)+\frac{\mathcal Q}{M}
+\frac1M\sum_j\eta_j+
\left(1-\frac mM\right)\sum_jy_j
\ge M-\frac T3.
\]
The proof must use that all three \(E_j\) are midpoint pullbacks of one affine triple and that the same actual lower/upper cap families cover them.
five-cap-low-m-chain-rigidity.success_criterion: Success is a complete stability or transport proof coupling the four actual defects at the common affine triple, or an exact rational compatible realization violating the bound and all original strict row inequalities. Marginal, Venn-cell, or independently optimized row estimates do not count.

five-cap-low-m-complement-bm-gate.relation_to_goal: This abstracts the exact mechanism that excluded the full asymmetric fixed-polygon family in round 106. It is a stronger necessary test than a scalar cap table whenever one first row is negative on the whole midpoint body. Applied before clipping searches, it removes every area triple violating the reverse gate from that geometric five-cap branch. It does not by itself cover normal forms for which no row has the stated midpoint sign.
five-cap-low-m-complement-bm-gate.statement:
Let \(A_0,A_1,A_2\subset\mathbb R^2\) be compact two-dimensional convex polygons satisfying
\[
\frac{A_0+A_2}{2}\subseteq A_1.
\]
Put
\[
m=|A_0|,\qquad k=|A_1|,\qquad M=|A_2|,
\qquad T=m+k+M,\qquad q=\frac{2T}{9},
\]
with
\[
m<M,\qquad \frac T3<M<\frac{4T}{9}.
\]
Let \(\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\lambda_3\) be nonconstant affine functions with pairwise nonparallel linear parts and
\[
\lambda_1+\lambda_2+\lambda_3=1.
\]
Let \(c\) be the centroid of \(A_1\), and assume
\[
\lambda_1<0\quad\text{on }\frac{A_0+A_2}{2},
\qquad \lambda_1(c)<1.
\]
For arbitrary real \(s_2,s_3\), define, for \(j=2,3\),
\[
x_j=|A_0\cap\{\lambda_j\ge-s_j\}|,\qquad
b_j=|A_1\cap\{\lambda_j\ge0\}|,\qquad
y_j=|A_2\cap\{\lambda_j\ge s_j\}|.
\]
Put
\[
D=q-\frac{4k}{9}=\frac{2(m+M-k)}9,
\]
and assume
\[
0<D<m.
\]
Prove that the two strict row inequalities
\[
x_j+b_j+y_j<q\qquad(j=2,3)
\]
imply the strict complement Brunn-Minkowski gate
\[
\frac{\left(\sqrt{m-D}+\sqrt M\right)^2}{4}<q.
\]
Consequently, the reverse weak inequality excludes both residual rows simultaneously.
five-cap-low-m-complement-bm-gate.status_reason: Accepted fact `893ee8e32fab035c` proves the registered complement Brunn-Minkowski gate, including strict boundary handling and the exact normalized area region excluded by its reverse weak inequality. This closes `five-cap-low-m-complement-bm-gate`. The result filters the low-\(M\) five-cap branch whenever one row has the stated midpoint sign; it does not close frames for which no row is strictly negative on the midpoint body.
five-cap-low-m-complement-bm-gate.success_criterion: A proof must identify the residual row whose middle cap strictly contains the centroid, treat arbitrary shifts and endpoint clips, prove the complementary midpoint inclusion in the other residual middle cap, justify the deletion-allocation inequality and all strict signs, and handle cutting-line boundaries. It should also state exactly which scalar area region the reverse gate excludes. A fixed-polygon calculation alone is insufficient.

five-cap-low-m-defect-ledger.relation_to_goal: This isolates four actual nonnegative defects that must all be simultaneously small and closes an explicit algebraic area subregion. Reversing the strict defect budget closes the low-\(M\) five-cap branch.
five-cap-low-m-defect-ledger.statement:
In the low-\(M\) five-cap normal form of accepted fact `a6fbd3f54d7ec4c7`, use \(m=|A_0|\), \(k=|A_1|\), \(M=|A_2|\), \(g=M-T/3\), row cap areas \(x_j,b_j,y_j\), closed midpoint graph volumes \(d_j\), midpoint multiplicity excess \(\mathcal Q\), and same-index indicator-cover slacks
\[
\eta_j=Mx_j+my_j-d_j.
\]
Prove the exact decomposition
\[
\delta_j=\frac{\eta_j}{M}+\left(1-\frac mM\right)y_j
\]
and hence every strict realization satisfies
\[
\left(\sum_jb_j-k\right)+\frac{\mathcal Q}{M}
+\frac1M\sum_j\eta_j+
\left(1-\frac mM\right)\sum_jy_j<g.
\]
Also prove the centroid/complement necessary condition
\[
\left(\sqrt{m-\frac{2(m+M-k)}9}+\sqrt M\right)^2<\frac{20k}{9}.
\]
five-cap-low-m-defect-ledger.status_reason: Accepted fact `3081dc9f6b1f023f` proves the exact four-defect decomposition, strict budget, and centroid/complement algebraic exclusion.
five-cap-low-m-defect-ledger.success_criterion: Success requires the exact midpoint-cylinder inclusion, decomposition of every height-shift defect, multiplicity identity, all constants, and the centroid/complement Brunn-Minkowski minimization with strict boundary cases. Scalar cap tables are insufficient.

five-cap-low-m-fixed-chain-calibration.relation_to_goal: The low-\(M\) defect ledger has lower and upper defect \(3/25\) for this calibration, while \(M-T/3=37/300\). The proposed common-arrangement bound supplies exactly the missing \(1/300\), contradicting the strict five-cap budget. It tests simultaneous placement of the common midpoint images, which all independent chain Brunn-Minkowski inequalities fail to control. An exact rational violation would be the first actual-body survivor of this fixed three-chain stress model.
five-cap-low-m-fixed-chain-calibration.statement:
In an affine plane with nonconstant \(\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\lambda_3\) satisfying
\[
\lambda_1+\lambda_2+\lambda_3=1,
\]
let \(A_0,A_1,A_2\) be compact two-dimensional convex polygons with
\[
|A_0|=\frac14,\qquad |A_1|=1,\qquad |A_2|=\frac{81}{100},
\qquad \frac{A_0+A_2}{2}\subseteq A_1.
\]
Let \(s_1,s_2,s_3\in\mathbb R\) satisfy
\[
s_1+s_2+s_3>1,
\]
and define
\[
C_{0j}=A_0\cap\{\lambda_j\ge-s_j\},\qquad
C_{2j}=A_2\cap\{\lambda_j\ge s_j\}.
\]
For \(I\subseteq\{1,2,3\}\), let \(P_I\) be the exact cell of points
belonging to \(C_{0j}\) exactly for \(j\in I\). Require the exact positive
lower-label masses
\[
|P_{\{1\}}|=\frac9{100},\qquad
|P_{\{2\}}|=\frac1{25},\qquad
|P_{\{1,3\}}|=\frac3{500},\qquad
|P_{\{2,3\}}|=\frac{57}{500},
\]
with every other label cell null. Require
\[
|C_{21}|=|C_{22}|=|C_{23}|=0,
\]
so the common upper-uncovered convex set is all of \(A_2\).
For
\[
B_j=A_1\cap\{\lambda_j\ge0\},\qquad b_j=|B_j|,
\]
assume the three strict row capacities
\[
b_1+\frac{12}{125}<\frac{103}{225},\qquad
b_2+\frac{77}{500}<\frac{103}{225},\qquad
b_3+\frac3{25}<\frac{103}{225}.
\]
Prove the quantitative middle-multiplicity bound
\[
\sum_{j=1}^3b_j-1\ge\frac1{300},
\]
or give exact rational polygons and affine functions satisfying every displayed condition and the strict reverse inequality.
five-cap-low-m-fixed-chain-calibration.status_reason: Accepted fact `6fd8449bc38cf0bc` proves that the complete fixed calibration has no realization: its prescribed lower-cell support already contradicts the affine identity and convex two-dimensional lower body. Therefore the requested universal middle-surplus conclusion for this exact calibration is vacuous. This closes only `five-cap-low-m-fixed-chain-calibration`; it does not establish the needed quantitative midpoint bound for any realizable lower-cell table or the locked theorem.
five-cap-low-m-fixed-chain-calibration.success_criterion: A proof must use one common affine triple, convexity of all three bodies, and the simultaneous midpoint inclusions from every nonempty lower label into middle labels contained in it. Marginal cell areas or separate Brunn-Minkowski bounds are insufficient. A refutation must give rational vertices, affine functions, exact cell tables, compatibility, and all three strict row capacities.

fixed-allocation-centroid-region-reducti.relation_to_goal:
This isolates the remaining global geometry after the exact cap-profile
inversion: there is always a nonempty range of fixed mass allocations for
which the two component regions are separately nonempty and contain the two
natural centroids. The locked theorem would follow from proving that one
middle region intersects its paired endpoint region. This is a
fixed-allocation, same-index formulation and does not use the false additive
measure or aggregate-average shortcuts.
fixed-allocation-centroid-region-reducti.statement:
Assume the locked problem and the strict area-triangle inequalities, put
\[
 t=\frac{2T}{9},\qquad m=\min(a_0,a_2),
\]
and use the directional quantiles of accepted fact
`17ca54faa05ad878`. For \(0\le a\le a_1\), define the ordinary middle
depth region
\[
 \mathcal M(a)=
 A_1\cap\bigcap_{q\in\mathbb S^1}
 \{z:q\cdot z\ge D_{1,q}(a)\},
\]
using \(\mathcal M(0)=A_1\). For \(0\le b\le m\), define
\[
 \mathcal E(b)=
 \bigcap_{\substack{q\in\mathbb S^1\\0\le u\le b}}
 \left\{z:
 2q\cdot z\ge Q_{0,q}(u)+Q_{2,q}(b-u)
 \right\},
\]
using \(\mathcal E(0)=\mathbb R^2\).

Prove that the allocation interval
\[
 J=
 \left[
 \max\left\{0,t-\frac{4m}{9}\right\},
 \min\left\{t,\frac{4a_1}{9}\right\}
 \right]
\]
is nonempty. For every \(a\in J\), prove
\[
 g_1\in\mathcal M(a),\qquad
 \frac{g_0+g_2}{2}\in\mathcal E(t-a),
\]
and prove that \(\mathcal M(a)\) and \(\mathcal E(t-a)\) are closed convex
regions with the correct nesting in \(a\). Finally prove the exact
reduction
\[
 \mathcal M(a)\cap\mathcal E(t-a)\ne\varnothing
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 D_t\ne\varnothing,
\]
where \(D_t\) is the true middle depth region of accepted fact
`d2d117bcc58a1ba0`.
fixed-allocation-centroid-region-reducti.status_reason:
Accepted fact `66f17f4981c30108` proves the full registered reduction:
the allocation interval has positive length, both paired regions are closed
and convex with the stated opposite nesting, the two natural centroids give
their separate nonemptiness, every endpoint convention is handled, and any
paired intersection lies in the true depth region.
fixed-allocation-centroid-region-reducti.success_criterion:
Success requires a complete proof from accepted quantile/profile facts and
the planar \(4/9\) centroid-cap bound, including zero demand, capacity
endpoints, closedness, convexity, nesting, and the exact implication to
\(D_t\). It must not assert that the two regions intersect. If any stated
containment or nesting direction is false, give an exact compatible
polygonal counterexample and the corrected reduction.

fixed-allocation-paired-intersection.relation_to_goal:
Accepted fact `66f17f4981c30108` proves that any such intersection lies
in the true middle depth region at \(2T/9\), so this statement would
produce the required point throughout the remaining strict area region.
It is a global fixed-allocation architecture and is stronger than merely
showing both component regions are separately nonempty.
fixed-allocation-paired-intersection.statement:
Assume the locked problem and the strict area-triangle region. Put
\(t=2T/9\), and let \(J\), \(\mathcal M(a)\), and
\(\mathcal E(t-a)\) be the exact closed convex regions of accepted fact
`66f17f4981c30108`.

Prove
\[
 \exists a\in J:\qquad
 \mathcal M(a)\cap\mathcal E(t-a)\ne\varnothing.
\]
The proof should use compatibility, the opposite nesting of the two

general-upper-strip-localization-theorem.relation_to_goal:
The same threshold is currently certified only in restricted or
minimal-middle settings.  A general proof removes the full normalized upper
strip \(s\ge1+r/2\) for arbitrary compatible shapes and supplies a genuinely
global localization result rather than another fixed-family calculation.
general-upper-strip-localization-theorem.statement:
Let \(A_0,A_1,A_2\subset\mathbb R^2\) be arbitrary compact
two-dimensional convex bodies satisfying
\[
\frac{A_0+A_2}{2}\subseteq A_1.
\]
Write \(M=\max\{|A_0|,|A_2|\}\), \(m=\min\{|A_0|,|A_2|\}\),
\(k=|A_1|\), and \(T=M+m+k\).  Prove or refute
\[
k\ge M+\frac m2
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\max_{y\in S}h_S(y)\ge\frac{2T}{9}.
\]
The proof must be unconditional under the locked hypotheses.  If it uses a
three-cap certificate and a balanced pancake decomposition, it must justify
the certificate orientation, the barycentric measure identity, terminal
carrier structure, horizontal carriers at all three heights, zero-mass
branches, and every strict-to-nonstrict limit.
general-upper-strip-localization-theorem.status_reason: Accepted fact `776f5d2aa96794fd` proves the registered arbitrary-body upper-strip localization theorem, including equality and the limiting passage from polytopes.
general-upper-strip-localization-theorem.success_criterion:
Give a complete proof from accepted certificate facts and a rigorously
constructed two-balanced convex-carrier mixture, followed by a pointwise leaf
ledger whose expectation contradicts a counterexample when
\(k\ge M+m/2\).  The proof must repair the horizontal covered-endpoint case,

global-3d-centerpoint-rounding.statement: Let \(\mu=\mathcal H_2|_S\). Prove the claim, prove a weaker sufficient version that still implies the locked target, or give an exact compatible counterexample to the rounding claim.
global-3d-centerpoint-rounding.status_reason: Accepted facts `1cbbb61f95f700c2` and `4a62bbfa8766d234` respectively refute multiplicative depth preservation and show that the threshold-only assignment is logically equivalent to the locked theorem. The ordinary \(T/4\) depth region can be nonempty and entirely disjoint from all supported planes. Thus ordinary centerpoint existence and convexity do not yield an independent rounding bridge.
global-3d-centerpoint-rounding.success_criterion: A complete proof with all boundary and support cases, or an exact compatible rational-polytope example with a rigorously identified \(T/4\)-deep point for which the proposed rounding conclusion fails. A merely heuristic projection argument is not sufficient.

global-all-slice-deformation.relation_to_goal:
Accepted theorem `96f5513b8ab88a8f` gives \(\Psi(0)\ge0\) for the minimal
compatible middle slice \(B\). Continuity plus the stated zero-barrier
property prevents \(\Psi\) from crossing from nonnegative to negative as
the middle slice expands to \(A_1\). Hence \(\Psi(1)\ge0\), which is exactly
the locked conclusion. Unlike the false middle-only cap-shaving route, the
maximum defining \(\Psi\) ranges over all three supported slices.
global-all-slice-deformation.statement:
Fix compatible endpoint bodies and put
\[
B=\frac{A_0+A_2}{2},\qquad
L_s=(1-s)B+sA_1\quad(0\le s\le1).
\]
Let
\[
S_s=(\{0\}\times A_0)\cup(\{1\}\times L_s)\cup(\{2\}\times A_2),
\]
\[
\Psi(s)=\max_{y\in S_s}h_{S_s}(y)
-\frac{2(|A_0|+|L_s|+|A_2|)}9.
\]
Prove the zero-barrier property: if \(\Psi(s)\ge0\) for \(0\le s\le s_0\)
and \(\Psi(s_0)=0\), then
\[
\liminf_{h\downarrow0}
\frac{\Psi(s_0+h)-\Psi(s_0)}h\ge0.
\]
It is enough to prove any stronger inclusion-monotonicity or concavity
statement that rigorously implies \(\Psi(s)\ge0\) on \([0,1]\) from
\(\Psi(0)\ge0\).
global-all-slice-deformation.status_reason: Accepted fact `a49f2b26cc468e4c` supplies continuity and active-set derivative bookkeeping, but the registered derivative condition does not prevent finite right-hand crossing. The sharper parent target `global-minkowski-first-zero` remains open and is split into outer-middle activation and an exact finite-increment viability condition.

global-bonus-grunbaum-reduction.statement:

\[
G_1^u(\langle u,z\rangle)
+(G_0^u\square G_2^u)(2\langle u,z\rangle)
\ge
\frac{4s}{9}+\frac{2(a_0+a_2-s)}9
=\frac{2(a_0+a_2+s)}9.
\]
Handle the complementary area region by accepted fact `2f9be517307232c7`, audit the horizontal middle halfspaces, and formulate the exact max-min functional whose lower bound is now the decisive remaining theorem.

global-depth-profile-normal-form.relation_to_goal: This rewrites the original three-dimensional minimization as a single family of one-dimensional cap profiles. It quantifies out both endpoint slices and exposes the endpoint contribution to the middle slice as one infimal convolution, replacing the legacy branch-specific notation.
global-depth-profile-normal-form.statement:
For \(u\in\mathbb S^1\), define
\[
G_i^u(c):=\left|A_i\cap\{w:\langle u,w\rangle\le c\}\right|.
\]
Prove:

1. For \(z\in A_0\) and \(z\in A_2\), the three-slice depth equals the ordinary planar halfspace depth in that endpoint body.
2. For \(z\in A_1\), apart from the two slice-parallel halfspaces already present in accepted fact `400272f6de6c67bb`,
\[
h_S((1,z))
=\inf_{u\in\mathbb S^1}
\left[
G_1^u(\langle u,z\rangle)
+\inf_{c_0+c_2=2\langle u,z\rangle}
\bigl(G_0^u(c_0)+G_2^u(c_2)\bigr)
\right].
\]
State the exact role of the two horizontal halfspaces and show that they cannot bind at level \(2T/9\) in the balanced region \(a_i<T/2\).
global-depth-profile-normal-form.status_reason:

global-indexed-product-cover.relation_to_goal:
Accepted fact `d2d117bcc58a1ba0` turns failure of the middle

therefore contradicts that certificate. Together with the accepted outer
area branches, it proves the locked theorem. This formulation precedes both

global-indexed-product-cover.statement:
Assume the locked compatibility condition and the full strict residual area
strip. Let affine functions \(f_1,f_2,f_3:\mathbb R^2\to\mathbb R\) and
numbers \(s_1,s_2,s_3\) satisfy
\[
f_1+f_2+f_3=-1.
\]
For \(i=1,2,3\), define
\[
B_i=A_1\cap\{f_i\le0\},\quad
C_{0i}=A_0\cap\{f_i-s_i\le0\},\quad
C_{2i}=A_2\cap\{f_i+s_i\le0\}.
\]
Prove the global row inequality
\[
\max_{1\le i\le3}
\bigl(|B_i|+|C_{0i}|+|C_{2i}|\bigr)
\ge\frac{2T}{9}.
\]
The proof must retain the same-index pullback sets
\[
E_i=\left\{(x_0,x_2)\in A_0\times A_2:
f_i\!\left(\frac{x_0+x_2}{2}\right)<0\right\}
\]
and the inclusions
\[
E_i\subseteq
(C_{0i}\times A_2)\cup(A_0\times C_{2i}),
\qquad
A_0\times A_2=\bigcup_iE_i,
\]
rather than replacing them only by separate scalar union bounds.
global-indexed-product-cover.success_criterion:

using a joint geometric or nonlinear covering invariant. If false, give an

global-middle-depth-region-helly.relation_to_goal: This identifies the legacy three-function case tree as one global Helly failure certificate for a convex middle depth region. It is the finite dual object required by a global proof.

\]

global-minkowski-first-zero.relation_to_goal: Accepted fact `96f5513b8ab88a8f` gives \(\Psi(0)\ge0\), and `a49f2b26cc468e4c` gives continuity and the exact active-set derivative bookkeeping. It is a global deformation route independent of completing the five- and six-cap case ledgers.
global-minkowski-first-zero.statement:
Fix \(A_0,A_2\), put \(B=(A_0+A_2)/2\), and interpolate the middle slice by
\[
L_s=(1-s)B+sA_1,\qquad 0\le s\le1.
\]
Use the notation \(M(s),a(s),q(s)\), and \(\Psi(s)\) of accepted fact `a49f2b26cc468e4c`. Prove the following first-zero barrier: whenever \(\Psi(s_0)=0\), there is \(\varepsilon>0\) such that
\[
\Psi(s)\ge0\qquad(s_0\le s\le \min\{1,s_0+\varepsilon\}).
\]
The proof must allow the maximizing middle point and all active halfspaces to switch. If the barrier is false, give an exact compatible polygonal interpolation and an exact local violation.

A mere nonnegative first derivative at the zero is insufficient. Alternatively, an exact rational polygonal local violation closes this proposed architecture as false.

global-paired-depth-regions.relation_to_goal:
If \(z=(x_0+x_2)/2\), then for every direction \(q\) and every allocation
\(c_0+c_2=2q\cdot z\), either \(c_0\ge q\cdot x_0\) or
\(c_2\ge q\cdot x_2\). Hence the endpoint contribution is at least
\(\min\{d_{A_0}(x_0),d_{A_2}(x_2)\}\ge u\), while the middle contribution is
at least \(d_{A_1}(z)\ge t-u\). The horizontal halfspaces are harmless in
the strict residual strip. Thus the stated intersection gives a supported
point of depth at least \(t\) without a common directionwise allocation,
contact optimization, or auxiliary coupling.
global-paired-depth-regions.statement:
Let \(A_0,A_1,A_2\) satisfy the locked problem and the full strict residual
area strip of accepted fact `15bb2c1680a0254e`. Put
\[
t=\frac{2T}{9},\qquad m=\min\{a_0,a_2\},
\]
and, for \(0\le u\le a_i\), let
\[
D_i(u)=\{x\in A_i:d_{A_i}(x)\ge u\}.
\]
Prove that there exist
\[
t-\frac{4a_1}{9}\le u\le\frac{4m}{9},
\qquad x_0\in D_0(u),\qquad x_2\in D_2(u)
\]
such that
\[
\frac{x_0+x_2}{2}\in D_1(t-u).
\]
The endpoint \(u=t-4a_1/9\), all closed depth-region conventions, and both
orders of \(a_0,a_2\) must be included.

global-pairwise-row-ledger.statement:
Assume the locked compatibility condition and let affine functions
\(f_1,f_2,f_3:\mathbb R^2\to\mathbb R\) and numbers \(s_1,s_2,s_3\)
satisfy \(f_1+f_2+f_3=-1\). Define

\]
\[

Then determine the strongest consequence of these three pairwise inequalities,
