global-profile-minorant-measure.relation_to_goal:
The planar centerpoint theorem applied to \(\nu\) gives a point \(z\in A_1\)
whose every halfplane has \(\nu\)-mass at least \(\nu(A_1)/3\ge2T/9\).
The displayed domination then gives middle-slice mixed-integer depth at least
\(2T/9\), so this lemma proves the locked theorem after the accepted
large-slice reduction. It strictly extends the accepted hybrid midpoint
measure, whose total mass is only \(a_1+\min(a_0,a_2)\).
global-profile-minorant-measure.statement:
Assume the locked problem and the strict area-triangle region
\[
a_i<a_j+a_k\qquad(\{i,j,k\}=\{0,1,2\}).
\]
For \(q\in\mathbb S^1\), write
\[
F_{i,q}(r)=|A_i\cap\{w:q\cdot w\le r\}|
\]
and
\[
\Phi_q(r)=F_{1,q}(r)+
\inf_{\lambda\in\mathbb R}
\bigl(F_{0,q}(r+\lambda)+F_{2,q}(r-\lambda)\bigr).
\]
Prove that there is a finite Borel measure \(\nu\), supported on \(A_1\),
such that
\[
\nu(A_1)\ge\frac{2T}{3}
\]
and, simultaneously for every \(q\in\mathbb S^1\) and \(r\in\mathbb R\),
\[
\nu(\{w:q\cdot w\le r\})\le\Phi_q(r).
\]
global-profile-minorant-measure.status_reason:
Accepted fact `cc15b3162b7f66ee` gives an exact compatible strict-area
triangle example for which one closed-halfplane profile constraint forces
every supported minorant measure to have mass at most \(5/4\), while the
registered statement requires mass at least \(3/2\). Thus the proposed
single additive measure does not exist universally. This refutes only the
auxiliary architecture, not the locked theorem.
global-profile-minorant-measure.success_criterion:
Success is either a complete construction and proof of the single measure
\(\nu\), including all directions and boundary halfplanes, or an exact finite
dual obstruction showing that such a measure need not exist for a compatible
triple. A dual obstruction must rule out every Borel measure satisfying the
displayed halfplane inequalities, not merely the known midpoint-pushforward
candidate.

global-profile-superlinearity.relation_to_goal: Superadditivity makes \(R_t\) a lower-support function and immediately implies every positive-spanning Farkas inequality in accepted fact `9328166a552ec875`; that fact and `d2d117bcc58a1ba0` then give a middle-slice point of depth at least \(2T/9\). An exact compatible counterexample would rule out this global architecture without bearing against the locked theorem unless it also empties the true depth region.
global-profile-superlinearity.statement:
Let \(t=2T/9\), let \(\rho_q(t)\) be the exact directional threshold from accepted facts `17ca54faa05ad878`, `65512ded3a06d971`, and `d2d117bcc58a1ba0`, and extend it homogeneously by
\[
R_t(0)=0,\qquad R_t(p)=\|p\|\rho_{p/\|p\|}(t)\quad(p\ne0).
\]
Determine whether compatibility \((A_0+A_2)/2\subseteq A_1\), together with the residual area hypotheses forced by a global counterexample, implies
\[
R_t(p)+R_t(r)\le R_t(p+r)\qquad(p,r\in\mathbb R^2).
\]
If full superadditivity is false, determine whether the exact weaker positive-spanning inequality
\[
\sum_{i=1}^3 R_t(p_i)\le0
\quad\text{whenever }p_1+p_2+p_3=0
\]
still follows from the compatible cap profiles. An abstract continuous model is insufficient: any obstruction must be an exact compatible convex-body instance.
global-profile-superlinearity.status_reason: Accepted fact `271d583278d20859` gives an exact compatible rational-triangle counterexample to homogeneous threshold superadditivity, while proving that the same instance still satisfies every positive-spanning inequality because its true depth region is nonempty. This meets the negative success criterion and leaves only the weaker Farkas balance viable.
global-profile-superlinearity.success_criterion: Success is either a complete proof of the stated superadditivity or positive-spanning inequality for all compatible triples in the residual regime, including zero demands and antipodal/collinear limits, or an exact rational compatible polygonal counterexample with directly verified cap quantiles and a strict violated inequality. Floating-point evidence alone is insufficient.

global-six-sector-helly-capture.relation_to_goal: Accepted fact `7694bc07b24d1290` proves that every such fan has at most one selected row at or below \(t\). Therefore the requested two-row capture contradicts \(D_t=\varnothing\) and proves the existence of a middle-slice witness. This is weaker than requiring one fan center to be deep in every direction and is not implied by continuity of the directional profile alone.
global-six-sector-helly-capture.statement:
Let
\[
t=\frac{2T}{9}
\]
and, for \(z\in A_1\) and \(u\in\mathbb S^1\), define the exact row mass
\[
\Psi(z,u)=
F_{1,u}(u\cdot z)+
\min_{c_0+c_2=2u\cdot z}
\bigl(F_{0,u}(c_0)+F_{2,u}(c_2)\bigr).
\]
Assume the locked compatibility condition and the full strict residual area strip. Prove that if the exact middle depth region \(D_t\) is empty, then there is an oriented concurrent fan \((z;q_1,q_2,q_3)\) satisfying all equal-six-sector and alternating-orientation conclusions of accepted fact `7694bc07b24d1290`, together with distinct \(i,j\) such that
\[
\Psi(z,q_i)\le t,\qquad
\Psi(z,q_j)\le t.
\]
global-six-sector-helly-capture.success_criterion: Success is a complete topological or geometric proof that an empty exact profile intersection forces two selected low rows in one equal-six-sector fan. It must use actual compatible convex bodies and the exact row profile. An abstract continuous-circle model is only an obstacle. An exact compatible polygonal counterexample to the stated capture implication is also decisive for this architecture.

global-six-sector-row-interpolation.relation_to_goal: If the interpolation inequality holds, accepted fact `7694bc07b24d1290` gives \(R_{(2)}>2T/9\), so the fan center is a full-depth witness and the locked theorem follows. An exact counterexample would show that the six-sector ledger alone is a finite-direction phenomenon and prevent further unsupported angular interpolation.
global-six-sector-row-interpolation.statement:
Use the notation and hypotheses of accepted fact `7694bc07b24d1290`. For its equal-six-sector center \(z\), let
\[
R_i=\Psi(z,q_i),
\qquad
R_{(1)}\le R_{(2)}\le R_{(3)}.
\]
Determine whether the all-direction interpolation inequality
\[
\inf_{u\in\mathbb S^1}\Psi(z,u)\ge R_{(2)}
\]
holds for every compatible triple in the strict residual strip. If it is false, give exact compatible rational polygons, an exact equal-six-sector fan, and one exact direction \(u\) for which
\[
\Psi(z,u)<R_{(2)}.
\]
global-six-sector-row-interpolation.status_reason:
Accepted fact `d5ee798890c7e1b4` gives exact compatible rational polygons in
the strict residual strip for which all three rows selected by an equal-six-
sector fan equal \(11/6\), while an unselected opposite direction has row
\(3/2\).  Hence the proposed interpolation from the selected fan rows to all
directions is false.  The example still satisfies the locked theorem, so this
closes only the interpolation subgoal.
global-six-sector-row-interpolation.success_criterion: Success is a complete proof of the all-direction inequality, including directions between fan normals and all endpoint allocation regimes, or an exact rational counterexample verified directly from cap areas. Numerical sampling alone is insufficient, but it may be used to locate an exact example.

global-six-sector-starvation.relation_to_goal: This generalizes the triangle-only centroid starvation ledger `6eb36ee892a70d82` to every convex middle slice using one global six-sector partition. In the strict residual area strip the displayed bound should imply that at most one of the three balanced fan directions can miss the \(2T/9\) row target. It does not by itself control directions between the fan lines; the exact remaining extension must be identified rather than assumed.
global-six-sector-starvation.statement:
Let \(A_1\) be an arbitrary planar convex body of area \(a_1\). Choose three concurrent lines that divide \(A_1\) into six cyclic sectors of equal area \(a_1/6\), and orient their normals \(q_1,q_2,q_3\) so that the three lower halfplanes cover the plane and each pair of upper halfplanes cuts out one alternating sector. Let \(z\) be the concurrency point and define
\[
J_i=\inf_{c_{0i}+c_{2i}=2q_i\cdot z}
\left(F_{0,q_i}(c_{0i})+F_{2,q_i}(c_{2i})\right).
\]
Prove the arbitrary-body pairwise ledger
\[
J_i+J_j\ge
\min\left\{\min(a_0,a_2),\ a_0+a_2-\frac{2a_1}{3}\right\}
\qquad(i\ne j),
\]
and determine the strongest exact consequence for the three row masses \(a_1/2+J_i\) at target \(2T/9\). State precisely what remains before the concurrency point can be a full-depth witness in every direction.
global-six-sector-starvation.status_reason: Accepted fact `7694bc07b24d1290` meets the success criterion. It constructs the equal-area concurrent six-sector fan for every middle convex body, proves the exact pairwise endpoint ledger, and shows that at most one of the three selected fan rows can be at or below the target throughout the strict residual strip. It also states the remaining all-direction gap explicitly.
global-six-sector-starvation.success_criterion: Success is a complete proof of existence and orientation of the six-sector partition, the pairwise endpoint Brunn--Minkowski ledger with all boundary cases, the residual-area comparison with \(2T/9\), and an explicit statement of the remaining all-direction gap. A cited equipartition theorem must be quoted exactly from a primary source and checked for absolutely continuous area measure on a convex body.

global-small-endpoint-ratio-exclusion.relation_to_goal:
This removes an entire neighborhood of the degenerate endpoint-ratio
boundary from the full locked problem, not merely from the triangular
matrix model.  It converts the accepted sequential pinch contradiction
into a uniform global exclusion and confines any counterexample to a
compact area-ratio range bounded away from both zero and the accepted
upper cutoff.
global-small-endpoint-ratio-exclusion.statement:
Prove that there exists \(r_0>0\) such that every compatible three-slice
instance in the locked problem with
\[
\frac{\min\{|A_0|,|A_2|\}}{\max\{|A_0|,|A_2|\}}<r_0
\]
satisfies the \(2T/9\) centerpoint conclusion.  The slices are arbitrary
two-dimensional convex polytopes, not triangles.  Derive the uniform
constant by contradiction from the accepted residual strip and the
accepted arbitrary-body pinch compactification and moving-frame estimates.
global-small-endpoint-ratio-exclusion.status_reason:
Accepted fact `a1a5ff87332a439a` proves the registered shape-free uniform
exclusion: all compatible convex-polytopal instances with sufficiently
small positive endpoint-area ratio satisfy the locked \(2T/9\) conclusion.
global-small-endpoint-ratio-exclusion.success_criterion:
A complete quantifier argument showing that a failure for arbitrarily
small positive endpoint ratio would produce a normalized counterexample
sequence satisfying the hypotheses of the accepted moving-frame pinch
facts, whose two exact estimates on the same deficit contradict one
another.

global-support-deficit-closing.relation_to_goal: The closing inequality is a genuinely global coupling among the three Helly directions: an adversary cannot independently suppress all endpoint bonuses. It is the main new invariant suggested by the reset.
global-support-deficit-closing.statement:
For \(u\in\mathbb S^1\), put
\[
m_i(u):=\min_{x\in A_i}\langle u,x\rangle,\qquad
\gamma_i^u(r):=
\left|A_i\cap\{\langle u,x\rangle\le m_i(u)+r\}\right|,
\]
where \(\gamma_i^u(r)=0\) for \(r\le0\). For \(z\in A_1\), define
\[
d_u(z):=2\langle u,z\rangle-m_0(u)-m_2(u).
\]

Prove that the endpoint bonus in the middle depth profile is
\[
(\gamma_0^u\square\gamma_2^u)(d_u(z)).
\]
If \(u_1,u_2,u_3\) have positive weights \(\nu_i\) with
\(\sum_i\nu_i u_i=0\), prove the closing identity and inequality
\[
\sum_i\nu_i d_{u_i}(z)
=\sum_i\nu_i h_{-(A_0+A_2)}(u_i)\ge0.
\]
Determine the exact equality and zero-bonus cases for two-dimensional endpoint bodies.
global-support-deficit-closing.status_reason:
Accepted fact `508b5d8f1a3d6fca` proves the exact infimal-convolution
formula, the positively weighted support-deficit closing identity, its
equality characterization, and the strict conclusion that at least one bonus
is positive for three positively spanning directions.
global-support-deficit-closing.success_criterion: Success is the exact translated infimal-convolution identity, support-function proof, and full equality/zero analysis. Merely invoking subadditivity without matching the cap convention is insufficient.

global-three-direction-mixed-area.relation_to_goal: The displayed inequality is exactly the missing global Farkas balance in accepted fact `9328166a552ec875`. A mixed-area proof would aggregate all three directions before optimizing their individual caps and could replace the current cap-by-cap analysis. A rigorous obstruction showing that every single-body valuation loses the midpoint compatibility term would also sharply redirect the search.
global-three-direction-mixed-area.statement:
Let \(q_1,q_2,q_3\in\mathbb S^1\) be noncollinear and let \(\alpha_i>0\) satisfy \(\sum_i\alpha_iq_i=0\). For a planar convex body \(K\), thresholds \(c_i\), and caps \(K_i=K\cap\{q_i\cdot x\le c_i\}\), derive an exact translation-invariant mixed-area or boundary-valuation formula that controls
\[
\sum_i\alpha_i c_i
\]
by the three cap areas and their overlap geometry. Apply the formula simultaneously to the three compatible slices and the optimized thresholds defining \(\rho_{q_i}(2T/9)\). Determine whether it proves
\[
\sum_i\alpha_i\rho_{q_i}(2T/9)\le0.
\]
The task is to establish one concrete valuation identity or inequality, not to rename the existing row-surplus ledger.
global-three-direction-mixed-area.status_reason: Accepted fact `8ef24abd811bff34` meets the stated success criterion. It proves the exact positive-spanning triangle valuation identity, shows why intrinsic cap-intersection valuations cannot control the Farkas sum, and isolates opposite-state cross-slice transport as the first missing term. Its exact compatible homothetic example also rules out an unconditional profile-balance argument outside the residual area regime.
global-three-direction-mixed-area.success_criterion: Success is a proved valuation identity and a complete derivation of the positive-spanning threshold inequality for compatible bodies, or a proved exact obstruction to this valuation architecture together with the first missing cross-slice term. Any cited theorem must be stated exactly and checked against the cap orientation, normalization, and non-smooth polygonal case.

global-two-triangle-sharpness.relation_to_goal: This identifies the true tight boundary geometry and explains the factorization \(2/9=(4/9)(1/2)\). It supplies the equality-limit model that a global proof must reproduce and the correct location for a focused falsification audit.
global-two-triangle-sharpness.statement:
Let \(\Delta\subset\mathbb R^2\) be a triangle of area \(1\) containing \(0\), and for \(0<\varepsilon\le1\) put
\[
A_0=A_1=\Delta,\qquad A_2=\varepsilon\Delta.
\]
Prove compatibility and the exact upper bound
\[
\sup_{y\in S}h_S(y)\le \frac49+\varepsilon^2.
\]
Conclude
\[
\limsup_{\varepsilon\downarrow0}
\frac{\sup_{y\in S}h_S(y)}
{|A_0|+|A_1|+|A_2|}
\le\frac29,
\]
so the universal constant \(2/9\) cannot be improved. Include a direct proof that the maximum planar halfspace depth of a triangle is \(4/9\).
global-two-triangle-sharpness.status_reason:
Accepted fact `43e70f89f224c5d7` gives an admissible family
\(A_0=A_1=\Delta\), \(A_2=\varepsilon\Delta\) whose normalized maximum
depth tends to \(2/9\). Thus no larger universal constant is possible.
global-two-triangle-sharpness.success_criterion: Success is a compatible explicit family, a uniform depth upper bound on all three slices, and the exact limiting ratio. An argument only for centroids or only for endpoint slices is insufficient.

global-zero-surplus-label-rigidity.relation_to_goal: The low-\(M\) five-cap defect ledger in accepted fact `3081dc9f6b1f023f` shows that a hypothetical counterexample must make the middle-cover surplus, endpoint-cover surplus, same-index graph slack, and large-endpoint cap mass simultaneously small. This subgoal identifies the exact zero-defect geometry: the unique labels on \(A_0\), all midpoint translates, and \(A_1\) must collapse to one common row. A quantitative stability version of this collapse would give the missing lower bound in `five-cap-low-m-chain-rigidity`.
global-zero-surplus-label-rigidity.statement:
Let \(A_0,A_1,A_2\subset\mathbb R^2\) be nonempty two-dimensional compact convex bodies with
\[
\frac{A_0+A_2}{2}\subseteq A_1.
\]
Let \(f_1,f_2,f_3\) be nonconstant affine functions with pairwise nonparallel linear parts and \(f_1+f_2+f_3=-1\). Let \(s_1+s_2+s_3>1\), and put
\[
x_j=|A_0\cap\{f_j-s_j\le0\}|,\quad
b_j=|A_1\cap\{f_j\le0\}|,\quad
y_j=|A_2\cap\{f_j+s_j\le0\}|.
\]
Assume the exact zero-surplus identities
\[
\sum_jx_j=|A_0|,\qquad
\sum_jb_j=|A_1|,\qquad
\sum_jy_j=0.
\]
Prove that some \(r\in\{1,2,3\}\) satisfies
\[
|A_0\setminus\{f_r-s_r\le0\}|=0,\qquad
|A_1\setminus\{f_r\le0\}|=0.
\]
Consequently the \(r\)-th row has mass at least \(|A_0|+|A_1|\).
global-zero-surplus-label-rigidity.status_reason: Accepted fact `ea6c0c97668fdba3` proves the registered zero-surplus label-collapse statement, including null cutting lines, support contacts, Fubini exceptional sets, translate overlap, and the common-label conclusion on both \(A_0\) and \(A_1\).
global-zero-surplus-label-rigidity.success_criterion: Success is a complete proof using the actual common affine triple and midpoint inclusion, including null cutting lines, empty unique-label cells, and all support contacts, or an exact compatible convex-body counterexample. A scalar partition or an argument assuming that measurable label cells are automatically connected is insufficient.

height-shear-invariance.relation_to_goal:
This permits height-linear translations of the outer slices without changing
the problem. In particular, it connects the common-vertex and centered
placements of homothetic triples and makes fixed positive results reusable.
height-shear-invariance.statement:
Prove that the invertible affine shear
\[
F_d(x,z)=(x,z+(x-1)d)
\]
preserves all three-slice halfspace depths and sends slices \(A_i\) to
\(A_i+(i-1)d\). State the exact transformation rule for witness points and
show that the Hausdorff two-measure on each slice is unchanged.
height-shear-invariance.status_reason: Accepted fact `ecee03aff61db31e` proves the exact affine-shear invariance and witness transport.
height-shear-invariance.success_criterion:
Give a self-contained proof for every closed halfspace in both directions,
including preservation of slice areas, total mass, and the infimum defining
depth. No appeal to an unstated affine-invariance principle.

homothetic-area-parameter-reduction.relation_to_goal:
This prevents the geometric workers from proving bounds on an unnecessarily
large or incorrectly normalized parameter set and identifies exactly which
scalar inequalities a triangle-family proof may use.
homothetic-area-parameter-reduction.statement:
Normalize a common-vertex homothetic triangle triple as
\((a\Delta,\Delta,c\Delta)\) with \(a\ge c>0\). Starting from the exact
residual area strip in accepted fact `15bb2c1680a0254e`, derive the complete
piecewise scalar domain for \(a,c\), including which of \(a\ge1\),
\(c\le1\), \(a+c\le2\), and \(a^2<1+c^2\) follow in each normalization.
homothetic-area-parameter-reduction.status_reason: Accepted fact `8be4b2011a05cfd2` gives the exact residual parameter equivalence, all piecewise endpoints, and the \(a\ge1\) versus \(a<1\) split.
homothetic-area-parameter-reduction.success_criterion:
Give an exact equivalence, not only necessary conditions. Track the choice of
largest outer area and the scale used to set the middle homothety to one.
Separate compatibility from failures of the accepted sufficient criteria.

homothetic-centroid-outer-bound.relation_to_goal:
The balance inequality \(a^2<1+c^2\) would then imply
\[
D(4/9+c^2)>\frac{2D(a^2+1+c^2)}9,
\]
settling the full residual common-vertex triangle family by a single explicit
point.
homothetic-centroid-outer-bound.statement:
Let \(\Delta\) be a nondegenerate triangle of area \(D\), with all
homotheties centered at one vertex, and let
\[
A_0=a\Delta,\qquad A_1=\Delta,\qquad A_2=c\Delta,
\]
where \(a\ge1\ge c>0\), \(a+c\le2\), and \(a^2<1+c^2\).
Prove, if true, that the middle-slice centroid \(g\) satisfies
\[
h_S((1,g))\ge D\left(\frac49+c^2\right).
\]
homothetic-centroid-outer-bound.status_reason: The proposed uniform centroid bound is false on the overbroad parameter domain; a necessary condition surviving the exact side-parallel cap family is \(a+c-2/3\ge\sqrt2\,c\).
homothetic-centroid-outer-bound.success_criterion:
Prove the displayed lower bound uniformly in \(a,c\), with all projected
vertex-order and endpoint cases. If it is false, return the first exact
parameter obstruction and the weakest corrected scalar hypothesis suggested
by the derivation, not a numerical grid.

homothetic-convex-centroid.relation_to_goal:
This is the arbitrary-shape analogue of accepted triangle theorem
`aef70a60593c53a2`. It would solve all homothetic residual triples whose
common homothety center lies in the middle body.
homothetic-convex-centroid.statement:
Let \(K\subset\mathbb R^2\) be a two-dimensional convex body of area \(D\),
let \(p\in K\), and define
\[
A_0=p+a(K-p),\qquad A_1=K,\qquad A_2=p+c(K-p),
\]
where
\[
a\ge c>0,\qquad 1<a^2+c^2,\qquad a+c<2,\qquad
a^2<1+c^2.
\]
Prove, if true, that the centroid \(g\) of \(K\) satisfies
\[
h_S((1,g))\ge\frac{2D(a^2+1+c^2)}9.
\]
homothetic-convex-centroid.status_reason: Accepted theorem `ec49e1b230bc2b95` composes the exact geometric reduction and anchored weighted-tail theorem to prove the full residual common-center homothetic convex-body case at the middle centroid.
homothetic-convex-centroid.success_criterion:
Reduce every halfspace to a one-dimensional projection inequality and prove it
for every concave section-length density. If additional information about
\(p\) is necessary, state the sharp corrected hypothesis and prove the
resulting theorem.

homothetic-tail-reduction.relation_to_goal: This turns the newly normalized Brunn-Minkowski equality family into one exact analytic inequality. Proving that inequality would settle the residual common-body homothetic case, while the reduction itself becomes a reusable accepted bridge from geometry to one dimension.
homothetic-tail-reduction.statement:
For a common-center homothetic triple
\[
A_0=p+a(K-p),\qquad A_1=K,\qquad A_2=p+c(K-p),
\]
with \(p\in K\), \(a\ge c>0\), \(1<a^2+c^2\), \(a+c<2\), and \(a^2<1+c^2\), prove rigorously that the middle centroid is a \(2T/9\) witness if the normalized one-dimensional inequality
\[
G(1)+a^2G(w_0)+c^2G(w_2)\ge \frac{2(1+a^2+c^2)}9,
\qquad aw_0+cw_2=2,
\]
holds for every compactly supported nonnegative concave probability density \(h\) of mean \(1\). Establish every projection, monotonicity, endpoint, and horizontal-halfspace step.
homothetic-tail-reduction.status_reason: Accepted fact `95f17bf1e5ee59f0` proves the exact anchored projection reduction, projected-center monotonicity, endpoint parametrization, and horizontal-halfspace checks for the stated residual common-center homothetic family.
homothetic-tail-reduction.success_criterion: A self-contained candidate lemma with correct quantifiers, a complete derivation from accepted halfspace and shear facts, and no appeal to unverified triangular extremality.

hybrid-midpoint-centerpoint-regime.relation_to_goal: This is a witness-side global reduction suggested by the Fable consultation. If true, it closes an arbitrary-shape area regime without analyzing the three-halfspace certificate and confines the remaining balanced problem to a narrow normalized area band. It therefore tests whether the proof should pivot away from certificate-side local bonus optimization.
hybrid-midpoint-centerpoint-regime.statement:
Assume the locked problem and put \(m=\min(a_0,a_2)\), \(M=\max(a_0,a_2)\). Let \(\widehat\mu\) be the probability law of \((X_0+X_2)/2\), where \(X_0,X_2\) are independent and uniformly distributed on \(A_0,A_2\), and define the finite planar measure
\[
\nu=\mathbf 1_{A_1}\,dw+m\widehat\mu.
\]
Prove rigorously that the halfplane depth of \(\nu\) at any \(z\in A_1\) lower-bounds the tilted part of \(h_S((1,z))\). Deduce that if
\[
2M\le a_1+m,
\]
then some \(z\in A_1\) satisfies \(h_S((1,z))\ge2T/9\). Handle normalization, closed-halfplane boundaries, the location of a centerpoint, and slice-parallel halfspaces exactly.
hybrid-midpoint-centerpoint-regime.status_reason: Accepted fact `452b737aaf90a400` proves the hybrid midpoint-measure lower bound and closes the full regime \(2\max(a_0,a_2)\le a_1+\min(a_0,a_2)\).
hybrid-midpoint-centerpoint-regime.success_criterion: A complete proof of both the hybrid-measure directional lower bound and the stated \(2M\le a_1+m\) theorem, using only declared accepted predecessors and an exact planar centerpoint theorem or a self-contained proof. An exact counterexample to either assertion also resolves the subgoal.

hybrid-route-adversarial-audit.relation_to_goal: The consultation is advisory and must not enter the fact graph without a hostile independent audit. A counterexample would prevent another long false route; a clean residual-band reduction would reorganize future subgoals around global area geometry rather than local certificate cases.
hybrid-route-adversarial-audit.statement: Independently audit the proposed hybrid midpoint-measure theorem in `hybrid-midpoint-centerpoint-regime`: try to falsify its probability normalization, event inclusion, centerpoint location, closed-boundary convention, and passage from tilted to full mixed-integer depth. If it survives, derive the exact normalized residual area region after combining it only with accepted large-slice and compatibility facts, and identify any overlap with already accepted regimes.
hybrid-route-adversarial-audit.status_reason: Accepted fact `d1498a01819203fa` independently validates the hybrid construction and gives the exact normalized residual area band, its breakpoints, realizability, overlap, and sharp-family placement.
hybrid-route-adversarial-audit.success_criterion: Either an exact admissible counterexample to a proposed step, or a rigorous candidate theorem giving the hybrid implication and the exact residual \((x,y)\)-band with all strict and weak inequalities checked. Computational searches alone do not satisfy this criterion.

indexed-chain-common-coupling-duality.relation_to_goal: This is the first representation retaining all three actual midpoint graphs through one shared endpoint coupling. It converts the arbitrary-body proof into a joint multiplicity-transport inequality and excludes further scalar/Venn projections.
indexed-chain-common-coupling-duality.statement:
Assume \(M=|A_0|\ge |A_2|=m\), and let
\[
\Pi_m=\{\pi\ge0:\pi(A_0\times A_2)=m,\ \pi_0\le\mu_0,\ \pi_2=\mu_2\}.
\]
For every affine \(f\), including all constant cases, prove
\[
\tau(E_f)=\sup_{\pi\in\Pi_m}\pi(E_f).
\]
For normalized \(f_1+f_2+f_3=-1\), derive the exact simultaneous formulas
\[
\max_i(b_i+\tau(E_i))
=\sup_{\pi\in\Pi_m}\max_i(b_i+\pi(E_i))
=\sup_{\lambda\in\Delta_3}\left(\sum_i\lambda_i b_i+
\sup_{\pi\in\Pi_m}\int\sum_i\lambda_i\mathbf1_{E_i}\,d\pi\right).
\]
Finally, with \(N=\sum_i\mathbf1_{E_i}\) and
\(\Gamma=\sup_{\pi\in\Pi_m}\int N\,d\pi\), prove
\[
\max_i(b_i+\tau(E_i))\ge\frac{\sum_i b_i+\Gamma}{3}.
\]
indexed-chain-common-coupling-duality.status_reason: Accepted fact `f347fefedf08f4e2` proves the unequal-mass common-coupling identity, every constant case, the simultaneous maximum/simplex formulas, and the joint multiplicity lower bound.
indexed-chain-common-coupling-duality.success_criterion: Success requires both directions of the coupling identity with unequal endpoint masses, atomless and constant rows, measurable quantile/disintegration details, completion to a full capacitated coupling, and every supremum/minimax interchange justified without assuming attainment.

indexed-pullback-chain-cover-duality.relation_to_goal:
This removes endpoint slope optimization exactly and retains the full
same-index pullback geometry. It turns the open
`global-indexed-product-cover` route into a sharp measurable chain-graph
covering statement rather than a product-volume relaxation. The equivalence
identifies the precise next lemma whose proof, together with accepted fact
`d2d117bcc58a1ba0`, would yield the global row inequality and hence the
locked theorem.
indexed-pullback-chain-cover-duality.statement:
Let \(A_0,A_2\subset\mathbb R^2\) be compact two-dimensional convex
bodies and let \(f:\mathbb R^2\to\mathbb R\) be affine. Define
\[
E_f=\left\{(x_0,x_2)\in A_0\times A_2:
f\left(\frac{x_0+x_2}{2}\right)<0\right\}
\]
and
\[
\tau(E_f)=\inf\left\{|U|+|V|:
U\subseteq A_0,\ V\subseteq A_2\text{ measurable},\
E_f\subseteq(U\times A_2)\cup(A_0\times V)\right\}.
\]

Prove, with the correct constant-affine boundary conventions, that
\[
\tau(E_f)=
\inf_{\sigma\in\mathbb R}
\left(
\left|A_0\cap\{f-\sigma\le0\}\right|
+
\left|A_2\cap\{f+\sigma\le0\}\right|
\right).
\]

For a normalized three-row certificate \(f_1+f_2+f_3=-1\), define
\(B_i=A_1\cap\{f_i\le0\}\). Prove that the universal row inequality over
all independent endpoint slopes is equivalent, except for explicitly
settled constant rows, to
\[
\max_i\bigl(|B_i|+\tau(E_{f_i})\bigr)\ge\frac{2T}{9}.
\]
indexed-pullback-chain-cover-duality.status_reason:
Accepted fact `a2a1f8532c91018f` proves the measurable chain-cover duality,
all constant-affine boundary cases, and the exact equivalence between the
universal independent-slope row inequality and
\(\max_i(b_i+\tau(E_{f_i}))\ge2T/9\).
indexed-pullback-chain-cover-duality.success_criterion:
Success requires both directions of the measurable vertex-cover equality,
including empty complements, unattained infima, level-set nullity, constant
positive, constant negative, and zero-constant cases. The three-row
equivalence must justify independence of the slopes and separately dispose
of every constant row. No appeal to finite graph duality without a complete
measure argument is sufficient.

interior-three-fan-side-cap-bound.relation_to_goal: The latest proportional-strip audit excludes the fan-center boundary case and shows that this pure planar interior implication is exactly the remaining obstruction for that Regime A family. Accepted facts `44d54af9bf8d0bd5` and `640eff7c0417543d` cover only the noncentered body and a restricted triangle, respectively.
interior-three-fan-side-cap-bound.statement:
Let \(B\subset\mathbb R^2\) be a compact two-dimensional convex body of area \(S\), let \(O\in\operatorname{int}B\), and let \(g_1,g_2\) be nonparallel linear forms vanishing at \(O\). Put
\[
b_1=|B\cap\{g_1\le0\}|,\qquad
b_2=|B\cap\{g_2\le0\}|,\qquad
b_3=|B\cap\{g_1+g_2\ge0\}|.
\]
Prove or disprove the exact implication
\[
\frac S4<b_3<\frac{79S}{180},\qquad b_1,b_2<\frac S2
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\max\{b_1,b_2\}\ge\frac{447S}{1000}.
\]
A proof of the stronger inequality
\[
\max\{b_1,b_2\}\ge2\sqrt{Sb_3}-2b_3
\]
on \(S/4\le b_3\le4S/9\) is sufficient.
interior-three-fan-side-cap-bound.status_reason: Accepted fact `18a556eb816782fb` proves the stronger arbitrary-body interior three-fan implication \(b_1,b_2<447S/1000\Rightarrow b_3>79S/180\), including compactness, fan-ray, asymmetric-triangle, equality, and general convex-body boundary cases.
interior-three-fan-side-cap-bound.success_criterion: Success is a verifier-ready proof for every compact convex body, with a genuine compactness/extremal or localization argument that covers asymmetric singleton-sector triangles, all six-sector degeneracies, and boundary limits; or an exact rational convex-polygon counterexample satisfying the strict displayed hypotheses. A symmetric triangle calculation or random search is not sufficient.

joint-multiplicity-transport-bound.relation_to_goal: Together with the common-coupling duality, the displayed uniform inequality implies \(\max_i(b_i+\tau(E_i))\ge2T/9\), hence closes `global-indexed-product-cover` and the locked theorem. The weighted fallback is exactly equivalent to that row target.
joint-multiplicity-transport-bound.statement:
Assume the locked compatibility condition, the strict residual strip, \(M=|A_0|\ge|A_2|=m\), normalized affine rows \(f_1+f_2+f_3=-1\), and
\[
b_i=|A_1\cap\{f_i\le0\}|<L:=\frac{2T}{9}\qquad(i=1,2,3).
\]
Using the common capacitated coupling set \(\Pi_m\), the midpoint graphs \(E_i\), and \(N=\sum_i\mathbf1_{E_i}\), prove
\[
\sup_{\pi\in\Pi_m}\int(N-1)\,d\pi
\ge
\frac{2M-m-a_1}{3}-\left(\sum_i b_i-a_1\right).
\]
If this uniform inequality is false, give an exact compatible rational polygonal counterexample in the stated low-middle-cap regime and prove instead, or sharply test, the exact deficit-weighted condition
\[
\sup_{\pi\in\Pi_m}\max_i\frac{\pi(E_i)}{L-b_i}\ge1.
\]
joint-multiplicity-transport-bound.status_reason: Accepted fact `48426e4615faac41` gives the exact compatible rational counterexample permitted by the success criterion and proves that only the deficit-weighted common-coupling condition remains viable.
joint-multiplicity-transport-bound.success_criterion: Success is a full geometric or transport proof using the actual midpoint sign multiplicity, endpoint capacities, and compatibility with \(A_1\), including strict/open boundaries; or an exact jointly realizable counterexample followed by a proof-status decision for the deficit-weighted condition. Product volumes, separate optimal couplings, or free cell tables do not count.

legacy-round-1.relation_to_goal: Preserves provenance only; it does not certify completion of the locked target.
legacy-round-1.statement: Historical round-1 claims created before subgoal tracking.
legacy-round-1.success_criterion: Historical bucket; no new candidates may target it.

localization-to-triangles.relation_to_goal:
Combined with accepted theorem `aef70a60593c53a2`, such a reduction would
settle the homothetic arbitrary-shape family without repeating the triangle
cap analysis.
localization-to-triangles.statement:
Prove a localization or shadow-system lemma reducing failure of the
homothetic-convex centroid inequality to a planar triangle with a homothety
center at a vertex, while preserving the scalar parameters and the offending
halfspace direction and slope.
localization-to-triangles.status_reason: The registered preservation claim is false when the marked homothety center equals the centroid: no nondegenerate triangle can keep that point simultaneously as a vertex and as its centroid. Any future localization must use weaker invariants.
localization-to-triangles.success_criterion:
Give a self-contained deformation or a precisely stated primary-source
theorem with all applicability checks. Track the centroid, homothety center,
halfspace mass, and inequality direction exactly.

middle-cover-coupling.relation_to_goal:
The condition contains every compatible family with \(a_0=a_2\) and also a
genuine area region beyond the accepted fixed-midpoint criterion. It reduces
the remaining balanced regime to quantitatively unequal outer slices.
middle-cover-coupling.statement:
Prove or refute the following precise residual theorem. If a compatible
triple satisfies
\[
2\max\{a_0,a_2\}\le a_1+\min\{a_0,a_2\},
\]
then some point of the middle slice has halfspace depth at least \(2T/9\).
The proof should use the exact at-most-three-halfspace cover reduction and
the midpoint relation between \(A_0,A_2\), and \(A_1\).
middle-cover-coupling.status_reason:
Accepted theorem `87035f4e1344144e` proves the registered area criterion by
an exact product-measure charging argument. It yields a middle-slice point of
depth at least \(2T/9\) whenever
\[
2\max\{a_0,a_2\}\le a_1+\min\{a_0,a_2\}.
\]
In particular it settles every compatible triple with equal outer areas,
including \(A_0=A_2\). The full balanced theorem remains open when the larger
outer area is more than half the sum of the other two areas.
middle-cover-coupling.success_criterion:
Give a complete contradiction to a strict low-mass cover of the middle
slice, including the product-measure integration and all strict inequalities.
Alternatively give an exact compatible counterexample to the stated theorem,
not merely to one proposed point.

middle-enlargement-transfer.relation_to_goal:
A transfer principle would reduce the general compatible problem to the
Minkowski-minimal middle slice plus a controlled added-measure term.
middle-enlargement-transfer.statement:
Let \(B=(A_0+A_2)/2\subseteq A_1\). Derive a quantitative theorem transferring
a \(2(|A_0|+|B|+|A_2|)/9\) depth witness for the minimal triple
\((A_0,B,A_2)\) to a \(2T/9\) witness for \((A_0,A_1,A_2)\), under the weakest
provable condition on the added middle measure \(A_1\setminus B\).
middle-enlargement-transfer.status_reason: Accepted fact `1c0264823debcab3` gives the exact necessary-and-sufficient local transfer condition, the sharp scalar-slack consequence, and a same-area obstruction showing why added-area location matters.
middle-enlargement-transfer.success_criterion:
Track the same witness against every halfspace and prove the exact extra-mass
lower bound needed. If no condition depending only on the added area can
work, give the first exact geometric obstruction and a corrected local
condition.

middle-excess-transfer-geometry.relation_to_goal: The universal problem differs from the minimal exact-Minkowski triple only by added middle mass. The accepted transfer lemma says precisely what that added mass must do, so this task attacks the correct local geometry rather than total area alone.
middle-excess-transfer-geometry.statement:
Let \(B=(A_0+A_2)/2\subseteq A_1\) and \(E=A_1\setminus B\). Use accepted transfer fact `1c0264823debcab3` to find a geometrically defined \(z\in B\) for which the exact local condition
\[
|E\cap K_H|\ge\left(\frac{2|E|}{9}-\sigma(H)\right)_+
\]
holds for every halfspace through \((1,z)\), assuming the minimal triple on \(B\) has a \(2/9\) witness. Prove a nontrivial general transfer regime beyond scalar slack alone, or isolate an exact unavoidable obstruction.
middle-excess-transfer-geometry.status_reason: Accepted lemma `aa2c2c12a537e83c` proves exact transfer for every radial homothetic enlargement of the minimal middle slice in the stated balanced bridge regime, including enlargements beyond the accepted scalar-slack threshold.
middle-excess-transfer-geometry.success_criterion: A candidate transfer lemma with explicit hypotheses automatically satisfied by a meaningful class of convex enlargements, together with an exact implication to the locked target; or a sharp example falsifying the proposed automatic condition.

midpoint-center-universal.relation_to_goal:
Together with the accepted large-slice lemma, a universal positive answer would
settle the locked problem. The accepted fact `9fa81a67fd2eaafc` already proves a
quantitative lower bound at this point, so the task is to close or refute only
its residual area regime.
midpoint-center-universal.statement:
Determine whether every compatible balanced triple is solved by the explicit
point \(y=(1,(g_0+g_2)/2)\). Prove the full \(2T/9\) bound at this point or give
an exact compatible balanced counterexample to this point choice.
midpoint-center-universal.status_reason:
Accepted counterexample `58bda9b5e8e68d8e` gives explicit rational compatible
rectangles in the balanced regime and a halfspace through
\((1,(g_0+g_2)/2)\) of mass strictly below \(2T/9\). This refutes the proposed
universal midpoint point choice, but not the locked existential target.
midpoint-center-universal.success_criterion:
Return either a self-contained theorem proving
\(h_S(1,(g_0+g_2)/2)\ge2T/9\) for all compatible triples with every
\(a_i<T/2\), or explicit rational convex polygons and a halfspace proving that
this point has depth below \(2T/9\). A failure of this point does not by itself
disprove the locked theorem.

midpoint-mixture-center.relation_to_goal:
If the proposed \(4/9\) center exists, the accepted large-slice theorem
settles the unbalanced case, while balance gives
\(T<2(a_1+m)\); the domination then proves the locked \(2T/9\) target.
An exact counterexample would close this sharply stated bridge and show that
the middle-cover \(1/3\) argument cannot be upgraded in this way.
midpoint-mixture-center.statement:
Let \(X_i\) be uniform on \(A_i\), let \(\nu\) be the law of
\((X_0+X_2)/2\), and put \(m=\min\{a_0,a_2\}\). Define the finite planar
measure
\[
\eta(E)=|A_1\cap E|+m\,\nu(E).
\]
First prove the exact domination of every normal-form halfspace through
\((1,c)\) by the corresponding halfplane mass \(\eta\). Then decide whether
there always exists \(c\in A_1\) such that every closed halfplane containing
\(c\) has \(\eta\)-mass at least \(4(a_1+m)/9\).
midpoint-mixture-center.status_reason:
Accepted fact `1790a353b242874b` proves the exact midpoint-mixture
domination for independent uniform outer points. It also gives a rational
homothetic-triangle counterexample to the registered universal \(4/9\)
planar-center claim. Thus the domination is reusable, but a uniform
\(4(a_1+\min\{a_0,a_2\})/9\) center bound is false. The counterexample has a
large middle slice, so a weaker target-adapted claim restricted to the
balanced residual regime remains open.
midpoint-mixture-center.success_criterion:
Return either a self-contained theorem proving the domination and the
quantified \(4/9\) planar center claim for every compatible triple, or
rational compatible polygons plus an exact proof that the maximum
halfplane depth of \(\eta\) is below \(4(a_1+m)/9\). Numerical sampling alone
does not close the subgoal.

minkowski-canonical-center.relation_to_goal: Accepted fact `9fa81a67fd2eaafc` already uses this point but loses information by bounding only one outer cap. The exact-Minkowski identity may force compensating middle mass beyond that area-only estimate.
minkowski-canonical-center.statement:
Determine whether the canonical point
\[
z=\frac{g_0+g_2}{2}\in\frac{A_0+A_2}{2}
\]
always satisfies the \(2T/9\) depth bound when \(A_1=(A_0+A_2)/2\) and the area triple lies outside all accepted area-sufficient regimes. Prove the bound using coupled outer caps and the exact middle Minkowski sum, or give a complete exact halfspace showing this point is insufficient while preserving the broader family as open.
minkowski-canonical-center.status_reason: The fixed canonical witness is false. The recorded exact rational residual Minkowski triple has a tilted halfspace through \((g_0+g_2)/2\) of mass \(161/9<2T/9\), while another point is already accepted as positive for that triple. A universal proof must select a movable geometry-dependent center.
minkowski-canonical-center.success_criterion: A verified theorem for the residual exact-Minkowski family at this point, or an explicit rational-polytopal compatible example and exact low-mass halfspace through the point proving that a movable center is necessary.

minkowski-centroid-deficit.relation_to_goal: This is a deliberately weaker, steady-progress version of `minkowski-middle-centroid`. Even if the centroid is not universally valid, an exact area or deficit envelope can certify a new region and isolate the first parameter range where genuinely shape-sensitive information is required.
minkowski-centroid-deficit.statement: For the minimal family \(B=(A_0+A_2)/2\), with \(M=\max\{|A_0|,|A_2|\}\), \(m=\min\{|A_0|,|A_2|\}\), and \(b=|B|\), derive an explicit rigorous lower bound for the depth at \((1,g_B)\) that uses both centroidal middle-cap information and the lower and upper Brunn-Minkowski cap inclusions. Optimize all auxiliary cap variables exactly.
minkowski-centroid-deficit.status_reason: Accepted lemma `f8a1649f7072dce1` gives the exact scalar lower envelope at the centroid of the minimal middle slice using both conditional Brunn-Minkowski cap inequalities, proves where that relaxation is sharp, and certifies a nonempty new portion of the strict residual area strip.
minkowski-centroid-deficit.success_criterion: Give a finite closed-form lower envelope and prove it for every projection direction and slope, including empty and saturated caps. State and prove a nonempty residual parameter region where it reaches \(2(M+b+m)/9\), or prove exactly that this data cannot improve the existing area criteria by exhibiting feasible extremal cap data.

minkowski-centroid-same-index-payment.relation_to_goal:
The centroid of \(B\) is the midpoint of the endpoint centroids.  The affine
midpoint identity forces the middle halfspace covering this point to contain
at least one endpoint centroid in the same index.  Planar Grünbaum payments
on \(B\) and that endpoint then align automatically, bypassing the marginal
index-routing obstruction.
minkowski-centroid-same-index-payment.statement:
Let \(B=(A_0+A_2)/2\subseteq A_1\), let \(b=|B|\), and let
\[
H_i=\{(h,w):f_i(w)+s_i(h-1)\le0\}\qquad(i=1,2,3)
\]
be a normalized strict three-halfspace certificate whose open middle
sections cover \(\mathbb R^2\).  Prove that one \(H_i\) has mass at least
\[
\frac49\left(b+\min\{a_0,a_2\}\right).
\]
Consequently, prove that the certificate cannot be subthreshold whenever
\[
2\left(b+\min\{a_0,a_2\}\right)\ge T.
\]
minkowski-centroid-same-index-payment.status_reason:
The required centroid identity is false.  Handoff
`f38e3f2c249f409e.md` gives two rational triangles for which the midpoint of
the endpoint centroids is \((1/2,1/3)\), while the centroid of their
Minkowski average is \((23/42,5/14)\).  The affine midpoint routing and the
planar Grünbaum payment therefore occur at different points.
minkowski-centroid-same-index-payment.success_criterion:
A complete proof must establish the centroid identity for the Minkowski
average, use the same affine function and slope on both endpoint centroids,
apply the planar centroid-cap bound with correct containment and boundary
conventions, and verify the final \(2T/9\) algebra.

minkowski-centroid-stress.relation_to_goal: The failed proof does not decide whether the centroid theorem is false. One exact adversarial family prevents another unjustified universal claim; a positive boundary family can reveal the missing geometric inequality.
minkowski-centroid-stress.statement:
Pressure-test the fixed centroid \(g_B\) only in the exact omitted branch
\[
(M+m)/2\le b<M+m
\]
using rational triangles or quadrilaterals. Seek either a complete exact low-mass halfspace through \(g_B\), or a proved positive all-halfspace certificate for a nonhomothetic family that reaches the difficult boundary.
minkowski-centroid-stress.status_reason: Accepted fact `f6775d043a3341f1` gives an exact rational nonhomothetic triangle family on the boundary \(b=(M+m)/2\), proves that the actual middle centroid differs from the outer-centroid midpoint, and controls every halfspace through it strictly above \(2T/9\).
minkowski-centroid-stress.success_criterion: Return exact rational polygon data and symbolic cap calculations. A negative result must exhibit one halfspace through \(g_B\) below \(2T/9\). A positive result must control all directions and slopes for the stated family. Numerical grids alone are working memory, not a candidate.

minkowski-core-bonus-transfer.relation_to_goal:
The previous proposed inequality
\(\gamma_B(d/2)\le(\sqrt{\gamma_0(d)}+\sqrt{\gamma_2(d)})^2/4\) is false.
This subgoal isolates the missing endpoint-to-core transfer without reviving
the rejected sum-bonus bridge.  A successful quantitative payment can be
combined with the triangle covering game or directly with
`three-cap-global-budget`.
minkowski-core-bonus-transfer.statement:
Let \(B=(A_0+A_2)/2\).  For a direction \(u\), write endpoint cap profiles
from their lower support lines as \(\gamma_0^u,\gamma_2^u\), write the
corresponding \(B\)-cap profile as \(\gamma_B^u\), and put
\[
E_u(d)=(\gamma_0^u\square\gamma_2^u)(d).
\]
Find and prove a correct quantitative lower-payment principle that converts
the fact that three directional caps cover \(B\) into a lower bound on at
least one actual endpoint payment \(E_{u_i}(d_i)\), strong enough to advance
the three-cap global budget.  The principle may use directional widths or
mixed areas in addition to \(a_0,a_2\), but it must be explicit and uniform.
minkowski-core-bonus-transfer.status_reason:
Accepted fact `7aecfa43fb452e02` proves a correct width-sensitive
lower bound from a Minkowski-core cap fraction to the actual endpoint
infimal-convolution payment.  Its direction-dependent \(Q_u\) form remains
available for global assembly; the coarse \(Q_u\ge\min(a_0,a_2)\) corollary
alone is not claimed to close the whole strict triangle-area region.
minkowski-core-bonus-transfer.success_criterion:
Success requires an explicit theorem with all hypotheses and constants, a
complete proof with the correct inequality directions, and a demonstrated
numerical implication for the \(2T/9\) budget in at least one nontrivial area
regime.  A qualitative statement that one bonus is positive, already covered
by accepted fact `508b5d8f1a3d6fca`, is insufficient.

minkowski-cover-upper.relation_to_goal: This is the cover-dual alternative to selecting \(g_B\). A contradiction proves that some middle point is deep even if no canonical point can be fixed. The new finite tent formula makes each defect exact; the remaining issue is coupling the three halfspaces.
minkowski-cover-upper.statement: Assume a strict low-mass cover of \(B=(A_0+A_2)/2\) by at most three middle sections in the missing upper-\(b\) branch. Combine accepted facts `a5309a9087686166` and `541afa94853c6bab` to derive a contradiction from the affine-slack convolution defects, using the joint cover geometry rather than independent per-halfspace cap areas.
minkowski-cover-upper.status_reason: Accepted fact `8829f28c0fdd962e` couples all halfspaces through their common product cover and rules out strict low-mass covers on an explicit nonempty upper residual strip by forcing an affine-slack defect contradiction.
minkowski-cover-upper.success_criterion: Give a self-contained aggregate inequality that contradicts the strict necessary bound on a nonempty part of the omitted branch, or on the whole branch. Treat relative support scales and the common three-halfspace intersection pattern; three unrelated one-halfspace optimizations without an aggregate conclusion are insufficient.

minkowski-depth-region.relation_to_goal: The accepted fixed-center two-density reduction is exact but its center can fail. This subgoal turns the needed movable center into a precise directional selection problem. Convexity or interval structure would permit a Helly-type attack; an exact obstruction prevents relying on a false quasiconcavity claim.
minkowski-depth-region.statement:
For \(B=(A_0+A_2)/2\), derive the exact one-dimensional formula for the tilted-halfspace depth at an arbitrary point \(z\in B\). In centered projection coordinates it should identify the directional functional
\[
\Phi_q(s)=F_B(s)+\min_{u+v=2s}\bigl(F_0(u)+F_2(v)\bigr),
\qquad s=\langle q,z-z_0\rangle,
\]
with all support clipping made exact. Determine whether each superlevel set
\[
I_q(t)=\{s:\Phi_q(s)\ge t\}
\]
is an interval, and convert the family \(I_q(2T/9)\) into a correct planar intersection or selection criterion for a witness.
minkowski-depth-region.status_reason: Accepted lemma `a6099e9164a694ce` gives the exact arbitrary-center directional functional, proves its continuous monotone interval structure, and converts existence of a middle-slice witness into an exact planar intersection criterion equivalent by Helly to every three directional constraints intersecting.
minkowski-depth-region.success_criterion: Prove the arbitrary-center formula with endpoint cases. Then either prove the stated interval and planar-selection structure and obtain a nontrivial sufficient selection theorem, or give exact concave section densities realized by convex polygons that refute the first claimed structural property. Merely restating Tukey-region convexity is insufficient.

minkowski-depth-region-upper.relation_to_goal: Even if the middle centroid fails, the locked target for the minimal family needs only some point of \(B\). The accepted arbitrary-center formula turns that question into an exact planar selection problem and avoids repeating fixed-center inequalities.
minkowski-depth-region-upper.statement:
Use the exact directional threshold regions in accepted fact `a6099e9164a694ce` to prove that the witness intersection
\[
\bigcap_{q\in\mathbb S^1}R_q(2T/9)
\]
is nonempty throughout the missing upper-\(b\) branch, without assuming that it contains \(g_B\). Equivalently, rule out every three-direction Helly obstruction using the geometry of \(B=(A_0+A_2)/2\).
minkowski-depth-region-upper.status_reason: Accepted fact `e34ffd778c178549` constructs an adaptive middle-slice point by combining planar and four-dimensional Grünbaum inequalities, and certifies an explicit nonempty subregion with \(b\) close to \(M+m\).
minkowski-depth-region-upper.success_criterion: Prove the three-direction intersection in the entire omitted branch or a rigorously stated nonempty subregion, with every use of Helly or separation explicit. An exact three-direction obstruction may close the proposed selection lemma but is not a counterexample to the locked theorem unless full low-mass covers are supplied for all slices.

minkowski-equality-family.relation_to_goal:
Compatibility always gives \((A_0+A_2)/2\subseteq A_1\). Equality removes
unused middle-slice area and is therefore a natural extremal class. It includes
the smallest nonhomothetic pentagon family left by the round-3 certificate
obstacle and is not covered by centroid alignment in general.
minkowski-equality-family.statement:
Determine the locked \(2T/9\) conclusion for the sharply delimited family
\[
A_1=\frac{A_0+A_2}{2}.
\]
Either prove the conclusion for every pair of two-dimensional convex
polytopes \(A_0,A_2\), or construct a complete exact counterexample within
this equality family.
minkowski-equality-family.status_reason: Accepted theorem `96f5513b8ab88a8f` proves the required \(2T/9\) conclusion for every minimal compatible family \(A_1=(A_0+A_2)/2\).
minkowski-equality-family.success_criterion:
Return either a self-contained theorem proving the exact target for every
Minkowski-equality triple, or explicit rational polygons together with the
finite low-mass halfspace covers required by accepted fact
`8f5f00ddd4f22d2f`. A calculation for one proposed point alone is insufficient.

minkowski-equality-normalization.relation_to_goal:
This isolates the full equality family inside the open
`minkowski-equality-family` subgoal and determines whether the new homothetic
shape theorem would close it.
minkowski-equality-normalization.statement:
For compatible planar convex bodies with
\[
A_1=\frac{A_0+A_2}{2}
\]
and equality in the planar Brunn–Minkowski area inequality, prove the exact
homothetic representation of \(A_0,A_1,A_2\), and use affine shear invariance
to give the simplest canonical placement for the depth problem.
minkowski-equality-normalization.status_reason: Accepted fact `eee2bdfe64ccf5b1` proves the requested equality-boundary characterization and depth-preserving canonical normalization. The broader `minkowski-equality-family` remains open because exact Minkowski equality without Brunn-Minkowski area equality is strictly more general.
minkowski-equality-normalization.success_criterion:
State the equality theorem with a primary source or prove it directly in the
planar full-dimensional case. Give explicit translations, scale factors, and
the shear vector; do not conflate equality \(A_1=(A_0+A_2)/2\) with equality
of areas alone.

minkowski-middle-centroid.relation_to_goal: The accepted outer-centroid midpoint can fail even in the minimal Minkowski-sum family, so a geometry-dependent point is necessary. The centroid of the actual middle Minkowski sum is the simplest such point. A positive answer closes the open `minkowski-equality-family`; a negative answer sharply rules out this witness without refuting the locked theorem.
minkowski-middle-centroid.statement:
Let \(A_0,A_2\subset\mathbb R^2\) be nonempty two-dimensional convex polytopes, let
\[
B=\frac{A_0+A_2}{2},
\qquad S_B=(\{0\}\times A_0)\cup(\{1\}\times B)\cup(\{2\}\times A_2),
\]
and let \(g_B\) be the centroid of \(B\). In the strict balanced residual area regime, decide whether
\[
h_{S_B}((1,g_B))\ge \frac{2(|A_0|+|B|+|A_2|)}9
\]
always holds.
minkowski-middle-centroid.status_reason: Accepted theorem `672fff6fcf7486e3` proves that the centroid of \(B=(A_0+A_2)/2\) is a \(2T/9\) witness for every strictly balanced minimal Minkowski-sum triple. Together with accepted large-slice theorem `2f9be517307232c7`, this exhausts all area regimes in the minimal family.
minkowski-middle-centroid.success_criterion: Return either a complete all-halfspace proof for every residual pair \(A_0,A_2\), including slice-parallel cases, or explicit rational polygons and one exact halfspace through \((1,g_B)\) of mass strictly below the target. Sampled directions or a failure of a coarse bound do not count.

minkowski-middle-centroid-repair.relation_to_goal: The lower branch \(2b<M+m\) has a valid upper-cap argument, while the displayed upper branch was skipped by an invalid algebraic comparison. Proving this repair would complete the centroid strategy for the minimal Minkowski-sum family. A counterexample refutes only the fixed centroid, not the locked theorem.
minkowski-middle-centroid-repair.statement:
Let \(B=(A_0+A_2)/2\), \(M=\max\{|A_0|,|A_2|\}\), \(m=\min\{|A_0|,|A_2|\}\), and \(b=|B|\). In the strict balanced regime, settle the exact parameter branch omitted by the quarantined fact `672fff6fcf7486e3`:
\[
M<m+b,\qquad \frac{M+m}{2}\le b<M+m.
\]
Decide whether the centroid \(g_B\) always satisfies \(h_{S_B}((1,g_B))\ge2(M+m+b)/9\).
minkowski-middle-centroid-repair.status_reason: Accepted theorem `96f5513b8ab88a8f` closes the complete minimal family by an exhaustive case split, so the stronger fixed-centroid refinement is no longer required for the locked target. This does not assert that the middle centroid works in every nonresidual instance.
minkowski-middle-centroid-repair.success_criterion: Give a complete all-halfspace proof for the entire displayed branch, without citing the quarantined fact, or explicit rational polygons and an exact low-mass halfspace through \(g_B\). Every cap-empty, saturated, and support-face case must be included.

minkowski-support-clearance.relation_to_goal: The exact failure audit identifies the first missing quantity: when one outer cap is empty, the threshold on the other outer body is determined by the distance from the lower support of \(B\) to its centroid. Concavity gives nonzero cap mass, and mixed-area information may make it large enough for the target.
minkowski-support-clearance.statement: In the missing upper-\(b\) branch of `minkowski-middle-centroid-repair`, derive a sharp lower bound on the outer cap sum through \(g_B\) using signed support clearances, projection widths, concave section densities, and the identity \(B=(A_0+A_2)/2\). The bound must improve the area-only envelope `f8a1649f7072dce1`, whose scalar extremizer permits an empty large-outer cap.
minkowski-support-clearance.status_reason: Accepted fact `c2c5ebf411bfdef8` proves a sharp support-clearance lower bound for the outer cap sum, including empty and saturated caps, and certifies the nonempty omitted subregion \(b\ge M+m/2\).
minkowski-support-clearance.success_criterion: Prove a normalized inequality valid for every pair of planar convex bodies and every direction that certifies a nonempty portion of the omitted branch not covered by `f8a1649f7072dce1`, or prove the complete branch. If the proposed width data are insufficient, give exact realizable concave densities showing the sharp obstruction.

minkowski-two-density-reduction.relation_to_goal: The full exact-Minkowski family is the smallest middle slice allowed by compatibility. Unlike the homothetic case it has two unrelated projection densities, so the next reusable bridge must identify their correct coupled tail constraint rather than assume a common density.
minkowski-two-density-reduction.statement:
For the exact Minkowski family
\[
A_1=\frac{A_0+A_2}{2},
\]
derive a rigorous one-dimensional projection formulation for all tilted halfspaces through a canonical middle point. Express the three cap masses using the two outer concave section densities and the middle Minkowski-sum section density, and prove every valid inclusion or Brunn-Minkowski lower bound including empty and saturated cap cases. Isolate one exact analytic inequality whose proof would imply \(2T/9\).
minkowski-two-density-reduction.status_reason: Accepted lemma `756b87a16a89ea8f` gives the exact one-dimensional section-density and cap formula at the outer-centroid midpoint for every minimal Minkowski-sum triple, handles empty and saturated caps correctly, and isolates the remaining directional inequality. Its rational shear example also proves that the actual middle density cannot be eliminated.
minkowski-two-density-reduction.success_criterion: A candidate lemma with an explicit point, exact threshold parametrization, all endpoint cases, and a sharply stated two-density analytic target; or one exact obstruction showing why the proposed canonical point or cap inequality cannot work.

multiaffine-rounding-localization.relation_to_goal: The large-box theorem itself cannot trigger for exactly three slices, but the rounding transfer could still supply a new joint cross-slice charge in the finite-interior, boundary, or tail branches. The key question is whether full base-box availability can be replaced by phase-dependent anchors drawn from the three existing slices.
multiaffine-rounding-localization.statement: Audit and compare the three attachment formulations of the multiaffine rounding method: simultaneous fractional-phase argmax, sequential triangular rounding with unit-capacity preimages, and abstract phase-core/phase-deficit injection. Prove the strongest common measure-transfer lemma that is correct, and determine whether it has a localized version usable when the base projection contains only the integer slices \(0,1,2\).
multiaffine-rounding-localization.status_reason: Handoff `906955f8c345497a.md` audits all three rounding formulations, proves their common capacity-one deficit-transfer lemma, and proves that every no-deficit three-slice localization inherits the phase-core obstruction. This meets the registered success criterion. The positive-deficit paired-support integral remains a separate future direction.
multiaffine-rounding-localization.success_criterion: Check every measurability, capacity, injectivity, and halfspace-monotonicity claim. Then either derive an exact nonredundant three-slice transfer inequality from anchors on slices \(0,1,2\), or prove that any such local use is equivalent to the phase-core condition and therefore inherits its projection obstruction. Correct general techniques without a target implication should be recorded as working memory, not promoted as facts.

multislice-affine-selector-transfer.relation_to_goal: This tests whether the attachment's average-deep affine-selector argument gives a genuinely new fact for the locked three-slice problem or only restates the accepted affine-centroid theorem. A non-centroid selector with total planar depth at least \(4T/9\) would close a new compatible class.
multislice-affine-selector-transfer.statement:
Let \(C\subset\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^2\) be a compact convex polytope whose nonempty integer slices are \(A_z\), \(z\in I\subset\mathbb Z\), with total slice area \(T=\sum_{z\in I}|A_z|\). Suppose \(q(z)=az+b\in A_z\) is an affine selector and let \(\delta_z\) be the planar halfspace depth of \(q(z)\) in \(A_z\). Prove
\[
\max_{z\in I} h_S((z,q(z)))\ge \frac12\sum_{z\in I}\delta_z.
\]
Determine exactly when this gives \(2T/9\), and whether its three-slice specialization adds anything beyond accepted fact `4dfa9b673b27fea1`.
multislice-affine-selector-transfer.status_reason: Accepted fact `dcf65c9de5a176bb` proves the complete affine-selector transfer and gives an exact compatible three-slice family outside the three nearest accepted certificates. This fully meets the registered theorem and nonredundancy criteria.
multislice-affine-selector-transfer.success_criterion: Give a boundary-complete proof for every finite integer slice set, including horizontal ambient halfspaces, zero selector depths, endpoint medians, and ties. For relevance, either exhibit an exact compatible three-slice family not covered by `4dfa9b673b27fea1` for which the selector condition proves \(2T/9\), or prove that the \(2T/9\) specialization is subsumed by an accepted fact and should not be added.

nested-mixture-center-region.relation_to_goal:

nested-mixture-center-region.statement:

\[
\eta(E)=|\Delta\cap E|
+c^2D\,\frac{|k\Delta\cap E|}{k^2D}.
\]
Prove that some explicitly selected \(z=z(a,c)\in\Delta\) has
\(\eta\)-halfplane depth at least
\[
\frac{2D(a^2+1+c^2)}9.
\]
nested-mixture-center-region.status_reason: The common-\(U\) coupling fails on the exact residual triangle parameters \((a,c)=(2503/2500,1/20)\); the next positive test is a non-diagonal coupling or direct three-slice proof for this same triple.
nested-mixture-center-region.success_criterion:

\]
with all homotheties centered at one vertex, derive an exact finite

to \((\lambda_0,\lambda_1,\lambda_2)=(201/200,1,101/1000)\) and identify a

maximin.
nested-triangle-normal-form.status_reason: Accepted fact `cb46be6a5648e0bd` gives the exact finite polynomial-system reduction, while accepted fact `c0a4f6ae5d1dab55` supplies a certified positive application to the fixed extreme parameters.
nested-triangle-normal-form.success_criterion:

nine-cover-diagonal-normal-cell.relation_to_goal:
Accepted fact `3c143dfcc90fab8e` excludes the analogous fixed normal cell
with \(u_1=(1,2)\) for the same transverse triple.  The diagonal cell has the

nine-cover-diagonal-normal-cell.statement:
For
\[
\begin{aligned}
A_0&=\operatorname{conv}\{(0,0),(1/2,0),(0,1/2)\},\\
A_1&=\operatorname{conv}\{(-1/2,1/2),(0,0),(3/4,0),
                         (1/2,1/4),(-1/2,3/4)\},\\
A_2&=\operatorname{conv}\{(0,0),(1,0),(-1,1)\},
\end{aligned}
\]
whose strict target is \(11/48\), take
\[
u_1=(1,1),\qquad u_2=(-1,0),\qquad u_3=(0,-1).
\]
Define
\[
M_r(c)=\inf_{k\in\mathbb R}\sum_{j=0}^2
\left|A_j\cap\{w:u_r\cdot w\le c+k(j-1)\}\right|
\]
and
\[
R_r=\sup\{c\in\mathbb R:M_r(c)<11/48\}.
\]
Determine \(R_1,R_2,R_3\) exactly and decide the sign of
\[
R_1+R_2+R_3.
\]
If the sum is positive, give exact rational strict-low halfspaces whose
height-one traces cover the plane.  If it is nonpositive, give the exact
Farkas certificate excluding this whole normal cell.

nine-cover-diagonal-normal-cell.success_criterion:

Then decide the direct nine-cover route on the entire family: either give one rational (alpha\in\mathcal I) and exact strict-low covers of all three slices as required by accepted fact `8f5f00ddd4f22d2f`, or prove that every compatible member has a protected middle point and therefore no strict-low interior cover of its middle slice.

and have endpoint ratio \(1/4<3/8\). By accepted fact

nonconcurrent-three-cap-inequality.statement:

\[
f_1+f_2+f_3=-1.

Put
\[
H_i=\{f_i\leq0\},\qquad b_i=|K\cap H_i|.
\]
Prove
\[
5(b_1+b_2+b_3)-6\min_i b_i\geq4|K|.
\]

Also derive the exact-cell form. If \(s_i\) is the area of the cell lying
only in \(H_i\), \(d_i\) is the area of the opposite doubleton cell, and
\(g\) is the triple-cell area, then
\[
s_1+s_2+s_3+5g\geq6\min_i(s_i-d_i).
\]

\Delta b\le\varphi_\delta(w_0),\qquad

additional joint invariant missing from the separate endpoint-cap

to both closest \(A_2\) axis endpoints.  For the later full lens
system, this lemma reduces uniform positivity to excluding its
intersection with (8); the supplied accepted facts do not themselves
give that final parameter elimination.

## Proof

The midpoint constants cancel because
\[
p_i=f_i-L_i,\qquad q_i=f_i+L_i.
\]
Thus for an \(A_0\) point with coordinates \((X,Y)\) and an \(A_2\)
point,
\[
2r=p_j+q_j,\qquad 2s=p_\ell+q_\ell.
\tag{9}
\]
This is the parameter form of the midpoint map used in accepted fact
`77e4f1bd725f32f9`.

On the \(A_2\) section \(V=0\), the endpoint \(U=u+H_2\) has
\[
(q_j,q_\ell)=(-\theta,0).
\]
On the section \(q_j=0\), the endpoint \(t=w_0\) has
\[
(q_j,q_\ell)=(0,-w_0).
\]
Both points belong to the compact polygon \(A_2\).  Convexity
therefore gives the whole segment
\[
D=\operatorname{conv}\{(-\theta,0),(0,-w_0)\}\subseteq A_2.
\tag{10}
\]

First prove (2).  The coordinate image of \(P_0^\circ\) lies in
\[
T_\delta=\{(X,Y):X\ge0,\ Y\ge0,\ X+Y\le\delta\}
\]
and has coordinate area \(\Delta b\).  The part of \(T_\delta\) with
\(Y\le t\) has coordinate area exactly
\(\varphi_\delta(t)\).  Hence
\[
\left|
P_0^\circ\cap\{Y\ge w_0\}
\right|_{\rm coord}
\ge
\bigl(\Delta b-\varphi_\delta(w_0)\bigr)_+.
\tag{11}
\]
Adding the point \((q_j,q_\ell)=(0,-w_0)\) and dividing by two maps
this set injectively into \(\{r\ge0,s\ge0\}\).  Coordinate and
physical areas are related by the factor \(\Delta\), and midpoint
scaling multiplies planar area by \(1/4\).  This proves the first term
of (2).  The same argument with
\((q_j,q_\ell)=(-\theta,0)\) and the cap \(X\le\theta\) proves the
second term.

Now fix \(n\ge1\).  For \(i=0,\ldots,n\), convexity and (10) give
\[
q_i=\left(-\frac{i}{n}\theta,
-\left(1-\frac{i}{n}\right)w_0\right)\in A_2.
\tag{12}
\]
Let
\[
E_i=P_0^\circ\cap
\left\{
X\ge\frac{i}{n}\theta,\quad
Y\ge\left(1-\frac{i}{n}\right)w_0
\right\}.
\tag{13}
\]
By (9),
\[
\frac{E_i+q_i}{2}
\subseteq B\cap\{r\ge0,s\ge0\},
\]
so
\[
\left|B\cap\{r\ge0,s\ge0\}\right|
\ge\frac{1}{4\Delta}\max_{0\le i\le n}|E_i|_{\rm coord}.
\tag{14}
\]

Assume first \(\theta w_0>0\).  If
\[
\frac{X}{\theta}+\frac{Y}{w_0}>1+\frac1n,
\tag{15}
\]
then \((X,Y)\) belongs to at least one \(E_i\).  Indeed, if
\(X/\theta\ge1\), take \(i=n\); if \(Y/w_0\ge1\), take \(i=0\).
Otherwise the interval
\[
\left[1-\frac{Y}{w_0},\frac{X}{\theta}\right]
\subset(0,1)
\]
has length greater than \(1/n\), so it contains some grid point
\(i/n\).  Thus the complement of \(\bigcup_iE_i\) in
\(P_0^\circ\) is contained in the triangle
\[
\left\{X,Y\ge0:
\frac{X}{\theta}+\frac{Y}{w_0}
\le1+\frac1n\right\},
\]
whose coordinate area is
\[
\frac{\theta w_0}{2}\left(1+\frac1n\right)^2.
\tag{16}
\]
It follows that
\[
\left|\bigcup_{i=0}^nE_i\right|_{\rm coord}
\ge
\left(
\Delta b-
\frac{\theta w_0}{2}\left(1+\frac1n\right)^2
\right)_+.
\tag{17}
\]
Since there are \(n+1\) sets,
\[
\max_i|E_i|_{\rm coord}
\ge\frac1{n+1}
\left|\bigcup_iE_i\right|_{\rm coord}.
\]
Combining this with (14)-(17) gives (3).  If
\(\theta=0\) or \(w_0=0\), one endpoint in (10) is the origin, so
\(P_0^\circ/2\subseteq B\cap\{r\ge0,s\ge0\}\).  Its physical area is
\(b/4\), which is at least the right side of (3).  Hence (3) also
holds on both zero-offset boundaries.

If \(2\Delta b\le\theta w_0\), every numerator in (3) is nonpositive.
If \(2\Delta b>\theta w_0\), then for all sufficiently large integers
\(n\),
\[
2\Delta b\,n^2>\theta w_0(n+1)^2,
\]
so (3) is strictly positive.  This proves (4).  Since
\(f_j+f_k+f_\ell=-1\), every point with \(r,s>0\) has
\(f_k=-1-r-s<0\).  Cutting lines have area zero.  Therefore zero
strict \(R_k\)-area forces every lower bound in (2)-(3) to vanish,
which gives (5)-(6).

\[

=\frac{91471}{8000000}.
\]
Substitution in (2) gives
\[

\frac{1622001}{40000000}
-\frac{91471}{8000000}
\right)
=\frac{582323}{80000000},
\]
proving (7).  Independently, the \(n=1\) instance of (3) gives
\[

`fa0e57b225178b3b`,
\[

\varphi_{100}\left(\frac{2029}{20}\right)=5000,
\]
and
\[
2\Delta b=\frac{56501}{200}
<
\frac{10145}{2}=\theta w_0.
\]
This proves (8) and the claimed exact calibration of the remaining
joint obstruction.

\]

\[

\]

\[

\]
which proves the asserted formula for \(f_k\).

Let \(a_1,\ldots,a_{10}\) be the cyclic \(A_0\) vertices listed in accepted fact `ba7a0577628a5b73`.  Let \((U_i,V_i)\), \(0\le i\le9\), be the cyclic \(A_2\) vertices listed in accepted fact `79e06fd7932f4121`, and put

opposite-separated-one-breakpoint-midpoi.relation_to_goal:
For any compatible middle extension \(K\supseteq S\) satisfying the three crossing equations, the three middle caps cover \(K\), so \(|K|\le\kappa_{\max}\). The \(j\)-crossing then requires
\[
|K\cap\{f_j\le0\}|
\le \frac{2(M+m+\kappa_{\max})}{9}-s_j,
\]
whereas midpoint containment makes this cap at least the corresponding cap of \(S\). Thus the strict endpoint-only inequality excludes the entire separated one-breakpoint central opposite-pair subcase of `canonical-opposite-band-section`. A rational refutation localizes the remaining work to simultaneous middle-cap extension.
opposite-separated-one-breakpoint-midpoi.statement:
Let \(N=\{j,k,\ell\}\). Let \(f_j,f_k,f_\ell\) be nonconstant affine functions with pairwise nonparallel linear parts and
\[
f_j+f_k+f_\ell=-1.
\]
Let \(L_j+L_k+L_\ell<-1\), put
\[
p_i=f_i-L_i,\qquad q_i=f_i+L_i,
\]
and let \(A_0,A_2\) be compact two-dimensional convex polygons with
\[
M=|A_0|\ge m=|A_2|>0.
\]
Use the exact-cell convention of accepted fact `0e51a47a9add571f`. Assume the complete positive endpoint supports are exactly
\[
\mathcal S_P=\bigl\{\{j\},\varnothing,\{\ell\},\{k,\ell\}\bigr\},
\]
\[
\mathcal S_Q=\bigl\{\{j\},\{j,k\},N,\{k,\ell\}\bigr\},
\]
with every listed cell of positive area. Assume both affine cut intersections
\[
p_k=p_\ell=0,\qquad q_k=q_\ell=0
\]
lie outside the corresponding endpoint polygon. Assume exactly one of the six levels \(p_i=0,q_i=0\) contains a polygon vertex, its adjacent chord pieces have unequal affine slopes, and the other five levels contain no endpoint vertex.

For
\[
u_i=|A_0\cap\{p_i\le0\}|,\qquad
v_i=|A_2\cap\{q_i\le0\}|,\qquad
s_i=u_i+v_i,
\]
assume
\[
s_i<m\qquad(i=j,k,\ell),
\]
and the strict first lower-crossing alternative
\[
\rho_{A_0,i}^{+}(0)<\rho_{A_2,i}^{-}(0)
\qquad(i=j,k,\ell)
\]
in the notation of accepted fact `eddda25c734d34bc`.

Put
\[
S=\frac{A_0+A_2}{2},\qquad
\kappa_{\max}=2(M+m)-3(s_j+s_k+s_\ell),
\]
and assume
\[
|S|\le\kappa_{\max}.
\]
Prove
\[
\left|S\cap\{f_j\le0\}\right|
>
\frac{2(M+m+\kappa_{\max})}{9}-s_j,
\]
or give exact rational endpoint polygons satisfying every hypothesis and the reverse weak inequality.

phase-fixed-calibration-support-depth-co.statement:
Let \(s>0\).  Decide exact rational convex-polytopal realizability of the
following fixed proper-proper phase calibration in common support
coordinates.  Let \(P,Q,R\subset\mathbb R^2\) be rational
two-dimensional convex polygons with
\[
\frac{P+Q}{2}\subseteq R
\]
and
\[
|P|=16s,\qquad |Q|=s,\qquad |R|=\frac{151}{10}s.
\]
Require
\[
|P\cap\{x\le0\}|=|Q\cap\{X\le0\}|=\frac{s}{8},
\]
\[
|P\cap\{y\le0\}|=|Q\cap\{Y\le0\}|=\frac{s}{5},
\]
\[
|Q\cap\{X+Y\ge-2-\delta\}|=\frac{3s}{4},
\qquad \max_{p\in P}(x(p)+y(p))=\delta,
\]

pinch-counterexample-two-triangle-limit.statement:

\[
x_n=m_n/M_n\to0,\qquad y_n=a_{1,n}/M_n\to1.

State exactly what can be concluded about the small endpoint limit, which may be a segment rather than a point.
pinch-counterexample-two-triangle-limit.status_reason: Accepted fact `f882a944b9fbef55` proves the full pinch compactification, triangle equality-rigidity, point-or-segment small-endpoint alternative, and unique centroidal edge-frame limit for every minimal certificate.

pinch-endpoint-or-middle-routing.status_reason: Accepted fact `48609f0c0f15edd8` proves the endpoint, hybrid, and reflected-saturation routing branches and closes an explicit nonempty centrally symmetric homothetic subregion beyond the hybrid area condition.

`de3c80720a026e04`, and `0b5d84877f51b7c3`, prove that such a sequence is

\]

pinch-midpoint-multiplicity-balance.statement:
Assume a hypothetical sequence of genuine counterexamples in the strict
small-\(r\) residual strip, normalized by
\[
|A_{0,n}|=1,\qquad |A_{2,n}|=r_n\to0,\qquad
|A_{1,n}|=s_n,\qquad 1-r_n<s_n<1+r_n.
\]
For an arbitrary normalized minimal certificate, let
\(f_{1,n}+f_{2,n}+f_{3,n}=-1\), define
\[
p_{i,n}=\left|A_{1,n}\cap\{f_{i,n}\le0\}\right|,
\]
and put
\[
N_n(u,v)=
\#\left\{i:
f_{i,n}\left(\frac{u+v}{2}\right)<0
\right\},
\]
\[

\frac1{r_n}
\int_{A_{0,n}\times A_{2,n}}N_n(u,v)\,du\,dv.

positive-frame-support-area-gap.statement:
Let \(K\subset\mathbb R^2\) be a convex body and let nonzero vectors
\(v_1,v_2,v_3\) satisfy
\[
v_1+v_2+v_3=0,\qquad \det(v_1,v_2)\ne0.
\]
Prove
\[
\left(\sum_{i=1}^3 h_K(v_i)\right)^2
\ge 2|\det(v_1,v_2)|\,|K|.
\]
More precisely, prove that the intersection of the three support
halfplanes
\[
P=\bigcap_{i=1}^3\{x:\langle v_i,x\rangle\le h_K(v_i)\}
\]
is a triangle of area
\[
|P|=
\frac{\left(\sum_i h_K(v_i)\right)^2}
{2|\det(v_1,v_2)|},
\]
and determine the equality case in the area inequality.
positive-frame-support-area-gap.status_reason: Accepted fact `b099cf442fe337a6` proves the registered support-triangle area identity, the required lower bound, and the equality characterization.
positive-frame-support-area-gap.success_criterion:
