projection-quantile-depth-erosion-dualit.relation_to_goal: This turns the all-direction projection-quantile prefilter into an exact two-dimensional convex feasibility test. Future counterexample searches can compute the depth region and test whether a reflected translate of \(A_2\) fits inside it; explicit directions are needed only when the erosion is empty.
projection-quantile-depth-erosion-dualit.statement:
Let \(A_0,A_2\subset\mathbb R^2\) be compact two-dimensional convex bodies with \(M=|A_0|>m=|A_2|>0\). Define
\[
D_m(A_0)=\{p\in\mathbb R^2:d_{A_0}(p)\ge m\}.
\]
For every nonzero linear form \(\lambda\), define
\[
q(\lambda)=\inf\{s:|A_0\cap\{\lambda\le s\}|\ge m\},
\qquad
\beta(\lambda)=\max_{a\in A_2}\lambda(a).
\]
Prove the exact equivalence:
\[
\exists z\in\mathbb R^2\ \text{with}\ z-A_2\subseteq D_m(A_0)
\]
if and only if every triple of nonzero linear forms satisfying \(\lambda_1+\lambda_2+\lambda_3=0\) obeys
\[
\sum_{i=1}^3(q(\lambda_i)+\beta(\lambda_i))\le0.
\]
Equivalently, failure of the translated containment produces a zero-sum triple with strictly positive sum, and common positive scaling then makes the sum exceed \(2\), the necessary budget in accepted fact `19703e1e768865b1`.
projection-quantile-depth-erosion-dualit.status_reason: Accepted fact `9aa8eaca3b60ecf3` proves the exact closed depth-region containment duality, including the infinite-to-finite reduction, planar Helly step, strict Farkas sign, homogeneity, and two-direction padding.
projection-quantile-depth-erosion-dualit.success_criterion: A self-contained proof that \(D_m(A_0)\) is represented by the quantile halfplanes, followed by a finite Helly reduction and the correct strict Farkas alternative. It must justify positive homogeneity, the reduction to at most three nonzero directions, padding a two-direction certificate if necessary, and every equality/boundary case.

projection-quantile-depth-region-obstruc.relation_to_goal: This abstracts the mechanism in accepted fact `eeb8a6b3b5e04d6c` from one rational triangle pair to arbitrary endpoint convex bodies. It yields an exact, all-direction prefilter for future counterexample searches: a translated containment \(z-A_2\subset\{d_{A_0}>m\}\) rules out every possible three-direction certificate before affine constants or middle extensions are considered.
projection-quantile-depth-region-obstruc.statement:
Let \(A_0,A_2\subset\mathbb R^2\) be compact two-dimensional convex bodies with areas \(M>m>0\). For \(p\in A_0\), let
\[
d_{A_0}(p)=\inf\{|A_0\cap H|:H\text{ is a closed planar halfspace containing }p\}.
\]
Suppose there exists \(z\in\mathbb R^2\) such that
\[
d_{A_0}(z-a)>m\qquad\text{for every }a\in A_2.
\]
For each nonzero linear form \(\lambda\), define
\[
q(\lambda)=\inf\{q:|A_0\cap\{\lambda\le q\}|\ge m\},
\qquad
\beta(\lambda)=\max_{a\in A_2}\lambda(a).
\]
Prove
\[
q(\lambda)+\beta(\lambda)<\lambda(z)
\]
for every nonzero \(\lambda\). Consequently every triple \(\lambda_1+\lambda_2+\lambda_3=0\) has
\[
\sum_i(q(\lambda_i)+\beta(\lambda_i))<0,
\]
and therefore cannot satisfy the counterexample projection-quantile budget in accepted fact `19703e1e768865b1`.
projection-quantile-depth-region-obstruc.status_reason: Accepted fact `4565d02e3cfa153e` proves the registered arbitrary-convex-body depth-region obstruction, including cap continuity, quantile attainment, strictness, and all support-line boundary cases.
projection-quantile-depth-region-obstruc.success_criterion: A self-contained proof of quantile attainment/continuity and the strict inequality for every nonzero direction, with no smoothness or strict-convexity assumptions and all support-line boundary cases covered.

projection-quantile-nonparallel-perturba.relation_to_goal: The exact erosion duality may initially return two opposite directions. Counterexample construction needs a nondegenerate planar fan. Strict positive budget should persist under a zero-sum generic perturbation once continuity of the cap quantile in the direction is proved.
projection-quantile-nonparallel-perturba.statement:
Under the hypotheses and notation of accepted fact `9aa8eaca3b60ecf3`, suppose no translate \(z-A_2\) is contained in \(D_m(A_0)\). Prove that there exist three pairwise nonparallel nonzero linear forms
\[
\lambda_1+\lambda_2+\lambda_3=0
\]
such that
\[
\sum_{i=1}^3(q(\lambda_i)+\beta(\lambda_i))>0.
\]
Consequently a common positive scaling makes the sum exceed \(2\). In particular, an empty depth erosion always has a genuinely two-dimensional projection-quantile survivor; it is not restricted to the two-direction Farkas degeneration.

quantitative-near-triangle-chord-section.statement:
Let
\[
\Delta=\operatorname{conv}\{(0,0),(1,0),(0,1)\},\qquad g=(1/3,1/3).
\]
Find an explicit rational \(\delta_{\mathrm{chord}}>0\) with the following property. Suppose \(K\subset\mathbb R^2\) is a compact two-dimensional convex body with
\[
|K\mathbin{\triangle}\Delta|\le\delta_{\mathrm{chord}}|K|.
\]
Let \(\varphi_1,\varphi_2,\varphi_3\) be proper affine functions whose three vertex-value vectors have Euclidean norm \(1\) and, after relabeling, lie within \(1/1000\) of the three permutations of
\[
\frac{(2,-1,-1)}{\sqrt6}.
\]
Put \(d_i=-\varphi_i(g)\) and
\[
L_i(u)=
\frac{\mathcal H^1(K\cap\{\varphi_i=\varphi_i(g)+u\})}
{\|\nabla\varphi_i\|}.
\]
Prove that some \(L_*>0\) satisfies
\[
\left|\frac{L_i(u)}{L_*}-1\right|\le\frac1{100}
\]
for every \(i\) and every \(|u|\le\max_j|d_j|\). Alternatively, give an exact convex sequence showing that no positive \(\delta_{\mathrm{chord}}\) can make this formulation true.

r134-final-three-slice-centerpoint.statement:
# Three-slice mixed-integer centerpoint problem

Let \(C\subset\mathbb{R}^3\) be a compact polytope such that

\[
S:=C\cap(\mathbb{Z}\times\mathbb{R}^2)
  =(\{0\}\times A_0)\cup(\{1\}\times A_1)\cup(\{2\}\times A_2),
\]

where each \(A_i\subset\mathbb{R}^2\) is a nonempty two-dimensional convex
body. Write

\[
a_i:=|A_i|,
\qquad
T:=a_0+a_1+a_2.
\]

For \(y\in S\), define its halfspace depth by

\[
h_S(y):=
\inf\left\{
\mathcal{H}_2(S\cap H):
H\subset\mathbb{R}^3\text{ is a closed halfspace and }y\in H
\right\}.
\]

Here \(\mathcal{H}_2\) is the two-dimensional Hausdorff measure, so
\(\mathcal{H}_2(S\cap H)\) is the sum of the planar areas contributed by the
three slices.

Determine whether there always exists \(y^*\in S\) such that

\[
h_S(y^*)\ge \frac{2}{9}T.
\]

## Statement

Let \(D\) be a nondegenerate triangle of physical area \(\Delta\), and use barycentric coordinates on \(D\). For real parameters \(a,b,c,d,e,f\), let \(H(a,b,c,d,e,f)\) be the possibly degenerate cyclic polygon with vertices
\[
\begin{aligned}
x_0&=(1-f,f,0),&x_1&=(a,1-a,0),\\
x_2&=(0,1-b,b),&x_3&=(0,c,1-c),\\
x_4&=(d,0,1-d),&x_5&=(1-e,0,e).
\end{aligned}
\]
Let \(\ell_a,\ell_b,\ell_c,\ell_d,\ell_e,\ell_f,s_1,s_2,s_3\in\mathbb Q\) be arbitrary, and impose
\[
\begin{gathered}
a,b,c,d,e,f\geq0,\qquad
a\geq\ell_a,\ b\geq\ell_b,\ c\geq\ell_c,\ d\geq\ell_d,\ e\geq\ell_e,\ f\geq\ell_f,\\
s_3\leq a+f\leq1,\qquad
s_1\leq b+c\leq1,\qquad
s_2\leq d+e\leq1.
\end{gathered}
\tag{1}
\]
Define the effective geometric lower bounds
\[
A=\max\{0,\ell_a\},\quad B=\max\{0,\ell_b\},\quad
C=\max\{0,\ell_c\},\quad D_0=\max\{0,\ell_d\},\quad
E=\max\{0,\ell_e\},\quad F=\max\{0,\ell_f\},
\tag{2}
\]
and the effective target sums
\[
t_3=\max\{s_3,A+F\},\qquad
t_1=\max\{s_1,B+C\},\qquad
t_2=\max\{s_2,D_0+E\}.
\tag{3}
\]
The bound polytope (1) is nonempty if and only if
\[
t_1\leq1,\qquad t_2\leq1,\qquad t_3\leq1.
\tag{4}
\]
Equivalently, all three effective lower-bound pair sums and all three requested lower sums are at most \(1\).

Assume (4). There is a loss minimizer with
\[
a+f=t_3,\qquad b+c=t_1,\qquad d+e=t_2.
\tag{5}
\]
For a specified pair, its requested constraint is itself tight, for example \(a+f=s_3\), if and only if \(s_3\geq A+F\); if \(s_3<A+F\), that equality is infeasible and the constraint is redundant. The analogous criteria are \(s_1\geq B+C\) and \(s_2\geq D_0+E\). Equality in these comparisons is allowed.

Put
\[
a_0=A,\quad a_1=t_3-F,\qquad
b_0=B,\quad b_1=t_1-C,\qquad
d_0=D_0,\quad d_1=t_2-E
\tag{6}
\]
and
\[
\Gamma(u,v,w)=uv+(t_1-v)w+(t_2-w)(t_3-u).
\tag{7}
\]
Then the exact minimum relative area loss is
\[
\begin{aligned}
m=\min\{&
\Gamma(a_0,b_0,d_0),\Gamma(a_0,b_0,d_1),
\Gamma(a_0,b_1,d_0),\Gamma(a_0,b_1,d_1),\\
&\Gamma(a_1,b_0,d_0),\Gamma(a_1,b_0,d_1),
\Gamma(a_1,b_1,d_0),\Gamma(a_1,b_1,d_1)\}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{8}
\]
Thus the exact maximum physical area in this closed fiber is
\[
\max |H|=\Delta(1-m).
\tag{9}
\]
The coefficient \(m\) and all feasibility and corner data in (2)-(8) are obtained by exact rational arithmetic and finite rational comparisons; (9) then multiplies by the physical scale \(\Delta\). Formula (8) remains valid when any interval in (6) collapses, when any parameter is zero, and when \(t_i=1\), which forces the corresponding support edge to have zero length. Points of (1) whose pair sum is \(1\) even when \(t_i<1\) are also included and are covered by the tightening argument.

For the numerical lower bounds, sums, and support-triangle scale in accepted fact `faa6f23d89f50659`, formula (8) gives
\[
m=
\frac{40\,351\,140\,305\,732\,756\,252\,537}
     {52\,732\,819\,270\,053\,605\,182\,500}
\]
and, with \(\Delta=9801/20000\),
\[
\max |H|=
\frac{12\,381\,678\,964\,320\,848\,929\,963}
     {107\,607\,018\,202\,333\,650\,000\,000}.
\tag{10}
\]
The certificate applies exactly to fibers with the displayed cyclic support-edge parametrization and constraints (1). It makes no assertion that a different cyclic order or a different support-incidence type admits the same parametrization.

## Proof

The nonnegativity constraints and the six stated lower bounds are equivalent to the effective bounds (2). If (1) has a feasible point, then
\[
a+f\geq\max\{s_3,A+F\}=t_3,
\]
while \(a+f\leq1\), so \(t_3\leq1\). The same argument gives \(t_1,t_2\leq1\). Conversely, if (4) holds, then
\[
(a,f)=(A,t_3-A),\qquad
(b,c)=(B,t_1-B),\qquad
(d,e)=(D_0,t_2-D_0)
\]
satisfy every constraint: for instance \(t_3-A\geq F\) follows from \(t_3\geq A+F\). This proves the exact feasibility test, including negative raw lower bounds and negative or redundant \(s_i\).

The relative loss is
\[
L(a,b,c,d,e,f)=ab+cd+ef.
\tag{11}
\]
It is coordinatewise nondecreasing on the nonnegative orthant. More explicitly, suppose \(a+f>t_3\), put \(r=a+f-t_3\), and choose
\[
\rho_a=\min\{r,a-A\},\qquad \rho_f=r-\rho_a.
\]
Since
\[
r\leq(a-A)+(f-F),
\]
we have \(0\leq\rho_a\leq a-A\) and \(0\leq\rho_f\leq f-F\). Replacing \(a,f\) by \(a-\rho_a,f-\rho_f\) preserves feasibility, makes their sum \(t_3\), and changes the loss by
\[
L(a-\rho_a,b,c,d,e,f-\rho_f)-L(a,b,c,d,e,f)
=-\rho_a b-\rho_f e\leq0.
\]
The identical construction for \(b,c\) decreases the loss by a quantity of the form \(\rho_b a+\rho_c d\), and that for \(d,e\) decreases it by a quantity of the form \(\rho_d c+\rho_e f\). Applying the three reductions successively proves (5), with no strict-positivity assumption. Hence zero partners and every tie are included.

The equality \(a+f=s_3\) is compatible with the lower bounds exactly when \(s_3\geq A+F\); under feasibility it is then the effective equality in (5). If \(s_3<A+F\), every feasible point has \(a+f\geq A+F>s_3\), so the requested equality is impossible. This proves the three stated tightness criteria.

On the equality face (5), eliminate
\[
f=t_3-a,\qquad c=t_1-b,\qquad e=t_2-d.
\]
The remaining feasible set is exactly the box
\[
[a_0,a_1]\times[b_0,b_1]\times[d_0,d_1],
\tag{12}
\]
because, for example, \(a\geq A\) and \(f\geq F\) are exactly \(a_0\leq a\leq a_1\). Its intervals are nonempty by (3). Substitution in (11) gives
\[
\Phi(a,b,d)=ab+(t_1-b)d+(t_2-d)(t_3-a)=\Gamma(a,b,d).
\tag{13}
\]
This polynomial is affine in each variable separately. If all three intervals in (12) have positive length, repeated one-dimensional affine interpolation expresses \(\Phi(a,b,d)\) as
\[
\sum_{i,j,k\in\{0,1\}}
\lambda_i(a)\mu_j(b)\nu_k(d)\Phi(a_i,b_j,d_k),
\tag{14}
\]
where the eight coefficients are nonnegative and sum to \(1\). Therefore every box value is at least the least corner value, and a corner realizing that least value is feasible. If an interval collapses, omit that interpolation step; (8) merely lists duplicate corners. Thus (8) is exact in every collapsed, zero-parameter, and slope-tie case.

The two vertices adjacent to the second barycentric corner cut from \(D\) a triangle of area \(\Delta ab\); the analogous corner triangles have areas \(\Delta cd\) and \(\Delta ef\). The upper sum constraints in (1) give the stated cyclic order, so these corner triangles have disjoint interiors. Consequently, including coincident vertices and collinear limits,
\[
|H|=\Delta(1-ab-cd-ef)=\Delta(1-L).
\tag{15}
\]
Combining (8), (11), and (15) proves (9).

For the data recorded in accepted fact `faa6f23d89f50659`, each requested sum exceeds its corresponding effective lower-bound sum, so \(t_i=s_i\), and (6) is exactly the three-variable box recorded there. Its exact margins give
\[
s_2-b_1-d_1>0,\qquad a_1-d_1>0,\qquad
a_1-b_0+s_1-s_3>0.
\]
Thus (13) first decreases to \(a=a_1\), then increases with \(b\) and with \(d\), selecting the corner \((a_1,b_0,d_0)\). Direct substitution gives the value of \(m\) and the scaled area in (10). The prescribed area in that predecessor exceeds (10) by
\[
\frac{11\,664\,845\,540\,778\,202\,767\,703}
     {122\,979\,449\,374\,095\,600\,000\,000}>0,
\]
so the general formula reproduces its numerical contradiction. This check uses only the fixed incidence type stated here and does not extend the conclusion to any other terminal code.

## Statement

Put
\[
\Pi=\{(y_1,y_2,y_3):y_1+y_2+y_3=1\},\qquad
p=\frac{199}{300},
\]
\[
D=\{y\in\Pi:y_i\leq p\ (i=1,2,3)\},\qquad
\delta=3p-1=\frac{99}{100},\qquad
\lambda_i=\frac{p-y_i}{\delta}.
\]
Thus \(\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\lambda_3\) are barycentric coordinates on
\(D\), and its three sides are
\(S_i=\{\lambda_i=0\}\).

Let \(A_2\) and \(K\) be the fixed rational polygons in accepted facts
`f22ebf3f8e4e4666` and `007cd9d294748c86`. Let \(A\) be any compact
two-dimensional convex polygon satisfying the invariant consequences
of an actual terminal first-event release:
\[
|A|=
M:=
\frac{481\,886\,268\,000\,037\,895\,503}
     {2\,295\,616\,388\,316\,451\,200\,000},
\tag{1}
\]
each endpoint cap \(A\cap\{y_i>p\}\) has area zero,
\[
\frac{A+A_2}{2}\subseteq K,
\tag{2}
\]
and every genuine vertex of \(A\) lies on \(\partial D\). Repeated
listed points and points made collinear at the release event may have
been deleted, in any number.

Then
\[
A\cap S_i\neq\varnothing\qquad(i=1,2,3).
\tag{3}
\]
In particular, the full crossing, cell-positivity, contact, and
zero-charge capacity hypotheses of the actual terminal state imply
(3), since accepted facts `f22ebf3f8e4e4666` and
`007cd9d294748c86` certify (1), (2), preservation of the zero caps,
two-dimensionality through the first event, and deletion without
changing the convex set.

## Proof

First, the zero-cap condition and two-dimensionality imply
\(A\subseteq D\). Indeed, suppose that some \(x\in A\) had
\(y_i(x)>p\). Choose interior points \(z_1,z_2\) such that
\(x,z_1,z_2\) are noncollinear. For all sufficiently small
\(\varepsilon>0\), both
\(x+\varepsilon(z_j-x)\) still satisfy \(y_i>p\). Their convex hull
with \(x\) is a positive-area triangle contained in
\(A\cap\{y_i>p\}\), contradicting the zero area of that cap.

For every \(x\in A\) and every vertex \(q\) of \(A_2\), (2) gives
\((x+q)/2\in K\), hence \(x\in2K-q\). Therefore
\[
A\subseteq
D\cap\bigcap_{q\in\operatorname{vert}(A_2)}(2K-q)=:F.
\tag{4}
\]
Accepted fact `faa6f23d89f50659` gives this exact admissible endpoint
region and, in the barycentric coordinates above, its
counterclockwise vertices:
\[
\begin{array}{c|ccc}
 &\lambda_1&\lambda_2&\lambda_3\\ \hline
v_0&\dfrac{1\,604\,909}{4\,410\,450}&
     \dfrac{2\,805\,541}{4\,410\,450}&0\\[1mm]
v_1&\dfrac{54\,077}{381\,150}&
     \dfrac{327\,073}{381\,150}&0\\[1mm]
v_2&0&\dfrac{99\,373}{153\,450}&
     \dfrac{54\,077}{153\,450}\\[1mm]
v_3&0&\dfrac{437}{1782}&\dfrac{1345}{1782}\\[1mm]
v_4&\dfrac{437}{4455}&0&\dfrac{4018}{4455}\\[1mm]
v_5&\dfrac{877\,259}{3\,682\,800}&0&
     \dfrac{2\,805\,541}{3\,682\,800}.
\end{array}
\tag{5}
\]
Consequently
\[
F\cap S_1=[v_2,v_3],\qquad
F\cap S_2=[v_4,v_5],\qquad
F\cap S_3=[v_0,v_1].
\tag{6}
\]

Suppose that \(A\cap S_i=\varnothing\) for some \(i\). Every genuine
vertex of \(A\) lies on \(\partial D=S_1\cup S_2\cup S_3\), so every
such vertex lies on the other two sides. By (4) and (6), \(A\), which
is the convex hull of its genuine vertices, is contained in the
corresponding four-endpoint hull:
\[
\begin{array}{c|c}
\text{missing side}&\text{containing hull}\\ \hline
S_1&Q_1=\operatorname{conv}\{v_4,v_5,v_0,v_1\}\\
S_2&Q_2=\operatorname{conv}\{v_0,v_1,v_2,v_3\}\\
S_3&Q_3=\operatorname{conv}\{v_2,v_3,v_4,v_5\}.
\end{array}
\tag{7}
\]
This containment does not require either contact interval in (6) to
have two distinct terminal vertices.

The physical area of \(D\) is
\[
\Delta=\frac{\delta^2}{2}=\frac{9801}{20000}.
\tag{8}
\]
Using \((\lambda_1,\lambda_2)\), the standard barycentric triangle has
coordinate area \(1/2\), so a shoelace area in those coordinates is
multiplied by \(2\Delta\). Exact substitution of (5) gives
\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c}
 &|Q_i|&M-|Q_i|\\ \hline
Q_1&
\dfrac{4\,700\,003\,535\,239}{33\,145\,200\,000\,000}&
\dfrac{305\,404\,067\,125\,655\,072\,143}
      {4\,483\,625\,758\,430\,568\,750\,000}\\[3mm]
Q_2&
\dfrac{2\,394\,647\,111\,471}{21\,751\,537\,500\,000}&
\dfrac{2\,772\,093\,294\,078\,263\,403\,463}
      {27\,769\,553\,084\,473\,200\,000\,000}\\[3mm]
Q_3&
\dfrac{1\,986\,705\,764\,389}{31\,136\,400\,000\,000}&
\dfrac{324\,929\,350\,963\,953\,271\,213\,529}
      {2\,223\,878\,376\,181\,562\,100\,000\,000}.
\end{array}
\tag{9}
\]
Every entry in the last column is strictly positive. Thus (7) would
give
\[
|A|\leq |Q_i|<M,
\]
contradicting (1). Hence no side can be missing, which proves (3).

It remains to check that deletion and degeneracy do not evade the
argument. Deleting a repeated point or a point lying between its two
neighbors does not change the convex set, its area, (2), its caps, or
its side contacts. If such a redundant point lies on a supporting
side \(S_i\), both endpoints of the containing segment also lie on
\(S_i\), because the nonnegative affine coordinate \(\lambda_i\)
vanishes at their convex combination only when it vanishes at both.
The same observation covers simultaneous collinear deletions.
One-point side contacts, triangle-corner contacts, and zero-length
support faces merely reduce the set of genuine vertices used in (7).
Finally, collapse to a segment or point is impossible because the
preserved value \(M\) in (1) is positive. Thus all deletion and
terminal-incidence degeneracies are included.

## Statement

Assume the Regime A scalar hypotheses and notation of accepted fact `879a3c45b5f50670`. Write the two closed endpoint cell rows as
\[
(p,x_i,x_\ell,\zeta)
\quad\hbox{and}\quad
(q,b_i,b_\ell,\omega),
\tag{1}
\]
where
\[
x_i=u_i-\zeta,\quad x_\ell=u_\ell-\zeta,\quad
b_i=v_i-\omega,\quad b_\ell=v_\ell-\omega.
\]
Thus
\[
p+x_i+x_\ell+\zeta=1,\qquad
q+b_i+b_\ell+\omega=r.
\tag{2}
\]

Consider only the following scalar requirements:
\[
c_i,c_\ell\ge0,\qquad
c_i+c_\ell\ge s-c_j,
\tag{3}
\]
\[
c_i+x_i+\zeta+b_i+\omega<t,\qquad
c_\ell+x_\ell+\zeta+b_\ell+\omega<t,
\tag{4}
\]
and the necessary scalar consequence of high-high midpoint containment in the \(j\)-cap,
\[
\frac14(\sqrt p+\sqrt q)^2\le c_j.
\tag{5}
\]
After \(c_i,c_\ell\) are projected out, (2)-(5), nonnegativity of all cells, and \(q>0\) are equivalent to
\[
\boxed{
\begin{gathered}
p>0,\quad q>0,\quad \zeta,\omega\ge0,\quad
p+\zeta\le1,\quad q+\omega\le r,\\
p+q>1+r+\zeta+\omega-\delta,\qquad
\frac14(\sqrt p+\sqrt q)^2\le c_j,\\
x_i+x_\ell=1-p-\zeta,\qquad
b_i+b_\ell=r-q-\omega,
\end{gathered}}
\tag{6}
\]
where \(\delta=2t-s+c_j\), and the last line allows every nonnegative split. This is an exact scalar projection only; it does not assert that every point of (6) is realized by convex bodies.

Every point of (6) also satisfies
\[
c_j>\frac t2+\frac{\zeta+\omega}{5},
\qquad
8r+\frac95(\zeta+\omega)<1+s.
\tag{7}
\]

Now fix precisely
\[
(r,s,t,c_i,c_\ell,c_j)
=
\left(
\frac1{16},\frac{47}{50},\frac{89}{200},
\frac{43}{100},\frac{43}{100},\frac{29}{80}
\right).
\tag{8}
\]
The rows
\[
\left(\frac{499}{500},\frac1{1000},\frac1{1000},0\right),
\qquad
\left(\frac1{25},\frac9{800},\frac9{800},0\right)
\tag{9}
\]
satisfy all scalar requirements (2)-(5), the Regime A window, and the root tail. In contrast, replacing only the two rows in (9) by the calibrated rows of accepted fact `bc026780453747b8`,
\[
\left(\frac{97}{100},\frac3{200},\frac3{200},0\right),
\qquad
\left(\frac9{200},\frac1{160},\frac1{160},\frac1{200}\right),
\tag{10}
\]
while holding all six quantities in (8) fixed violates both inequalities in (4). Therefore the universal fixed-cap scalar substitution
\[
\text{arbitrary scalar-feasible rows}\longmapsto\text{the rows in (10)}
\]
is invalid. This statement neither supplies an actual Alternative 1 counterexample nor excludes a geometric reduction based on additional constraints.

## Proof

Put
\[
m_i=x_i+\zeta+b_i+\omega,\qquad
m_\ell=x_\ell+\zeta+b_\ell+\omega.
\tag{11}
\]
If cap values satisfy (3)-(4), then
\[
s-c_j
\le c_i+c_\ell
<2t-m_i-m_\ell,
\]
and hence
\[
m_i+m_\ell<2t-s+c_j=\delta.
\tag{12}
\]
Conversely, suppose (12) holds. The Regime A window in `879a3c45b5f50670` gives
\[
\delta<\frac13<t<s.
\tag{13}
\]
Indeed, \(s>1-r\) gives \(t>4/9\), while \(r<1/3\) and \(s>1-r\) give
\[
7s>7(1-r)>2(1+r),
\]
which is equivalent to \(t<s\).
Thus \(t-m_i\) and \(t-m_\ell\) are positive, and
\[
(t-m_i)+(t-m_\ell)>s-c_j.
\tag{14}
\]
If \(s-c_j>0\), the open interval
\[
\left(
\max\{0,s-c_j-(t-m_\ell)\},
\min\{t-m_i,s-c_j\}
\right)
\]
is nonempty by (14). Choose \(c_i\) in it and put
\[
c_\ell=s-c_j-c_i.
\]
Then \(c_i,c_\ell\ge0\), (3) holds with equality, and both inequalities in (4) are strict. If \(s-c_j=0\), choose \(c_i=c_\ell=0\). The resulting cap values are also at most \(s\), because they are less than \(t<s\).

Using (2),
\[
\begin{aligned}
m_i+m_\ell
&=x_i+x_\ell+b_i+b_\ell+2\zeta+2\omega\\
&=1+r-p-q+\zeta+\omega.
\end{aligned}
\]
Therefore (12) is equivalent to the strict inequality for \(p+q\) in (6). All other cell conditions in (6) are exactly the nonnegative solutions of (2). Adjoining (5) proves the claimed equivalence.

Because \(p,q>0\), equation (6) gives
\[
4c_j
\ge(\sqrt p+\sqrt q)^2
>p+q
>1+r+\zeta+\omega-\delta.
\tag{15}
\]
The identity
\[
1+r-\delta=\frac52t-c_j
\]
turns (15) into the first inequality in (7). Combining that inequality with the root tail \(c_j+r<t\) gives
\[
r+\frac{\zeta+\omega}{5}<\frac t2
=\frac{1+r+s}{9},
\]
which is the second inequality in (7).

For (8), one has
\[
\delta=2t-s+c_j=\frac5{16}.
\tag{16}
\]
Moreover,
\[
0<\frac1{16}<\frac15,\qquad
\frac{15}{16}<\frac{47}{50}<\frac{17}{16},
\]
so these values lie in the first Regime A strip, and
\[
c_j+r=\frac{17}{40}<\frac{89}{200}=t,
\qquad
\delta=\frac5{16}\ge\frac1{16}=r.
\tag{17}
\]
Also
\[
0<\frac5{16}<\frac{2-s-r}{3}
=\frac{133}{400}<\frac13.
\]

The rows in (9) have totals \(1\) and \(1/16\), with \(q=1/25>0\). Their two low marginals are equal:
\[
m_i=m_\ell
=\frac1{1000}+\frac9{800}
=\frac{49}{4000}.
\tag{18}
\]
Hence, for both \(h=i,\ell\),
\[
c_h+m_h
=\frac{43}{100}+\frac{49}{4000}
=\frac{1769}{4000}
<\frac{1780}{4000}
=t.
\tag{19}
\]
The covering inequality in (3) holds because
\[
c_i+c_\ell+c_j
=\frac{489}{400}
>\frac{47}{50}=s.
\tag{20}
\]
Finally,
\[
\frac14\left(
\sqrt{\frac{499}{500}}+\sqrt{\frac1{25}}
\right)^2
<\frac{29}{80}.
\tag{21}
\]
Indeed, after multiplication by \(4\), inequality (21) is
\[
\frac25\sqrt{\frac{499}{500}}<\frac{103}{250},
\]
and its left side is less than \(2/5=100/250\). This verifies every scalar condition claimed for (9).

For the calibrated rows (10), each low marginal is instead
\[
\frac3{200}+\frac1{160}+\frac1{200}
=\frac{21}{800}.
\tag{22}
\]
With the six quantities in (8) unchanged,
\[
c_h+\frac{21}{800}
=\frac{43}{100}+\frac{21}{800}
=\frac{365}{800}
>\frac{356}{800}
=t
\qquad(h=i,\ell).
\tag{23}
\]
Thus the row replacement fails (4), proving exactly the stated failure of fixed-cap scalar substitution. Since no convex bodies are constructed, the proof makes no geometric-counterexample or general geometric-reduction claim.

|P+Q|=\frac{24079}{20000}<\frac43=4c_j.
\]
Hence neither compatibility at the level of total midpoint area nor the positive-cell root-cap area produces a contradiction.

This survivor is already nondegenerate in both adjacent mixed cells and lies in the fully outward split-apex order. Indeed, \(P\) has coordinate width \(101/20\) in each direction and maximum horizontal and vertical chord length \(1/5\), so
\[

Thus the calibrated aspect constant is false for an exact variable cell row even before considering the fully inward envelope branch. \]

## Statement

Assume the complete Alternative 1 hypotheses of accepted facts `bc026780453747b8` and `92a1b537d7e7876c`, and all notation, branch conditions, and scalar inequalities of accepted fact `8b69ff3587679629`.  Thus
\[
p=\frac{97}{100},\qquad
\delta=\frac3{100},\qquad
k=\frac{65+29\sqrt{65}}{400},
\]
\[
A=a+1,\qquad B=b+1,\qquad
0\le X\le A\le W,\qquad 0\le Y\le B\le H,
\]
and the applicable cap, defect, anchor, support-polygon, zero-level, chord-order, and maximum-chord inequalities of that accepted fact all hold.

First, for arbitrary real \(\alpha,\beta\), define
\[
\ell_1(u,v)=u-A-\alpha v,\qquad
\ell_2(u,v)=v-B-\beta u.
\]
For a counterclockwise cyclic vertex list \(V=(v_0,\ldots,v_{m-1})\) and an affine function \(\ell\), define \(\operatorname{Clip}_{\ell}(V)\) edge by edge.  For the directed edge \(p\to q\), concatenate the following list:
\[
\begin{array}{c|c}
(\ell(p),\ell(q))&\text{output}\\ \hline
\ell(p)\le0,\ \ell(q)\le0&(q)\\
\ell(p)\le0<\ell(q)&
\left(\dfrac{\ell(q)p-\ell(p)q}{\ell(q)-\ell(p)}\right)\\[2mm]
\ell(p)>0\ge\ell(q)&
\left(\dfrac{\ell(p)q-\ell(q)p}{\ell(p)-\ell(q)},q\right)\\[2mm]
\ell(p)>0,\ \ell(q)>0&()
\end{array}                                                    \tag{27}
\]
and delete consecutive repeated vertices.  Every denominator used in (27) is strictly positive in the branch in which it occurs.

Put
\[
V^{(0)}=((0,0),(W,0),(W,H),(0,H)),\qquad
V^{(1)}=\operatorname{Clip}_{\ell_1}(V^{(0)}),\qquad
V^{(2)}=\operatorname{Clip}_{\ell_2}(V^{(1)}).             \tag{28}
\]
If \(V^{(2)}=(z_0,\ldots,z_{m-1})\), cyclically, then the exact envelope formula is
\[
|\mathcal E|=
\begin{cases}
\displaystyle\frac12\sum_{i=0}^{m-1}\det(z_i,z_{i+1}),
&m\ge3,\quad z_m=z_0,\\[2mm]
0,&m<3.
\end{cases}                                                \tag{29}
\]
Equations (27)-(29) are a finite piecewise rational formula: the first clipping has at most five vertices and the second has at most six.  They cover every sign of \(\alpha,\beta\), all box-edge and box-corner incidences, redundant inequalities, collinearities, and all ties.

The possible non-box intersection coordinates generated by (27) are
\[
(A,0),\quad (A+\alpha H,H),\quad
\left(0,-\frac A\alpha\right),\quad
\left(W,\frac{W-A}{\alpha}\right),                         \tag{30}
\]
for the first line, with the last two used only after the sign of
\(\alpha\ne0\) and segment incidence have been fixed, and
\[
(0,B),\quad (W,B+\beta W),\quad
\left(-\frac B\beta,0\right),\quad
\left(\frac{H-B}{\beta},H\right),                          \tag{31}
\]
for the second line, with the last two treated analogously.  If the two outer lines cross, their intersection is
\[
\left(
\frac{A+\alpha B}{1-\alpha\beta},
\frac{B+\beta A}{1-\alpha\beta}
\right),                                                   \tag{32}
\]
and (32) is used only in a crossing branch, where the sign of
\(1-\alpha\beta\) has already been fixed.  If
\(\alpha\beta=1\), no division by \(1-\alpha\beta\) occurs.  In that
case
\[
\ell_2=-\beta\ell_1-(B+\beta A).                           \tag{33}
\]
For \(\beta<0\), the two halfplanes in (33) are coincident when
\(B+\beta A=0\), and otherwise one is redundant or is the stricter
parallel halfplane.  For \(\beta>0\), they cut out the parallel strip
\[
-A-\frac B\beta\le\ell_1\le0.
\]
Formula (29) applies unchanged in all of these parallel branches.

Adjoin to the complete scalar system of accepted fact
`8b69ff3587679629` the necessary inequality
\[
\frac pD+E\le|\mathcal E|.                                \tag{34}
\]
Then every scalar tuple in every one of its cap, defect, outer-slope,
support-polygon, zero-level, and chord-order branches satisfies
\[
\frac W{M_x}+\frac H{M_y}
<
\frac{5000}{291}.                                        \tag{35}
\]
In particular, the weak bound requested in the subgoal holds.

## Proof

Formula (27) is the exact intersection of a directed segment with one
closed affine halfplane.  In an inside-to-outside crossing its
intersection parameter has denominator
\(\ell(q)-\ell(p)>0\), while in an outside-to-inside crossing the
displayed denominator is \(\ell(p)-\ell(q)>0\).  Thus no division is
performed before its denominator sign is fixed.  Sequential clipping
of a convex counterclockwise polygon preserves its boundary order, so
(28) is exactly the intersection of the box and the two outer
halfplanes.  Formula (29) is its signed-triangle, equivalently
triangle/trapezoid-subtraction, area formula.  A boundary endpoint is
always treated as inside.  Consequently an edge or corner tie merely
creates a repeated or collinear vertex with zero signed contribution.
If all vertices satisfy an inequality, that clipping is unchanged,
which covers redundancy.  Direct solution of the relevant edge-line
and line-line equations gives (30)-(33).  This proves the claimed
boundary-complete formula, including \(\alpha=0\), \(\beta=0\), and
\(\alpha\beta=1\).

We now eliminate the augmented scalar system.  The case \(a=b=0\) is
immediate: equations (18) and (20) of accepted fact
`8b69ff3587679629` give \(M_x=W\) and \(M_y=H\), so the aspect sum is
\(2\).  Exactly one zero offset is excluded by the same accepted
fact.  Hence assume \(a,b>0\).

Set
\[
\xi=\frac1\sigma,\qquad
\eta=\frac1\rho,\qquad
d=\frac D\delta=\frac{100D}{3}.                           \tag{36}
\]
The inner-support conditions give
\[
\xi\ge\frac ab,\qquad
\eta\ge\frac ba,\qquad
\xi\eta\ge1.                                             \tag{37}
\]
Define the exact support-defect lower bound
\[
\Psi=
\begin{cases}
\displaystyle
\frac{a^2\eta+b^2\xi-2ab}{2(\xi\eta-1)},&\xi\eta>1,\\[2mm]
\displaystyle\frac{ab}{2},&\xi\eta=1.
\end{cases}                                               \tag{38}
\]
Equations (8)-(10) of accepted fact `8b69ff3587679629` say
\(E\ge\Psi\).  Its anchor, derived there from accepted facts
`92a1b537d7e7876c` and `bc026780453747b8`, therefore gives
\[
z:=D\Psi\le DE\le k.                                     \tag{39}
\]

The cap inequalities imply, without a sign assumption,
\[
\alpha\le d-\xi,\qquad \beta\le d-\eta.                  \tag{40}
\]
Indeed, if \(q_x=\alpha+\xi>0\), then
\(D\ge\delta q_x\); if \(q_x\le0\), then
\(\alpha\le-\xi<d-\xi\).  The proof for \(\beta\) is identical.

If \(Y>0\), the point \(R=(W,Y)\in K\) gives
\[
\alpha_K\ge\frac{W-A}{Y}.
\]
Together with \(\alpha\ge\alpha_K\), (40), and \(Y\le B\), this gives
\[
W\le A+B\max\{d-\xi,0\}.
\]
If \(Y=0\), the zero-level implication in accepted fact
`8b69ff3587679629` gives \(W=A\), so the same bound holds.  Coordinate
exchange gives
\[
H\le B+A\max\{d-\eta,0\}.                                \tag{41}
\]

Increasing either outer coefficient enlarges its halfplane on the
nonnegative quadrant.  Equations (40)-(41) therefore put
\(\mathcal E\) inside
\[
\begin{aligned}
\overline{\mathcal E}
={}&[0,A+B\max\{d-\xi,0\}]
\times[0,B+A\max\{d-\eta,0\}]\\
&{}\cap
\{(u,v):u-A\le(d-\xi)v,\quad
v-B\le(d-\eta)u\}.                                      \tag{42}
\end{aligned}
\]
Normalize \(u=AU\), \(v=BV\), and put
\[
r=(d-\xi)\frac BA,\qquad
s=(d-\eta)\frac AB.                                     \tag{43}
\]
Then
\[
|\overline{\mathcal E}|=AB\,F(r,s),                     \tag{44}
\]
where the complete exact branch formula is
\[
F(r,s)=
\begin{cases}
\displaystyle 1+\frac{r+s}{2}+rs,
&r\ge0,\ s\ge0,\\[2mm]
\displaystyle\frac{2+r+s}{2(1-rs)},
&
\begin{array}{l}
r\ge0,\ -1\le s\le0,\ \text{or}\\
s\ge0,\ -1\le r\le0,\ \text{or}\\
-1\le r\le0,\ -1\le s\le0,\\
(r,s)\ne(-1,-1),
\end{array}\\[5mm]
\displaystyle-\frac1{2s},
&s\le-1,\ r\ge-1,\\[2mm]
\displaystyle-\frac1{2r},
&r\le-1,\ s\ge-1,\\[2mm]
\displaystyle\frac{2rs+r+s}{2rs(rs-1)},
&r\le-1,\ s\le-1,\ (r,s)\ne(-1,-1),\\[2mm]
\displaystyle\frac12,&r=s=-1.
\end{cases}                                               \tag{45}
\]
On overlaps along branch boundaries the displayed values agree.
For \(r,s\ge0\), (45) is the area of the enlarged box after
subtracting the two disjoint corner triangles of areas \(r/2\) and
\(s/2\).  The second branch is the signed trapezoid with the two-line
intersection
\[
\left(\frac{1+r}{1-rs},\frac{1+s}{1-rs}\right).
\]
In the third and fourth branches one descending outer line cuts out
the contained triangle.  In the fifth branch the two descending
triangles meet in a four-vertex polygon.  The last branch is the
parallel/coincident line \(U+V=1\).  Thus (45) also follows directly
from (27)-(29), with no omitted edge or equality case.

We need one exact inequality for (45).  Put \(t=A/B>0\) and
\[
L=\xi+\eta+2-2d=2-rt-\frac{s}{t}.                        \tag{46}
\]
If \(L>0\), then every branch of (45) satisfies
\[
ABF(r,s)\le\frac{(A+B)^2}{2L}.                           \tag{47}
\]
Here are division-free certificates for all branches.  After dividing
the difference in (47) by \(AB\), it is enough to prove
\[
t+\frac1t+2-2F(r,s)
\left(2-rt-\frac{s}{t}\right)\ge0.                       \tag{48}
\]

For \(r,s\ge0\), set
\[
c=2+r+s+2rs.
\]
Multiplication of (48) by \(t\) gives the quadratic
\[
(1+cr)t^2+2(1-c)t+(1+cs),
\]
whose discriminant is
\[
-4rs(r+s+2rs)c\le0.
\]
For the second branch, the left side of (48) is exactly
\[
\frac{(1+s-t-rt)^2}{(1-rs)t}\ge0.                        \tag{49}
\]
For \(s\le-1,\ r\ge-1\), it is
\[
\frac{2(1+s)+t(s-r)}{s}\ge0,                             \tag{50}
\]
because both terms in the numerator are nonpositive and \(s<0\).
The coordinate-swapped branch is identical; explicitly its value is
\[
\frac{r-s+2t(1+r)}{rt}\ge0.                              \tag{51}
\]
For \(r=-R\le-1\), \(s=-S'\le-1\), multiplication by the positive
denominator \(RS'(RS'-1)t\) leaves
\[
\begin{aligned}
&S'^2(R-1)^2\\
&\quad+2t\bigl(R+S'-3RS'+R^2S'^2\bigr)
+R^2t^2(S'-1)^2.                                        \tag{52}
\end{aligned}
\]
Writing \(R=1+u\), \(S'=1+v\), the middle parenthesis in
(52) is
\[
u^2+uv+2u^2v+v^2+2uv^2+u^2v^2\ge0.
\]
Finally, \(r=s=-1\) makes (48) zero.  This proves (47) on all open
branches and all their boundaries.

The support defect supplies the matching lower denominator.  If
\(\xi\eta>1\), let
\[
G=\begin{pmatrix}\xi&1\\1&\eta\end{pmatrix}.
\]
This matrix is positive definite and
\[
2\Psi=(a,b)G^{-1}(a,b)^{\mathsf T}.
\]
Cauchy-Schwarz in the \(G\)-inner product gives
\[
(a+b)^2
\le 2\Psi(\xi+\eta+2).                                  \tag{53}
\]
If \(\xi\eta=1\), (37) forces
\(\xi=a/b\), \(\eta=b/a\), and (53) is equality because
\(\Psi=ab/2\).  Thus (53) is valid in every support branch.

Put \(S=a+b\).  If \(L\le0\), (53) gives
\[
S^2\le4d\Psi=\frac{4z}{\delta}\le\frac{4k}{\delta}.       \tag{54}
\]
The same conclusion holds whenever \(S^2\le4d\Psi\), regardless of
the sign of \(L\).  Otherwise \(L>0\) and (53) gives
\[
L\ge\frac{S^2-4d\Psi}{2\Psi}>0.
\]
Combining this with (42), (44), and (47) yields
\[
|\mathcal E|
\le ABF(r,s)
\le
\frac{\Psi(S+2)^2}{S^2-4d\Psi}.                          \tag{55}
\]

The augmented envelope inequality (34) and \(E\ge\Psi\) give
\[
\frac pD+\Psi\le|\mathcal E|.
\]
Multiply this and (55) by \(D=\delta d\), and use
\(z=D\Psi\):
\[
p+z
\le
\frac{z(S+2)^2}{S^2-4z/\delta}.
\]
After multiplying by the positive denominator and cancelling
\(zS^2\), this is
\[
pS^2
\le
4z\left(S+1+\frac{p+z}{\delta}\right)
\le
4k\left(S+1+\frac{p+k}{\delta}\right),                   \tag{56}
\]
where the last step uses \(0<z\le k\).

Let
\[
S_0=\frac{4418}{291}
=\frac{5000}{291}-2
\]
and
\[
P(S)=pS^2-4k\left(S+1+\frac{p+k}{\delta}\right).
\]
Exact substitution gives
\[
P(S_0)
=
\frac{24{,}962{,}933-3{,}005{,}067\sqrt{65}}
     {174{,}600}
>0,                                                       \tag{57}
\]
because
\[
24{,}962{,}933^2
-65\cdot3{,}005{,}067^2
=36{,}170{,}225{,}120{,}704>0.
\]
Also
\[
P'(S_0)=\frac{8{,}641-87\sqrt{65}}{300}>0,               \tag{58}
\]
because
\[
8{,}641^2-65\cdot87^2=74{,}174{,}896>0.
\]
Since \(P'\) is increasing, (57)-(58) show that \(P(S)>0\)
for every \(S\ge S_0\).  Inequality (56), which says
\(P(S)\le0\), therefore implies \(S<S_0\).

The alternative estimate (54) gives the same conclusion, because
\[
S_0^2-\frac{4k}{\delta}
=
\frac{17{,}683{,}969-818{,}583\sqrt{65}}{84{,}681}
>0,                                                       \tag{59}
\]
and
\[
17{,}683{,}969^2
-65\cdot818{,}583^2
=269{,}167{,}681{,}280{,}176>0.
\]
Thus every augmented scalar branch has
\[
a+b+2<S_0+2=\frac{5000}{291}.                            \tag{60}
\]

It remains only to pass from offsets to the requested chord aspect.
If \(b\le Y\), equation (18) of accepted fact
`8b69ff3587679629` gives \(W/M_x=1\le A\).  If \(Y<b\), equation
(19) gives
\[
M_x\ge G_x
=W-\frac{a(b-Y)}b
\ge W-a,
\]
and hence, using \(W\ge A=a+1\),
\[
\frac W{M_x}\le\frac W{W-a}\le a+1=A.                   \tag{61}
\]
The coordinate-swapped chord formulas give
\[
\frac H{M_y}\le b+1=B.                                  \tag{62}
\]
Equations (60)-(62) prove (35).  All inherited cap, defect, anchor,
support-polygon, chord-order, redundancy, and tie branches were kept:
the proof used necessary consequences common to all of them and did
not assert actual-body realizability.

## Statement

Assume the complete Alternative 1 hypotheses of accepted facts `bc026780453747b8` and `92a1b537d7e7876c`.  Normalize the full positive coordinate-axis traces of \(P\) as in accepted fact `8b69ff3587679629`:
\[
[a,A]\times\{0\},\qquad \{0\}\times[b,B],
\qquad A=a+1,\quad B=b+1,
\]
and let \(D>0\) be the product of the two physical trace lengths.  Put
\[
p=\frac{97}{100},\qquad c=\frac3{200}.
\]
Thus the normalized positive-cell area is \(p/D\), and each normalized mixed-cap area is \(c/D\).

Choose a rightmost point \(R=(W,Y)\in P\) and a topmost point
\(T=(X,H)\in P\), with \(R\ne T\), and assume the mixed order
\[
0\leq X\leq A\leq W,\qquad 0\leq B\leq Y\leq H.
\tag{1}
\]
Then
\[
K=\operatorname{conv}\{(a,0),(A,0),R,T,(0,B),(0,b)\}
\subseteq P
\tag{2}
\]
has area
\[
T_K=\frac{AY+WH-XY+XB-ab}{2}.
\tag{3}
\]
The exact maximum horizontal chord length \(M_x=m_x(K)\) is obtained as follows.  Set
\[
G=A+\frac{(W-A)B}{Y}.
\tag{4}
\]
If \(H>B\), set
\[
J_x=W-\frac{X(Y-B)}{H-B};
\tag{5}
\]
then
\[
M_x=\max\{G,J_x\}.
\tag{6}
\]
If \(H=B\), necessarily \(Y=H=B\), and
\[
M_x=W=G.
\tag{7}
\]
The exact maximum vertical chord length \(M_y=m_y(K)\) is
\[
M_y=H\qquad(a\leq X).
\tag{8}
\]
If \(X<a\), then \(a>0\) and \(W>X\); setting
\[
G_y=H-\frac{b(a-X)}a,\qquad
J_y=H-\frac{(H-Y)(a-X)}{W-X},
\tag{9}
\]
one has
\[
M_y=\max\{G_y,J_y\}.
\tag{10}
\]
All equalities in (1), both alternatives \(a,b>0\) and \(a=b=0\), all collinear support faces, and the ties in (6) and (10) are included in (2)-(10).

For completeness, let
\[
\widehat\alpha
=\sup_{\substack{(u,v)\in P\\v>0}}\frac{u-A}{v},
\qquad
\widehat\beta
=\sup_{\substack{(u,v)\in P\\u>0}}\frac{v-B}{u}.
\tag{11}
\]
For positive inner supporting coefficients \(\sigma,\rho\) supplied by accepted fact `8b69ff3587679629`, put
\[
q_x=\widehat\alpha+\frac1\sigma,\qquad
q_y=\widehat\beta+\frac1\rho.
\tag{12}
\]
If \(q_x>0\), respectively \(q_y>0\), the corresponding normalized mixed cap is contained in a triangle of area \(1/(2q_x)\), respectively \(1/(2q_y)\).  If either quantity is zero, the two relevant support lines form a constant-width unbounded strip; if it is negative, they form an expanding wedge.  Thus (11)-(12) also cover nonattainment, zero outer coefficients, parallel supports, and every denominator degeneration without interpreting a zero denominator as a finite triangle.

Every actual \(P\) satisfying (1) obeys
\[
\frac{W}{m_x(P)}+\frac{H}{m_y(P)}
\leq\frac{5000}{291}.
\tag{13}
\]
The same conclusion holds for the coordinate-exchanged mixed order
\[
0\leq A\leq X\leq W,\qquad 0\leq Y\leq B\leq H.
\tag{14}
\]

## Proof

Accepted fact `8b69ff3587679629`, under the hypotheses of accepted facts `bc026780453747b8` and `92a1b537d7e7876c`, proves that an actual normalized trace has either \(a,b>0\) or \(a=b=0\).  It also supplies finite positive inner support coefficients satisfying
\[
y+\sigma(x-a)\geq0,\qquad x+\rho(y-b)\geq0
\tag{15}
\]
on the full normalized body.  When \(a,b>0\),
\[
b\geq\sigma a,\qquad a\geq\rho b,\qquad \sigma\rho\leq1.
\tag{16}
\]
When \(a=b=0\), choose one supporting line \(y+\sigma x=0\) at the origin and use the same line in the second form in (15), so that \(\rho=1/\sigma\).  Hence in every case relevant below the supports may be chosen with
\[
\sigma\rho\leq1.
\tag{17}
\]

We first justify the support polygon and all chord formulas.  The six successive cross products of the displayed vertex list in (2) are
\[
Y,\quad
(W-A)(H-Y)+Y(W-X),\quad
(W-X)(H-B)+X(H-Y),\quad
X,\quad a,\quad b.
\tag{18}
\]
They are nonnegative under (1).  The two boundary chains are coordinate-monotone, so after deleting coincident generators the list is simple; (18) therefore gives the boundary order of the convex polygon \(K\).  Zero values in (18) are exactly allowed collinear faces, including the coincident southwest generator when \(a=b=0\).  Shoelace gives (3).

Horizontal section length is affine between consecutive levels in
\(\{0,b,B,Y,H\}\).  At level \(B\), the segment from \((A,0)\) to \(R\) gives the chord of length \(G\).  If \(H>B\), the chord at level \(Y\) has left endpoint on the segment from \((0,B)\) to \(T\), hence has length \(J_x\).  The chord at level \(b\) has length
\[
A+\frac{(W-A)b}{Y}\leq G,
\]
the level-zero chord has length one, and the remaining vertex levels give no larger length.  This proves (4)-(6), including \(Y=B\), when \(G=J_x=W\), and \(Y=H\), when \(J_x=W-X\) is the possibly nontrivial top-face length.  If \(H=B\), (1) forces \(Y=H=B\), and the level-\(B\) chord has length \(W\), proving (7).  Thus no division by \(H-B\) is made on its zero stratum.

If \(a\leq X\), then \((X,0)\) belongs to the full horizontal trace and the segment from \((X,0)\) to \(T\) is a vertical chord of length \(H\).  No vertical chord can be longer, proving (8), including \(X=a\) and \(X=A\).  If \(X<a\), vertical section length is affine between consecutive levels in \(\{0,X,a,A,W\}\).  At abscissa \(X\) its length is \(G_y\), and at abscissa \(a\) its length is \(J_y\).  The level-zero vertical trace has length one; moreover \(G_y\geq1\).  Indeed, if \(X=0\), the full-trace implication in accepted fact `8b69ff3587679629` gives \(H=B\), so \(G_y=B-b=1\); if \(X>0\), then
\[
G_y\geq B-\frac{b(a-X)}a=1+\frac{bX}{a}\geq1.
\]
The section at \(A\) is no longer than the one at \(a\), and the rightmost section contributes no larger value.  This proves (9)-(10), including their maximum tie.  The branch \(X<a\) itself guarantees \(a>0\) and \(W-X>0\), so every denominator in (9) is positive.  Since \(K\subseteq P\) and \(K,P\) have the same coordinate widths,
\[
m_x(P)\geq M_x,\qquad m_y(P)\geq M_y.
\tag{19}
\]

The cap alternatives in (11)-(12) are the division-free alternatives proved in accepted fact `8b69ff3587679629`; they can also be seen directly by writing a lower-cap level as \(y=-t\).  Equations (15) and (11) confine its horizontal section to
\[
a+\frac t\sigma\leq x\leq A-\widehat\alpha t,
\]
whose available length is \(1-q_xt\).  If \(q_x>0\), integration up to \(1/q_x\) gives \(1/(2q_x)\); \(q_x=0\) and \(q_x<0\) give respectively the strip and wedge.  The vertical-section argument for the left cap is identical.  This verifies all cap and denominator assertions without assuming that either supremum in (11) is attained.

We now prove (13).  If \(Y=H\), then \(R\) simultaneously realizes both coordinate maxima.  If \(X=W\), then \(T\) does so.  In either case accepted fact `72d4135e14ce0663` gives (13), with no uniqueness or exposedness assumption.  These common-apex strata include \(H=B\), because then \(Y=H=B\).
Indeed, the normalized axis traces and \(P\subseteq\{x,y\geq0\}\) show that the coordinate widths occurring in that accepted fact are exactly \(W\) and \(H\).

It remains to assume
\[
Y<H,\qquad X<W.
\tag{20}
\]
Then \(H>B\).  The full-trace implication
\[
X=0\Longrightarrow H=B
\]
from accepted fact `8b69ff3587679629` shows that \(X>0\).  Define the finite endpoint coefficients
\[
\alpha=\frac{W-A}{Y}\geq0,\qquad
\beta=\frac{H-B}{X}>0,
\tag{21}
\]
and
\[
G=A+\alpha B,\qquad F=B+\beta A,\qquad q=\frac GW.
\tag{22}
\]
The endpoint choices in (21) occur among the ratios in (11), so
\[
\widehat\alpha\geq\alpha,\qquad
\widehat\beta\geq\beta.
\tag{23}
\]
In particular both cap coefficients in (12) are positive.  Since each normalized mixed-cap area is \(c/D\), their triangular capacities give
\[
D\geq2c\left(\alpha+\frac1\sigma\right),\qquad
D\geq2c\left(\beta+\frac1\rho\right).
\tag{24}
\]
Adding (24), and using (17), yields
\[
D\geq c\left(\alpha+\beta+\frac1\sigma+\frac1\rho\right)
\geq c(2+\alpha+\beta).
\tag{25}
\]

Because \(K\subseteq P\), equations (2)-(3) give
\[
DT_K\leq p.
\tag{26}
\]
Put
\[
L=T_K(2+\alpha+\beta).
\tag{27}
\]
Equations (25)-(26) imply the exact upper bound
\[
L\leq\frac pc=\frac{194}{3}.
\tag{28}
\]

We next extract a lower bound for \(L\) from the mixed support order.  Equations (21)-(22) give
\[
W=A+\alpha Y,\qquad H=B+\beta X.
\tag{29}
\]
Substitution into (3), using \(AB-ab=A+B-1\), gives the exact identity
\[
2T_K
=A+B-1+GY+FX-(1-\alpha\beta)XY.
\tag{30}
\]
Moreover,
\[
F-(1-\alpha\beta)Y
=(H-Y)+\beta(W-X)\geq0.
\tag{31}
\]
Thus
\[
2T_K\geq A+B-1+GY.
\tag{32}
\]

Since \(B\leq Y\), one has \(0<q\leq1\).  If \(q=1\), then
\[
\frac W{M_x}\leq\frac WG=1,
\tag{33}
\]
so the required horizontal estimate below is immediate.  Suppose \(q<1\), and set
\[
s=\sqrt{1-q}\in(0,1).
\tag{34}
\]
Then \(\alpha>0\), and
\[
Y=B+\frac{(1-q)G}{\alpha q}.
\tag{35}
\]
Using \(A,B\geq1\) and \(G=A+\alpha B\geq1+\alpha\), equations (32) and (35) give
\[
2T_K
\geq
2+\alpha+\frac{(1+\alpha)^2s^2}{\alpha(1-s^2)}.
\tag{36}
\]
The arithmetic-geometric mean inequality gives
\[
\alpha+\frac{(1+\alpha)^2s^2}{\alpha(1-s^2)}
\geq\frac{2s}{1-s},
\]
and therefore
\[
T_K\geq\frac1{1-s}.
\tag{37}
\]

On the other hand,
\[
1-q=\frac{\alpha(Y-B)}W.
\tag{38}
\]
Since \(H-B\geq Y-B\) and \(0<X\leq W\), equations (21) and (38) give
\[
\alpha\beta\geq1-q=s^2.
\tag{39}
\]
Hence
\[
2+\alpha+\beta\geq2(1+s).
\tag{40}
\]
Combining (27), (28), (37), and (40),
\[
\frac{2(1+s)}{1-s}\leq\frac{194}{3}.
\]
Thus \(s\leq47/50\), and
\[
q=1-s^2\geq\frac{291}{2500}.
\tag{41}
\]
Equations (4), (6), (19), and (41), together with the already treated case \(q=1\), prove
\[
\frac{W}{m_x(P)}
\leq\frac W{M_x}
\leq\frac WG
\leq\frac{2500}{291}.
\tag{42}
\]

\[

\tag{43}
\]
If \(X<a\), put

d=\frac{b(a-X)}a.
\]
Then \(0\leq d\leq b<Y\), while (9) gives \(G_y=H-d\) and \(J_y\geq Y\).  If \(H\leq2Y\), then \(J_y\geq H/2\).  If \(H>2Y\), then
\[
G_y=H-d>H-Y>\frac H2.
\]
Consequently (10) and (19) give
\[
\frac{H}{m_y(P)}\leq2.
\tag{44}
\]
Equations (42)-(44) yield the stronger bound
\[
\frac{W}{m_x(P)}+\frac{H}{m_y(P)}
\leq\frac{2500}{291}+2
=\frac{3082}{291}
<\frac{5000}{291},
\tag{45}
\]
which proves (13) on every non-common-apex stratum.

Finally consider (14).  Under the coordinate exchange
\((x,y)\mapsto(y,x)\), define
\[
a'=b,\quad A'=B,\quad b'=a,\quad B'=A,
\]
\[
R'=(W',Y')=(H,X),\qquad
T'=(X',H')=(Y,W).
\]
Then (14) becomes
\[
0\leq X'\leq A'\leq W',\qquad
0\leq B'\leq Y'\leq H',
\]
which is exactly (1).  Distinct support points, zero offsets, endpoint equalities, common-apex incidences, collinear faces, maximum-chord ties, and denominator-degenerate strata are merely interchanged.  Moreover
\[
\frac{W'}{m_x(P')}+\frac{H'}{m_y(P')}
=\frac{H}{m_y(P)}+\frac{W}{m_x(P)}.
\]
Thus the already proved boundary-complete result applies to (14), completing the coordinate-exchanged case.

residual-enlargement-cap-shaving.relation_to_goal: Accepted theorem `96f5513b8ab88a8f` makes the right-hand side nonnegative. The displayed monotonicity, or a complete minimal-counterexample reduction to \(K=B\), would therefore prove the locked target throughout the only area regime not already covered by accepted facts.
residual-enlargement-cap-shaving.statement:
Let \(A_0,A_2\subset\mathbb R^2\) be nonempty two-dimensional convex polytopes, let \(B=(A_0+A_2)/2\), and let \(B\subseteq K\) be a two-dimensional convex polytope. In the exact residual area regime of accepted fact `15bb2c1680a0254e`, prove that enlarging the middle slice from \(B\) to \(K\) cannot make the optimal normalized depth surplus negative. Equivalently, prove
\[
\max_{z\in K}h_{S_K}((1,z))-\frac{2(|A_0|+|K|+|A_2|)}9
\ge
\max_{z\in B}h_{S_B}((1,z))-\frac{2(|A_0|+|B|+|A_2|)}9,
\]
or prove a cap-shaving lemma that reduces every strict negative-surplus counterexample \(K\supsetneq B\) to a strictly smaller one and rigorously terminates at \(B\).
residual-enlargement-cap-shaving.status_reason: Accepted fact `ff63745f58556ffa` disproves the registered middle-only endpoint premise and identifies the endpoint-correct replacement as all-slice optimal-surplus monotonicity.
residual-enlargement-cap-shaving.success_criterion: Give a complete inclusion-monotonicity proof or a complete exposed-cap removal argument, including existence of an optimal witness, continuity under convex shaving, strict inequalities, and the limiting or finite termination step. residual-enlargement-cover-dual.relation_to_goal: This is the dual form of the sole remaining bridge \(B\subseteq A_1\). A valid transformation from a strict low-mass cover of \(S_K\) to a forbidden cover or depth violation for \(S_B\) would combine with `96f5513b8ab88a8f` to prove the locked target.
residual-enlargement-cover-dual.statement: Let \(B=(A_0+A_2)/2\subseteq K=A_1\) and assume the exact residual area regime of accepted fact `15bb2c1680a0254e`. Starting from the strict low-mass halfspace covers supplied by accepted fact `8f5f00ddd4f22d2f` under failure of the target for \(S_K\), prove an exact nested-cover inequality that contradicts the accepted minimal-family theorem `96f5513b8ab88a8f`. The argument must use the added middle region \(E=K\setminus B\) jointly across the at most three covering halfspaces, rather than requiring a fixed minimal-family witness to transfer.
residual-enlargement-cover-dual.status_reason: The exact obstacle proves that scalar cover allocation only recovers the residual inequality \(k+m<2M\) and isolates the missing geometry-sensitive three-cover excess bound.
residual-enlargement-cover-dual.success_criterion: Prove a self-contained joint allocation or cover-transformation lemma covering one, two, and three halfspaces, strict mass thresholds, zero planar normals, and all three slice covers. residual-enlargement-depth-region.relation_to_goal: The accepted normal form converts the remaining theorem into nonemptiness of an intersection of directional convex constraints. residual-enlargement-depth-region.statement: For \(B=(A_0+A_2)/2\subseteq K=A_1\), extend the exact directional superlevel-region construction of accepted fact `a6099e9164a694ce` from the minimal middle slice \(B\) to the enlarged slice \(K\). At threshold \(2(|A_0|+|K|+|A_2|)/9\) in the residual area regime, prove that every three directional superlevel halfplanes have a common point in \(K\), using \(B\subseteq K\) and accepted theorem `96f5513b8ab88a8f`; planar Helly would then give a universal middle-slice witness.
residual-enlargement-depth-region.status_reason: The exact obstacle records the enlarged directional functional, disproves pointwise nesting, excludes one- and two-halfplane covers, and reduces the remaining three-direction question to a joint surplus-allocation inequality.

A restatement of planar Helly without the missing three-direction estimate is not sufficient. If that estimate is false, return an exact obstruction and the weakest corrected estimate that could still close the bridge.

residual-full-balanced-threshold.relation_to_goal: Accepted fact `9328166a552ec875` makes this inequality sufficient for nonemptiness of the exact middle depth region, while accepted fact `2fdbcddaa185b50e` shows that the unconditional version is false only through a large-slice regime. residual-full-balanced-threshold.statement:

\[

\]
for every noncollinear positive-spanning triple \(\sum_i\alpha_iq_i=0\), using the exact direction-dependent optimizers and full endpoint infimal convolution. If the inequality is false even on the residual strip, give exact compatible rational polygons and determine whether another slice still supplies the locked target.

residual-rational-equality-triple.statement:

residual-rational-equality-triple.status_reason:

positively. At \(y_*=(1,-1,-1/5)\), an explicit centrally symmetric

residual-rational-equality-triple.success_criterion:

residual-three-cover-excess.relation_to_goal: Failure of the locked target yields strict low-mass covers by accepted fact `8f5f00ddd4f22d2f`. The residual area inequalities rule out one- and two-member middle covers. The displayed bound makes the sum of the three halfspace masses at least \(2T/3=3t\), contradicting their three strict upper bounds. Thus it would close the sole remaining arbitrary-enlargement regime.
residual-three-cover-excess.statement:
Let \(A_0,A_2,K\subset\mathbb R^2\) be nonempty two-dimensional convex polytopes, let
\[
B=\frac{A_0+A_2}{2}\subseteq K,\qquad
M=\max\{|A_0|,|A_2|\},\quad
m=\min\{|A_0|,|A_2|\},\quad
k=|K|,
\]
and assume the exact residual area regime of accepted fact `15bb2c1680a0254e`. Put \(T=M+m+k\) and \(t=2T/9\). Suppose three proper closed halfspaces \(H_j\subset\mathbb R^3\), each of slice mass strictly below \(t\), have interiors covering \(\{1\}\times K\). For
\[
P_{ij}=\{w\in\mathbb R^2:(i,w)\in H_j\},
\qquad i=0,1,2,\quad j=1,2,3,
\]
prove the geometry-sensitive excess inequality
\[
\left(\sum_{j=1}^3|K\cap P_{1j}|-k\right)
+
\left(\sum_{j=1}^3
\bigl(|A_0\cap P_{0j}|+|A_2\cap P_{2j}|\bigr)-m\right)
\ge
\frac{2M-k-m}{3}.
\]
residual-three-cover-excess.status_reason: The summed three-cover excess inequality is stronger than necessary. Exact round-22 calibrations show that its unconditional geometric mechanism fails, while the weaker canonical lifting-aware per-member allocation directly rules out the remaining cover.
residual-three-cover-excess.success_criterion: Prove the displayed inequality for every admissible three-halfspace cover, including zero planar normals, boundary-null issues, repeated or redundant halfspaces, and all residual endpoints. The proof must use actual affine geometry, not only scalar cap totals. If the inequality is false, give an exact geometric counterexample to this auxiliary inequality, identify which part of the locked-theorem contradiction survives, and state the weakest corrected joint inequality to test next. Do not search for a counterexample to the locked theorem.

same-index-centroid-routing-closure.relation_to_goal:

Prove that if some \(H_i\) contains both \((1,g_1)\) and \((j,g_j)\) in

\[
\mathcal H_2(S\cap H_i)>\frac{2T}{9}.
\]

six-cap-cover-exclusion.relation_to_goal: Together with the five-cap case and accepted fact `9b0c3eb7dcfba2c2`, this is exactly equivalent to the locked theorem. It is independent of the directionwise chain-cover and triangle calculations.

Use planar Helly on each slice to classify the subfamilies of at most three induced halfplanes that cover \(A_0,A_1,A_2\), and retain that deleting any cap must expose a point of \(S\). six-cap-pullback-centroid-ledger.relation_to_goal: This identifies the exact joint transport inequality left by the six-cap shifted reversal and localizes both endpoint areas. It prevents separate lower-profile or private-witness arguments from being mistaken for the remaining bridge.
six-cap-pullback-centroid-ledger.statement:

\[
N_z(x)=\sum_{j\in L}\mathbf1_{\{g_j(0,x)\le-g_j(2,z)\}},
\qquad

Prove:
\[
\sum_{j\in L}\left(F_j(0)-F_j(-g_j(2,z))\right)=E_0-X(z),
\]
the requested shifted reversal follows from
\[
|R_2|+\inf_{z\in R_2}X(z)
\le E_0+E_1+C_2+\Lambda_U,

the centroid of \(A_2\) lies strictly in \(R_2\), and
\[
a_2<\frac T2,\qquad a_0<\frac{2T}{5}.
\]
six-cap-pullback-centroid-ledger.status_reason: Accepted fact `84ac95a4d0cfd458` proves the pullback-multiplicity identity, the exact conditional joint-transport bridge, centroid localization, and both endpoint area bounds.

+E_1+C_2

six-cap-shifted-cap-reversal.success_criterion: Success is a complete proof using the actual three affine cap profiles, their height coupling, the large opposite triangular region, the upper leakage budget, and private sectors, including all equality and horizontal-section cases; or an exact rational realization of the full normal form violating the inequality. slice-depth-square-root-concavity.relation_to_goal:
The locked problem needs a point on an integer slice. This lemma
constructs a compatible middle-slice point from two outer points and
propagates their planar depths through the same affine transversal. It
retains position information absent from area-only transport and may
give new certified parameter regimes or a useful input to the
single-double common-frame bridge.
slice-depth-square-root-concavity.statement:
Let \(C\subset\mathbb R^3\) be a compact convex body. For every
\((x,z)\in C\), write \(C_x=\{u:(x,u)\in C\}\) and define
\[
d_C(x,z)=\inf\{|C_x\cap G|:G\subset\mathbb R^2
\text{ is a closed halfplane containing }z\}.
\]
Prove that
\[
(x,z)\longmapsto\sqrt{d_C(x,z)}
\]
is concave on \(C\). Derive the exact three-slice consequence: if
\((0,z_0),(2,z_2)\in C\) and \(z_1=(z_0+z_2)/2\), then every closed
three-dimensional halfspace containing \((1,z_1)\) has mixed slice
mass at least
\[
d_C(1,z_1)+\min\{d_C(0,z_0),d_C(2,z_2)\},
\]
and
\[
\sqrt{d_C(1,z_1)}
\ge\frac{\sqrt{d_C(0,z_0)}+\sqrt{d_C(2,z_2)}}2.
\]
slice-depth-square-root-concavity.status_reason:
Accepted fact `665c08dbed9743ca` proves joint square-root concavity of
planar slice depth for arbitrary compact convex sections and derives
the registered three-slice affine-transversal mass bound. It includes
lower-dimensional sections, zero depths, boundary-through-point
reduction, and all halfspace endpoint cases.
slice-depth-square-root-concavity.success_criterion:

boundary does not initially pass through the point, and all endpoint

slope-sum-endpoint-cover-dichotomy.relation_to_goal:

analysis.  The surviving common-frame routing problem has a one-sided strong

slope-sum-endpoint-cover-dichotomy.statement:
Let
\[
H_i=\{(h,w):f_i(w)+s_i(h-1)\le0\},\qquad
f_1+f_2+f_3=-1,
\]
be a normalized strict three-halfspace certificate, and put
\(\sigma=s_1+s_2+s_3\).  Prove that if \(|\sigma|<1\), then the three
open sections cover \(\mathbb R^2\) separately at each of the heights
\(0,1,2\), and consequently
\[
\sum_{i=1}^3\mathcal H_2(S\cap H_i)\ge T,
\qquad
\max_i\mathcal H_2(S\cap H_i)\ge\frac T3>\frac{2T}{9}.
\]
Hence every strict-low certificate at \(2T/9\) must satisfy
\(|\sigma|\ge1\).
slope-sum-endpoint-cover-dichotomy.status_reason:

certificate must have total slope of absolute value at least one.  For

slope-sum-endpoint-cover-dichotomy.success_criterion:

small-c-centroid-depth.relation_to_goal:

small-c-centroid-depth.statement:
Let \(\Delta\) be a nondegenerate triangle of area \(D\), with all
homotheties centered at one vertex, and set
\[

(A_0,A_1,A_2)=(a\Delta,\Delta,c\Delta).
\]
Prove that the centroid \(g\) of the middle triangle satisfies
\[
h_S((1,g))\ge D\left(\frac49+c^2\right)
>\frac{2D(a^2+1+c^2)}9.
\]
small-c-centroid-depth.status_reason: Accepted fact `0c56216dc93d67f2` proves the exact residual triple positive at the middle centroid with a strict rational margin above \(2T/9\).
small-c-centroid-depth.success_criterion:

normal form or an equivalent projected-vertex analysis. Include tied

small-c-centroid-region.relation_to_goal:

\]
In particular, decide whether the displayed assumptions alone suffice.
small-c-centroid-region.status_reason: Accepted theorem `bacab27d6c43776b` proves the centroid bound for all \(a\ge1\) and \(0<c\le1/(3\sqrt2)\), and hence the strict target throughout that residual subregion.

\]

\]

small-c-residual-coverage.statement:

\[

\]

support-contact-center-defect-budget.relation_to_goal: The exact identity \(4p+5q-4=(4p_0+5q-4)+2\mathcal C_\lambda/I\), together with accepted fact `52cbc42a8e62feb7`, shows that this center-defect budget closes the arbitrary-center empty-full support-contact case.
support-contact-center-defect-budget.statement:
In the remaining normalized empty-full support-contact case, write the
middle sections as
\[
K_u=[c(u)-v(u),c(u)+v(u)]
\]
and let \(p_0,q,I\) be the recentered crossing ratio, contact ratio,
and half-area used in accepted fact `52cbc42a8e62feb7`.  Prove from
the full midpoint inclusion with the two endpoint bodies that
\[
\mathcal C_\lambda[v,c]
\geq-\frac I2\left(4p_0+5q-4\right),
\]
where
\[
\mathcal C_\lambda[v,c]
=\frac12\int_0^1
\left[
\chi_{v(u)}(u-\lambda-c(u))
+\chi_{v(u)}(u-\lambda+c(u))
-2\chi_{v(u)}(u-\lambda)
\right]du.
\]
support-contact-center-defect-budget.success_criterion: Give a complete sectionwise or integrated proof using the endpoint-section Minkowski inclusion, not merely equal crossing marginals. If false, give exact rational endpoint bodies and a middle body satisfying the full midpoint inclusion, all canonical mass and crossing conditions, and a strict violation.

support-contact-center-moment-selection.relation_to_goal: The parent cross-height problem is reduced exactly to this center-sensitive functional. support-contact-center-moment-selection.statement:

\[
W=\frac{\operatorname{conv}(\{q_v\}\cup Q^+)-P}{2}\subseteq F
\]
and its infimal-convolution lower endpoint \(a_W(v)\). Prove that the explicit lower functional
\[
\int_J\!\left(5(2-v)-\min\{2-v,a_W(v)\}-4r(v)\right)\,dv
+5\int_{v>0}\!
\left[\min\{b_W(v),2-v\}-a_W(v)\right]_+\,dv
\]
is nonnegative.

The proof must construct a measurable bounded-multiplicity selection of minimizers in the infimal convolution that charges \(|Q^+|\) and \(N-H\) simultaneously, and must remain literal when \(T=|Q^+|-(N-H)=0\) or either placed-tail half has zero area. Equivalently, give a complete normalized exact geometric counterexample with negative functional.
support-contact-center-moment-selection.success_criterion: Success is a complete selection/transport proof with measurability, multiplicity, endpoint, and zero-stratum checks, or a full rational normalized support-contact counterexample. inequality \(5C\ge4(L+U)\), closing the arbitrary-center empty-full

hull-excess bounds for \((G\setminus B)\cap H_\pm\), the absolute common
crossing level, and the equality of the two crossing caps of \(K\).

-\int_{v\le0}4f(v)\,dv\ge0

support-contact-depth-criterion-paramete.relation_to_goal: Accepted fact `d54b7af318521d6b` rules out strict support-contact failure whenever the displayed depth criterion holds. support-contact-depth-criterion-paramete.statement:

\[

and let \(0<a\le m\). If \(0\le\lambda\le\mu\le\nu\le m\) is the sorting of \(\{a,d_2,d_3\}\), assume
\[
4\lambda+5\mu<4m.
\]
Retain both same-direction Brunn-Minkowski consequences of common midpoint compatibility:
\[
t-d_i\ge\frac{(\sqrt{u_i}+\sqrt{v_i})^2}{4},
\qquad
k-t+d_i\ge\frac{(\sqrt{M-u_i}+\sqrt{m-v_i})^2}{4}
\quad(i=2,3).
\]
Define
\[
p=\sqrt{M/u_2},\qquad q=\sqrt{M/u_3},\qquad
C=\frac{pq-p-q}{p+q},
\]
\[
B_i=\frac1{\sqrt{1+u_i/v_i}-1}\quad(i=2,3).
\]
Decide whether these exact scalar and compatibility constraints force
\[
C\ge\max\{B_2,B_3\}.
\]
If they do not, give an exact rational choice of \(M,m,k,a,u_i,v_i\) satisfying every hypothesis and the strict reverse for at least one \(B_i\).

support-contact-empty-proper-midpoint-ar.relation_to_goal: In the unique empty-full crossing-equality stratum with an empty-proper second crossing, accepted fact `15bb2c1680a0254e` gives \(k/M<U(m/M)\). support-contact-empty-proper-midpoint-ar.statement:
Let \(P,Q\subset\mathbb R^2\) be compact two-dimensional convex polygons with
\[
|P|=M\ge m=|Q|>0,\qquad
0<r:=m/M<\rho:=\frac{27-2\sqrt{26}}{25}.
\]
Let \(\delta>0\), and assume the normalized empty-full equality-row and empty-proper strict-row support geometry
\[
P\subseteq\{x\ge-\delta,\ y\ge0,\ x+y\le0\},\qquad \min_Px=-\delta,
\]
\[
Q\subseteq\{x+y\ge0\},\qquad Q\cap\{x+y=0\}\ne\varnothing.
\]
Put
\[
v_1=|Q\cap\{x\le\delta+2\}|,\qquad
d_2=|Q\cap\{y\le0\}|.
\]
Assume there is \(a\) with
\[
0\le v_1<a<m,\qquad 0<d_2<m,\qquad a+d_2<m,
\]
\[
4\min\{a,d_2\}+5\max\{a,d_2\}<4m.
\]
Retain the genuine lower-crossing profile at \(y=0\):
\[
|P\cap\{y\le s\}|+|Q\cap\{y\le-s\}|\ge d_2
\quad\text{for every }s<0,
\]
and the same sum is strictly below \(d_2\) for arbitrarily small \(s>0\).
Define
\[
U(r)=
\begin{cases}
1+r,&0<r\le1/2,\\
2-r,&1/2<r<\rho.
\end{cases}
\]
Prove
\[
\left|\frac{P+Q}{2}\right|\ge M\,U(r),
\]
or give exact rational polygons satisfying every hypothesis and violating this inequality.

The transport must assign positive-length minimizer fibers to full horizontal sections, preserve the \(|Q^+|\) and \(N-H\) masses, and remain meaningful when \(T=0\) or either placed-tail half has zero area.

Equivalently, give a complete normalized exact geometric counterexample for which every admissible argmin disintegration violates the required marginal domination or the lower functional is negative.
support-contact-endpoint-atom-disintegra.status_reason: Accepted counterexample fact `3668e592cd8866b6` proves that unit-dominated argmin-supported endpoint/kink disintegrations cannot preserve even the smaller required mass on a complete strict normalized triple. support-contact-epp-equality-sep.relation_to_goal: Accepted fact `4e176b68a1636efc` leaves at most one tail equality. support-contact-epp-equality-sep.statement:
Assume the normalized support-contact and residual hypotheses of accepted facts `4e176b68a1636efc`, `624b129b68e0fdee`, `4ec05d1da924da91`, and `15bb2c1680a0254e`. Use normalized polygons \(P,Q,R\) with
\[
\frac{P+Q}{2}\subseteq R,\qquad \min_Px=-\delta,
\]
and define
\[
\alpha_E=|E\cap\{y\le0\}|,\qquad
\beta_E=|E\cap\{x+y\ge0\}|.
\]
Retain both exact crossing equalities
\[
\alpha_P+\alpha_Q+\alpha_R=t,\qquad
\beta_P+\beta_Q+\beta_R=t.
\]
Require row \(3\) to be the unique tail-equality row in its proper-proper state:

## Statement

Let
\[
\mathcal L=\{(x,y):x\le-|y|\},\qquad
\mathcal R=\{(x,y):x\ge|y|\},\qquad
\mathcal U=\{(x,y):y\ge|x|\},
\]
and take
\[
A_0=\{(x,y):|y|\le1344,\ -2021\le x\le-1-|y|\},
\]
\[
A_2=\operatorname{conv}\{(0,0),(2087,-12),(2087,12)\},
\qquad
K=[-1043,1043]\times[-678,678].
\]
Put
\[
B=\frac{A_0+A_2}{2},\qquad
Y=K\cap\mathcal U\cap\{x\ge1\},\qquad
G=\operatorname{conv}(B\cup Y),
\]
and let
\[
D(x,y)=(u,v)=(x+y,x-y),\qquad F=D(G),\qquad s=u+v.
\]
This is the integral triple of accepted fact
\(85353495158713c3\).  It satisfies all retained hypotheses of the
support-contact diagonal-tail placement subgoal.  In particular,
\[
M=3\,623\,424,\quad m=25\,044,\quad k=2\,828\,616,\quad
t=1\,439\,352,\quad \pi=1\,414\,308,
\]
\[
C=1\,415\,664,\qquad \delta=2021,\qquad
\theta=\left|A_2\cap\{x\ge2023\}\right|
=\frac{3\,156\,480}{2087},
\]
\[
A_0\subseteq\mathcal L,\quad A_2\subseteq\mathcal R,\quad
B\subseteq K,\quad M>k>m>0,\quad 0<t<M,
\]
\[
\min_{A_0}x=-\delta,\qquad
\min_{A_2}(x+y)=\min_{A_2}(x-y)=0,
\]
\[
|K\cap\{x+y\ge0\}|=|K\cap\{x-y\ge0\}|=\pi.
\]
Both diagonal contacts are genuine lower crossings,
\[
C+m-t=1356>0,\qquad
t-C-v_1=\frac{326\,508}{2087}>0,
\]
where \(v_1=m-\theta\), the positive forced tail obeys
\[
\frac{A_0+(A_2\cap\{x\ge2023\})}{2}
\subseteq B\cap\{x\ge1\},
\]
and both hull-excess budgets are bounded by
\[
103\,248<\pi-\frac m4=1\,408\,047.
\]
The two contact points in \(Q=D(A_2)\) are
\[
q_u=(0,\sigma)=(0,0),\qquad q_v=(\tau,0)=(0,0).
\]
With \(P=-D(A_0)\), the joint contact copy is \(E=-P/2\).
Moreover, \(\alpha=\beta=1721\), the contact-box conclusion
\(M\le2\alpha\beta\) holds, and
\[
7C+2\pi-2k-4\alpha\beta=-4\,766\,332<0.
\]

The two exact transformed cell areas are
\[
\left|F\cap\{s\le2\}\right|
=\frac{5\,699\,312\,934}{2087},
\qquad
\left|F\cap\{v\le0\}\right|
=\frac{5\,732\,444\,706}{2099}.
\]
Consequently
\[
5\left|F\cap\{s\le2\}\right|
-4\left|F\cap\{v\le0\}\right|
=\frac{11\,959\,840\,836\,642}{4\,380\,613}>0,
\]
and
\[
\Phi(G)
=\frac12\left(
5\left|F\cap\{s\le2\}\right|
-4\left|F\cap\{v\le0\}\right|
\right)
=\frac{5\,979\,920\,418\,321}{4\,380\,613}>0.
\]

For the exact residual decomposition, define, up to their null
boundary lines,
\[
A_-=F\cap\{s\le2,\ v\le0\},\qquad
A_+=F\cap\{s\le2,\ v\ge0\},
\]
\[
Y'=F\cap\{s\ge2,\ v\le0\}.
\]
Then
\[
|Y'|=458\,329,\qquad
|A_-|=\frac{4\,770\,412\,135}{2099},\qquad
|A_+|=\frac{2\,007\,007\,722\,721}{4\,380\,613}.
\]
The contact data are
\[
T_\tau=7\,246\,848,\qquad U_\sigma=0,\qquad
|E|=\frac{T_\tau}{4}=1\,811\,712,
\]
and \(E\subseteq A_-\).  Hence
\[
|A_-\setminus E|=\frac{967\,628\,647}{2099}.
\]
The saving slack has the exact disjoint-region decomposition
\[
\begin{aligned}
5|F\cap\{s\le2\}|-4|F\cap\{v\le0\}|
&=|A_-|+5|A_+|-4|Y'|\\
&=\left(\frac{T_\tau+5U_\sigma}{4}-4|Y'|\right)
  +|A_-\setminus E|+5|A_+|\\
&=-21\,604+\frac{967\,628\,647}{2099}
  +5\frac{2\,007\,007\,722\,721}{4\,380\,613}\\
&=\frac{11\,959\,840\,836\,642}{4\,380\,613}>0.
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus the two regions not captured by the contact-copy bound are
exactly \(A_-\setminus E\) and \(A_+\) for this triple.

## Proof

Accepted fact \(85353495158713c3\) verifies the displayed polygons,
all mass and crossing identities, the two strict absolute-level
inequalities, positive forced tail and midpoint containment, both
hull-excess budgets, the contact points, and the strict scalar sign.
Accepted fact \(e8c7d289faa42849\) supplies the contact-box
conclusion from these contacts and midpoint inclusion.  Accepted fact
\(81ddf2d6ab5b6a17\) supplies the joint-copy containment and exact
contact-tail Jacobian, while accepted fact \(d50fa08d9577c890\)
supplies the weighted-cell reduction used below.

The cyclic vertices of \(G\), already verified in accepted fact
\(85353495158713c3\), are
\[
\begin{aligned}
&\left(-\frac{2021}{2},-672\right),(33,-678),(371,-678),
(1043,-6),\\
&(1043,6),(678,678),(1,678),
\left(-\frac{2021}{2},672\right).
\end{aligned}
\]
Applying \(D\) gives the following cyclic vertices of \(F\):
\[
\begin{aligned}
V_0&=\left(-\frac{3365}{2},-\frac{677}{2}\right),&
V_1&=(-645,711),\\
V_2&=(-307,1049),&
V_3&=(1037,1049),\\
V_4&=(1049,1037),&
V_5&=(1356,0),\\
V_6&=(679,-677),&
V_7&=\left(-\frac{677}{2},-\frac{3365}{2}\right).
\end{aligned}
\]
The line \(s=2\) meets the edge \([V_0,V_1]\) at
\[
I=\left(-\frac{1\,412\,515}{2087},
\frac{1\,416\,689}{2087}\right),
\]
because the interpolation parameter from \(V_0\) to \(V_1\) is
\(2023/2087\).  Its other relevant contact with the clipped polygon
is \(V_6=(679,-677)\), which already has \(s=2\).  Therefore
\[
F\cap\{s\le2\}
=\operatorname{conv}\{V_0,I,V_6,V_7\}.
\]
The signed doubled shoelace sum in this cyclic order is
\[
-\frac{11\,398\,625\,868}{2087},
\]
so
\[
\left|F\cap\{s\le2\}\right|
=\frac{5\,699\,312\,934}{2087}.
\]

The line \(v=0\) meets \([V_0,V_1]\) at
\[
J=\left(-\frac{2\,829\,180}{2099},0\right),
\]
because the interpolation parameter is \(677/2099\).  Hence
\[
F\cap\{v\le0\}
=\operatorname{conv}\{V_0,J,V_5,V_6,V_7\}.
\]
Its signed doubled shoelace sum is
\[
-\frac{11\,464\,889\,412}{2099},
\]
which gives
\[
\left|F\cap\{v\le0\}\right|
=\frac{5\,732\,444\,706}{2099}.
\]
Putting the two areas over the common denominator
\(2087\cdot2099=4\,380\,613\) gives
\[
5|F\cap\{s\le2\}|
=\frac{59\,814\,289\,242\,330}{4\,380\,613},
\]
\[
4|F\cap\{v\le0\}|
=\frac{47\,854\,448\,405\,688}{4\,380\,613}.
\]
Their difference is the asserted positive transformed slack.

The determinant of \(D\) has absolute value \(2\).  Also,
\[
x\le1\Longleftrightarrow s\le2,
\qquad
\mathcal L\cup\mathcal U
=D^{-1}(\{v\le0\}).
\]
It follows directly from the definition
\[
\Phi(G)=5|G\cap\{x\le1\}|
-4|G\cap(\mathcal L\cup\mathcal U)|
\]
that \(\Phi(G)\) is one half of the transformed slack, proving its
displayed exact value and sign.

It remains to audit what the contact-copy bound missed.  Since
\(G\subseteq K\), \(Y\subseteq G\), and, for \(s\ge2\), the condition
\(v\le0\) is exactly \(x\ge1\) and \(y\ge x=|x|\), one has
\[
Y'=D(Y)=\operatorname{conv}\{(2,0),(679,-677),(1356,0)\}.
\]
Thus \(|Y'|=458\,329\).  The two remaining left cells have cyclic
descriptions
\[
A_-=\operatorname{conv}\{V_0,J,(2,0),V_6,V_7\},
\]
\[
A_+=\operatorname{conv}\{J,I,(2,0)\}.
\]
Subtracting \(Y'\) from \(F\cap\{v\le0\}\) gives
\[
|A_-|
=\frac{5\,732\,444\,706}{2099}-458\,329
=\frac{4\,770\,412\,135}{2099}.
\]
The second polygon is a triangle with horizontal base from \(J\) to
\((2,0)\) and height \(1\,416\,689/2087\).  Therefore
\[
|A_+|
=\frac12\left(2+\frac{2\,829\,180}{2099}\right)
\frac{1\,416\,689}{2087}
=\frac{2\,007\,007\,722\,721}{4\,380\,613}.
\]

Finally, accepted fact \(85353495158713c3\) gives
\[
P=\operatorname{conv}\{(1,1),(2689,1),(3365,677),
(677,3365),(1,2689)\},
\]
\[
|P|=7\,246\,848,\qquad \sigma=\tau=0,\qquad
T_\tau=|P|,\qquad U_\sigma=0.
\]
The two contact copies coincide with \(E=-P/2\).  Since every point
of \(P\) has both coordinates at least \(1\), every point of \(E\)
has \(s\le-1\) and \(v\le-1/2\).  Thus \(E\subseteq A_-\), and the
homothety gives
\[
|E|=\frac{|P|}{4}=1\,811\,712.
\]
Consequently
\[
|A_-\setminus E|
=\frac{4\,770\,412\,135}{2099}-1\,811\,712
=\frac{967\,628\,647}{2099}.
\]
The weighted-cell identity from accepted fact
\(d50fa08d9577c890\) is, in the present notation,
\[
5|F\cap\{s\le2\}|-4|F\cap\{v\le0\}|
=|A_-|+5|A_+|-4|Y'|.
\]
Splitting \(A_-=E\mathbin{\dot\cup}(A_-\setminus E)\) yields the
claimed exact residual decomposition.  In particular, the failed
contact-only inequality loses \(21\,604\), while the two omitted
regions contribute
\[
\frac{967\,628\,647}{2099}
+5\frac{2\,007\,007\,722\,721}{4\,380\,613},
\]
which proves the positive final slack.
