## Proof

The displayed description of \(A_0\) is the convex pentagon with
cyclic vertices
\[
(-2021,-1344),\quad(-1345,-1344),\quad(-1,0),\quad
(-1345,1344),\quad(-2021,1344).
\]
Every point of \(A_0\) satisfies \(x\le-1-|y|<-|y|\), so
\(A_0\subseteq\mathcal L\).  A vertical section of \(A_2\) at
\(0\le x\le2087\) is
\[
\left[-\frac{12x}{2087},\frac{12x}{2087}\right],
\]
so \(A_2\subseteq\mathcal R\).

The coordinate ranges in the Minkowski sum give
\[
-2021\le x(A_0)+x(A_2)\le-1+2087=2086
\]
and
\[
-1356\le y(A_0)+y(A_2)\le1356.
\]
Therefore
\[
B\subseteq[-1043,1043]\times[-678,678]=K.
\]
Direct integration and triangle and rectangle area formulas give
\[
M=2(1344)(2020)-1344^2=3\,623\,424,
\]
\[
m=(2087)(12)=25\,044,\qquad
k=(2086)(1356)=2\,828\,616.
\]
Set
\[
\pi=1\,414\,308,\qquad t=m+\pi=1\,439\,352.
\]
Then
\[
2(M+m+k)=12\,954\,168=9t,
\]
so this is exactly the canonical value
\(t=2(M+m+k)/9\).  The displayed values also give
\(M>k>m>0\) and \(0<t<M\).

The rectangle \(K\) is centrally symmetric and both diagonal lines
pass through its center.  Hence
\[
|K\cap\{x+y\ge0\}|
=|K\cap\{x-y\ge0\}|=\frac k2=\pi.
\]
On \(A_0\), both \(x+y\) and \(x-y\) are at most \(-1\).
For every \(0<a<1\), therefore,
\[
A_0\cap\{x+y\ge-a\}
=A_0\cap\{x-y\ge-a\}=\varnothing.
\]
The origin is the unique point of \(A_2\) on either diagonal boundary,
and every strip
\[
A_2\cap\{0\le x+y<a\},\qquad
A_2\cap\{0\le x-y<a\}
\]
has positive area.  Consequently
\[
\pi+|A_0\cap\{x+y\ge-a\}|
+|A_2\cap\{x+y\ge a\}|<\pi+m=t
\]
and the identical strict inequality holds with \(x-y\).  Thus both
contacts are genuine lower crossings, including their one-sided
strictness.

Since
\[
C=2(678)(1044)=1\,415\,664,
\]
one has
\[
C-\pi=1356,\qquad C+m-t=1356>0.
\]
The forced tail is
\[
A_2^+=A_2\cap\{x\ge\delta+2\}
=A_2\cap\{x\ge2023\}.
\]
Similarity of the removed triangle gives
\[
\theta:=|A_2^+|
=12\left(2(64)-\frac{64^2}{2087}\right)
=\frac{3\,156\,480}{2087}.
\]
Thus \(v_1=m-\theta\), and
\[
t-C-v_1
=\theta-(C-\pi)
=\frac{326\,508}{2087}>0.
\]
This proves both strict absolute-level inequalities and
\(\theta>C-\pi>0\).  For \(a_0\in A_0\) and \(a_2\in A_2^+\),
\[
x\left(\frac{a_0+a_2}{2}\right)
\ge\frac{-2021+2023}{2}=1.
\]
Hence the positive forced tail has the required containment
\[
\frac{A_0+A_2^+}{2}\subseteq B\cap\{x\ge1\}.
\]

For completeness, the cyclic vertices of \(B\) are
\[
\begin{aligned}
&\left(-\frac{2021}{2},-672\right),(33,-678),(371,-678),
(1043,-6),\\
&(1043,6),(371,678),(33,678),
\left(-\frac{2021}{2},672\right).
\end{aligned}
\]
Since
\[
Y=\operatorname{conv}\{(1,1),(1,678),(678,678)\},
\]
the cyclic vertices of \(G=\operatorname{conv}(B\cup Y)\) are
\[
\begin{aligned}
&\left(-\frac{2021}{2},-672\right),(33,-678),(371,-678),
(1043,-6),\\
&(1043,6),(678,678),(1,678),
\left(-\frac{2021}{2},672\right).
\end{aligned}
\]
The shoelace formula gives
\[
|B|=2\,326\,701,\qquad |G|=2\,429\,949,
\qquad |G\setminus B|=103\,248.
\]
On the other hand,
\[
\pi-\frac m4=1\,408\,047.
\]
For each of
\[
H_u=\{x+y\ge0\},\qquad H_v=\{x-y\ge0\},
\]
the relevant excess is bounded by the total excess:
\[
|(G\setminus B)\cap H_u|,
\ |(G\setminus B)\cap H_v|
\le103\,248<1\,408\,047=\pi-\frac m4.
\]
Thus both inherited hull-excess constraints hold.

The four vertices of \(D(K)\) show
\[
\alpha=\beta=1043+678=1721.
\]
Substitution gives
\[
7C+2\pi-2k-4\alpha\beta
=-4\,766\,332<0,
\]
so the additional canonical scalar sign is retained as well.

The exact polygon \(P=-D(A_0)\) has cyclic vertices
\[
(1,1),\quad(2689,1),\quad(3365,677),\quad
(677,3365),\quad(1,2689),
\]
and
\[
|P|=2M=7\,246\,848.
\]
Also
\[
Q=\operatorname{conv}\{(0,0),(2075,2099),(2099,2075)\}.
\]
Its two actual contact faces meet only at the origin, so
\(\sigma=\tau=0\).  Since \(p_u,p_v\ge1\) throughout \(P\),
\[
T_\tau=|P|=7\,246\,848,\qquad U_\sigma=0.
\]
The translation vector between the two contact copies is
\[
d=q_v-q_u=(0,0).
\]
Thus the two copies coincide,
\[
\frac{q_u-P}{2}=\frac{q_v-P}{2}=-\frac P2,
\]
and their exact clipped-overlap quantity is maximal:
\[
\left|\{p\in P:p+d\in P,\ p_u+p_v\ge-4\}\right|
=|P|=7\,246\,848.
\]

Applying \(D\) to \(Y\) gives
\[
Y'=\operatorname{conv}\{(2,0),(679,-677),(1356,0)\},
\qquad |Y'|=458\,329.
\]
Therefore
\[
16|Y'|=7\,333\,264
>7\,246\,848=T_\tau+5U_\sigma,
\]
with exact deficit \(86\,416\).

It remains to retain the forced midpoint body and locate the failure.
Put
\[
Q^+=D(A_2^+),\qquad
R=\frac{Q^+-P}{2}.
\]
The preceding midpoint argument gives
\[
R\subseteq S\cap\{u+v\ge2\}.
\]
Exact Minkowski addition gives the following cyclic vertices of \(R\):
\[
\begin{aligned}
&\left(-\frac{1\,412\,515}{2087},
\frac{1\,416\,689}{2087}\right),(-645,711),(-307,1049),
(1037,1049),\\
&(1049,1037),(1049,-307),(711,-645),
\left(\frac{1\,416\,689}{2087},
-\frac{1\,412\,515}{2087}\right).
\end{aligned}
\]
Clipping either \(R\) or \(S=D(B)\) by \(Y'\) gives the same cyclic
polygon
\[
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{conv}\biggl\{&(2,0),
\left(\frac{1\,416\,689}{2087},
-\frac{1\,412\,515}{2087}\right),
(711,-645),\\
&(1049,-307),(1049,0)\biggr\}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus the forced midpoint body is retained exactly:
\[
R\cap Y'=S\cap Y'.
\]
The shoelace formula gives
\[
|S\cap Y'|=\frac{1\,716\,343\,007}{4174},
\qquad
|Y'\setminus S|=\frac{196\,722\,239}{4174}.
\]
The right side of the local-gap rearrangement is
\[
\frac{T_\tau+5U_\sigma}{16}-|S\cap Y'|
=\frac{174\,178\,465}{4174}.
\]
Hence this counterexample violates \((\mathrm{LG})\) by
\[
\frac{196\,722\,239-174\,178\,465}{4174}=5401.
\]
Multiplication by \(16\) recovers the exact localized deficit
\(16(5401)=86\,416\).

It remains only to prove the quantified rearrangement.  Let
\(S_0,Y_0\subseteq\mathbb R^2\) be Lebesgue-measurable sets of finite
area and let \(T,U\in[0,\infty)\).  By definition,
\[
Y_0=(S_0\cap Y_0)\mathbin{\dot\cup}(Y_0\setminus S_0)
=Y_{\mathrm{in}}\mathbin{\dot\cup}Y_{\mathrm{miss}}.
\]
Finite additivity gives
\[
|Y_0|=|Y_{\mathrm{in}}|+|Y_{\mathrm{miss}}|.
\]
Therefore
\[
\begin{aligned}
T+5U\ge16|Y_0|
&\Longleftrightarrow
\frac{T+5U}{16}
\ge |Y_{\mathrm{in}}|+|Y_{\mathrm{miss}}|\\
&\Longleftrightarrow
|Y_{\mathrm{miss}}|
\le\frac{T+5U}{16}-|Y_{\mathrm{in}}|.
\end{aligned}
\]
This proves \((\mathrm{LG})\), and substituting
\(S_0=D(B)\), \(Y_0=Y'\), \(T=T_\tau\), and \(U=U_\sigma\)
gives the stated local-gap form of the localized inequality.

## Proof

We first verify the complete canonical setting.  Direct area
calculation gives
\[
M=38\left(\frac{3055}{19}-20\right)=5350,\qquad
m=\frac12\cdot210\cdot\frac{20}{21}=100,\qquad
k=200\cdot20=4000.
\]
Consequently
\[
t=\frac{2(5350+100+4000)}9=2100,\qquad
\pi=t-m=2000.
\]
In particular \(M\ge m>0\) and \(0<t<M\).

Every point of \(A_0\) has \(x\le-20\) and \(|y|\le19\), so
\(A_0\subset\mathcal L\), with a strict gap of at least \(1\) from
both diagonal boundary rays.  A vertical section of \(A_2\) at
\(0\le x\le210\) is
\[
\left[-\frac{x}{441},\frac{x}{441}\right],
\]
so \(A_2\subseteq\mathcal R\).  Its only point on either boundary ray
of \(\mathcal R\) is \((0,0)\).  Hence
\[
\min_{A_2}(x+y)=\min_{A_2}(x-y)=0
\]
and both diagonal contacts may be chosen at the common vertex
\((0,0)\), giving \(\sigma=\tau=0\).

The six cyclic vertices of \(B\) are
\[
\begin{aligned}
&\left(-\frac{3055}{38},-\frac{19}{2}\right),
\left(\frac{935}{38},-\frac{409}{42}\right),
\left(95,-\frac{409}{42}\right),\\
&\left(95,\frac{409}{42}\right),
\left(\frac{935}{38},\frac{409}{42}\right),
\left(-\frac{3055}{38},\frac{19}{2}\right).
\end{aligned}
\]
All have \(-100<x<100\) and \(|y|<10\).  Thus \(B\subseteq K\).
The rectangle \(K\) is centrally symmetric, so every line through its
center bisects its area.  Therefore
\[
|K\cap\{x+y\ge0\}|=|K\cap\{x-y\ge0\}|=\frac k2=2000=\pi.
\]

The contacts are genuine in the required one-sided sense.  If
\(0<a<1\), then
\[
A_0\cap\{x+y\ge-a\}
=A_0\cap\{x-y\ge-a\}=\varnothing.
\]
For either nonnegative affine coordinate \(x+y\) or \(x-y\) on
\(A_2\), the strip where that coordinate is \(<a\) has positive area.
Thus
\[
|A_2\cap\{x+y\ge a\}|<m,\qquad
|A_2\cap\{x-y\ge a\}|<m,
\]
and hence both required strict crossing inequalities are
\(\pi+0+\text{(an area \(<m\)} )<\pi+m=t\).

The absolute-level quantities are
\[
C=101\cdot20=2020,\qquad
\delta+2=\frac{3093}{19}.
\]
Similarity of the sections of the triangle \(A_2\) gives
\[
v_1
=100\left(\frac{(3093/19)}{210}\right)^2
=100\left(\frac{1031}{1330}\right)^2
=\frac{1\,062\,961}{17\,689}.
\]
Therefore
\[
C+m=2120>2100=t
\]
and
\[
t-C-v_1
=80-\frac{1\,062\,961}{17\,689}
=\frac{352\,159}{17\,689}>0.
\]
Equivalently, with
\[
\theta=m-v_1=\frac{705\,939}{17\,689},
\]
one has
\[
\theta-(C-\pi)
=\theta-20
=\frac{352\,159}{17\,689}>0.
\]
The tail \(A_2^+=A_2\cap\{x\ge\delta+2\}\) is therefore
two-dimensional and positive-area.  For \(a_0\in A_0\) and
\(a_2\in A_2^+\),
\[
x\left(\frac{a_0+a_2}{2}\right)
\ge\frac{-\delta+(\delta+2)}2=1,
\]
which proves the required forced-tail inclusion
\[
\frac{A_0+A_2^+}{2}\subseteq B\cap\{x\ge1\}.
\]

Here
\[
Y=\operatorname{conv}\{(1,1),(1,10),(10,10)\}.
\]
Exact convex-hull enumeration gives the cyclic vertices
\[
\begin{aligned}
G=\operatorname{conv}\biggl\{&
\left(-\frac{3055}{38},-\frac{19}{2}\right),
\left(\frac{935}{38},-\frac{409}{42}\right),
\left(95,-\frac{409}{42}\right),\\
&\left(95,\frac{409}{42}\right),(10,10),(1,10),
\left(-\frac{3055}{38},\frac{19}{2}\right)
\biggr\}.
\end{aligned}
\]
The shoelace formula on the displayed cyclic lists gives
\[
|B|=\frac{2\,706\,035}{798},\qquad
|G|=\frac{3\,636\,729}{1064},
\]
and hence
\[
|G\setminus B|
=|G|-|B|
=\frac{86\,047}{3192}<27.
\]
It follows for both
\[
H_u=\{x+y\ge0\},\qquad H_v=\{x-y\ge0\}
\]
that
\[
|(G\setminus B)\cap H_u|,
\ |(G\setminus B)\cap H_v|
<27<1975=\pi-\frac m4.
\]
Thus both inherited hull-excess budgets hold with large strict slack.

The four vertices of \(D(K)\) are
\[
(-110,-90),\quad(-90,-110),\quad(110,90),\quad(90,110).
\]
Thus \(\alpha=\beta=110\), and the additional scalar sign is
\[
7C+2\pi-2k-4\alpha\beta
=7(2020)+2(2000)-2(4000)-4(110)^2
=-38260<0.
\]

We next rederive the exact weighted-cell reduction and all constants.
Write \(S=D(B)\), \(F=D(G)\), and \(s=u+v\).  Up to null boundary
lines, put
\[
A=F\cap\{s\le2,\ v\le0\},\qquad
B_+=F\cap\{s\le2,\ v\ge0\}.
\]
Since \(G\subseteq K\), \(Y\subseteq G\), and
\(s\ge2,\ v\le0\) implies \(u=s-v\ge0\), one has exactly
\[
F\cap\{s\ge2,\ v\le0\}=Y'.
\]
Consequently
\[
5|F\cap\{s\le2\}|\ge4|F\cap\{v\le0\}|
\]
is equivalent to
\[
|A|+5|B_+|\ge4|Y'|.
\tag{1}
\]

For general contact levels, a point
\((q_v-p)/2\), where \(q_v=(\tau,0)\), satisfies
\[
s=\frac{\tau-p_u-p_v}{2}\le2
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
p_u+p_v\ge\tau-4,
\]
and it has \(v=-p_v/2\le0\).  Since the affine map has area
factor \(1/4\), this copy contributes \(T_\tau/4\) to \(A\).
Likewise, for \(q_u=(0,\sigma)\),
\[
s=\frac{\sigma-p_u-p_v}{2}\le2
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
p_u+p_v\ge\sigma-4,
\]
and
\[
v=\frac{\sigma-p_v}{2}\ge0
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad p_v\le\sigma.
\]
It contributes \(U_\sigma/4\) to \(B_+\).  Hence
\[
|A|+5|B_+|\ge\frac{T_\tau+5U_\sigma}{4}.
\tag{2}
\]
This rederives both actual thresholds and the factor \(1/4\).

The translated-copy overlap is also exact.  If
\[
d=q_v-q_u=(\tau,-\sigma),
\]
then \((q_u-p)/2\) belongs to the \(q_v\)-copy precisely when
\(p+d\in P\).  The two left-cut conditions then agree.  Thus, with
\[
I=\left|\{p\in P:p+d\in P,\ p_u+p_v\ge\sigma-4\}\right|,
\]
\[
\left|
\left(\frac{q_u-P}{2}\cup\frac{q_v-P}{2}\right)
\cap\{s\le2\}
\right|
=\frac{T_\sigma+T_\tau-I}{4}.
\tag{3}
\]

For the present triple, the \((s,v)=(u+v,v)\) sections of \(P\) are
\[
P=\left\{(s,v):
40\le s\le\frac{6110}{19},\
\frac s2-19\le v\le\frac s2+19\right\}.
\tag{4}
\]
In particular \(|P|=10700\), \(p_v\ge1\), and the actual
thresholds are
\[
\sigma-4=\tau-4=-4.
\]
It follows that
\[
T_\sigma=T_\tau=10700,\qquad U_\sigma=0.
\tag{5}
\]
Moreover \(d=0\), so the two copies coincide and
\[
I=10700.
\]
Thus (3) retains the maximal possible translated overlap rather than
treating the copies as disjoint.

For completeness, the corresponding sections of \(Q=D(A_2)\) are
\[
Q=\left\{(s,v):
0\le s\le420,\
\frac{220}{441}s\le v\le\frac{221}{441}s\right\}.
\tag{6}
\]
The forced tail is obtained by imposing
\[
s\ge2(\delta+2)=\frac{6186}{19}.
\]
Consequently the forced-tail midpoint body
\[
R=\frac{Q^+-P}{2}
\]
has the following cyclic vertices in \((s,v)\)-coordinates:
\[
\begin{aligned}
&\left(2,-\frac{24256}{2793}\right),
\left(\frac{935}{19},\frac{5932}{399}\right),
\left(190,\frac{3581}{42}\right),\\
&\left(190,\frac{4399}{42}\right),
\left(\frac{935}{19},\frac{13703}{399}\right),
\left(2,\frac{29842}{2793}\right).
\end{aligned}
\tag{7}
\]
This explicitly retains the horizontal \(s\)-placement and the
vertical split at \(v=0\).

On the other hand,
\[
Y'=\operatorname{conv}\{(2,-9),(2,0),(20,0)\},
\qquad |Y'|=81.
\tag{8}
\]
Clipping the displayed polygon \(B\) by \(Y\) gives
\[
B\cap Y
=\operatorname{conv}\left\{
(1,1),
\left(\frac{10141}{1045},\frac{10141}{1045}\right),
\left(1,\frac{27049}{2793}\right)
\right\}.
\]
After applying \(D\), this is the triangle
\[
S\cap Y'
=\operatorname{conv}\left\{
(2,0),
\left(\frac{20282}{1045},0\right),
\left(2,-\frac{24256}{2793}\right)
\right\}.
\tag{9}
\]
The same triangle is exactly \(R\cap\{v\le0\}\), as is immediate
from (7).  Thus the forced-tail body supplies the whole right-bad
part of \(D(B)\), not merely a marginal lower bound.  Its area is
\[
|S\cap Y'|
=\frac12\left(\frac{20282}{1045}-2\right)
\cdot\frac{24256}{2793}
=\frac{73\,544\,192}{972\,895}.
\tag{10}
\]

The convex hull of \(R\) and \(Y'\) still creates very little new
area above \(v=0\).  Its \(v\ge0\) part has cyclic vertices
\[
\begin{aligned}
&(2,0),(20,0),
\left(190,\frac{3581}{42}\right),
\left(190,\frac{4399}{42}\right),\\
&\left(\frac{935}{19},\frac{13703}{399}\right),
\left(2,\frac{29842}{2793}\right),
\end{aligned}
\]
whereas its intersection with \(S\cap\{v\ge0\}\) has the same list
with the lower chain \((2,0),(20,0)\) replaced by
\[
(2,0),\quad
\left(\frac{20282}{1045},0\right),\quad
\left(\frac{935}{19},\frac{5932}{399}\right).
\]
The shoelace formula gives
\[
\left|
\bigl(\operatorname{conv}(R\cup Y')\setminus S\bigr)
\cap\{v\ge0\}
\right|
=\frac{38\,081\,077}{1\,667\,820}.
\tag{11}
\]
Direct enumeration of \(\operatorname{conv}(S\cup Y')=D(G)\)
shows that its new \(v\ge0\) part is exactly the same region.  Hence
\[
\left|
\bigl(\operatorname{conv}(S\cup Y')\setminus S\bigr)
\cap\{v\ge0\}
\right|
=\frac{38\,081\,077}{1\,667\,820}
<23<3950=2\pi-\frac m2.
\tag{12}
\]
This both verifies the second inherited budget in \(D\)-coordinates
and proves that the second alternative of the registered dichotomy
is false.

Finally, (5) and (10) give
\[
T_\tau+5U_\sigma=10700,
\]
whereas
\[
\begin{aligned}
16|S\cap Y'|+32\pi-8m
&=
16\frac{73\,544\,192}{972\,895}
+32(2000)-8(100)\\
&=\frac{62\,663\,671\,072}{972\,895}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Their strict difference is
\[
\frac{52\,253\,694\,572}{972\,895}>0,
\]
so the first alternative is false as well.

The source of the failure is now exact.  From (8)--(10),
\[
|Y'\setminus S|
=81-\frac{73\,544\,192}{972\,895}
=\frac{5\,260\,303}{972\,895}.
\tag{13}
\]
The inherited quantity \(2\pi-m/2=3950\) is only an upper bound for
this actual missing right-bad area; here it exceeds (13) by orders of
magnitude.  Equations (1)--(2) show that the exact sufficient payment
is
\[
T_\tau+5U_\sigma
\ge16|Y'|
=16|S\cap Y'|+16|Y'\setminus S|.
\tag{14}
\]
Indeed, this counterexample satisfies the corrected threshold
\(10700\ge16\cdot81=1296\).  Replacing the last term in (14) by the
full unused upper budget is not a valid necessary alternative, and
(11)--(12) show that the unused budget need not reappear as transverse
hull excess.

b=|Q\cap\{x\ge\delta+2\}|.

\[

\]

\quad\text{for every }s<0,
\]
and that the same sum is strictly below \(d_2\) for every sufficiently small \(s>0\).

\[

0<|Q\cap\{x+y\ge0\}|<m,
\]
\[

\]
\[
|P\cap\{x+y\ge-s\}|+|Q\cap\{x+y\ge s\}|\ge m
\quad\text{for every }s<0,
\]
and that the same sum is strictly below \(m\) for every sufficiently small \(s>0\).

Finally, assume that a real number \(a\) satisfies
\[
0<a<m,\qquad a+d_2<m,
\]
\[
4\min\{a,d_2\}+5\max\{a,d_2\}<4m,
\qquad b>m-a.
\]
Prove
\[
\left|\frac{P+Q}{2}\right|>M\,U(r),
\]
or give exact rational polygons and rational parameters satisfying every displayed hypothesis and the reverse weak inequality.
support-epp-midpoint-area-implication.status_reason: Accepted fact `33eb057e70ac0f43` gives exact rational triangles satisfying every registered empty-proper and proper-proper shifted-profile hypothesis, the scalar gate, and \(b>m-a\), while their midpoint area is strictly below \(M U(r)\). This closes `support-epp-midpoint-area-implication` by refutation. It does not close the parent support-contact orbit or refute the locked theorem; any remaining exclusion must use the prescribed cap equalities of one compatible middle extension rather than total midpoint area alone.
support-epp-midpoint-area-implication.success_criterion: A proof must use both complete one-sided shifted profiles, not only their values at zero, and must justify every mixed-area or section inequality including support-face and equality cases. A refutation must use rational vertices and rational parameters, verify all cap areas and the two full shifted-profile inequalities exactly, verify strictness on a positive interval to the right of zero, and compute the midpoint area exactly. A floating-point search or an endpoint cap table is insufficient.

support-epp-positive-midpoint-cap-gate.relation_to_goal:
If a compatible residual middle polygon \(R\supseteq B\) of area \(k<MU(r)\) satisfies the empty-proper crossing cap equation
\[
|R\cap\{y\le0\}|=t-d_2,\qquad t=\frac{2(M+m+k)}9,
\]
then, because the cutting line has area zero,
\[
|B\cap\{y>0\}|
\le k-(t-d_2)
=\frac{7k-2M-2m}{9}+d_2
<
\frac{7MU(r)-2M-2m}{9}+d_2.
\]
Therefore the proposed lower bound closes the E-PP/S-EP parent orbit using the actual placement of the midpoint body, even though accepted fact `33eb057e70ac0f43` refutes the corresponding total-area bound. A rational refutation identifies endpoints that survive this first middle-cap capacity gate.
support-epp-positive-midpoint-cap-gate.statement:
Let \(P,Q\subset\mathbb R^2\) be compact two-dimensional convex polygons with
\[
M=|P|\ge m=|Q|>0,\qquad r=\frac mM,
\qquad 0<r<\rho:=\frac{27-2\sqrt{26}}{25}.
\]
Put
\[
U(r)=
\begin{cases}
1+r,&0<r\le\frac12,\\[2pt]
2-r,&\frac12<r<\rho.
\end{cases}
\]
Assume \(\delta>0\), \(\min_Px=-\delta\), and \(P\subseteq\{y\ge0\}\). Define
\[
d_2=|Q\cap\{y\le0\}|,\qquad
b=|Q\cap\{x\ge\delta+2\}|.
\]
Assume
\[
0<d_2<m,
\]
\[
|P\cap\{y\le s\}|+|Q\cap\{y\le-s\}|\ge d_2
\quad\text{for every }s<0,
\]
and that the same sum is strictly below \(d_2\) for every sufficiently small \(s>0\).

Assume also
\[
0<|P\cap\{x+y\ge0\}|<m,\qquad
0<|Q\cap\{x+y\ge0\}|<m,
\]
\[
|P\cap\{x+y\ge0\}|+|Q\cap\{x+y\ge0\}|=m,
\]
\[
|P\cap\{x+y\ge-s\}|+|Q\cap\{x+y\ge s\}|\ge m
\quad\text{for every }s<0,
\]
and that the same sum is strictly below \(m\) for every sufficiently small \(s>0\).

Finally, assume a real number \(a\) satisfies
\[
0<a<m,\qquad a+d_2<m,
\]
\[
4\min\{a,d_2\}+5\max\{a,d_2\}<4m,
\qquad b>m-a.
\]
With
\[
B=\frac{P+Q}{2},
\]
prove the positive-side midpoint-cap bound
\[
|B\cap\{y>0\}|
>
\frac{7M\,U(r)-2M-2m}{9}+d_2,
\]
or give exact rational polygons and parameters satisfying every hypothesis and the reverse weak inequality.
support-epp-positive-midpoint-cap-gate.status_reason: Accepted fact `5e723405fce2d727` gives exact rational endpoint polygons satisfying both complete shifted profiles, the scalar gate, and a full far contact cap, while strictly reversing the proposed positive-side midpoint-cap bound. This closes `support-epp-positive-midpoint-cap-gate` by refutation. The E-PP/S-EP parent orbit remains open and now requires simultaneous use of at least two middle-cap equations.
support-epp-positive-midpoint-cap-gate.success_criterion: A proof must use both complete shifted profiles and the far contact cap, not only Brunn-Minkowski for \(P\) and \(Q\cap\{y\ge0\}\), and must justify the strict inequality throughout the two residual branches. A refutation must give rational vertices and parameters, verify all cap areas and both complete profiles exactly, and compute the positive-side cap of the full midpoint polygon by exact Minkowski addition and clipping. Floating-point evidence or a total-area calculation is insufficient.

symmetric-overlap-bridge.relation_to_goal:
The accepted fixed-instance proof `7ef000fb953c88a6` uses this construction
with one explicit \(c\). Abstracting it converts the locked target into the
geometric selection problem \(\Phi(c)\ge4T/9\), without restricting slice
shapes or centroid alignment.
symmetric-overlap-bridge.statement:
For any \(c\in A_1\), define the centrally symmetric overlap
\[
\Phi(c):=
\left|A_1\cap(2c-A_1)\right|
+2\left|A_2\cap(2c-A_0)\right|.
\]
Prove the exact depth reduction
\[
h_S((1,c))\ge\frac12\Phi(c),
\]
including arbitrary closed halfspaces and possible boundary mass.
symmetric-overlap-bridge.status_reason:
Accepted lemma `446ebd1e738cf6dd` proves the requested general reduction:
\(h_S((1,c))\ge\Phi(c)/2\) for every \(c\in A_1\), including all boundary
mass and degenerate-halfspace cases. Thus \(\Phi(c)\ge4T/9\) is a valid
sufficient condition for the locked target.
symmetric-overlap-bridge.success_criterion:
Produce a self-contained lemma valid for all compatible convex-polytopal
triples and all \(c\in A_1\), with the reflection inclusions and
halfspace-symmetry argument checked exactly. State explicitly that
\(\Phi(c)\ge4T/9\) implies the locked depth bound at \((1,c)\).

symmetric-overlap-selection.relation_to_goal:
Combined with the registered symmetric-overlap depth bridge and the accepted
large-slice theorem, a universal positive selection result would settle the
locked target. A counterexample would refute only this bridge strategy and
would identify the geometry not captured by central symmetry.
symmetric-overlap-selection.statement:
In the balanced compatible regime, determine whether there must exist
\(c\in A_1\) such that
\[
\left|A_1\cap(2c-A_1)\right|
+2\left|A_2\cap(2c-A_0)\right|
\ge\frac{4T}{9}.
\]
Prove this exact selection inequality or give an explicit compatible
counterexample to the inequality.
symmetric-overlap-selection.status_reason:
Accepted counterexample `f46d97e9c51bfd84` refutes the proposed universal
selection inequality. For the balanced compatible family
\(A_0=A_1=\Delta,\ A_2=\Delta/4\), the exact global maximum is
\(\max_c\Phi(c)=57/16<33/8=4T/9\), although the locked target still holds by
the accepted homothetic-triangle theorem.
symmetric-overlap-selection.success_criterion:
Return either a complete proof of the quantified overlap inequality with all
constants and support restrictions explicit, or rational convex polygons for
which the global maximum over \(c\in A_1\) is proved below \(4T/9\). An average
bound or sampled maximization alone is insufficient.

tail-axis-aligned-rectangle-true-profile.relation_to_goal:
The accepted surrogate counterexample `e1c09b85b6ceb583` is a long-thin
axis-aligned rectangle triple, but its true \(\ell\)-profile already makes
\(I_\ell\) empty.  Exhausting the full rectangle family tests whether exact
piecewise-quadratic endpoint profiles, rather than Brunn lower bounds, close
the principal unequal-width mechanism in `canonical-tail-exclusion`.
tail-axis-aligned-rectangle-true-profile.statement:
In the shared coordinates
\[
g_i=x,\qquad g_\ell=y,\qquad g_q=1-x-y,
\]
let \(A_0,A_2\) be arbitrary nonempty two-dimensional rational
axis-aligned rectangles and set
\[
K=\frac{A_0+A_2}{2}.
\]
Assume the exact residual area domain of `15bb2c1680a0254e`, relabel so
\(M=|A_0|\ge m=|A_2|\), put \(t=2(M+m+|K|)/9\), and assume
\[
c_q+m<t.
\]
With
\[
f_i=-x,\qquad f_\ell=-y,\qquad f_q=x+y-1,
\]
define \(\mu_j(a)\) and \(I_j=\{a:\mu_j(a)<t\}\) as in
`canonical-tail-exclusion`.  Prove
\[
I_i=\varnothing\quad\text{or}\quad I_\ell=\varnothing,
\]
or give an exact rational counterexample.
tail-axis-aligned-rectangle-true-profile.status_reason:
Accepted fact `23e739786446ffe1` proves canonical tail exclusion for the
entire axis-aligned rectangle family with minimal middle body.  It optimizes
both true endpoint profiles and covers every coordinate and diagonal cap
breakpoint.
tail-axis-aligned-rectangle-true-profile.success_criterion:
A proof must optimize both endpoint cap sums exactly across every rectangle
breakpoint and include all empty, partial, full, and equality cells.  A
counterexample must verify compatibility, the residual domain, the strict
\(q\)-tail, and exact rational shifts witnessing both \(I_i\) and \(I_\ell\)
nonempty.

tail-both-rows-support-hull-bound.relation_to_goal:
The left side is exactly the area of the support-minimal row-aligned triangle
containing \(B\).  Accepted counterexample `e1c09b85b6ceb583` shows the
bound is false without the two true-profile assumptions, but that example
has \(I_\ell=\varnothing\).  Proving the bound in the genuinely undecided
branch is the first necessary gate for any triangle extremal reduction of
`canonical-tail-exclusion`.
tail-both-rows-support-hull-bound.statement:
Assume the complete hypotheses and notation of `canonical-tail-exclusion`.
Relabel \(\{i,\ell,q\}=\{1,2,3\}\), put
\[
x=g_i,\qquad y=g_\ell,\qquad g_q=1-x-y,
\qquad B=\frac{A_0+A_2}{2},
\]
and assume
\[
c_q+m<t,\qquad D_0=3t-k-m>m,\qquad
I_i\ne\varnothing,\qquad I_\ell\ne\varnothing.
\]
Prove or refute the strict support-hull bound
\[
\frac12\left(
\max_B(x+y)-\min_B x-\min_B y
\right)^2<M+m.
\]
tail-both-rows-support-hull-bound.success_criterion:
A proof must use the actual definitions of \(I_i,I_\ell\) and the true
optimized endpoint cap profiles, not only the \(\Psi\) surrogates.  A
refutation must give exact rational compatible polygons satisfying both
nonemptiness conditions and all residual and tail hypotheses, and compute
the true profiles exactly.

tail-cap-breakpoint-support-coupling.relation_to_goal:
This is the first sharply isolated equality case left by the round-101
exposed-face obstacle.  Proving it removes all cap-breakpoint and
projection-support cases from the support-hull route, leaving only the
interior section-balance case.  An exact compatible refutation would show
that even the proposed boundary reduction is false and would supply a new
tail calibration with the complete middle-cap block.
tail-cap-breakpoint-support-coupling.statement:
Assume the complete hypotheses and notation of
`tail-exposed-face-minimizer-shift-coupling`.  In particular, after
relabeling, write `x=g_i`, `y=g_l`, choose shifts `a_i,a_l` minimizing the
two true endpoint profiles, and normalize them by
\[
\widehat A_0=A_0+(a_i,a_\ell),\qquad
\widehat A_2=A_2-(a_i,a_\ell).
\]
Assume
\[
c_q+m<t,\qquad I_i\ne\varnothing,\qquad I_\ell\ne\varnothing,
\qquad \frac{(d_0+d_2)^2}{8}\ge M+m.
\]
Prove or refute the following breakpoint implication.  If, for some
\(r\in\{0,2\}\), either
\[
0\notin\operatorname{int}\operatorname{proj}_x(\widehat A_r)
\quad\text{or}\quad
0\notin\operatorname{int}\operatorname{proj}_y(\widehat A_r),
\]
then
\[
c_i+u_i+v_i\ge t
\quad\text{or}\quad
c_\ell+u_\ell+v_\ell\ge t.
\]
The projection condition includes an empty or full normalized cap and a cut
meeting the endpoint only in an exposed projection face.
tail-cap-breakpoint-support-coupling.success_criterion:
A proof must use compatibility, all three clips of the same middle polygon,
the strict \(q\)-tail, the actual minimizing shifts, and the exposed
support-face identities.  Support values, endpoint areas, or first-order
section conditions alone are insufficient by the round-101 thin-band family.
A refutation must give exact rational polygons \(A_0,A_2,K\), verify
compatibility and the residual strip, compute the two true profile minima,
and check every strict and breakpoint condition exactly.

tail-discrete-zero-profile-overlap-surpl.relation_to_goal: The breakpoint classification recorded for `tail-cap-breakpoint-support-coupling` reduces every strict-outside normalized profile to the discrete values \(0\) or \(m\). This subgoal isolates the \(Z_0\) orbit in which both non-tail profiles equal zero and explicitly restricts to the intended high-defect regime \(D_0>m\). Its conclusion removes that orbit from `canonical-tail-exclusion`; it does not address exposed-face/proper profiles or the other discrete substitutions.
tail-discrete-zero-profile-overlap-surpl.statement:
Let \(P,Q,K\subset\mathbb R^2\) be compact two-dimensional convex polygons with
\[
M=|P|\ge m=|Q|>0,\qquad k=|K|,
\qquad \frac{P+Q}{2}\subseteq K,
\]
\[
t=\frac{2(M+m+k)}9.
\]
Assume the exact residual area domain of accepted fact `15bb2c1680a0254e`. Define
\[
c_i=|K\cap\{x\ge0\}|,\qquad
c_\ell=|K\cap\{y\ge0\}|,\qquad
c_q=|K\cap\{x+y\le1\}|,
\]
\[
p_x=|P\cap\{x\ge0\}|+|Q\cap\{x\ge0\}|,\qquad
p_y=|P\cap\{y\ge0\}|+|Q\cap\{y\ge0\}|.
\]
Assume the double discrete-zero profile
\[
p_x=p_y=0,
\]
the three strict row inequalities
\[
c_i+p_x<t,\qquad c_\ell+p_y<t,\qquad c_q+m<t,
\]
and the high-defect condition
\[
D_0:=3t-k-m>m.
\]
For a convex polygon \(E\), put
\[
d(E)=\max_E(x+y)-\min_Ex-\min_Ey,
\]
and retain the support condition
\[
\frac{(d(P)+d(Q))^2}{8}\ge M+m.
\]
Prove that no such configuration exists. Equivalently, with
\[
\mathcal E_K=c_i+c_\ell+c_q-k,
\]
prove the overlap-surplus lower bound
\[
\mathcal E_K\ge D_0,
\]
which contradicts the three strict row inequalities.
tail-discrete-zero-profile-overlap-surpl.success_criterion: A proof must use the common compatible middle polygon and its exact pair/triple clip cells, retain the strict \(q\)-tail and every equality boundary, and explain how the support statistic enters the two-dimensional surplus. Positivity of the surplus alone is insufficient. A refutation must give rational vertices for \(P,Q,K\), verify midpoint containment by exact facet checks, compute all three clips and the overlap surplus exactly, and verify the residual strip, \(D_0>m\), and the support inequality.

tail-exposed-face-minimizer-shift-coupli.relation_to_goal:
The conclusion contradicts \(I_i,I_\ell\ne\varnothing\), so it proves the
support-hull bound left open in round 100.  The missing mechanism must use
the exposed faces attaining \(d_0,d_2\) together with the two actual
minimizing shifts.  Accepted obstacle calibration in
`.math-prover/handoffs/af8332205c6f4b58.md` shows inequalities using only
the eight cap areas cannot prove it.
tail-exposed-face-minimizer-shift-coupli.statement:
Assume the complete hypotheses of `canonical-tail-exclusion`, relabel
\(\{i,\ell,q\}=\{1,2,3\}\), and put
\[
x=g_i,\qquad y=g_\ell,\qquad
B=\frac{A_0+A_2}{2}.
\]
Assume \(c_q+m<t\), \(D_0>m\), and \(I_i,I_\ell\ne\varnothing\).
Choose shifts \(a_i,a_\ell\) minimizing the two true endpoint sums, and
write
\[
\begin{aligned}
u_i&=|A_0\cap\{x\ge-a_i\}|,&
v_i&=|A_2\cap\{x\ge a_i\}|,\\
u_\ell&=|A_0\cap\{y\ge-a_\ell\}|,&
v_\ell&=|A_2\cap\{y\ge a_\ell\}|.
\end{aligned}
\]
For \(r\in\{0,2\}\), define
\[
d_r=\max_{A_r}(x+y)-\min_{A_r}x-\min_{A_r}y.
\]
Prove
\[
\frac{(d_0+d_2)^2}{8}\ge M+m
\]
forces at least one of
\[
c_i+u_i+v_i\ge t,\qquad
c_\ell+u_\ell+v_\ell\ge t.
\]
tail-exposed-face-minimizer-shift-coupli.success_criterion:
A proof must identify how the exposed support faces enter an actual
Minkowski or section argument at the minimizing shifts and must handle
support-face and cap-breakpoint equalities.  A refutation must give one
exact rational compatible realization satisfying the support inequality
and both strict row inequalities.

tail-exposed-face-overlap-surplus.relation_to_goal: Adding the three strict tail inequalities gives the strict reverse of the proposed overlap-surplus bound. Therefore a proof excludes the irreducible exposed-face breakpoint cell of `tail-cap-breakpoint-support-coupling`. The remaining strict-outside breakpoint cases have discrete profile values \(0\) or \(m\). An exact compatible violation would show that even exposed-face section control does not supply the missing common-middle overlap payment.
tail-exposed-face-overlap-surplus.statement:
Let \(P,Q,K\subset\mathbb R^2\) be compact two-dimensional convex polygons with
\[
|P|=M\ge m=|Q|>0,\qquad |K|=k,\qquad \frac{P+Q}{2}\subseteq K,
\qquad t=\frac{2(M+m+k)}9,
\]
and assume the residual strip of accepted fact `15bb2c1680a0254e`. Define
\[
c_i=|K\cap\{x\ge0\}|,\quad
c_\ell=|K\cap\{y\ge0\}|,\quad
c_q=|K\cap\{x+y\le1\}|,
\]
\[
p_x=|P\cap\{x\ge0\}|+|Q\cap\{x\ge0\}|,\qquad
p_y=|P\cap\{y\ge0\}|+|Q\cap\{y\ge0\}|.
\]
Assume \(b=0\) is a global minimizer of each true shifted profile
\[
|P\cap\{x\ge-b\}|+|Q\cap\{x\ge b\}|,
\qquad
|P\cap\{y\ge-b\}|+|Q\cap\{y\ge b\}|.
\]
Retain the strict tail inequalities
\[
c_q+m<t,\qquad c_i+p_x<t,\qquad c_\ell+p_y<t.
\]
Assume the irreducible \(x\)-breakpoint state
\[
\max_Px=0,\qquad |P\cap\{x\ge0\}|=0,\qquad
0<|Q\cap\{x\ge0\}|<m,
\]
\[
L_{Q,x}(0+)\le\mathcal H_1(P\cap\{x=0\}),
\]
and define
\[
d_R=\max_R(x+y)-\min_Rx-\min_Ry\qquad(R=P,Q).
\]
Assume
\[
\frac{(d_P+d_Q)^2}{8}\ge M+m.
\]
With
\[
\mathcal E_K=c_i+c_\ell+c_q-k,\qquad D_0=3t-k-m,
\]
prove
\[
\mathcal E_K\ge D_0-p_x-p_y,
\]
or give exact rational polygons satisfying every hypothesis and violating it.
tail-exposed-face-overlap-surplus.success_criterion: Success is a complete common-plane proof using the actual inclusion \((P+Q)/2\subseteq K\), exposed support faces, the true profile minima, and the exact pair/triple clip cells, or an exact rational compatible violation. Endpoint support data without the same middle polygon and its exact clip-cell areas, a rectangle-only restatement of accepted fact `23e739786446ffe1`, or floating-point evidence does not count.

tail-exposed-fixed-middle-feasibility.relation_to_goal: The fixed \(K\) has the exact residual area, strict \(q\)-tail, two strict row budgets at prospective profile value \(1/10\), and pair/triple clip surplus strictly below the registered overlap target. A feasible endpoint pair would therefore give a complete common-plane counterexample to `tail-exposed-face-overlap-surplus` and expose a genuine failure of that tail mechanism. Exact infeasibility identifies which profile, support, or compatibility condition supplies the missing payment in the first aligned thin-strip family.
tail-exposed-fixed-middle-feasibility.statement:
Use coordinates \(u=x-y\), \(v=x+y\), so \(dx\,dy=\frac12\,du\,dv\), and fix
\[
M=1,\qquad m=\frac13,\qquad k=\frac{17}{25},\qquad
t=\frac{302}{675},
\]
\[
K=\left\{(u,v):
-100\le u\le100,\quad
\frac{101}{100}\le v\le\frac{1271}{1250}
\right\}.
\]
Decide whether there are rational parameters defining two-dimensional polygons
\[
P=\{v_P^-\le v\le v_P^+,\ u_P^-\le u\le-v\},
\]
\[
Q=[u_Q^-,u_Q^+]\times[v_Q^-,v_Q^+]
\]
such that
\[
|P|=1,\qquad |Q|=\frac13,\qquad P+Q\subseteq2K,
\]
\[
|P\cap\{x\ge0\}|+|Q\cap\{x\ge0\}|=\frac1{10},
\]
\[
|P\cap\{y\ge0\}|+|Q\cap\{y\ge0\}|=\frac1{10},
\]
and \(b=0\) is a global minimizer of both true profiles
\[
|P\cap\{x\ge-b\}|+|Q\cap\{x\ge b\}|,
\qquad
|P\cap\{y\ge-b\}|+|Q\cap\{y\ge b\}|.
\]
Also require
\[
\max_Px=0,\qquad 0<|Q\cap\{x\ge0\}|<\frac13,
\]
\[
L_{Q,x}(0+)\le\mathcal H_1(P\cap\{x=0\}),
\]
and, with \(d_R=\max_R(x+y)-\min_Rx-\min_Ry\),
\[
\frac{(d_P+d_Q)^2}{8}\ge\frac43.
\]
Either give exact rational feasible parameters, or prove this entire aligned family infeasible by exhausting all exact cap-breakpoint cells.
tail-exposed-fixed-middle-feasibility.status_reason: Accepted fact `5e220548124b44b4` proves the entire declared aligned endpoint family infeasible over the reals. The decisive contradiction uses the positive lower \(v\)-support forced by containment in the fixed thin-strip middle polygon: either \(P\) already contributes area \(1\) to the \(y\)-profile, or \(Q\) is covered by its nonnegative \(x\)- and \(y\)-caps, whose prescribed total is at most \(1/5<|Q|=1/3\). Hence no rational endpoint completion exists for this fixed \(K\).
tail-exposed-fixed-middle-feasibility.success_criterion: Success is an exact rational feasible parameter point with every area, global profile minimum, support statistic, section inequality, and containment checked, or a complete symbolic elimination over all breakpoint chambers of the declared family. A numerical search, partial chamber audit, or endpoint data without the fixed common middle polygon does not count.

tail-general-middle-to-row-triangle-redu.relation_to_goal:
Accepted fact `776bfada2b5ea3d7` excludes every row-aligned triangular
middle body with arbitrary compatible convex endpoints.  The registered
reduction would therefore prove the remaining \(D_0>m\) branch of
`tail-middle-cap-width-coupling`, and with the accepted complementary chamber
would close `canonical-tail-exclusion`.  If the reduction is false, the first
failed transfer identifies the extra middle-shape statistic that a general
proof must retain.
tail-general-middle-to-row-triangle-redu.statement:
Assume every hypothesis of the open subgoal
`tail-middle-cap-width-coupling`, with
\[
x=g_i,\qquad y=g_\ell,\qquad g_q=1-x-y,
\]
and suppose its joint inequality fails for a rational convex middle polygon
\(K\):
\[
\Psi_i(R_i)+\Psi_\ell(R_\ell)<2t-c_i-c_\ell.
\]
Prove or refute the following reduction.  There is a rational row-aligned
triangle
\[
\widetilde K=\{(x,y):x\ge-a,\ y\ge-b,\ x+y\le c\}
\]
such that the same \(A_0,A_2,g_i,g_\ell,g_q\) satisfy
\[
\frac{A_0+A_2}{2}\subseteq\widetilde K,
\]
the strict residual area hypotheses, \(\widetilde D_0>m\), and
\(\widetilde c_q+m<\widetilde t\), while
\[
\Psi_i(R_i)+\Psi_\ell(R_\ell)
<2\widetilde t-\widetilde c_i-\widetilde c_\ell.
\]
tail-general-middle-to-row-triangle-redu.status_reason:
Accepted counterexample `e1c09b85b6ceb583` also disproves the registered
row-triangle reduction: every row-aligned triangle containing its midpoint
body has area above the strict residual upper bound \(M+m\).  The reduction
fails before any cap-area transfer.
tail-general-middle-to-row-triangle-redu.success_criterion:
A proof must preserve the same endpoint profiles and verify the residual,
tail, and strict-deficit inequalities after compression, including boundary
cases.  A refutation must give exact rational \(K,A_0,A_2\) satisfying the
premise but show that every natural minimal row-aligned triangle fails a
named required transfer; a qualitative warning that caps are nonmonotone is
insufficient.

tail-middle-cap-width-coupling.relation_to_goal:
Brunn concavity gives
\[
\inf_a\mu_j(a)\ge c_j+\Psi_j(R_j).
\]
The displayed joint inequality therefore makes at least one of
\(I_i,I_\ell\) empty and closes the remaining \(D_0>m\), arbitrary unequal-width
part of `canonical-tail-exclusion`. Accepted fact `c40219b4edc1e373`
covers the complementary \(D_0\le m\) support-gap chamber, while
`e46ceefe535e9fa0` and `da3f020359d33bf2` cover only special shape classes.
tail-middle-cap-width-coupling.statement:
Assume every hypothesis of the open `canonical-tail-exclusion` subgoal, relabel
\(\{i,\ell,q\}=\{1,2,3\}\), and assume \(c_q+m<t\) and
\[
D_0=3t-k-m>m.
\]
Put \(g_j=-f_j\). For \(r\in\{0,2\}\), define
\[
\alpha_{rj}=\min_{A_r}g_j,\quad
\beta_{rj}=\max_{A_r}g_j,\quad
w_{rj}=\beta_{rj}-\alpha_{rj},
\]
\[
R_j=\beta_{0j}+\beta_{2j},\qquad

\end{cases}

\[

\]

\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
E+p_i+p_\ell\ge D_0,

tail-zero-fixed-six-cone-gluing.relation_to_goal: The obstacle for `tail-discrete-zero-profile-overlap-surplus` gives exact rational endpoints \(P,Q\) whose midpoint core is contained in \(D\), and verifies every residual, zero-profile, support, and strict cap-budget condition for precisely these six cone areas and strip area. An infeasibility proof identifies the convex gluing mechanism missing from the general overlap-surplus argument, but closes only this fixed calibration unless it proves a parameter-uniform inequality.
tail-zero-fixed-six-cone-gluing.statement:
Let
\[
D=\operatorname{conv}\left\{(0,0),
\left(-\frac{174}{121},0\right),
\left(0,-\frac{121}{200}\right)\right\}.
\]
Decide whether there exists a compact two-dimensional rational convex polygon \(K\subset\mathbb R^2\) such that
\[
D\subseteq K,\qquad |K|=1,
\]
and whose areas in the following six open cones are, in the displayed order,
\[
\begin{array}{c|c}
\text{cone}&\text{required area}\\ \hline
x<0,\ y<0&\dfrac{870}{2000}\\[2pt]
x>0,\ y<0,\ x+y>0&\dfrac{240}{2000}\\[2pt]
x<0,\ y>0,\ x+y>0&\dfrac{260}{2000}\\[2pt]
x>0,\ y>0&\dfrac{628}{2000}\\[2pt]
x<0,\ y>0,\ x+y<0&\dfrac1{2000}\\[2pt]
x>0,\ y<0,\ x+y<0&\dfrac1{2000}.
\end{array}
\]
Require in addition
\[
\left|K\cap\{0<x+y\le1\}\right|=\frac1{3000}.
\]
Either construct such a rational polygon and verify all areas exactly, or prove that no convex polygon, rational or otherwise, satisfies these conditions.
tail-zero-fixed-six-cone-gluing.status_reason: Accepted fact `0548e5e23c7fb2cc` proves that the complete fixed six-cone calibration is infeasible for every compact convex set. The two prescribed small negative-sum side cones and the contained negative-axis triangle force all positive-quadrant points below \(x+y=1\), contradicting the prescribed positive-quadrant and strip areas. This closes only `tail-zero-fixed-six-cone-gluing`; the parameter-uniform double-zero tail overlap-surplus subgoal remains open.

A nonexistence proof must apply to arbitrary convex \(K\), account for all three cutting lines and boundary-zero cases, and use the containment of \(D\). A scalar area table or separate non-glued cone pieces is insufficient.

tail-zero-side-cone-cost.relation_to_goal: Accepted fact `0548e5e23c7fb2cc` proves one fixed calibration by this mechanism. The parameter-uniform dichotomy converts two exact pair-cone areas and the two negative-axis core intercepts into a quantitative obstruction to placing positive-quadrant mass beyond the inhomogeneous \(q\)-cut. In the double-zero tail branch, it supplies a new common-middle inequality unavailable from clip multiplicity alone; it still must be coupled to endpoint geometry to bound \(p,q\).
tail-zero-side-cone-cost.statement:
Let \(K\subset\mathbb R^2\) be a compact two-dimensional convex set. Let \(p,q>0\) and assume
\[
\operatorname{conv}\{(0,0),(-p,0),(0,-q)\}\subseteq K.
\]
Define
\[
\beta=\left|K\cap\{x<0,\ y>0,\ x+y<0\}\right|,
\]
\[
\gamma=\left|K\cap\{x>0,\ y<0,\ x+y<0\}\right|,
\]
\[
\alpha=\left|K\cap\{x>0,\ y>0\}\right|,
\qquad
\eta=\left|K\cap\{0<x+y\le1\}\right|.
\]
Prove the dichotomy
\[
\alpha\le\eta
\]
or
\[
2\beta\left(\frac1{p^2}+\frac1p\right)
+2\gamma\left(\frac1{q^2}+\frac1q\right)>1.
\]
Equivalently, if the weighted side-cone cost is at most \(1\), then every positive-quadrant point of \(K\) lies in \(0<x+y\le1\) up to the cutting-line boundaries, and hence \(\alpha\le\eta\).
tail-zero-side-cone-cost.status_reason: Accepted fact `c3aabe018c39779d` proves the parameter-uniform side-cone cost dichotomy for arbitrary compact convex middle bodies, including strictness at \(x+y>1\) and all cutting-line boundaries. This closes `tail-zero-side-cone-cost`. To apply it to the full double-zero tail orbit, one still needs to derive usable negative-axis intercepts \(p,q\) from the compatible endpoint core and the two positive singleton cones.
tail-zero-side-cone-cost.success_criterion: A proof must work for arbitrary compact convex \(K\), derive the exact triangle areas forced by each positive-quadrant point, track the strictness when \(x+y>1\), and handle the three cutting lines as null boundaries. It must not cite the fixed numerical calibration as the proof. A refutation must give an exact rational convex polygon and exact cone areas violating the dichotomy.

tight-direction-allocation-singleton.statement:

`17ca54faa05ad878`, `65512ded3a06d971`, and

\[
 q\cdot z=\rho_q(t),
\]
then the feasible fixed-allocation interval
\[
 J_q(z)=
 \left[
 \max\{0,t-I_q(2q\cdot z)\},
 \min\{t,F_{1,q}(q\cdot z)\}
 \right]
\]
is the singleton
\[
 J_q(z)=\{F_{1,q}(q\cdot z)\}.
\]
Consequently, if one fixed allocation \(a\) certifies \(z\) in three
tight directions, their three middle cap areas are all equal to \(a\).
Include zero-demand and capacity endpoints.

allocation interval is exactly the singleton given by the actual middle
cap area, identifies it with the unique outer optimizer, handles all

Assume the full surviving below-half singleton-singleton transformed triangular system of accepted facts `63975845ca0e2926` and `a5bbbf5d61041b23`, with \((I_0,I_1,I_2)=(\{1\},\{2\},\varnothing)\). Prove the exact anchoring inequality
\[
A+c_1\ge t=\frac{2(1+A+B)}9,
\]
or give exact rational \(L,U,V,\sigma\) satisfying the complete barycentric system and all three strict row masses with \(A+c_1<t\).
triangle-below-half-singleton-anchor.success_criterion: The proof must use the full common matrices, compatibility, middle cap geometry, and all three row inequalities; a scalar cap vector is insufficient. A refutation must list complete rational matrices and shifts and verify the transformed system exactly.

triangle-below-half-singleton-p0-width.relation_to_goal: Accepted fact `4fd689ae05942244` reduces the universal width-product bridge to a lower bound on one small-endpoint coordinate-difference width. The endpoint-centroid midpoint signs and the small-endpoint cap budgets are the remaining inputs that can provide it.
triangle-below-half-singleton-p0-width.statement:
Assume the full below-half singleton-singleton branch and notation of accepted fact `4fd689ae05942244`. For \(j=2,3\), let \(f_j=x_1-x_j\), and define
\[
R_2=
\frac{18B\rho_1}{3B+2A-2}
+\frac{9B\rho_2}{1+B-A},
\qquad
R_3=
\frac{18B\rho_1}{3B+2A-2}
+\frac{18B\rho_3}{3-2(A+B)}.
\]
Prove that for some \(j=2,3\),
\[
\operatorname{width}_{f_j}(P_0)>\frac{R_j}{B}.
\]
Together with the strict bounds \(\operatorname{width}_{f_j}(P_2)<R_j\) from `4fd689ae05942244`, deduce the midpoint parallelogram obstruction and exclude the branch. Alternatively, give exact rational endpoints satisfying every branch hypothesis and both reverse width inequalities.
triangle-below-half-singleton-p0-width.status_reason: The exact obstacle in handoff `2fbc20c94b94405d.md` shows that opposite endpoint translation preserves the midpoint body and all relevant widths while increasing both proposed right sides without bound once the first caps become `u_1=1` and `v_1=0`. The width target therefore cannot be proved before establishing `A+c_1 >= t` or an equivalent full-row anchoring condition.
triangle-below-half-singleton-p0-width.success_criterion: The proof must derive the lower bound from accepted full-branch hypotheses without assuming a cap-free large endpoint or an active one-positive cell, and must handle all support ties. A refutation must verify the exact centroid, area, containment, cap, and width conditions and distinguish an endpoint obstruction from a full matrix counterexample.

triangle-below-half-singleton-width.relation_to_goal: Accepted fact `030a39d4d243e22a` proves the width-to-parallelogram mechanism when the large endpoint is cap-free and the small endpoint has the specified extreme-centroid active cell. A universal coordinate-difference width product above one closes the entire below-half singleton-singleton orbit; an exact endpoint refutation identifies which missing cap geometry must be retained.
triangle-below-half-singleton-width.statement:
Assume the full surviving transformed triangular \(N=3\) system of accepted facts `63975845ca0e2926` and `a5bbbf5d61041b23` with \(t\le1/2\), \(I_0=\{1\}\), \(I_1=\{2\}\), and \(I_2=\varnothing\). Thus \(0<A<B\), \(A/B<3/8\), \(A+B>1\), \(B<1+A\), and \((P_0+P_2)/2\subseteq P_1\), where \(|P_1|=1\). For \(j=2,3\), put \(f_j(x)=x_1-x_j\). Prove that for at least one \(j\),
\[
B\frac{\operatorname{width}_{f_j}(P_0)}
{\operatorname{width}_{f_j}(P_2)}>1.
\]
Deduce by an explicit midpoint parallelogram, including every support tie and edge-order boundary, that no normalized-area-one middle triangle can contain \((P_0+P_2)/2\). Alternatively, give an exact rational full strict system, or an exact rational endpoint pair satisfying every stated geometric and residual hypothesis for which both displayed width products are at most one.
triangle-below-half-singleton-width.success_criterion: The proof must derive the width product from the full strict system rather than assume the cap-free or active-cell hypotheses of `030a39d4d243e22a`, and must construct the parallelogram without choosing an invalid independent vertex labeling. A refutation must verify the complete stated centroid, area, containment, and width conditions exactly; only a full matrix witness may be called a counterexample.

triangle-bonus-arbitrary-frame.relation_to_goal:
Accepted fact `d2d117bcc58a1ba0` reduces any global counterexample to a
minimal three-halfplane cover of exactly this type.  This statement removes
the edge-parallel restriction from the sharp triangle model and is the first
shape-complete test of the proposed bonus-Grünbaum mechanism.
triangle-bonus-arbitrary-frame.statement:
Let \(\Delta\) be a nondegenerate planar triangle of area \(s\).  Let
\(L_1,L_2,L_3\) be closed halfplanes whose interiors cover
\(\mathbb R^2\), and suppose no two of their interiors cover
\(\mathbb R^2\).  Put \(p_i=|\Delta\cap L_i|\).  Prove that for every
\(e_1,e_2,e_3\ge0\),
\[
\max_i(p_i+e_i)\ge \frac49s+\frac{e_1+e_2+e_3}{3}.
\]
triangle-bonus-arbitrary-frame.status_reason:
The registered statement is false.  The exact obstacle in handoff
`da3f95af66cd4151.md` uses a minimal three-halfplane cover with cap areas
\((0,0,1)\) and bonuses \((1,1,0)\), for which the claimed lower bound is
\(10/9>1\).  Future work must use the structure of actual endpoint bonuses
or impose a quantitative small-bonus/near-equality condition.
triangle-bonus-arbitrary-frame.success_criterion:
A complete proof must handle arbitrary orientations and offsets, all ways the
three halfplanes cut the triangle, all nonnegative bonus triples, and all
degenerate boundary cases.  A reduction to finitely many explicitly proved
algebraic inequalities is acceptable; a numerical scan or an edge-parallel
proof alone is not.

triangle-bonus-arbitrary-small-frame.relation_to_goal:
The unrestricted bonus statement is false by the exact obstacle recorded for
`triangle-bonus-arbitrary-frame`.  This small-bonus version targets the
near-sharp regime.  If it holds and \(\min(a_0,a_2)\le a_1/100\), accepted
fact `0b5d84877f51b7c3` allows sub-bonuses totaling
\(\min(a_0,a_2)\); it then yields the same \(4a_1/9+m/3\) payment as the
edge-frame fact without assuming aligned cuts.
triangle-bonus-arbitrary-small-frame.statement:
Let \(\Delta\) be a nondegenerate planar triangle of area \(s\).  Let
\(L_1,L_2,L_3\) be closed halfplanes whose interiors cover
\(\mathbb R^2\), with no two interiors covering \(\mathbb R^2\), and put
\(p_i=|\Delta\cap L_i|\).  Prove that for all
\[
0\le e_i\le\frac{s}{100}\qquad(i=1,2,3),
\]
one has
\[
\max_i(p_i+e_i)\ge
\frac49s+\frac{e_1+e_2+e_3}{3}.
\]
triangle-bonus-arbitrary-small-frame.status_reason:
The exact rational cover in handoff `d0a949a038974144.md` has cap areas
\(p_1=p_3=50000000/111669789\) and
\(p_2=25000000/57108249\).  With bonuses
\((0,1/100,0)\), every corrected cap is strictly below
\(4/9+1/300\).  Therefore the registered \(1/100\) statement is false.
triangle-bonus-arbitrary-small-frame.success_criterion:
A proof must be uniform over arbitrary orientations, offsets, and all
triangle placements, with the explicit constant \(1/100\).  It must handle
every cap-combinatorial type and boundary case.  Compactness without an
explicit stability modulus, numerical evidence, or the already disproved
unrestricted statement is insufficient.

triangle-bonus-edge-frame.relation_to_goal:
This is the exact sharp covering game on the limiting triangle family from
accepted fact `43e70f89f224c5d7`.  It supplies the calibrated \(4/9\) and
\(1/3\) coefficients needed before attacking arbitrary three-direction
covers.  It is not by itself sufficient for the locked theorem.
triangle-bonus-edge-frame.statement:
Let \(\Delta\) be a nondegenerate planar triangle of area \(s\), with
barycentric coordinates \(\beta_1,\beta_2,\beta_3\).  For
\(0\le b_i\le1\), let
\[
L_i=\{x:\beta_i(x)\ge b_i\},\qquad
p_i=|\Delta\cap L_i|.
\]
Assume \(L_1\cup L_2\cup L_3=\mathbb R^2\), equivalently
\(b_1+b_2+b_3\le1\).  Prove that for every \(e_1,e_2,e_3\ge0\),
\[
\max_i(p_i+e_i)\ge \frac49s+\frac{e_1+e_2+e_3}{3},
\]
and determine all equality cases.
triangle-bonus-edge-frame.status_reason:
Accepted fact `79125fb2149eb8c2` proves the exact edge-frame
bonus-Grunbaum inequality for a triangle, including the plane-cover
equivalence, all boundary cases, and the equality characterization.
triangle-bonus-edge-frame.success_criterion:
A self-contained proof must establish the plane-cover equivalence, the exact
cap-area formula, the stated inequality for all nonnegative bonuses including
boundary cases, and the equality characterization.  No unproved stability or
general Grünbaum assertion may be used.

triangle-boundary-generic-perturbation.relation_to_goal: Accepted fact `bce2c51784540e70` proves this mechanism when exactly one entry is zero. A simultaneous generic perturbation would reduce every multi-zero boundary stratum to the already classified all-nonzero system, so no separate higher-codimension enumeration would be needed. Together with a future contained-support exclusion, it would finish every zero-entry boundary in this incidence orbit.
triangle-boundary-generic-perturbation.status_reason: Accepted fact `6986d9aa136ba907` proves that every arbitrary zero-entry boundary strict system is an arbitrarily small limit of all-nonzero strict systems in the contained-support orbit, while making no exclusion claim about that orbit.
triangle-boundary-generic-perturbation.success_criterion: Success is a complete perturbation proof for an arbitrary nonempty zero set, including determinant, centroid-incidence, compatibility, repeated endpoint values, and strict row masses, followed only by the stated reduction to the contained-support chamber. A codimension-one restatement or genericity assertion without an explicit perturbation space is insufficient.

triangle-centroid-row-incidence.relation_to_goal: The cyclic chamber is now closed because every middle row has the same large cap. For general invertible \(L\), the first missing global structure is whether the endpoint-centroid row can avoid every middle-centroid row. An exact incidence classification partitions the remaining triangular counterexample search into finitely many sign patterns and may rule out entire matrix chambers before optimization.
triangle-centroid-row-incidence.statement: In the surviving triangular \(N=3\) normal form, use the transformed coordinate-cap model \(P_0,P_1,P_2\) from accepted fact `09393c6edf1fc4e2`. Classify exactly which row indices can contain the centroids of \(P_0\) and \(P_1\) under three strict row-mass inequalities. At minimum, prove the same-row centroid incidence is impossible by combining the two planar Grünbaum bounds with the residual area inequalities. Then use the coordinate-sum planes and the exact triangle cap formula to eliminate as many of the remaining disjoint incidence patterns as possible, or exhibit a strict rational scalar/matrix survivor of one precisely declared pattern.
triangle-centroid-row-incidence.status_reason: Accepted fact `13c0df55864b79eb` gives the complete centroid-incidence classification, strict cross-cap budgets, and the additional \(A+B\le5/4\) vertex-sign and distinct-positive-column restrictions requested by the registered subgoal.
triangle-centroid-row-incidence.success_criterion: A verifier-ready lemma giving all forced disjointness, cardinality, sign, and cap-area inequalities for the centroid-incidence sets, together with an exact exclusion of at least one positive-dimensional noncyclic chamber or an exact rational full-system survivor. Merely restating that each three-halfplane cover contains a centroid is insufficient.

triangle-centroid-starvation-ledger.relation_to_goal:
At the middle centroid, every direction has middle contribution at least
\(4a_1/9\), and the only equality directions are the three displayed
centroidal vertex-cap directions. The missing payment is exactly \(d\).
Thus the proposed assertion would reduce any failure of the centroid witness
to one tight direction. A subsequent two-dimensional witness shift could
then exploit the other two paid directions. Even a sharp counterexample is
valuable because it decides whether Fable's proposed three-way exchange is a
real body-level invariant or only a numerical artifact.
triangle-centroid-starvation-ledger.statement:
Assume the locked problem, the full strict residual area strip of accepted
fact `15bb2c1680a0254e`, and that \(A_1\) is a nondegenerate triangle.
Write
\[
M=\max\{a_0,a_2\},\qquad m=\min\{a_0,a_2\},\qquad
d=\frac{2(M+m-a_1)}9,
\]
and let \(g_1\) be the centroid of \(A_1\).

For the three directions \(q_i\) whose lower caps through \(g_1\) are the
three centroidal vertex caps of \(A_1\), define the exact endpoint payments
\[
J_i=
\inf_{c_0+c_2=2q_i\cdot g_1}
\left(F_{0,q_i}(c_0)+F_{2,q_i}(c_2)\right).
\]

Prove that at most one index satisfies \(J_i<d\). If this literal claim is
false, give an exact compatible rational residual counterexample and replace
it by the strongest correct quantitative inequality among
\((J_1,J_2,J_3)\) that follows from midpoint containment and the common
three-cap partition of \(A_1\).
triangle-centroid-starvation-ledger.status_reason:
Accepted fact `6eb36ee892a70d82` proves the literal claim in the stronger
pairwise form
\[
J_i+J_j\ge
\min\left\{m,\ M+m-\frac{8a_1}{9}\right\}>2d
\]
for every two distinct centroid-tight directions. Hence at most one
direction has \(J_i\le d\), including all boundary cases.
triangle-centroid-starvation-ledger.success_criterion:
Success requires a complete proof using actual endpoint bodies, exact
infimal convolution, midpoint containment, and the exact triangle cap
partition, with strict and boundary cases handled. A false result requires
explicit rational polygons or triangles, exact residual and compatibility
checks, and exact evaluations showing two \(J_i<d\). A replacement inequality
must be stated with exact constants and must be strong enough to constrain a
common witness shift; merely observing that one \(J_i\) is positive is
insufficient.

Its singleton positive support is contained in the second row's two-positive support, a sign geometry not covered by accepted facts `b894a3da1107beaf` or `76bff99d5eaaa46f`. Excluding it removes one third of the remaining open chamber problem in `triangle-three-row-exclusion`; an exact full witness would refute the all-triangle route and could refute the locked target.

Assume the full transformed triangular (N=3) system and canonical notation of accepted facts `64760c76cadff481`, `09393c6edf1fc4e2`, `f8e871d10dac1791`, and `82b7c8c40e88aaf1`, in the incidence orbit

Restrict to the open middle sign chamber
\[

\]
Prove that no nondegenerate matrices (U,V,L) and independent shifts (sigma_1,sigma_2,sigma_3) satisfy midpoint compatibility, the strict residual area strip, and all three strict low-row inequalities. Alternatively, give an exact rational or algebraic witness satisfying the complete original (N=3) system.

triangle-chamber-contained-two.success_criterion: Success is a complete exact exclusion of this chamber in the original (U,V,L,\sigma) system, including determinant, compatibility, cap-order, zero-demand, and strict-boundary cases, or one exact complete witness. A middle-matrix or scalar calibration without endpoint matrices and shifts is insufficient.

Prove that the complete system has no strict counterexample in this chamber, or give an exact rational or algebraic compatible (U,V,L,\sigma) witness satisfying all three original strict low-row inequalities.
triangle-chamber-crossed-two.status_reason: Accepted fact `37f97f30533ded8d` eliminates the complete crossed two-positive-support chamber, uniformly over all endpoint completions and independent shifts.

Every endpoint cap ordering, determinant sign, independent shift, equality boundary used in an intermediate weak inequality, and strict final row inequality must be covered. Prove that the complete system has no strict counterexample in this chamber, or give an exact rational or algebraic compatible (U,V,L,\sigma) witness satisfying all three original strict low-row inequalities.
triangle-chamber-equal-two.status_reason: Accepted fact `20ed70c898723fda` eliminates the complete equal two-positive-support chamber, uniformly over all endpoint completions and independent shifts.
triangle-chamber-equal-two.success_criterion: Success is an exact chamber-wide elimination in the full (U,V,L,\sigma) system or an exact complete witness. The proof must include all endpoint and strict-boundary cases and may use symbolic computation only through a reproducible exact certificate. Middle signs alone are insufficient.

triangle-chamber-one-two.statement:

\[

\]
Restrict to the open middle sign chamber

J_1=\{2\},\qquad J_2=\{1,3\},\qquad J_3=\{1\}.

Prove that no nondegenerate matrices (U,V,L) and independent shifts (sigma_1,sigma_2,sigma_3) satisfy midpoint compatibility, the strict residual area strip, and all three strict low-row inequalities. Alternatively, give an exact rational or algebraic compatible witness satisfying the complete (N=3) system.
triangle-chamber-one-two.status_reason: Accepted fact `76bff99d5eaaa46f` eliminates the entire open chamber (J_1=\{2\},J_2=\{1,3\},J_3=\{1\}) in the full exact (N=3) system.
