Symbolic computation may support the result only when accompanied by a reproducible exact certificate. A middle-matrix calibration without endpoint matrices and shifts is not a witness.

triangle-contained-b-ge-one.relation_to_goal: Accepted fact `8772b8ab38a4e1b6` excludes the strongest fixed survivor with (B>1) by a third-row endpoint lower bound after normalizing actual endpoint row minima. Extending that mechanism throughout (B\ge1) would remove the first natural half of the sole contained-support chamber. A witness would refute the proposed chamber exclusion and may give a triangle counterexample.
triangle-contained-b-ge-one.statement:
Assume the full transformed triangular (N=3) system, incidence orbit, and sole surviving open middle chamber of accepted facts `f8e871d10dac1791` and `89f1aef98e9b8915`:
\[
J_1=\{2\},\qquad J_2=\{2,3\},\qquad J_3=\{1\},
\]
with normalized areas (0<A<B), (t=2(1+A+B)/9\le1/2), and the strict residual conditions. Under the additional regime (B\ge1), prove that no compatible nonsingular (U,V,L) and independent shift (\sigma) satisfy all three strict low-row inequalities. Alternatively, give an exact rational or algebraic full witness in this regime.
triangle-contained-b-ge-one.status_reason: Accepted fact `806575336d04fac7`, using accepted facts `31dfbaba9be6f34d` and `cc32eb5039621c6b`, excludes every `B>1` branch, while accepted fact `27ae487131bcd122` includes `B=1`.
triangle-contained-b-ge-one.success_criterion: Success is a chamber-wide exact contradiction for every (B\ge1), including all middle parameters, endpoint orders, determinant signs, compatibility boundaries, and independent shifts, or one exact full witness. A fixed calibration or scalar relaxation is insufficient.

triangle-contained-b-le-one.relation_to_goal: The fixed (B>1) proof uses that the larger normalized endpoint cannot fit as a subtriangle of the simplex after a nonpositive row-minimum shift. That sign argument fails when (B\le1), making this a genuinely different area regime. Together with the (B\ge1) subgoal, its exclusion closes the only all-nonzero triangle chamber; accepted fact `6986d9aa136ba907` would then reduce every zero boundary to the same contradiction.
triangle-contained-b-le-one.statement: Assume the same full transformed triangular (N=3) system, incidence orbit, and sole contained-support chamber, now under the complementary regime (B\le1). Prove that no compatible nonsingular (U,V,L) and independent shift (\sigma) satisfy all three strict low-row inequalities, or give an exact rational or algebraic full witness. Equality (B=1) must be covered literally.
triangle-contained-b-le-one.status_reason: Accepted fact `27ae487131bcd122` proves a middle-only inequality that contradicts all strict rows throughout (B\le1), including (B=1), and composes with accepted boundary perturbation to cover every zero-entry stratum in that regime.
triangle-contained-b-le-one.success_criterion: Success is a complete exact exclusion for (B\le1), including equality and every endpoint cap boundary, or one exact full witness. Arguments that assume the (B>1) sign of the row-minimum sum or test selected middle matrices do not count.

triangle-contained-endpoint-stability.relation_to_goal: The round-119 obstacle shows that every completion of the exact surviving middle calibration must nearly partition the bottom endpoint caps while making all top caps nearly empty. The displayed inequality is the first precise compatibility statement that would rule out that behavior and close the only remaining nonzero-entry chamber in accepted fact `89f1aef98e9b8915`. An exact refutation prevents this route from being retried and supplies concrete endpoint geometry for a witness search.
triangle-contained-endpoint-stability.statement:
Use the full transformed triangular (N=3) system and canonical notation of accepted facts `64760c76cadff481`, `f8e871d10dac1791`, and `89f1aef98e9b8915` in the sole surviving open chamber
\[
J_1=\{2\},\qquad J_2=\{2,3\},\qquad J_3=\{1\}.
\]
With (A=|\det U|), (B=|\det V|), (t=2(1+A+B)/9), middle cap fractions (c_i), and endpoint cap fractions (u_i,v_i), prove or refute the chamber-wide inequality
\[
A\left(\sum_{i=1}^3u_i-1\right)+B\sum_{i=1}^3v_i
\ge 3t-A-\sum_{i=1}^3c_i.
\]
A refutation must give exact compatible nondegenerate (U,V,L,\sigma) data in this chamber and verify every quantity. A proof, combined with the summed strict row budgets, excludes the entire chamber.
triangle-contained-endpoint-stability.status_reason: Accepted fact `806575336d04fac7` excludes the entire containing chamber through the exact capacity partition, so the auxiliary summed endpoint-stability inequality is no longer needed. This status makes no claim about the truth of that separate inequality.
triangle-contained-endpoint-stability.success_criterion: Success is a proof for every compatible completion, with all endpoint orders, determinant signs, independent shifts, and equality cases, or an exact full compatible counterexample to the inequality. A scalar cap table or middle-only calibration is insufficient.

triangle-contained-fixed-completion.relation_to_goal: Accepted fact `7d66445eba62df98` proves that these fixed (A,B,L) satisfy every known middle and scalar condition in the sole surviving contained-support chamber, but asserts no endpoints. A rational completion is a complete exact (N=3) witness for this chamber and may yield a triangle counterexample. Exact infeasibility identifies the missing endpoint constraint without requiring a universal inequality.
triangle-contained-fixed-completion.statement:
Fix the exact rational middle and area data from accepted fact `7d66445eba62df98`:
\[
A=\frac18,\qquad B=\frac{11249}{10000},\qquad
t=\frac{22499}{45000},
\]
\[
L=
\begin{pmatrix}
-32877&46362&-17003\\
-67122&2&53678\\
100000&-46363&-36674
\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Decide exact endpoint completion in the full system of accepted facts `64760c76cadff481` and `09393c6edf1fc4e2`: either give rational nonsingular column-stochastic matrices (U,V) and a rational independent shift vector (\sigma) satisfying row-min compatibility and all three strict low-row inequalities, or prove that no real (U,V,\sigma) complete these fixed data.
triangle-contained-fixed-completion.status_reason: Accepted fact `8772b8ab38a4e1b6` proves a global third-row lower bound for every real compatible endpoint completion of the fixed calibration, so the fixed completion system is infeasible.
triangle-contained-fixed-completion.success_criterion: Success is exact rational (U,V,\sigma) data with determinants, column sums, row-min compatibility, cap areas, and strict row budgets checked, or a complete exact infeasibility proof over all real endpoint matrices and shifts. Floating-point infeasibility, a local search, or failure of one ansatz is insufficient.

triangle-contained-full-composition.relation_to_goal: Accepted fact `27ae487131bcd122` excludes \(B\leq1\). For \(B>1\), accepted facts `cc32eb5039621c6b` and `31dfbaba9be6f34d` should form an exhaustive weak-inequality partition according to whether both actual inverse-capacity arguments are at least the join \(h\), or at least one is at most \(h\). Accepted fact `6986d9aa136ba907` should then transfer the complete open-chamber exclusion to every zero-entry boundary system. This composition would close `triangle-chamber-contained-two` and `triangle-contained-b-ge-one`, but it would not by itself exclude the other centroid-incidence or residual regimes in `triangle-three-row-exclusion`.
triangle-contained-full-composition.statement:
Assume the surviving transformed triangular \(N=3\) system, incidence orbit, and residual regime of accepted facts `f8e871d10dac1791`, `89f1aef98e9b8915`, and `6986d9aa136ba907`:
\[
I_0=\{1,2\},\qquad I_1=\{3\},\qquad t\leq\frac12.
\]
Prove that no strict system exists in the contained-support middle chamber
\[
J_1=\{2\},\qquad J_2=\{2,3\},\qquad J_3=\{1\},
\]
for any admissible \(0<A<B\), including every all-nonzero switch branch, \(B=1\), and every stratum with one or more zero entries of the middle matrix.
triangle-contained-full-composition.status_reason: Accepted fact `806575336d04fac7` composes the `B<=1` exclusion, both exhaustive `B>1` switch alternatives, and the zero-entry perturbation theorem without assigning a limiting boundary branch.
triangle-contained-full-composition.success_criterion: Success is a complete accepted-only composition that states the exact common hypotheses and notation maps, partitions \(B\leq1\) from \(B>1\), proves the two \(B>1\) switch alternatives exhaustive including \(d=e\) and both switch equalities, and applies the accepted perturbation theorem to all zero-entry strata without assuming a branch is preserved at the boundary. It must claim no conclusion outside the stated incidence orbit and residual regime.

triangle-contained-third-envelope.relation_to_goal: Accepted fact `8772b8ab38a4e1b6` proves this endpoint lower bound for one exact third row and area pair using a lossless row-minimum normalization and triangle-cap capacity. A parameter-uniform version would exclude the contained chamber in one step, independently of the (B\ge1/B\le1) split, and then accepted fact `6986d9aa136ba907` would absorb every zero boundary.
triangle-contained-third-envelope.statement:
In the full sole contained-support chamber, write the third middle row as
\[
g=L_{3*}=(p,-a,-b),\qquad p,a,b>0,qquad p-a-b>3,
\]
and (c_3=p^2/((p+a)(p+b))<t). Determine a universal exact lower envelope for
\[
A\mathcal C((LU)_{3*};-\sigma_3)
+B\mathcal C((LV)_{3*};\sigma_3)
\]
over every compatible column-stochastic endpoint pair (U,V) with areas (A,B) and every shift (\sigma_3). Prove that this envelope is at least (t-c_3) throughout the contained-support chamber, or give exact chamber data and a full compatible endpoint completion strictly below the budget.
triangle-contained-third-envelope.status_reason: Accepted fact `83ae76262528a9f8` gives the exact branch-aware finite capacity envelope and a rational obstruction showing why the first two strict rows are indispensable for a full chamber conclusion.
triangle-contained-third-envelope.success_criterion: Success is a closed-form or exact piecewise lower envelope with a complete proof on all chamber parameters and endpoint boundary cells, followed by the budget comparison, or an exact full compatible counterexample to that comparison. A sufficient condition covering only one calibration or one (B) regime is a partial candidate only if sharply stated.

triangle-cover-asymptotic-edge-rigidity.relation_to_goal: A residual counterexample with \(x\to0\), \(y\to1\) has middle cap masses at most \(4/9+o(1)\). This lemma would give the missing anchored common-frame stability directly for a triangle, without relying on the published unanchored Grünbaum stability theorem. It is the qualitative alignment input needed before using the accepted edge-frame payment.
triangle-cover-asymptotic-edge-rigidity.statement:
Let \(\Delta\subset\mathbb R^2\) be a fixed unit-area triangle with barycentric coordinates \(\beta_1,\beta_2,\beta_3\). For each \(n\), let \(L_{1,n},L_{2,n},L_{3,n}\) be proper closed halfplanes whose interiors form a minimal cover of \(\mathbb R^2\), and put \(p_{i,n}=|\Delta\cap L_{i,n}|\). Assume
\[
\max_i p_{i,n}\longrightarrow\frac49.
\]
Prove that, after passing to a subsequence and relabeling once, the cap sides and boundary lines converge to
\[
\{\beta_i\ge1/3\},\qquad \{\beta_i=1/3\}\qquad(i=1,2,3),
\]
respectively. State and prove a precise affine-coordinate notion of convergence that includes cuts through vertices and rules out parallel or escaping limits. If the assertion is false, give an exact counterexample sequence.
triangle-cover-asymptotic-edge-rigidity.status_reason: Accepted fact `fe06938594bbc0e2` proves the full sequential anchored edge-frame rigidity, including all offset, vertex, parallel, relabeling, and strict-cover limit issues.
triangle-cover-asymptotic-edge-rigidity.success_criterion: A complete sequential compactness and equality-classification proof, including all degeneracies and the strict-cover-to-limit boundary issue, or an exact sequence disproving the claimed convergence.

triangle-cover-first-order-bonus-stabili.relation_to_goal: Accepted fact `82eb4941d401611c` shows the exact arbitrary-frame bonus inequality is false, but its exhibited deficit is quadratic while the frame and bonus perturbations are linear. A verified first-order stability statement would show that this failure is negligible in the pinch scale and would permit the accepted edge-frame budget to survive asymptotically.
triangle-cover-first-order-bonus-stabili.statement:
Let \(\Delta\) be a fixed unit-area triangle. For each \(n\), let \(L_{1,n},L_{2,n},L_{3,n}\) be a minimal cover of \(\mathbb R^2\) by interiors of proper closed halfplanes, let \(p_{i,n}=|\Delta\cap L_{i,n}|\), and let \(e_{i,n}\ge0\). Assume
\[
\eta_n:=\max_i p_{i,n}-\frac49\longrightarrow0,
\qquad
E_n:=\max_i e_{i,n}\longrightarrow0.
\]
Determine whether the uniform first-order stability assertion
\[
\frac{\displaystyle
\frac49+\frac13\sum_i e_{i,n}
-\max_i(p_{i,n}+e_{i,n})}
{\eta_n+E_n}
\longrightarrow0
\]
holds whenever the numerator is positive. If true, prove it with an explicit finite-\(n\) modulus or inequality. If false, give an exact rational or algebraic counterexample sequence and identify the correct leading-order obstruction.
triangle-cover-first-order-bonus-stabili.status_reason: Accepted fact `ec6e09a5f4174d11` proves the registered first-order little-o stability and the explicit \(51\sqrt{\eta}\) normalized-error bound.
triangle-cover-first-order-bonus-stabili.success_criterion: A rigorous proof of the displayed sequential limit with a usable explicit modulus, or an exact counterexample sequence whose normalized deficit has a positive limit. Numerical sampling alone is not sufficient.

triangle-cyclic-chamber-upper-s.relation_to_goal: Accepted fact `b8a065ca6eeaad3f` handles only \(A=1/4,B=1\). The same exact middle-cap identity and small-end covering charge depend affinely on \(A,B\), and should remove a full two-dimensional area-parameter region from this tube-exterior chamber.
triangle-cyclic-chamber-upper-s.statement:
Assume the exact \(N=3\) triangular barycentric system in the surviving orientation, with
\[
A=|\det U|\le B=|\det V|,\qquad
r=\frac AB,\qquad S=\frac1B,\qquad 0<r<\frac38.
\]
Suppose that after row and column permutations the scale-free middle-row matrix is
\[
\begin{pmatrix}
p&-a&-b\\
-b&p&-a\\
-a&-b&p
\end{pmatrix},
\qquad p>a+b>0.
\]
Prove that
\[
\max_i\left(M_i-\frac{2(1+A+B)}9\right)
>
\frac{2S+r-2}{9S}.
\]
Consequently the entire cyclic chamber is infeasible whenever \(S\ge1-r/2\), including equality.
triangle-cyclic-chamber-upper-s.status_reason: Accepted fact `502f13a9d8075464` proves the registered strict cyclic-chamber gap and excludes the full region \(S\ge1-r/2\), including the equality boundary.
triangle-cyclic-chamber-upper-s.success_criterion: A self-contained exact proof with arbitrary allowed endpoint matrices and allocations, deriving the displayed strict gap and checking the equality boundary \(S=1-r/2\). No claim outside the declared cyclic chamber is required.

triangle-cyclic-complement-bm-envelope.relation_to_goal: The accepted aggregate charge in `b8a065ca6eeaad3f` discards all large-end caps and closes only part of the area domain after generalization. The complement midpoint inclusion couples the two endpoint allocations row by row. Its sharp scalar envelope may close the remaining low-\(S\) cyclic chamber or isolate the exact additional geometric input still needed.
triangle-cyclic-complement-bm-envelope.statement:
In the exact triangular \(N=3\) system, assume the scale-free middle-row matrix is, up to row and column permutations,
\[
R=
\begin{pmatrix}
p&-a&-b\\
-b&p&-a\\
-a&-b&p
\end{pmatrix},
\qquad p>a+b>0.
\]
Put
\[
c=\frac{p^2}{(p+a)(p+b)}.
\]
For row \(i\), let \(x_i\) and \(y_i\) be the absolute areas of its caps in the endpoint triangles of areas \(A\le B\). Prove
\[
\sum_i x_i\ge A
\]
and
\[
\sqrt{A-x_i}+\sqrt{B-y_i}\le2\sqrt{1-c}
\qquad(i=1,2,3).
\]
Then solve exactly the resulting scalar minimization problem for
\[
E=\sum_i(x_i+y_i)
\]
over \(0\le x_i\le A\), \(0\le y_i\le B\), and determine the sharp explicit lower bound on \(E\) in terms of \(A,B,c\).
triangle-cyclic-complement-bm-envelope.status_reason: Accepted fact `175c06cec5338340` proves the registered complement-midpoint Brunn--Minkowski inequality, solves the complete scalar allocation problem sharply in all chambers, and identifies the exact remaining scalar residual.
triangle-cyclic-complement-bm-envelope.success_criterion: A verifier-ready proof of both geometric inequalities, including open/closed boundary conventions and degenerate cap complements, followed by a complete exact solution of the finite scalar optimization. State precisely the \((A,B,c)\) region where \(3c+E\) reaches the three-row target, and the exact residual region if it does not.

triangle-cyclic-residual-geometric-reali.relation_to_goal: By the accepted triangular iff system, any strict rational realization is a counterexample to the locked target. An exact exclusion removes a substantial cyclic chamber that survives the balanced-neighborhood and aggregate endpoint-cover bounds.
triangle-cyclic-residual-geometric-reali.statement:
In the exact triangular \(N=3\) barycentric system, restrict the middle-row matrix, up to row and column permutations and positive scale, to
\[
\begin{pmatrix}
p&-a&-b\\
-b&p&-a\\
-a&-b&p
\end{pmatrix},
\qquad p>a+b>0.
\]
Determine whether the remaining low-\(S\), low-endpoint-ratio parameter region contains a full geometric realization: column-stochastic nonsingular endpoint matrices \(U,V\) satisfying exact midpoint compatibility, and height levels \(\sigma_i\), for which all three literal row masses are strictly below \(2(1+|\det U|+|\det V|)/9\). Produce a strict rational realization if one exists; otherwise prove an exact geometric or quantile obstruction on a nontrivial chamber containing the scalar calibration \(p=65\), \(a=b=32\), \(|\det U|=441/4000\), \(|\det V|=441/400\).
triangle-cyclic-residual-geometric-reali.status_reason: Accepted fact `ebc88d35821abdcb` excludes the entire declared cyclic one-positive chamber, including the registered scalar calibration, by a common endpoint-centroid cover argument with a strict row-mass gap.
triangle-cyclic-residual-geometric-reali.success_criterion: Either a rational \(U,V,L,\sigma\) certificate whose determinants, column sums, compatibility minima, residual inequalities, and three strict cap masses are all checked exactly, or a verifier-ready theorem excluding a sharply declared positive-dimensional cyclic parameter chamber using the full geometric constraints rather than only scalar cap budgets.

triangle-double-proper-capacity-composit.relation_to_goal: The round-125 capacity attempt failed because \(p/s\) and \(r/s\) could diverge in middle-only data. Accepted fact `987dc770ddaf5b3b` removes that obstruction and gives a fixed shifted-cap decrement. Composing that decrement with the proper-cap image and the three row budgets can close the surviving below-half double-singleton branch.
triangle-double-proper-capacity-composit.statement:
Assume the full proper-small-cap double-singleton branch of accepted facts `a61bda3f7065e3e1` and `987dc770ddaf5b3b`. Use the canonical middle rows \((p,-a,-b)\) and \((-c,r,-d)\), put \(s=(2-(g_2)_3)/4\), and let
\[
D=\frac{(P_0\cap\{x_3<0\})+g_2}{2}.
\]
Prove the exact capacity inequality
\[
\left|P_1\cap\{x_1>s\}\right|
+\left|P_1\cap\{x_2>s\}\right|
<
\frac{A(1-u_3)}4,
\]
using the uniform support-ratio bound, all three literal row inequalities, and endpoint compatibility. Deduce that the required containment of \(D\) in the union of those two deep caps is impossible. Alternatively, give exact rational full matrices satisfying the proper branch and all three strict row masses, or isolate the first exact scalar inequality still missing after `987dc770ddaf5b3b`.
triangle-double-proper-capacity-composit.status_reason: The exact obstacle in handoff `ceb6fe3cfaf042e0.md` shows that the bound from `987dc770ddaf5b3b`, even with all compressed scalar covers and row budgets, lies on the wrong side of the required comparison with `A(1-u_3)/4`. The proposed composition is therefore insufficient. The surviving test is the full common-matrix optimization of the exact joint gap `G` on every cap-order and endpoint min-column stratum.
triangle-double-proper-capacity-composit.success_criterion: The proof must compare the exact union-capacity upper bound with \(A(1-u_3)/4\), retain strictness uniformly over the residual area strip and every cap-order boundary, and use all full-system constraints needed for the comparison. A counterexample must be a complete exact matrix witness; a scalar or middle-only feasible point is an obstacle, not a counterexample.

triangle-double-proper-deep-cap-capacity.relation_to_goal: The round-124 obstacle proves that properness at endpoint level zero supplies no uniform bonus at the translated centroid level. The displayed two-deep-cap containment is the first surviving shape-sensitive coupling. A branch-wide capacity contradiction closes `triangle-double-singleton-proper`; a feasible exact matrix point redirects the search toward a full counterexample.
triangle-double-proper-deep-cap-capacity.statement:
Assume the full proper-small-cap double-singleton branch of `triangle-double-singleton-proper` and the notation of accepted fact `a61bda3f7065e3e1`:
\[
t\leq\frac12,\qquad I_0=\{3\},\qquad I_1=\{1,2\},\qquad 0<u_3<1,
\]
with endpoint centroids \(g_0,g_2\). Define
\[
D=\frac{(P_0\cap\{x_3<0\})+g_2}{2}.
\]
Then \(|D|=A(1-u_3)/4\) and
\[
D\subseteq
\left(P_1\cap\left\{x_1>\frac{2-(g_2)_3}{4}\right\}\right)
\cup
\left(P_1\cap\left\{x_2>\frac{2-(g_2)_3}{4}\right\}\right).
\]
Using the exact middle support and cap-order strata together with the two strict literal row inequalities for rows \(1,2\), prove that the right-hand union has capacity strictly less than \(A(1-u_3)/4\), contradicting the containment, or give exact rational full matrices showing that the capacity comparison can be feasible.
triangle-double-proper-deep-cap-capacity.status_reason: The exact obstacle packet in handoff `4a36002d89b4454d.md` gives a rational nonsingular middle-matrix family in which the shifted deep-cap fractions approach their zero-level values while the two registered row budgets remain strict. The proposed two-row capacity bound is therefore false without a new endpoint-compatibility and third-row estimate controlling the support-to-threshold ratios.
triangle-double-proper-deep-cap-capacity.success_criterion: Success is a complete exact capacity bound across every middle row-3 sign and cap-order stratum, all determinant signs, compatibility boundaries, and shifts, or one exact rational full matrix realization with the deep-cap set and all three original row masses audited. A scalar area table or the separate centroid `4/9` bounds is insufficient.

triangle-double-proper-joint-gap.relation_to_goal: The constant shifted-cap decrement is insufficient because \(A(1-u_3)\) can be tiny. The exact sign of \(G\) is the remaining capacity statement after all full-system variables are restored. Proving \(G<0\) closes the proper branch; a rational point with \(G\ge0\) is a full counterexample candidate.
triangle-double-proper-joint-gap.statement:
Assume the full proper-small-cap double-singleton branch of accepted facts `a61bda3f7065e3e1` and `987dc770ddaf5b3b`. In their canonical notation, define
\[
G=
c_1\left(1-\frac{s}{p}\right)_+^2
+c_2\left(1-\frac{s}{r}\right)_+^2
-\frac{A(1-u_3)}4.
\]
On every exact middle cap-order and endpoint compatibility min-column stratum, prove \(G<0\), or give one complete exact rational \(L,U,V,\sigma\) satisfying the proper branch, all determinant and compatibility conditions, and all three strict literal row masses with \(G\ge0\). A proof may first derive an exact common-middle cap inequality using the forced third row and the mean condition \(s_1+s_2>3\).
triangle-double-proper-joint-gap.status_reason: Accepted fact `b560c6034ab62114` proves that the full proper-small-cap double-singleton system is infeasible by incompatible exact bounds on the common nonpositive middle chamber. Consequently every cap-order and endpoint min-column stratum is excluded.
triangle-double-proper-joint-gap.success_criterion: The proof must retain the common column equations, \(s_1+s_2>3\), determinant nonzero, endpoint compatibility, the exact cap formulas, and all three strict row masses. A solver result requires an independently checkable exact certificate; a scalar relaxation is only an obstacle.

triangle-double-singleton-proper.relation_to_goal: Accepted fact `ba386361546eb82d` handles a full third small-endpoint cap in a parameter region, and accepted fact `8c5188758a915a64` handles one symmetric middle family for \(1/4\leq A/B<3/8\). The proper-cap branch remains a separate terminal component of `triangle-three-row-exclusion`. The decisive missing mechanism must use the actual proper cap together with the point \(h_3>1\), not another specialization of the symmetric middle matrix.
triangle-double-singleton-proper.statement:
Assume the full surviving triangular \(N=3\) system of accepted facts `09393c6edf1fc4e2`, `13c0df55864b79eb`, `291c24bb45bd4946`, and `64760c76cadff481`, with
\[
t\leq\frac12,qquad I_0=\{3\},\qquad I_1=\{1,2\},qquad 0<u_3<1.
\]
Thus \(0<A/B<3/8\), and accepted fact `a61bda3f7065e3e1` gives an endpoint-centroid midpoint \(h\in P_1\) with \(h_1,h_2<0\) and \(h_3>1\). Prove that no compatible nonsingular endpoint matrices, middle triangle, and independent shifts satisfy all three strict literal row inequalities throughout this proper-small-cap branch, or give one exact rational full witness to the original matrix system.
triangle-double-singleton-proper.status_reason: Accepted fact `b560c6034ab62114` excludes the complete proper-small-cap double-singleton branch registered in `triangle-double-singleton-proper`, including all ratio, cap-order, determinant-sign, and compatibility boundary cases in its hypotheses.
triangle-double-singleton-proper.success_criterion: Success is a complete exact exclusion of the stated branch for every \(0<A/B<3/8\), all middle sign and cap-order strata, determinant signs, compatibility boundaries, and shifts, or one exact rational full witness checked in the original system. A symmetric-row subfamily, fixed ratio, or scalar relaxation is insufficient.

triangle-double-support-ratio-compatibil.relation_to_goal: The round-125 deep-cap obstacle proves that the two zero-level middle row budgets alone do not bound the shifted cap capacity. Endpoint compatibility and the third literal row are the only remaining available constraints that can control \(\max\{p,r\}/s\). Such control supplies the missing quantitative loss for `triangle-double-singleton-proper`; an exact full divergent witness refutes this capacity route and may yield a counterexample.
triangle-double-support-ratio-compatibil.statement:
Assume the full proper-small-cap double-singleton branch of `triangle-double-singleton-proper` and accepted fact `a61bda3f7065e3e1`. Use the common column labeling in which the two \(I_1\) rows of \(P_1\) are
\[
(p,-a,-b),\qquad (-c,r,-d),
\]
with \(p,r,a,b,c,d>0\), and put
\[
s=\frac{2-(g_2)_3}{4}.
\]
Decide whether a sequence of full compatible strict systems can satisfy
\[
\frac{\max\{p,r\}}s\longrightarrow\infty.
\]
Either prove an explicit uniform upper bound, strong enough when inserted into the exact shifted-cap formulas to force the required deep-cap loss, or give an exact rational full strict system or a rigorously verified rational sequence showing that the ratio can diverge.
triangle-double-support-ratio-compatibil.status_reason: Accepted fact `987dc770ddaf5b3b` proves the uniform full-system estimate `max{p,r}/s < 22464` and the resulting fixed shifted-cap decrement. Thus the middle-only support-ratio divergence cannot occur after endpoint compatibility and the third strict row are imposed.
triangle-double-support-ratio-compatibil.success_criterion: The proof must work on the full endpoint compatibility min-column strata, retain determinant nonzero and all three strict literal rows, and derive an explicit bound whose substitution gives a strict capacity improvement. A divergent construction must verify the full matrix system exactly at every member or give one exact rational full counterexample; scalar profiles or a middle matrix alone are insufficient.

triangle-edge-frame-enhanced-payment.relation_to_goal: The accepted product-cover fact gives only \(\sum e_i\ge m\), which closes \(y\ge1-x/2\). The displayed strengthening is exactly the additional payment needed to reach \(2T/9\) throughout the lower pinch \(1-x<y<1-x/2\). It uses compatibility and the common edge frame rather than independent bonuses.
triangle-edge-frame-enhanced-payment.statement:
Assume the locked problem, let \(A_1\) be a nondegenerate triangle of area \(a_1\), and put \(m=\min(a_0,a_2)\), \(M=\max(a_0,a_2)\). Let \(H_1,H_2,H_3\) be a normalized strict three-halfspace certificate whose middle caps are edge-parallel vertex caps of \(A_1\). If \(e_i\) is the total endpoint contribution of \(H_i\), determine whether compatibility forces
\[
\sum_{i=1}^3e_i\ge
\frac23\bigl(M+m-a_1\bigr).
\]
If true, combine it with the accepted edge-frame triangle inequality to close the entire residual edge-frame case. If false, give an exact compatible polytopal triple and strict edge-frame certificate violating the bound, and derive the strongest correct area-dependent replacement.
triangle-edge-frame-enhanced-payment.status_reason: Accepted fact `ff2936496c91bca4` gives an exact compatible counterexample to the registered literal payment because the statement omitted residual balance. The same fact supplies the sharp slope-routed replacement and closes nonempty residual slope regions, but the corrected all-slope residual assertion remains open and must be registered separately.
triangle-edge-frame-enhanced-payment.success_criterion: A complete proof of the stated payment and the resulting depth bound, or a fully verified exact compatible counterexample together with a sharp replacement inequality that closes a nonempty part of the lower pinch.

triangle-fixed-completion-qe.relation_to_goal: The round-120 obstacle gives a lossless normalization to finitely many rational polynomial cells in ((\alpha,P,Q,\eta)). Deciding those cells is the first exact computational test of the sole surviving contained-support calibration. Feasibility gives a full triangle witness; infeasibility removes the strongest known fixed survivor and may expose a chamber-wide inequality.
triangle-fixed-completion-qe.statement:
Decide the exact fixed endpoint-completion problem of accepted fact `7d66445eba62df98` for
\[
A=\frac18,qquad B=\frac{11249}{10000},
\qquad
L=\begin{pmatrix}
-32877&46362&-17003\\
-67122&2&53678\\
100000&-46363&-36674
\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Use a branch-complete exact semialgebraic decision over all cap-order cells, determinant signs, and row-minimum choices. Either produce rational (U,V,\sigma) satisfying every original compatibility and strict row condition, or give a reproducible exact infeasibility certificate covering all real (U,V,\sigma).
triangle-fixed-completion-qe.status_reason: Accepted fact `8772b8ab38a4e1b6` proves a global third-row lower bound for every real compatible endpoint completion of the fixed calibration, so the fixed completion system is infeasible.
triangle-fixed-completion-qe.success_criterion: Success is one exact rational completion with every original condition checked, or a branch-complete exact real-algebraic infeasibility certificate with a reproducible script or hand-checkable cell certificates. Timeout, floating-point infeasibility, or elimination of selected cells is an obstacle only.

triangle-fixed-third-row.relation_to_goal: The third fixed-row allowance is the smallest endpoint budget by several orders of magnitude. Proving the displayed inequality makes the fixed completion impossible without full quantifier elimination. A refutation identifies the exact cap-order cell in which the remaining two rows must be tested and prevents the tiny-budget heuristic from being reused.
triangle-fixed-third-row.statement:
Use the lossless fixed-completion normalization recorded in the round-120 obstacle. Thus
\[
\frac{\sqrt2}{4}\le\alpha\le2-\frac{\sqrt{11249}}{100},
\]
(P,Q\) are nonnegative column-stochastic (3\times3) matrices, every row of (P) has minimum zero,
\[
|\det P|=\frac1{8\alpha^2},qquad
|\det Q|=\frac{11249}{10000(2-\alpha)^2},
\qquad \sum_i\eta_i>2-\alpha,
\]
and, for the fixed matrix (L) of accepted fact `7d66445eba62df98`,
\[
u_3=\mathcal C((LP)_{3*};-\eta_3/\alpha),qquad
v_3=\mathcal C((LQ)_{3*};\eta_3/(2-\alpha)).
\]
Prove the sharp third-row obstruction
\[
\frac18u_3+\frac{11249}{10000}v_3
\ge\frac{3909493241}{50010041655000},
\]
or give an exact tuple ((\alpha,P,Q,\eta)) satisfying every displayed reduced-domain condition and strictly refuting it. Include the lossless normalization derivation if the result is promoted as a chamber fact.
triangle-fixed-third-row.status_reason: Accepted fact `8772b8ab38a4e1b6` proves a global third-row lower bound for every real compatible endpoint completion of the fixed calibration, so the fixed completion system is infeasible.
triangle-fixed-third-row.success_criterion: Success is a global exact proof on the complete reduced domain, with every cap-order and determinant boundary, or an exact algebraic tuple satisfying all reduced constraints and the strict reverse inequality. A tuple omitting determinant, row-minimum, or sum constraints is insufficient.

triangle-n3-frontier-composition.relation_to_goal: This accepted-only composition would replace the obsolete contained-chamber frontier by the exact remaining triangular \(N=3\) frontier. It would leave two centroid-incidence orbits when \(t\leq1/2\), plus the structurally unclassified regime \(t>1/2\). It would not prove `triangle-three-row-exclusion` by itself.
triangle-n3-frontier-composition.statement:
Assume the full surviving triangular \(N=3\) system of accepted facts `09393c6edf1fc4e2`, `13c0df55864b79eb`, and `64760c76cadff481`, with all three literal row masses strictly below \(t=2(1+A+B)/9\). Prove that, after one simultaneous coordinate permutation, every remaining strict system satisfies exactly one of the following alternatives:

1. \(t>1/2\); or
2. \(t\leq1/2\), the large-endpoint centroid incidence set is empty, and the pair of nonempty disjoint centroid-incidence sets is either
   \[
   I_0=\{1\},\quad I_1=\{2\},
   \]
   or
   \[
   I_0=\{1\},\quad I_1=\{2,3\}.
   \]

In particular, prove that the third \(t\leq1/2\) orbit \(I_0=\{1,2\}, I_1=\{3\}\), including all nonzero middle chambers and arbitrary zero-entry boundary strata, is impossible by accepted fact `806575336d04fac7`.
triangle-n3-frontier-composition.status_reason: Accepted fact `63975845ca0e2926` gives the exact endpoint-oriented frontier composition: for `t<=1/2` only the singleton-singleton and singleton-double incidence orbits remain, while `t>1/2` remains separate.
triangle-n3-frontier-composition.success_criterion: Success is a complete accepted-only proof with exact endpoint-orientation and coordinate-relabeling maps, an exhaustive split at \(t=1/2\), use of accepted fact `a5bbbf5d61041b23` for the large-endpoint centroid set, and no claim that either remaining orbit or the \(t>1/2\) regime has been excluded.

triangle-n3-sign-cell-transport-ledger.relation_to_goal: This supplies the exact sign-cell transport inequalities in the only remaining triangular branch and closes a nontrivial algebraic area region. It leaves only double/triple-cell overlap configurations for the full three-row exclusion.
triangle-n3-sign-cell-transport-ledger.statement:
In the surviving coordinate-sign normal form of accepted fact `09393c6edf1fc4e2`, normalize \(|P_0|=m\), \(|P_1|=1\), \(|P_2|=M\), and partition each triangle into coordinate sign cells \(p_J,r_J,z_J\). For three strict low rows, prove:

1. With \(E_\ell\) the sign-multiplicity excess on slice \(\ell\),
\[
z_\varnothing>\frac{1+m+M}{3}+E_0+E_1+E_2.
\]
2. For every endpoint sign-cell pair with \(p_Jz_H>0\),
\[
\frac14(\sqrt{p_J}+\sqrt{z_H})^2
\le\sum_{\varnothing\ne K\subseteq J\cup H}r_K.
\]
3. If \(b_k>4/9\) is a coordinate cap containing the middle centroid and
\[
d=\frac{2(m+M-1)}9,
\]
then every strict system must satisfy
\[
\frac14(\sqrt{m-d}+\sqrt M)^2<\frac59.
\]
Hence the \(N=3\) survivor is impossible whenever
\[
\left(\sqrt{m-\frac{2(m+M-1)}9}+\sqrt M\right)^2\ge\frac{20}{9}.
\]
triangle-n3-sign-cell-transport-ledger.status_reason: Accepted fact `88133f67065def5c` proves all registered sign-cell identities, Brunn-Minkowski inequalities, centroid-cap bounds, and the exact algebraic area exclusion.
triangle-n3-sign-cell-transport-ledger.success_criterion: Success requires exact sign-cell identities, strict/open boundary handling, every Brunn-Minkowski containment, the centroid-cap selection, and the endpoint-deletion minimization leading to the displayed area exclusion. Midpoint images from different cell pairs must not be assumed disjoint.

\[
(J_1,J_2)=(\{2\},\{2,3\}),
\quad(\{1,2\},\{2,3\}),
\quad(\{2,3\},\{2,3\}),

triangle-open-chamber-composition.status_reason: Accepted fact `82b7c8c40e88aaf1` composes the five-chamber classification with the two accepted exclusions, leaving exactly three open nonzero-entry chambers and preserving all zero-entry boundary strata.

triangle-single-single-circumscribed-fam.relation_to_goal: The round-124 endpoint seed has midpoint area below one but exact minimum circumscribed-triangle area `321 sqrt(3)/400>1`. This seven-parameter thin-triangle family is the smallest controlled enlargement of that seed and of accepted fact `97445670737faf68`. A feasible member supplies the first exact endpoint and middle geometry in the cap-free singleton-singleton orbit; a family-wide obstruction identifies which geometric parameter must be added next.
triangle-single-single-circumscribed-fam.statement:
For rational parameters \(q>1\), \(a,b,c,d,h,\varepsilon,\eta>0\), let
\[
\Phi_r(u,v)=\left(\frac{u+v}{2},\frac{v-u}{2},r-v\right)
\]
and define the endpoint triangles
\[
P_0=\Phi_{1+q}\!\left(\operatorname{conv}\{(-a,h),(b,h),(b,h+\varepsilon)\}\right),
\]
\[
P_2=\Phi_{1-q}\!\left(\operatorname{conv}\{(-c,-d),(c,-d),(0,-d+\eta)\}\right).
\]
Restrict to the open rational parameter region in which \(P_0\) is nondegenerate, has centroid incidence \(I_0=\{1\}\), and has a positive one-positive \(2\)-cell; \(P_2\) is nondegenerate and coordinatewise nonpositive; the endpoint areas \(A\leq B\) satisfy \(A/B<3/8\), \(A+B>1\), and \(B<1+A\).

Decide exactly whether this family contains parameters for which the midpoint polygon \((P_0+P_2)/2\) is contained in a rational nondegenerate triangle \(P_1\subset H_1\) of Hausdorff area exactly one whose centroid incidence is \(I_1=\{2\}\). If feasible, give exact parameters and \(P_1\), including its containment and centroid signs. If infeasible, prove a parameter-uniform lower bound greater than one for the minimum area of every containing triangle, or another exact family-wide obstruction.
triangle-single-single-circumscribed-fam.status_reason: The registered statement incorrectly required literal Hausdorff area one together with rational vertices in the coordinate-sum plane. No candidate from this flawed subgoal is promoted.
triangle-single-single-circumscribed-fam.success_criterion: Success is one exact rational feasible member with all plane sums, endpoint signs, active cell, areas, residual inequalities, midpoint polygon, containing-triangle area, containment, and middle centroid signs checked, or an exact proof excluding the complete stated open parameter region including parallel-edge and support-contact boundaries in its closure. A midpoint-area calculation without the minimum containing-triangle audit is insufficient.

triangle-single-single-circumscribed-nor.relation_to_goal: This corrects only the area normalization in `triangle-single-single-circumscribed-family`; it does not alter the endpoint geometry. triangle-single-single-circumscribed-nor.statement:
For every coordinate-sum plane \(H_r\), use the normalized planar area
\[
|Q|_*:=\frac{2}{\sqrt3}\,\mathcal H_2(Q),
\]
so that \(\Phi_r(u,v)=((u+v)/2,(v-u)/2,r-v)\) preserves ordinary \((u,v)\)-area. For rational parameters \(q>1\), \(a,b,c,d,h,\varepsilon,\eta>0\), define
\[
P_0=\Phi_{1+q}\!\left(\operatorname{conv}\{(-a,h),(b,h),(b,h+\varepsilon)\}\right),
\]
\[
P_2=\Phi_{1-q}\!\left(\operatorname{conv}\{(-c,-d),(c,-d),(0,-d+\eta)\}\right).
\]
Restrict to the open rational parameter region in which \(P_0\) is nondegenerate, has centroid incidence \(I_0=\{1\}\), and has a positive one-positive \(2\)-cell; \(P_2\) is nondegenerate and coordinatewise nonpositive; and the normalized endpoint areas \(A=|P_0|_*\leq B=|P_2|_*\) satisfy \(A/B<3/8\), \(A+B>1\), and \(B<1+A\).

Decide exactly whether this family contains parameters for which \((P_0+P_2)/2\) is contained in a rational nondegenerate triangle \(P_1\subset H_1\) with \(|P_1|_*=1\) and centroid incidence \(I_1=\{2\}\). Give exact feasible data or a parameter-uniform obstruction.

triangle-single-single-circumscribed-nor.success_criterion: Success is one exact rational feasible member with every normalized area, plane sum, endpoint sign, active cell, residual inequality, midpoint containment, and middle centroid sign checked, or an exact proof excluding the complete stated parameter region. triangle-single-single-mixed-area.relation_to_goal: If the strict mixed-area bound holds, no area-one middle triangle can contain the endpoint midpoint body, so it eliminates the cap-free singleton-singleton branch with at least one active off-index cell before any middle-cap analysis. Accepted fact `003adef77e7c9efe` supplies a strong width mismatch, while accepted fact `97445670737faf68` verifies the mechanism only for one fixed seed. A rational refutation would show that width mismatch alone cannot close this branch and would supply a compatible-size endpoint seed for the full matrix search.
triangle-single-single-mixed-area.statement:
Assume the singleton-singleton transformed endpoint geometry of accepted facts `003adef77e7c9efe` and `a5bbbf5d61041b23`. Thus \(q>1\), \(P_0\subset H_{1+q}\) and \(P_2\subset H_{1-q}\) are nondegenerate triangles of areas \(A\leq B\), \(A/B<3/8\),
\[
I_0=\{1\},\qquad I_1=\{2\},
\]
the large endpoint is cap-free,
\[
P_2\subseteq\{x_1\leq0,x_2\leq0,x_3\leq0\},
\]
and at least one one-positive small-endpoint cell with index \(j\in\{2,3\}\) has positive area. Decide the global mixed-area assertion
\[
\left|\frac{P_0+P_2}{2}\right|>1.
\]
If it is true, prove it exactly for every such endpoint pair, including all edge-direction coincidences and support-contact boundaries. If it is false, give exact rational triangles satisfying every hypothesis and compute the midpoint Minkowski polygon and its area exactly.
triangle-single-single-mixed-area.status_reason: Accepted fact `030a39d4d243e22a` excludes the full singleton-singleton orbit by a stronger circumscribed-triangle obstruction, so deciding whether every midpoint Minkowski polygon itself has area greater than one is no longer needed for the target proof.
triangle-single-single-mixed-area.success_criterion: Success is a parameter-uniform exact mixed-area proof, or one exact rational counterexample to the asserted mixed-area inequality with every plane sum, centroid sign, active sign cell, cap-free condition, area ratio, edge ordering, and Minkowski area verified. triangle-single-single-parallelogram.relation_to_goal: Every parallelogram contained in a triangle has at most half its area. Therefore \(\Pi(K)>1/2\) rules out every normalized-area-one middle triangle containing \(K\) and closes the singleton-singleton orbit. Accepted fact `72810a77f1328d7c` proves this mechanism on one thin-triangle family; this subgoal asks whether the mechanism follows from the full incidence and area hypotheses rather than that parametrization.
triangle-single-single-parallelogram.statement:
Assume the full singleton-singleton endpoint geometry of `triangle-single-single-mixed-area`, including normalized planar area, \(A/B<3/8\), \(A+B>1\), \(B<1+A\), the cap-free large endpoint, and an active one-positive small-endpoint cell. Put
\[
K=\frac{P_0+P_2}{2}
\]
and let
\[
\Pi(K)=\sup\{|Q|:Q\subseteq K\text{ is a parallelogram}\}.
\]
Prove the affine-invariant bound \(\Pi(K)>1/2\), including every edge-direction coincidence and support-contact boundary, or give exact rational endpoint triangles satisfying all hypotheses and prove exactly that \(\Pi(K)\le1/2\).
triangle-single-single-parallelogram.status_reason: Accepted fact `030a39d4d243e22a` proves that the full singleton-singleton endpoint geometry forces a parallelogram of normalized area greater than `6/11` inside the midpoint Minkowski sum. Prove that each \(\Delta\cap L_i\) is a corner triangle containing exactly
one vertex of \(\Delta\), and that the three caps contain three distinct
vertices.

triangle-three-row-global-normal-form.statement:
Assume the \(N=3\) exact barycentric system of accepted fact `64760c76cadff481`, and write \(q=\sigma_1+\sigma_2+\sigma_3\), \(A=|\det U|\), \(B=|\det V|\), and \(M_i\) for the three row masses. Prove:

2. If \(q>1\), then \(\sum_iM_i\ge1+A\), and the strict low-row system is impossible whenever \(1+A\ge2B\).
3. If \(q<-1\), then \(\sum_iM_i\ge1+B\), and the strict low-row system is impossible whenever \(1+B\ge2A\).
4. Using the residual strip and accepted fact `a75a8435d7e8176f`, reduce every remaining strict system, up to swapping endpoints, to
\[
B=M,\qquad A=m,\qquad q>1,\qquad1+m<2M.
\]
Show that the genuinely three-row remaining case has \(\det L\ne0\), and rewrite it by the common affine map \(L\) and translation \(\sigma\) as three compatible triangles in the planes \(\sum x_i=1+q,1,1-q\), with the row masses equal to their three coordinate-nonnegative cap totals.
triangle-three-row-global-normal-form.status_reason: Accepted fact `09393c6edf1fc4e2` proves every aggregate branch, singular-\(L\) exclusion, and the exact coordinate-sign affine normal form requested by the subgoal.
triangle-three-row-global-normal-form.success_criterion: Success requires exact threshold-sum cover arguments, the residual area comparison, a proof that a singular \(L\) reduces to an already excluded two-row or high-mass case, and a literal affine/translation reconstruction of the remaining coordinate-sign model. triangular-projection-extremality.relation_to_goal:
Accepted theorem `aef70a60593c53a2` already proves the required inequality for
triangle projection splines. A valid extremality theorem would transfer that
proof to arbitrary convex bodies direction by direction.
triangular-projection-extremality.statement:
Let \(X\) be the projection of the uniform measure on a planar convex body
along a fixed linear functional, normalized to a compact interval, and let
its density be the concave section-length function. Derive the sharp lower
inequality for the three-threshold slope-coupled functional needed in
`homothetic-convex-centroid`, and prove that an extremizer may be taken to
have affine density, equivalently to come from a triangle.
triangular-projection-extremality.status_reason: The claimed affine-density extremality is false. An exact one-kink concave projection density with the required support, mean, and marked endpoint gives a strictly smaller tail functional than every admissible affine density.
triangular-projection-extremality.success_criterion:
State the exact functional, normalization, moment constraint, and boundary
conditions. Prove the extremal reduction, including densities with flat or
degenerate pieces. A heuristic appeal to localization is not sufficient.

triangular-two-routing-witness.relation_to_goal: Accepted reflected-depth facts convert the displayed inequality into a middle-slice witness for the locked target. The maximum permits a direction-dependent choice between two reflected routings and is therefore not refuted by the failed common-allocation architecture. A counterexample would decisively remove this witness-based replacement even in the sharp triangular regime.
triangular-two-routing-witness.statement:
Assume \(A_0\) is the larger outer slice, \(A_0\) and \(A_1\) are nondegenerate triangles, \(A_2\) is an arbitrary nonempty two-dimensional convex body, \((A_0+A_2)/2\subseteq A_1\), and the areas lie in the accepted strict residual strip. Determine whether there always exists \(z\in A_1\) such that for every \(q\in\mathbb S^1\),
\[
F_{1,q}(q\cdot z)+
\max\!\left\{
\min\!\left(a_2,F_{0,q}\!\left(2q\cdot z-\max_{A_2}q\cdot x\right)\right),
\min\!\left(a_0,F_{2,q}\!\left(2q\cdot z-\max_{A_0}q\cdot x\right)\right)
\right\}
\ge\frac{2T}{9}.
\]
Prove the statement or give exact compatible rational polygons violating it while identifying whether the true mixed depth region is nevertheless nonempty.
triangular-two-routing-witness.status_reason: Accepted fact `74e60bee4b401289` gives an exact compatible rational counterexample inside the strict residual strip, with all three slices triangular, to the proposed direction-adapted maximum of the two reflected routings. The true mixed depth region is nevertheless nonempty, so the witness architecture is false and the full endpoint infimal convolution must be retained.
triangular-two-routing-witness.success_criterion: A complete proof for all directions and support endpoints, or an exact rational compatible counterexample with every cap and residual-area condition checked. Numerical evidence without an exact certificate is insufficient.

two-tent-tail-inequality.relation_to_goal: Linear optimization with one moment constraint should attain its minimum on at most two tents. This route attacks the finite extremal family directly and is independent of finding a global functional-analytic dual certificate.
two-tent-tail-inequality.statement: Assuming only the explicit formulas for normalized tents on a common support \([0,L]\), prove the weighted-tail inequality for every probability mixture of at most two tents whose peak locations have mean \(3-L\). Reduce the claim to exact rational or polynomial inequalities in \(L\), the two peak locations, the mixing weight, \(a,c,w_0,w_2\), and discharge all chambers or identify the first exact unresolved chamber.
two-tent-tail-inequality.status_reason: The direct 75-chamber route is superseded by accepted fact `52e60b02804280c7`, whose single affine minorant proves the full tent-mixture inequality without the unresolved degree-eight sign check.
two-tent-tail-inequality.success_criterion: A candidate theorem covering all admissible two-tent mixtures, or a bounded exact chamber decomposition with a rigorously stated remaining polynomial sign problem.

two-triangle-pinch-routing.relation_to_goal: The previous audit shows that any genuinely dangerous pinch sequence should approach two triangles, while all common-center homothetic triangle triples are already closed. This subgoal attacks the remaining finite-dimensional relative-position problem directly and keeps the endpoint and middle witness options available.
two-triangle-pinch-routing.statement:
Assume the locked problem with the larger endpoint \(A_0\) and the middle body \(A_1\) both nondegenerate triangles, with arbitrary relative position and orientation, arbitrary compatible two-dimensional \(A_2\), and normalized residual parameters
\[
0<x=\frac{a_2}{a_0}\le\frac9{25},
\qquad
1-x<y=\frac{a_1}{a_0}<1+x.
\]
Using the exact middle profile, hybrid midpoint measure, and reflected-depth saturation as needed, prove the \(2T/9\) target for this two-triangle class, or prove it on a nonempty open subregion not already covered by the large-slice, hybrid, homothetic, minimal-middle, or aligned edge-frame facts. If the full statement is false, give an exact compatible counterexample.
two-triangle-pinch-routing.status_reason: Accepted fact `2b809ac6ae61991f` proves a reflected-core criterion for arbitrary compatible small endpoints and closes a genuinely open, nonaligned two-triangle subregion below the previous edge-frame area boundary.
two-triangle-pinch-routing.success_criterion: A verifier-ready theorem for the full stated class, or a rigorously quantified new open subregion with explicit witness and area footprint. An exact compatible counterexample is also decisive. Purely numerical evidence is not sufficient.

universal-centroid-residual-domain.relation_to_goal:
This turns the newly accepted arbitrary-body centroid theorem into an exact
shape-independent search domain.  In particular it would eliminate every
area ratio \(m/M\ge r_0\approx0.618423\) and the lower part of the old
residual strip for \(1/5<r<r_0\).
universal-centroid-residual-domain.statement:
Combine accepted facts `15bb2c1680a0254e` and `c02e26ea799dadd7`
to determine exactly which normalized residual area parameters remain
possible for a counterexample.  With
\[
M=1,\qquad r=m/M,\qquad s=a_1/M,
\]
prove that the centroid criterion is equivalent on the residual strip to
\[
7r-11-18s+12\sqrt{5s}\ge0.
\]
Define
\[
S_c(r)=\left(\frac{2\sqrt5+\sqrt{14r-2}}6\right)^2,\qquad
r_0=\frac{163-12\sqrt{51}}{125}.
\]
Prove, with all endpoint and squaring signs checked, that every counterexample
must lie in
\[
\begin{cases}
0<r\le1/5,\quad L(r)<s<U(r),\\
1/5<r<r_0,\quad S_c(r)<s<U(r),
\end{cases}
\]
where \(L,U\) are the exact residual boundaries in
`15bb2c1680a0254e`.
universal-centroid-residual-domain.status_reason: Accepted fact `6f36d5017fd780b5` proves the registered residual-domain characterization exactly.
universal-centroid-residual-domain.success_criterion:
Give an exact algebraic proof of the equivalence, monotonicity in \(s\), all
intersections with both piecewise residual boundaries, the values \(1/5\)
and \(r_0\), and the correct strict or nonstrict endpoint conventions.

universal-middle-centroid-area-criterion.relation_to_goal:
This strictly extends accepted fact `a6808da3e0b737ca`, whose statement is
restricted to triangular slices.  If valid, it removes the same normalized
area region for every compatible triple and can be used in all later
counterexample reductions without any shape hypothesis.
universal-middle-centroid-area-criterion.statement:
Let \(A_0,A_1,A_2\subset\mathbb R^2\) be arbitrary compact
two-dimensional convex bodies satisfying
\[
\frac{A_0+A_2}{2}\subseteq A_1.
\]
Write \(M=\max\{|A_0|,|A_2|\}\), \(m=\min\{|A_0|,|A_2|\}\),
\(a=|A_1|\), \(T=M+m+a\), and assume
\[
M-m<a<M+m.
\]
Set \(\delta=2(M+m-a)/9\).  Prove that if
\[
\left(\sqrt M+\sqrt{m-\delta}\right)^2\ge\frac{20a}{9},
\]
then the centroid \(g\) of \(A_1\) satisfies
\[
h_S((1,g))\ge\frac{2T}{9}.
\]
The proof must cover all endpoint allocations, horizontal halfspaces, equality
in the displayed hypothesis, and arbitrary convex bodies rather than only
triangles.
universal-middle-centroid-area-criterion.status_reason:
Accepted fact `c02e26ea799dadd7` proves the registered centroid criterion for
arbitrary compact two-dimensional convex bodies.  It retains every endpoint
allocation, treats horizontal and limiting halfspaces, and permits equality
in the area hypothesis.  This strictly extends the triangular statement in
accepted fact `a6808da3e0b737ca`.
universal-middle-centroid-area-criterion.success_criterion:
A self-contained proof derives the full endpoint infimal-convolution lower
bound from compatibility, planar Brunn–Minkowski, and the accepted planar
Grünbaum centroid inequality for arbitrary convex bodies.  It verifies all
strictness and boundary steps and concludes the exact locked depth statement
at the middle centroid.

weighted-nested-convex-center.relation_to_goal:
This is the shape-independent version of the successful common-\(U\) coupling
route. A theorem here would move beyond triangles toward the full Minkowski
equality family while remaining a positive proof strategy.
weighted-nested-convex-center.statement:
Let \(K\subset\mathbb R^2\) be a nonempty two-dimensional convex body, let
\(0<k\le1\), \(q>0\), and let \(kK\) be a homothetic copy with a common
center. For
\[
\eta(E)=|K\cap E|+q\,\frac{|kK\cap E|}{|kK|},
\]
derive a quantitative halfplane-depth lower bound for some point of \(K\)
that is strong enough, under an explicit scalar condition on \(k,q\), to
recover the \(2T/9\) target for homothetic three-slice triples.
weighted-nested-convex-center.status_reason: Choosing either component centroid for a nested weighted measure recovers exactly the already-certified large-slice or outer-centroid regimes and cannot enter the strict residual domain.
weighted-nested-convex-center.success_criterion:
State the exact bound and prove it from planar convexity. It may use a
precisely stated classical theorem with a primary source and an applicability
check. If the target strength requires an additional geometric parameter,
identify and prove the corrected bound rather than testing examples.

weighted-tail-dual-certificate.relation_to_goal: Together with the geometric reduction, this inequality proves the residual arbitrary-shape homothetic family, including the Brunn-Minkowski equality boundary normalized by accepted fact `eee2bdfe64ccf5b1`.
weighted-tail-dual-certificate.statement:
Prove the universal weighted-tail inequality
\[
G(1)+a^2G(w_0)+c^2G(w_2)\ge \frac{2(1+a^2+c^2)}9
\]
for every compactly supported nonnegative concave probability density of mean \(1\), every \(a\ge c>0\) satisfying \(1<a^2+c^2\), \(a+c<2\), and \(a^2<1+c^2\), and every real \(w_0,w_2\) satisfying \(aw_0+cw_2=2\). Seek a direct dual or supporting-line certificate that remains valid for one-kink extremizers.
weighted-tail-dual-certificate.status_reason: The registered density class was broader than the geometric normalization. Without anchoring the support at \(0\), translation makes the claim false: a decreasing triangular density on \([9/10,6/5]\) has mean \(1\), and for \(a=1\), \(c=1/2\), \(w_0=w_2=4/3\), both outer tails vanish while \(G(1)=4/9<1/2\). The corrected exact subgoal is `anchored-weighted-tail-dual`.
weighted-tail-dual-certificate.success_criterion: A complete proof covering all support lengths and threshold orderings, or one exact first obstruction that isolates a smaller remaining chamber without asserting a counterexample to the locked theorem.
